计算机就像小提琴。你可以想象一个新手先试用留声机，再试用小提琴。他说，后者听起来糟透了。这正是我们从人文学者和大多数计算机科学家那里听到的论调。他们说，计算机程序适合特定用途，但并不灵活。小提琴或打字机也同样如此，直到你学会怎样使用它。A computer is like a violin. You can imagine a novice trying first a phonograph and then a violin. The latter, he says, sounds terrible. That is the argument we have heard from our humanists and most of our computer scientists. Computer programs are good, they say, for particular purposes, but they aren't flexible. Neither is a violin, or a typewriter, until you learn how to use it.

Marvin Minsky，《为什么编程是表达理解不透彻、表述不严密的思想的良好媒介》，载《设计与规划》，(1967)Marvin Minsky, “Why Programming Is a Good Medium for Expressing Poorly-Understood and Sloppily-Formulated Ideas” in Design and Planning, (1967)

序Foreword

编写程序时，你有时会陷入困境。这也许是因为你意识到自己没有充分理解问题的某个方面，但更常见的原因是：你在程序设计的早期就作出了某个决定，例如选择某种数据结构或某种代码组织方式，结果发现它的限制太多，而且还很难撤销。Sometimes when you're writing a program, you get stuck. Maybe it's because you realize you didn't appreciate some aspect of the problem, but all too often it's because you made some decision early in the program design process, about a choice of data structure or a way of organizing the code, that has turned out to be too limiting, and also to be difficult to undo.

本书是一堂大师课，讲授保持灵活性的具体程序组织策略。如今我们都知道，虽然声明一个固定大小的数组来存放待处理数据非常容易，但这样的设计决定最终可能成为令人不快的限制，使程序无法处理超过某个长度的输入行，或无法处理超过某个固定数量的记录。许多安全漏洞，尤其是互联网代码中的安全漏洞，都源于分配了固定大小的内存缓冲区，却没有检查待处理的数据是否能装进缓冲区。动态分配的存储空间，无论由 C 风格的 malloc 库还是由自动垃圾收集器提供，虽然更复杂，却灵活得多，而且还有一个额外好处：不容易出错，尤其是在编程语言始终检查数组访问、确保索引不越界的情况下。这还只是一个非常简单的例子。This book is a master class in specific program organization strategies that maintain flexibility. We all know by now that while it is very easy to declare an array of fixed size to hold data to be processed, such a design decision can turn out to be an unpleasant limitation that may make it impossible to handle input lines longer than a certain length, or to handle more than a fixed number of records. Many security bugs, especially in the code for the Internet, have been consequences of allocating a fixed-size memory buffer and then failing to check whether the data to be processed would fit in the buffer. Dynamically allocated storage (whether provided by a C-style malloc library or by an automatic garbage collector), while more complicated, is much more flexible and, as an extra benefit, less error-prone (especially when the programming language always checks array references to make sure the index is within bounds). That's just a very simple example.

许多早期编程语言的设计，实际上作出了一项设计承诺，要反映被称为哈佛架构的硬件组织方式：代码在这里，数据在那里，代码的工作就是处理数据。但事实表明，代码与数据之间这种僵硬而疏远的分离，对程序组织构成了重大限制。早在二十世纪结束之前，我们就已从 ML、Scheme 和 Haskell 等函数式编程语言，以及 Simula、Smalltalk、C++ 和 Java 等面向对象编程语言中学到：能够把代码当作数据、把数据当作代码，以及把少量代码与相关数据捆绑在一起，而不是将代码和数据分别组织成整块，都有其优势。最灵活的数据形式是记录结构，其中不仅可以包含数字、字符等“基本数据项”，还可以包含对函数等可执行代码的引用。最强大的代码形式会构造其他代码，并将这些代码与恰到好处、经过精心选取的数据捆绑在一起；这样一个捆绑体不仅仅是“函数指针”，而是函数式语言中的闭包，或者面向对象语言中的对象。A number of early programming language designs in effect made a design commitment to reflect the style of hardware organization called the Harvard architecture: the code is here, the data is there, and the job of the code is to massage the data. But an inflexible, arm's-length separation between code and data turns out to be a significant limitation on program organization. Well before the end of the twentieth century, we learned from functional programming languages (such as ML, Scheme, and Haskell) and from object-oriented programming languages (such as Simula, Smalltalk, C++, and Java) that there are advantages to being able to treat code as data, to treat data as code, and to bundle smallish amounts of code and related data together rather than organizing code and data separately as monolithic chunks. The most flexible kind of data is a record structure that can contain not only “primitive data items” such as numbers and characters but also references to executable code, such as a function. The most powerful kind of code constructs other code that has been bundled with just the right amount of curated data; such a bundle is not just a “function pointer” but a closure (in a functional language) or an object (in an object-oriented language).

Jerry Sussman 和 Chris Hanson 凭借两人合计长达一个世纪的编程经验，介绍了一组在 MIT 数十年的教学中开发并检验过的技术，进一步扩展了这一实现灵活性的基本策略。不要只使用函数；要使用泛型函数，因为它具有普通函数所不具备的开放性。保持函数短小。函数返回的最佳结果，往往是另一个函数，而这个函数已用精心选取的数据加以定制。要做好将数据当作代码的准备，必要时甚至不妨在应用程序中创建一门新的嵌入式编程语言。（从一种角度看，Scheme 语言就是这样起步的：Lisp 的 MacLisp 方言不支持完全通用的函数闭包形式，因此 Jerry 和我干脆用 MacLisp 编写了一个嵌入式 Lisp 方言，来支持我们所需的那种函数闭包。）要做好准备，用一种更通用的数据结构替换原来的数据结构，使其涵盖原结构并扩展其能力。使用自动约束传播，避免过早确定哪些数据项是输入、哪些是输出。Jerry Sussman and Chris Hanson draw on their collective century of programming experience to present a set of techniques, developed and tested during decades of teaching at MIT, that further extend this basic strategy for flexibility. Don't just use functions; use generic functions, which are open-ended in a way that plain functions are not. Keep functions small. Often the best thing for a function to return is another function (that has been customized with curated data). Be prepared to treat data as code, perhaps even to the extreme of creating a new embedded programming language within your application if necessary. (That is one view of how the Scheme language got its start: the MacLisp dialect of Lisp did not support a completely general form of function closure, so Jerry and I simply used MacLisp to code an embedded dialect of Lisp that did support the kind of function closure we needed.) Be prepared to replace a data structure with a more general data structure that subsumes the original and extends its capabilities. Use automatic constraint propagation to avoid a premature commitment to which data items are inputs and which are outputs.

本书不是综述，也不是入门教程——如前所述，它是一堂大师课。在每一章中，请观看两位专家如何逐步开发一段可运行的代码来演示一种高级技术，如何一边开发一边解释策略，并不时停下来指出一个陷阱或消除一项限制。然后，在要求你动手时，要准备好通过扩展数据结构或编写额外代码，亲自展示这项技术；接着还要运用你的想象力和创造力，超越他们已经演示的内容。本书的思想丰富而深刻；认真研读文字和代码，定会有所收获。This book is not a survey, or a tutorial—as I said before, it is a master class. In each chapter, watch as two experts demonstrate an advanced technique by incrementally developing a chunk of working code, explaining the strategy as they go, occasionally pausing to point out a pitfall or to remove a limitation. Then be prepared, when called on, to demonstrate the technique yourself, by extending a data structure or writing additional code—and then to use your imagination and creativity to go beyond what they have demonstrated. The ideas in this book are rich and deep; close attention to both the prose and the code will be rewarded.

Guy L. Steele Jr.Guy L. Steele Jr.

前言Preface

我们都曾花费太多时间，试图把一段旧代码扭成另一副模样，以便用于编写它时根本没有意识到会需要的用途。这极大地浪费了时间和精力。不幸的是，各种压力迫使我们编写的代码只能很好地服务于极其特定的目的，其中很少有可重用的部分。但我们认为，事情不必如此。We have all spent too much time trying to deform an old piece of code so that it could be used in a way that we didn't realize would be needed when we wrote it. This is a terrible waste of time and effort. Unfortunately, there are many pressures on us to write code that works very well for a very specific purpose, with few reusable parts. But we think that this is not necessary.

要构建这样一种系统很困难：在比设计者预期更广泛的情境中，它仍能表现得令人满意。最好的系统是可演化的：只需少量修改，就能适应新情境。我们怎样才能设计出具有这种灵活性的系统？It is hard to build systems that have acceptable behavior over a larger class of situations than was anticipated by their designers. The best systems are evolvable: they can be adapted to new situations with only minor modification. How can we design systems that are flexible in this way?

如果为程序添加新特性时，我们只需添加一些代码，而不必修改现有代码库，那该多好。构建代码库时，只要采用某些组织原则，并在那时加入适当的钩子，我们往往就能做到这一点。It would be nice if all we had to do to add a new feature to a program was to add some code, without changing the existing code base. We can often do this by using certain organizing principles in the construction of the code base and incorporating appropriate hooks at that time.

对生物系统的观察，能让我们充分了解如何构建灵活且可演化的系统。最初为支持符号人工智能而开发的技术，可以视为增强程序及其他工程系统的灵活性和适应性的方法。相比之下，计算机科学中的常见实践，却在积极阻碍构建那些容易修改以用于新情境的系统。Observations of biological systems tell us a great deal about how to make flexible and evolvable systems. Techniques originally developed in support of symbolic artificial intelligence can be viewed as ways of enhancing flexibility and adaptability in programs and other engineered systems. By contrast, common practice of computer science actively discourages the construction of systems that are easily modified for use in novel settings.

我们经常把自己编进死胡同，不得不花费大量精力重构代码才能脱身。如今，我们积累了足够的经验，觉得已经能够辨识、分离并演示一些策略与技术；实践证明，它们能够有效地构建大型系统，使这些系统适应最初设计时未曾预料到的用途。本书将分享我们合计超过 100 年编程经验的部分成果。We have often programmed ourselves into corners and had to expend great effort refactoring code to escape from those corners. We have now accumulated enough experience to feel that we can identify, isolate, and demonstrate strategies and techniques that we have found to be effective for building large systems that can be adapted for purposes that were not anticipated in the original design. In this book we share some of the fruits of our over 100 years of programming experience.

关于本书This book

本书源于我们在 MIT 的计算机编程教学。多年前，我们开设这门课，希望让高年级本科生和研究生接触一些方法与技术，用于构建人工智能应用中的核心程序，例如数学符号操作系统和基于规则的系统。我们希望学生能灵活地构建这些系统，以便更容易将它们组合成更强大的系统。我们还希望向学生讲授依赖关系：如何跟踪它们，以及如何利用它们进行解释和控制回溯。This book was developed as the result of teaching computer programming at MIT. We started this class many years ago, intending to expose advanced undergraduate students and graduate students to techniques and technologies that are useful in the construction of programs that are central to artificial intelligence applications, such as mathematical symbolic manipulation and rule-based systems. We wanted the students to be able to build these systems flexibly, so that it would be easier to combine such systems to make even more powerful systems. We also wanted to teach students about dependencies—how they can be tracked, and how they can be used for explanation and to control backtracking.

虽然这门课过去和现在都很成功，但事实证明，起初我们对这些材料的理解，并没有最初以为的那么深。因此，我们投入大量精力打磨工具，使我们的思想更加精确。如今我们认识到，这些技术并非只适用于人工智能应用。我们认为，凡是构建复杂系统的人，例如构建计算机语言编译器和集成开发环境的人，都会从我们的经验中受益。本书以目前课堂使用的讲义和习题集为基础。Although the class was and is successful, it turned out that in the beginning we did not have as much understanding of the material as we originally believed. So we put a great deal of effort into sharpening our tools and making our ideas more precise. We now realize that these techniques are not just for artificial intelligence applications. We think that anyone who is building complex systems, such as computer-language compilers and integrated development environments, will benefit from our experience. This book is built on the lectures and problem sets that are now used in our class.

内容安排The contents

本书的材料远远超过一学期课程所能涵盖的范围。因此，每次开课，我们都会有所取舍。第 1 章介绍我们的编程理念。在这里，我们将灵活性放到自然与工程的宏大背景下加以展现。我们试图说明，灵活性与效率和正确性同样重要。在随后各章中，我们介绍各种技术，并用一组组习题来阐明它们。这是本书组织内容的一项重要原则。There is much more material in this book than can be covered in a single-semester class. So each time we offer the class we pick and choose what to present. Chapter 1 is an introduction to our programming philosophy. Here we show flexibility in the grand context of nature and of engineering. We try to make the point that flexibility is as important an issue as efficiency and correctness. In each subsequent chapter we introduce techniques and illustrate them with sets of exercises. This is an important organizing principle for the book.

第 2 章探讨一些普遍适用的方法，用来构建具有发展余地的系统。组织灵活系统的一种强有力的方法，是将其构建为一组领域专用语言的集合，每门语言都适合轻松表达某个子系统的构造。在这里，我们开发用于构建领域专用语言的基本工具：展示如何围绕可混搭的部件组织子系统，如何用组合子灵活地组合它们，如何用包装器使部件更加通用，以及如何通过抽象出领域模型来简化程序。In chapter 2 we explore some universally applicable ways of building systems with room to grow. A powerful way to organize a flexible system is to build it as an assembly of domain-specific languages, each appropriate for easily expressing the construction of a subsystem. Here we develop basic tools for the development of domain-specific languages: we show how subsystems can be organized around mix-and-match parts, how they can be flexibly combined with combinators, how wrappers can be used to generalize parts, and how we can often simplify a program by abstracting out a domain model.

第 3 章介绍一种威力极强、但也有潜在危险的灵活性技术：采用谓词分派的泛型过程。我们首先推广算术，使其能够处理符号代数表达式。随后展示如何通过为数据使用类型标签，让这种推广变得高效；并通过设计一个简单却容易扩展的冒险游戏，演示这项技术的威力。In chapter 3 we introduce the extremely powerful but potentially dangerous flexibility technique of predicate-dispatched generic procedures. We start by generalizing arithmetic to deal with symbolic algebraic expressions. We then show how such a generalization can be made efficient by using type tags for data, and we demonstrate the power of the technique with the design of a simple, but easy to elaborate, adventure game.

第 4 章介绍符号模式匹配，首先用它来实现项重写系统，随后结合合一，展示如何轻松实现类型推断。在这里，由于片段变量的存在，我们遇到了对回溯的需求。合一是我们首次看到表示和组合部分信息结构的威力的地方。本章最后将这一思想扩展到一般图的匹配。In chapter 4 we introduce symbolic pattern matching, first to enable term-rewriting systems, and later, with unification, to show how type inference can easily be made to work. Here we encounter the need for backtracking because of segment variables. Unification is the first place where we see the power of representing and combining partial-information structures. We end the chapter with extending the idea to matching general graphs.

第 5 章探讨解释和编译的威力。我们认为，程序员应当知道如何通过为一门更适于表达当前问题解法的语言构建解释器，来摆脱自己必须使用的编程语言的束缚。我们还展示如何在解释器／编译器系统中实现非确定性的 amb，从而自然地融入回溯搜索，以及如何使用续延。In chapter 5 we explore the power of interpretation and compilation. We believe that programmers should know how to escape the confines of whatever programming language they must use by making an interpreter for a language that is more appropriate for expressing the solution to the current problem. We also show how to naturally incorporate backtracking search by implementing nondeterministic amb in an interpreter/compiler system, and how to use continuations.

第 6 章展示如何构建由分层数据和分层过程组成的系统，其中每个数据项都可以附加各种元数据作为注解。底层数据的处理不受元数据影响，处理底层数据的代码甚至不知道元数据的存在，也不引用它。不过，元数据由其自身的过程处理，实际上与数据的处理并行进行。为阐明这一点，我们给数值量附加单位，并展示如何携带依赖信息，以说明数据是如何从原始来源推导而来的。In chapter 6 we show how to make systems of layered data and layered procedures, where each data item can be annotated with a variety of metadata. The processing of the underlying data is not affected by the metadata, and the code for processing the underlying data does not even know about or reference the metadata. However, the metadata is processed by its own procedures, effectively in parallel with the data. We illustrate this by attaching units to numerical quantities and by showing how to carry dependency information, giving the provenance of data, as derived from the primitive sources.

所有这些内容在第 7 章汇合起来；我们在这一章引入传播，以摆脱计算机语言中以表达式为中心的范式。在这里，我们以接线图的视角来看待模块的互连。这使我们能够灵活地整合来自多个来源的部分信息。利用分层数据支持依赖关系跟踪，就能实现依赖关系引导的回溯，从而大幅缩小大型复杂系统中的搜索空间。This is all brought together in chapter 7, where we introduce propagation to escape from the expression-oriented paradigm of computer languages. Here we have a wiring-diagram vision of connecting modules together. This allows the flexible incorporation of multiple sources of partial information. Using layered data to support tracking of dependencies enables the implementation of dependency-directed backtracking, which greatly reduces the search space in large and complex systems.

本书可用于组织多种高阶课程。我们在后续所有章节中都会使用第 2 章介绍的组合子思想和第 3 章介绍的泛型过程。不过，第 4 章的模式与模式匹配，以及第 5 章的求值器，在后面的章节中并未使用。第 5 章中后文唯一需要的材料，是 5.4 节和 5.4.1 节对 amb 的介绍。第 6 章的分层思想与泛型过程的思想密切相关，但又有新的变化。第 6 章以一个示例介绍了如何用分层实现依赖关系跟踪，这在传播（第 7 章）中成为不可或缺的要素；在那里，我们利用依赖关系优化回溯搜索。This book can be used to make a variety of advanced classes. We use the combinator idea introduced in chapter 2 and the generic procedures introduced in chapter 3 in all subsequent chapters. But patterns and pattern matching from chapter 4 and evaluators from chapter 5 are not used in later chapters. The only material from chapter 5 that is needed later is the introduction to amb in sections 5.4 and 5.4.1. The layering idea in chapter 6 is closely related to the idea of generic procedures, but with a new twist. The use of layering to implement dependency tracking, introduced as an example in chapter 6, becomes an essential ingredient in propagation (chapter 7), where we use the dependencies to optimize backtracking search.

SchemeScheme

本书中的代码用 Scheme 编写。Scheme 是 Lisp 的一种变体，以函数式编程为主。虽然 Scheme 并不是一门流行的语言，在工业界也未被广泛使用，但对本书而言，它是正确的选择。1The code in this book is written in Scheme, a mostly functional language that is a variant of Lisp. Although Scheme is not a popular language, or widely used in an industrial context, it is the right choice for this book.1

本书的目的是介绍和解释编程思想。由于许多原因，与更流行的语言相比，用 Scheme 编写的示例代码更短、更简单，更适于阐明这些思想。而且，有些思想用其他语言几乎不可能演示。The purpose of this book is the presentation and explanation of programming ideas. The presentation of example code to elucidate these ideas is shorter and simpler in Scheme than in more popular languages, for many reasons. And some of the ideas would be nearly impossible to demonstrate using other languages.

Lisp 家族以外的语言，在表达简单事物时也需要大量繁文缛节。唯一让我们的代码显得冗长的，是我们倾向于给计算对象取较长的描述性名称。Languages other than those in the Lisp family require lots of ceremony to say simple things. The only thing that makes our code long-winded is that we tend to use long descriptive names for computational objects.

Scheme 的语法极其简单：它只是自然语法分析树的一种表示，所需的语法分析工作极少。因此，编写解释器、编译器和代数表达式操作程序等处理程序文本的程序，就很容易。The fact that Scheme syntax is extremely simple—it is just a representation of the natural parse tree, requiring minimal parsing—makes it easy to write programs that manipulate program texts, such as interpreters, compilers, and algebraic expression manipulators.

重要的是，Scheme 是一门宽容的语言，而不是一门规训性的语言。它不会试图阻止程序员做“蠢事”。这让我们能够施展一些强大的手段，例如动态调整算术运算符的含义。在规则更加严格的语言中，我们就做不到这一点。It is important that Scheme is a permissive rather than a normative language. It does not try to prevent a programmer from doing something “stupid.” This allows us to play powerful games, like dynamically modulating the meanings of arithmetic operators. We would not be able to do this in a language that imposes more restrictive rules.

Scheme 允许赋值，但鼓励函数式编程。Scheme 没有静态类型，却具有非常强的动态类型约束，从而能够安全地进行动态存储分配和垃圾收集：用户程序无法凭空制造指针，也无法访问任意内存位置。这并不是说我们认为静态类型不好。它们当然有助于及早清除一大类错误。类似 Haskell 的类型系统也有助于思考策略。但对本书而言，静态类型带来的思维负担，会妨碍我们考虑那些可能有危险的灵活性策略。Scheme allows assignment but encourages functional programming. Scheme does not have static types, but it has very strong dynamic typing that allows safe dynamic storage allocation and garbage collection: a user program cannot manufacture a pointer or access an arbitrary memory location. It is not that we think static types are not a good idea. They certainly are useful for the early exorcism of a large class of bugs. And Haskell-like type systems can be helpful in thinking out strategies. But for this book the intellectual overhead of static types would inhibit consideration of potentially dangerous strategies of flexibility.

此外，Scheme 还提供了具体化的续延和动态绑定等特殊功能，而大多数其他语言都没有这些功能。借助它们，我们能够直接用原生语言实现非确定性的 amb 等强大机制，而不需要第二层解释。Also Scheme provides special features, such as reified continuations and dynamic binding, that are not available in most other languages. These features allow us to implement such powerful mechanisms as nondeterministic amb in the native language (without a second layer of interpretation).

Chris Hanson 和 Gerald Jay SussmanChris Hanson and Gerald Jay Sussman

1 自然与设计中的灵活性1 

Flexibility in Nature and in Design

要设计一种具有普遍用途、同时又能把任何特定工作做得很好的机制，是很困难的，因此，大多数工程系统都是为执行某项特定工作而设计的。像螺钉紧固件这样的通用发明十分罕见，却意义重大。数字计算机就是这样一种突破，因为它是一种通用机器，能够模拟任何其他信息处理机器。1 我们编写软件来配置计算机，使它通过这种模拟完成我们所需的具体工作。It is difficult to design a mechanism of general utility that does any particular job very well, so most engineered systems are designed to perform a specific job. General-purpose inventions, such as the screw fastener, are rare and of great significance. The digital computer is a breakthrough of this kind, because it is a universal machine that can simulate any other information-processing machine.1 We write software that configures our computers to effect this simulation for the specific jobs that we need done.

作为以往工程实践的延续，我们一直致力于设计能把特定工作做得很好的软件。每个软件都是为完成相对狭窄的任务而设计的。随着待解决的问题发生变化，软件也必须改变。但问题的小变化，往往并不只意味着软件的小变化。软件设计得过于紧绷，没有留下多少灵活性。因此，系统无法平稳演化。它们十分脆弱，一旦问题领域变化，就必须用全新的设计替换。2 这个过程既缓慢又昂贵。We have been designing software to do particular jobs very well, as an extension of past engineering practice. Each piece of software is designed to do a relatively narrow job. As the problem to be solved changes, the software must be changed. But small changes to the problem do not often entail only small changes to the software. Software is designed too tightly for there to be much flexibility. As a consequence, systems cannot evolve gracefully. They are brittle and must be replaced with entirely new designs as the problem domain changes.2 This is slow and expensive.

我们的工程系统并非一定要如此脆弱。互联网已从一个小系统扩展到全球规模。我们的城市在有机地演化，以适应新的商业模式、生活方式，以及交通和通信手段。事实上，通过观察生物系统，我们看到，构建能适应环境变化的系统是可能的，无论是作为个体，还是作为演化的群体。为什么我们设计和构建大多数软件时，不采用这种方式呢？这其中有历史原因，但主要原因是我们不知道如何普遍地做到这一点。目前，一个系统如果能在需求变化面前保持稳健，那也只是偶然。Our engineered systems do not have to be brittle. The Internet has been extended from a small system to one of global scale. Our cities evolve organically, to accommodate new business models, life styles, and means of transportation and communication. Indeed, from observation of biological systems we see that it is possible to build systems that can be adapted to changes in the environment, both individually and as an evolutionary ensemble. Why is this not the way we design and build most software? There are historical reasons, but the main reason is that we don't know how to do this generally. At this moment it is an accident if a system turns out to be robust in the face of changes in requirements.

添加式编程Additive programming

本书的目标是研究如何构建易于适应需求变化的计算系统。人们不应被迫修改一个已经正常工作的程序。应当能够通过向它添加内容，来实现新功能，或调整旧功能以满足新需求。我们称之为添加式编程。我们将探索在不破坏现有程序的前提下为它添加功能的技术。这些技术并不保证添加的部分正确无误：添加部分本身仍须调试；但它们不应意外损坏现有功能。Our goal in this book is to investigate how to construct computational systems so that they can be easily adapted to changing requirements. One should not have to modify a working program. One should be able to add to it to implement new functionality or to adjust old functions for new requirements. We call this additive programming. We explore techniques to add functionality to an existing program without breaking it. Our techniques do not guarantee that the additions are correct: the additions must themselves be debugged; but they should not damage existing functionality accidentally.

本书探讨的许多技术并不新颖，其中一些甚至可以追溯到计算的早期！它们也不是一个完备的集合，只是我们发现有用的一些技术。我们的目的并不是推广这些技术的使用，而是鼓励一种以灵活性为中心的思考方式。Many of the techniques we explore in this book are not novel: some of them date back to the early days of computing! They are also not a comprehensive set, but simply some that we have found useful. Our intention is not to promote the use of these techniques, but to encourage a style of thinking that is focused on flexibility.

要使添加式编程成为可能，就必须尽量减少关于程序如何工作以及将如何使用的假设。在程序设计和构建期间所作的假设，可能会缩小程序未来扩展的可能性。我们不作这样的假设，而是构建能够依据其运行环境即时作出决定的程序。我们将探讨几种支持此类设计的技术。In order for additive programming to be possible, it is necessary to minimize the assumptions about how a program works and how it will be used. Assumptions made during the design and construction of a program may reduce the possible future extensions of the program. Instead of making such assumptions, we build our programs to make just-in-time decisions based on the environment that the program is running in. We will explore several techniques that support this kind of design.

我们总能将程序组合起来，得到它们各自所支持行为的并集。但我们希望整体大于部分之和；我们希望组合后系统中的各部分彼此协作，使系统具备任何单个部分都无法独自提供的能力。不过，这里存在权衡：我们组合成系统的各个部分，必须清晰地分离关注点。如果一个部分能把一件事情做得极好，那么与集多种不同能力于一身的部分相比，它就更容易重用，也更容易调试。如果希望以添加的方式构建系统，就必须让各个部分在组合时，尽量减少非预期的相互作用。We can always combine programs to get the union of the behaviors that each supports. But we want the whole to be more than the sum of its parts; we want the parts of the combined system to cooperate to give the system capabilities that no one part can provide by itself. But there are tradeoffs here: the parts that we combine to make a system must sharply separate concerns. If a part does one thing extremely well, it is easier to reuse, and also easier to debug, than one that combines several disparate capabilities. If we want to build additively, it is important that the individual pieces combine with minimal unintended interactions.

为了便于添加式编程，我们构建的各个部分必须尽可能简单、通用。例如，如果一个部分所接受的输入范围，比解决当前问题严格所需的范围更广，那么它的适用范围就会比不这样做的部分更广。围绕标准化接口规范构建的部件族，则可以混搭出种类繁多的系统。为部件选择恰当的抽象层次十分重要：先确定这个部件族的论域，再面向该论域构建它。我们将在第 2 章开始考虑这些要求。To facilitate additive programming, it is necessary that the parts we build be as simple and general as we can make them. For example, a part that accepts a wider range of inputs than is strictly necessary for the problem at hand will have a wider applicability than one that doesn't. And families of parts that are built around a standardized interface specification can be mixed and matched to make a great variety of systems. It is important to choose the right abstraction level for our parts, by identifying the domain of discourse for the family and then building the family for that domain. We start consideration of these requirements in chapter 2.

为获得最大的灵活性，一个部件的输出范围应当相当小且定义明确，远远小于任何可能接收该输出的部件所能接受的输入范围。这类似于我们在计算机系统入门课程中向学生讲授的数字抽象中的静态约束规则 [126]。数字抽象的要旨是，输出信号始终优于下一级所能接受的输入信号，从而抑制噪声。For maximum flexibility the range of outputs of a part should be quite small and well defined—much smaller than the range of acceptable inputs for any part that might receive that output. This is analogous to the static discipline in the digital abstraction that we teach to students in introductory computer systems subjects [126]. The essence of the digital abstraction is that the outputs are always better than the acceptable inputs of the next stage, so that noise is suppressed.

在软件工程中，为纪念互联网先驱 Jon Postel，这项原则被奉为“Postel 定律”。他在描述互联网协议的 RFC760 [97] 中写道：“协议的实现必须稳健。每种实现都必须预期会与不同人创建的其他实现互操作。虽然本规范力求明确规定协议，但仍然可能存在不同的解释。一般来说，实现应当在发送行为上保守，在接收行为上宽容。”这通常被概括为：“对自己的行为要保守，对他人的输入要宽容。”In software engineering this principle is enshrined as “Postel's law” in honor of Internet pioneer Jon Postel. In RFC760 [97], describing the Internet protocol, he wrote: “The implementation of a protocol must be robust. Each implementation must expect to interoperate with others created by different individuals. While the goal of this specification is to be explicit about the protocol, there is the possibility of differing interpretations. In general, an implementation should be conservative in its sending behavior, and liberal in its receiving behavior.” This is usually summarized as “Be conservative in what you do, be liberal in what you accept from others.”

采用比表面看来所需更通用的部件，能将一定程度的灵活性融入系统的整个结构。系统可以容忍需求的小幅扰动，因为每个组件在构建时，就被设计为能够接受受到扰动的、带有噪声的输入。Using more general parts than appear to be necessary builds a degree of flexibility into the entire structure of our systems. Small perturbations of the requirements can be tolerated, because every component is built to accept perturbed (noisy) inputs.

面向特定论域的一族可混搭部件，是领域专用语言的基础。解决一类难题的最佳方式，往往是创建一门语言，即一组基本元素、组合手段和抽象手段，使这些问题的解法易于表达。因此，我们希望能够按需构建适当的领域专用语言，并灵活地组合这些语言。我们将在第 2 章开始思考领域专用语言。更有力的是，我们可以通过直接求值来实现这样的语言。第 5 章将进一步展开这一思想。A family of mix-and-match parts for a particular domain of discourse is the foundation of a domain-specific language. Often the best way to attack a family of hard problems is to make a language—a set of primitives, means of combination, and means of abstraction—that makes the solutions for those problems easy to express. So we want to be able to erect appropriate domain-specific languages as needed, and to combine such languages flexibly. We start thinking about domain-specific languages in chapter 2. More powerfully, we can implement such languages by direct evaluation. We expand on this idea in chapter 5.

一种增强灵活性的策略，是许多程序员应当熟悉的泛型分派。第 3 章将对此进行广泛探讨。泛型分派往往是一种有用的方法：根据传给过程的实参的具体情况，添加额外的处理过程（方法），以扩展该过程的适用范围。只要要求各处理过程响应互不相交的实参集合，就可以避免添加新处理过程时破坏现有程序。不过，与典型面向对象编程环境中的泛型分派不同，我们的泛型分派并不涉及类、实例和继承之类的概念。这些概念引入了多余的本体论承诺，从而削弱了关注点分离。One strategy for enhancing flexibility, which should be familiar to many programmers, is generic dispatch. We will explore this extensively in chapter 3. Generic dispatch is often a useful way to extend the applicability of a procedure by adding additional handlers (methods) based on details of the arguments passed to the procedure. By requiring handlers to respond to disjoint sets of arguments, we can avoid breaking an existing program when a new handler is added. However, unlike the generic dispatch in the typical object-oriented programming context, our generic dispatch doesn't involve ideas like classes, instances, and inheritance. These weaken the separation of concerns by introducing spurious ontological commitments.

一种截然不同的策略，是同时对数据和过程进行分层，我们将在第 6 章探讨。这一策略利用了这样一个思想：数据通常带有关联的元数据，元数据可以与数据一道处理。例如，数值数据往往带有关联的单位。我们将展示，如何通过提供事后添加层的灵活性，在完全不修改原程序的情况下，为程序增添新功能。A quite different strategy, to be explored in chapter 6, is to layer both data and procedures. This exploits the idea that data usually has associated metadata that can be processed alongside the data. For example, numerical data often has associated units. We will show how providing the flexibility of adding layers after the fact can enhance a program with new functionality, without any change to the original program.

我们还可以构建将多个来源的部分信息结合起来、以获得更完整答案的系统。当各项信息来自相互独立的信息源时，这种方法最为强大。在第 4 章中，我们将看到，类型推断实际上就是组合来自多个来源的部分信息。例如，数值比较要求数值输入并产生布尔输出，这类关于值的类型、可由局部推导出的线索，可以与其他局部类型约束结合起来，产生非局部的类型约束。We can also build systems that combine multiple sources of partial information to obtain more complete answers. This is most powerful when the contributions come from independent sources of information. In chapter 4 we will see how type inference is really a matter of combining multiple sources of partial information. Locally deducible clues about the type of a value, for example that a numerical comparison requires numerical inputs and produces a boolean output, can be combined with other local type constraints to produce nonlocal type constraints.

第 7 章将展示另一种组合部分信息的方法。附近恒星的距离可以利用视差，通过几何方法估算：测量地球绕太阳公转时，恒星的像相对于天空背景移动的角度。也可以利用我们对恒星结构与演化的理解，根据恒星的亮度及光谱来估算它的距离。将这些估算结合起来，就能得到比任何单独估算都更准确的估算。In chapter 7 we will see a different way to combine partial information. The distance to a nearby star can be estimated geometrically, by parallax: measuring the angle by which the star image shifts against the background sky as the Earth revolves around the Sun. The distance to the star can also be estimated by consideration of its brightness and its spectrum, using our understanding of stellar structure and evolution. Such estimates can be combined to get estimates that are more accurate than the individual contributions.

一个与之对偶的思想是利用简并：用多种方式计算同一事物，并根据需要将它们组合起来或加以调节。简并有许多有价值的用途，包括错误检测、性能管理和入侵检测。重要的是，简并也是添加式的：每个作出贡献的部分都自成一体，能够独立产生结果。简并的一种有趣用途，是根据上下文，从同一算法的不同实现中动态选择。这就不必预先假定某种实现将如何被使用。A dual idea is the use of degeneracy: having multiple ways to compute something, which can be combined or modulated as needed. There are many valuable uses for degeneracy, including error detection, performance management, and intrusion detection. Importantly, degeneracy is also additive: each contributing part is self-contained and can produce a result by itself. One interesting use of degeneracy is to dynamically select from different implementations of an algorithm depending on context. This avoids the need to make assumptions about how the implementation will be used.

面向灵活性的设计和构建，确实有其成本。一个能够接受比解决当前问题所需种类更多的输入的过程，其代码量会超过绝对必要的程度，也需要程序员付出超过绝对必要程度的思考。泛型分派、分层和简并也是如此，每种方法都会在内存空间、计算时间和／或程序员时间上带来固定开销。但软件的主要成本，是产品整个生命周期中程序员所花费的时间，包括维护以及为适应需求变化所作的调整。尽量减少重写和重构的设计，使总体成本降为增量添加的成本，而非全面重写的成本。换句话说，长期成本是加性的，而不是乘性的。Design and construction for flexibility has definite costs. A procedure that can take a greater variety of inputs than are necessary for solving the current problem will have more code than absolutely necessary and will take more thinking by the programmer than absolutely necessary. The same goes for generic dispatch, layering, and degeneracy, each of which involves constant overheads in memory space, compute time, and/or programmer time. But the principal cost of software is the time spent by programmers over the lifetime of the product, including maintenance and adaptations that are needed for changing requirements. Designs that minimize rewriting and refactoring reduce the overall costs to the incremental additions rather than complete rewrites. In other words, long-term costs are additive rather than multiplicative.

1.1 计算的架构1.1 Architecture of computation

来自建筑学的一个比喻，或许有助于说明我们所设想的这类系统。在理解建筑用地的性质和待建结构的要求之后，设计过程就从一个 parti 开始：它是设计的组织原则。3 parti 通常是一幅部件几何布局的草图。它也可以体现抽象思想，例如 Louis Isadore Kahn 的作品中 [130] 对“被服务空间”和“服务空间”的划分。这种分解旨在把建筑问题分成若干部分，将走廊、卫生间、设备间和电梯等基础设施支持，与它们所服务的空间分开，例如教学楼中的实验室、教室和办公室。A metaphor from architecture may be illuminating for the kind of system that we contemplate. After understanding the nature of the site to be built on and the requirements for the structure to be constructed, the design process starts with a parti: an organizing principle for the design.3 The parti is usually a sketch of the geometric arrangement of parts. The parti may also embody abstract ideas, such as the division into “served spaces” and “servant spaces,” as in the work of Louis Isadore Kahn [130]. This decomposition is intended to divide the architectural problem into parts by separating out infrastructural support, such as the hallways, the restrooms, the mechanical rooms, and the elevators, from the spaces to be supported, such as the laboratories, classrooms, and offices in an academic building.

parti 是一个模型，但通常还不是完全可用的结构。必须用功能元素来充实它。楼梯和电梯如何安排？暖通空调管道、给排水管道、电力和通信配线系统放在哪里？道路应当如何布设，才能适应服务车辆的配送方式？这些细化可能导致 parti 的修改，但 parti 仍然作为支架，细化工作围绕它展开。The parti is a model, but it is usually not a completely workable structure. It must be elaborated with functional elements. How do we fit in the staircases and elevators? Where do the HVAC ducts, the plumbing, the electrical and communications distribution systems go? How will we run a road to accommodate the delivery patterns of service vehicles? These elaborations may cause modifications of the parti, but the parti continues to serve as a scaffold around which these elaborations are developed.

在编程中，parti 是待执行计算的抽象规划。在小规模情形下，它可能是对算法和数据结构的抽象描述。在较大的系统中，它是计算的各个阶段与并行分支的抽象组合。在更大的系统中，它则是将各种能力分配到逻辑上、甚至物理上的各个区域。In programming, the parti is the abstract plan for the computations to be performed. At small scale the parti may be an abstract algorithm and data-structure description. In larger systems it is an abstract composition of phases and parallel branches of a computation. In even larger systems it is an allocation of capabilities to logical (or even physical) locales.

传统上，程序员无法像建筑师那样设计。在 Java 这类繁复的语言中，parti 与各种细化内容紧紧混杂在一起。真正描述所需行为的表达式，即“被服务空间”，与类型声明、类声明、库的导入和导出等“服务空间”，混杂得一塌糊涂。4 Lisp 或 Python 这类较精简的语言，几乎不给服务空间留下余地；人们甚至排斥添加仅供参考的声明，因为它们有损于裸露出来的 parti 之美。Traditionally, programmmers have not been able to design as architects. In very elaborate languages, such as Java, the parti is tightly mixed with the elaborations. The “served spaces,” the expressions that actually describe the desired behavior, are horribly conflated with the “servant spaces,” such as the type declarations, the class declarations, and the library imports and exports.4 More spare languages, such as Lisp or Python, leave almost no room for the servant spaces, and attempts to add declarations, even advisory ones, are shunned because they impede the beauty of the exposed parti.

建筑中的 parti 应当足够完整，能够据此创建可供分析和批评的模型。程序的骨架规划，也应当足以供人分析和批评；但它还应能够执行，以便实验和调试。正如建筑师必须充实 parti，才能实现所设计的结构，程序员也必须细化规划，才能实现所需的计算系统。分层（第 6 章介绍）就是构建允许这类细化的系统的一种方法。The architectural parti should be sufficiently complete to allow the creation of models that can be used for analysis and criticism. The skeleton plan of a program should be adequate for analysis and criticism, but it should also be executable, for experiment and for debugging. Just as an architect must fill in the parti to realize the structure being designed, a programmer must elaborate the plan to realize the computational system required. Layering (introduced in chapter 6) is one way to build systems that allow this kind of elaboration.

1.2 以智能部件实现灵活性1.2 Smart parts for flexibility

大型系统由许多较小的组件组成，每个组件都对整体功能有所贡献：要么直接提供其中一部分功能，要么按照系统架构师规定的某种模式与其他组件互连，通过协作建立所需功能。系统工程的一个核心问题，是确立允许组件互连的接口，从而将各组件的功能组合起来，构建复合功能。Large systems are composed of many smaller components, each of which contributes to the function of the whole either by directly providing a part of that function or by cooperating with other components to which it is interconnected in some pattern specified by the system architect to establish a required function. A central problem in system engineering is the establishment of interfaces that allow the interconnection of components so that the functions of those components can be combined to build compound functions.

对于相对简单的系统，系统架构师可以为各种接口制定形式化规范，要求待互连组件的实现者满足这些规范。事实上，电子技术的惊人成就，正是建立在能够制定并满足这类规范的基础上。高频模拟设备通过具有标准化阻抗特性的同轴电缆以及标准化的连接器系列互连 [4]。一个组件的功能及其接口行为，通常都只需几个参数就能规定 [60]。在数字系统中，情况更加清晰：对信号含义有静态规范，即数字抽象；对信号时序有动态规范 [126]；对组件的外形尺寸还有机械规范。5For relatively simple systems the system architect may make formal specifications for the various interfaces that must be satisfied by the implementers of the components to be interconnected. Indeed, the amazing success of electronics is based on the fact that it is feasible to make such specifications and to meet them. High-frequency analog equipment is interconnected with coaxial cable with standardized impedance characteristics, and with standardized families of connectors [4]. Both the function of a component and its interface behavior can usually be specified with only a few parameters [60]. In digital systems things are even clearer: there are static specifications of the meanings of signals (the digital abstraction); there are dynamic specifications of the timing of signals [126]; and there are mechanical specifications of the form factors of components.5

不幸的是，随着系统复杂性增加，这种事先规定的做法会越来越困难。我们可以规定一个下棋程序必须遵守规则，也就是说，它不能作弊；但要规定它必须下得好，又该从何着手呢？我们的软件系统由大量定制的、高度专门化的部件构成。组件的这种个性化特征，加剧了为软件组件制定规范的困难。Unfortunately, this kind of a priori specification becomes progressively more difficult as the complexity of the system increases. We could specify that a chess-playing program plays a legal game— that it doesn't cheat—but how would one begin to specify that it plays a good game of chess? Our software systems are built with large numbers of custom-made highly specialized parts. The difficulty of specifying software components is exacerbated by the individualized nature of the components.

相比之下，生物界能够构建复杂程度极高的系统，而不需要极其庞大的规范——考虑到它要解决的问题，尤其如此！我们体内的每个细胞，都是同一个受精卵的后代。所有细胞都具有完全相同的遗传配备，约相当于 1 GByte 的 ROM！然而，细胞却有皮肤细胞、神经元、肌肉细胞等不同种类。细胞自行组织成不同的组织、器官和器官系统。事实上，这 1 GByte 的 ROM 规定了如何用数量庞大、容易出故障的部件，构建出极其复杂的机器——人。它规定了如何操纵这些基本部件，以及如何配置它们；还规定了如何在各种恶劣条件下，让这台复合机器在漫长的一生中可靠运行，以及如何保护它，不让那些很想吃掉它的其他生物得逞！By contrast, biology constructs systems of enormous complexity without very large specifications (considering the problem to be solved!). Every cell in our bodies is a descendant of a single zygote. All the cells have exactly the same genetic endowment (about 1 GByte of ROM!). However, there are skin cells, neurons, muscle cells, etc. The cells organize themselves to be discrete tissues, organs, and organ systems. Indeed, the 1 GByte of ROM specifies how to build the enormously complex machine (the human) from a huge number of failure-prone parts. It specifies how to operate those basic parts and how to configure them. It also specifies how to operate that compound machine reliably, over a great range of hostile conditions, for a very long life span, and how to defend that machine from others that would love to eat it!

如果我们的软件组件更简单或更通用，它们的规范也会更简单。如果组件能够自行适应周围环境，其规范的精确程度就不那么重要了。生物系统同时利用这两种策略，构建稳健而复杂的有机体。区别在于，生物细胞可以动态配置，能够自行适应所处的上下文。这之所以可能，是因为细胞分化和专门化的方式取决于其环境。我们的软件通常没有这种能力，因此，我们必须手工调整每个部件。那么，生物系统究竟是如何运作的呢？If our software components were simpler or more general they would have simpler specifications. If the components were able to adapt themselves to their surroundings, the precision of their specification would be less important. Biological systems exploit both of these strategies to build robust complex organisms. The difference is that the biological cells are dynamically configurable, and able to adapt themselves to their context. This is possible because the way a cell differentiates and specializes depends on its environment. Our software doesn't usually have this ability, and consequently we must adapt each part by hand. How could biology possibly work?

再看一个例子。我们知道，大脑的各个组成部分通过庞大的神经元束连接在一起，而基因组中的信息量，远远不足以详细规定这些互连方式。大脑的各个部分很可能是以共享重要经历为基础，学会彼此通信的。6 因此，接口必须依据某些一致性规则、来自环境的信息，以及广泛的探索行为，自行配置。这在启动时间上代价相当高昂——配置出一个能够正常工作的人，需要若干年——但它提供了一种稳健性，是迄今为止我们的工程造物所不具备的。Consider another example. We know that the various components of the brain are hooked together with enormous bundles of neurons, and there is nowhere near enough information in the genome to specify that interconnect in any detail. It is likely that the various parts of the brain learn to communicate with each other, based on the fact that they share important experiences.6 So the interfaces must be self-configuring, based on some rules of consistency, information from the environment, and extensive exploratory behavior. This is pretty expensive in boot-up time (it takes some years to configure a working human), but it provides a kind of robustness that is not found in our engineered entities to date.

一种观点认为，生物系统使用的上下文信号是告知性的，而不是命令性的。7 没有一个总指挥发号施令，规定各个部分必须做什么；相反，各部分根据周围环境选择自己的角色。细胞的行为并不编码在信号中，而是分别在基因组中表达。信号的组合只是启用某些行为、禁用另一些行为。这种弱连接使得各个区域内所启用行为的实现可以变化，而不必修改界定这些区域的机制。因此，以这种方式组织的系统是可演化的：它们能够容纳某些区域内的适应性变异，而不改变其他区域内子系统的行为。One idea is that biological systems use contextual signals that are informative rather than imperative.7 There is no master commander saying what each part must do; instead the parts choose their roles based on their surroundings. The behaviors of cells are not encoded in the signals; they are separately expressed in the genome. Combinations of signals just enable some behaviors and disable others. This weak linkage allows variation in the implementation of the behaviors that are enabled in various locales without modification of the mechanism that defines the locales. So systems organized in this way are evolvable in that they can accommodate adaptive variation in some locales without changing the behavior of subsystems in other locales.

传统上，软件系统围绕命令式模型构建，其结构中内置了控制层级。各个部分被假定为没有头脑、唯命是从的执行者。这使适应变得非常困难，因为所有变化都必须反映到整个控制结构中。在社会系统中，我们深知严格权力结构和集中指挥的问题。但我们的软件却沿袭了这种有缺陷的模型。我们可以做得更好：让各个部分更聪明、各负其责，便能简化适应过程，因为只有直接受变化影响的部分才需要响应。Traditionally, software systems are built around an imperative model, in which there is a hierarchy of control built into the structure. The individual pieces are assumed to be dumb actors that do what they are told. This makes adaptation very difficult, since all changes must be reflected in the entire control structure. In social systems, we are well aware of the problems with strict power structures and centralized command. But our software follows this flawed model. We can do better: making the parts smarter and individually responsible streamlines adaptation, since only those parts directly affected by a change need to respond.

构型Body plans

所有脊椎动物的构型基本相同，但细节上的差异却极其巨大。事实上，所有左右对称的动物都具有共同的同源框基因，例如 Hox 基因簇。此类基因在发育中的动物体内产生一个近似的坐标系，将其划分为不同的区域。8 这些区域为细胞分化提供了上下文。而来自与邻近细胞接触的信息又提供了更多上下文，从细胞遗传程序所提供的可能行为中选择特定行为。9 连构建方法也是共通的：有导管腺体以及肺、肾等器官的形态发生，都基于同一种胚胎学技巧——上皮向间充质内陷，便会如魔法般自动地10 形成一片分支交错的盲端小管迷宫，周围环绕着正在分化的间充质。11All vertebrates have essentially the same body plan, yet the variation in details is enormous. Indeed, all animals with bilateral symmetry share homeobox genes, such as the Hox complex. Such genes produce an approximate coordinate system in the developing animal, separating the developing animal into distinct locales.8 The locales provide context for a cell to differentiate. And information derived from contact with its neighbors produces more context that selects particular behaviors from the possible behaviors that are available in the cell's genetic program.9 Even the methods of construction are shared—the morphogenesis of ducted glands, and organs such as lungs and kidneys, is based on one embryological trick: the invagination of epithelium into mesenchyme automagically10 produces a branching maze of blind-end tubules surrounded by differentiating mesenchyme.11

优秀的工程也有类似的风格，因为优秀设计具有模块性。以无线电接收机的设计为例。人们已经发现了几种主要“构型”，例如直接变频式、TRF（调谐射频式）和超外差式。每一种构型都有一系列区域，由工程上相当于 Hox 基因簇的东西界定，从天线到输出换能器，为整个系统确立布局。例如，超外差接收机（图 1.1）就有一组从头到尾排列的标准区域。Good engineering has a similar flavor, in that good designs are modular. Consider the design of a radio receiver. There are several grand “body plans” that have been discovered, such as direct conversion, TRF (tuned radio frequency), and superheterodyne. Each has a sequence of locales, defined by the engineering equivalent of a Hox complex, that patterns the system from the antenna to the output transducer. For example, a superheterodyne receiver (figure 1.1) has a standard set of locales (from nose to tail).

这一方案所确定的每个模块，又可以进一步分解为振荡器、混频器、滤波器和放大器等其他模块，如此不断分解，直至单个电子元件。此外，每个模块都可以用多种可能的方式实例化：射频部分可以只是一个滤波器，也可以是精细设计的滤波器与放大器组合。事实上，在模拟电视接收机中，混频器的一部分输出由视频链路按 AM 处理，另一部分则按 FM 处理以产生音频。而某些部分，例如变频器，还可以递归细化，仿佛 Hox 基因簇的某些部分被复制了一样，从而得到多次变频接收机。The modules identified in this plan each decompose into yet other modules, such as oscillators, mixers, filters, and amplifiers, and so on down to the individual electronic components. Additionally, each module can be instantiated in many possible ways: the RF section may be just a filter, or it may be an elaborate filter and amplifier combination. Indeed, in an analog television receiver part of the output of the mixer is processed as AM by the video chain and another part is processed as FM to produce the audio. And some sections, such as the converter, may be recursively elaborated (as if parts of the Hox complex were duplicated!) to obtain multiple-conversion receivers.

在生物系统中，这种区室结构也得到更高组织层级的支持。有些组织专门化为区室的边界，还有一些管道将各区室互连。器官以这类组织为边界，由这类管道互连；整个结构则被封装起来，容纳在体腔中。体腔是高等生物中内衬专门化组织的空腔。In biological systems this structure of compartments is also supported at higher levels of organization. There are tissues that are specialized to become boundaries of compartments, and tubes that interconnect them. Organs are bounded by such tissues and interconnected by such tubes, and the entire structure is packaged to fit into coeloms, which are cavities lined with specialized tissues in higher organisms.

类似技术也可用于软件。构型不过是一个将部分指定的组件组合起来的包装器。这是一种组合子：一种把子部件组合成更大部件的东西。我们可以创建组合子语言，在这种语言中，组件与组合体都具有相同的接口规范。使用组合子语言，可以从少量可混搭的组件构建任意大的组合体。自相似的结构使组合变得容易。在第 2 章中，我们将开始构建基于组合子的软件，而这一主题将贯穿本书其余所有章节。Similar techniques can be used in software. A body plan is just a wrapper that combines partially specified components. This is a kind of combinator: a thing that combines subparts together into a larger part. It is possible to create combinator languages, in which the components and the composite all have the same interface specification. In a combinator language, it is possible to build arbitrarily large composites from small numbers of mix-and-match components. The self-similar structures make combination easy. In chapter 2 we will begin to build combinator-based software, and this theme will run through all of the rest of the book.

利用领域专用语言，也能做到类似的事情。通过对领域进行抽象，我们可以在不同领域中使用同一份与领域无关的代码。例如，无论具体领域是什么，只要涉及数值，数值积分器就能派上用场。另一个例子是第 4 章的模式匹配，它可以应用于各种各样的领域。Something similar can be done with domain-specific languages. By making an abstraction of the domain, we can use the same domain-independent code in different domains. For example, numerical integrators are useful in any domain that has numerical aspects, regardless of the domain. Another example is pattern matching in chapter 4, which can be applied to a wide variety of domains.

生物机制具有通用性，因为原则上，每个组件都能充当任何其他组件。模拟电子元件不具有这种意义上的通用性。它们不会根据局部信号自行适应周围环境。但确实存在通用的电气构件，例如带有模拟接口的可编程计算机！12 对于低频应用，可以用这类构件构建模拟系统。如果每个构件都具有成为系统中任意构件所需的全部代码，但通过与邻近构件交互而实现专门化，并且封装中还有额外的、尚未专门化的“干细胞”，那么，我们就可以设想构建能够自行重配置、自行修复的模拟系统。但目前，我们仍然逐一设计和构建这些部件。Biological mechanisms are universal in that each component can, in principle, act as any other component. Analog electronics components are not universal in that sense. They do not adapt themselves to their surroundings based on local signaling. But there are universal electrical building blocks (a programmable computer with analog interfaces, for example!).12 For low-frequency applications one can build analog systems from such blocks. If each block had all of the code required to be any block in the system, but was specialized by interactions with its neighbors, and if there were extra unspecialized “stem cells” in the package, then we could imagine building self-reconfiguring and self-repairing analog systems. But for now we still design and build these parts individually.

在编程中，我们确实有通用元素这一概念：求值器。求值器接受对某项待执行计算的描述，以及该计算的输入。它产生的输出，与将这些输入交给一个专门实现所需计算的定制组件所产生的输出相同。在计算领域，我们有机会采用胚胎发育这种极其灵活的策略。第 5 章将详细阐述求值器技术的使用。In programming we do have the idea of a universal element: the evaluator. An evaluator takes a description of some computation to be performed and inputs to that computation. It produces the outputs that would arise if we passed the inputs to a bespoke component that implemented the desired computation. In computation we have a chance to pursue the powerfully flexible strategy of embryonic development. We will elaborate on the use of evaluator technology in chapter 5.

1.3 冗余与简并1.3 Redundancy and degeneracy

生物系统演化出了很强的稳健性。生物系统的一个特征是具有冗余。肝脏和肾脏等器官具有高度冗余：它们的能力远远超出完成工作所必需的程度，因此，一个人即使少了一个肾或一部分肝脏，也不会表现出明显的功能障碍。生物系统也具有高度简并：满足某个给定需求，通常有多种方式。13 例如，如果一根手指受伤，可以通过调整其他手指的姿势来拿起物体。我们可以从各种各样的来源获得生命所需的能量：我们能够代谢碳水化合物、脂肪和蛋白质，尽管消化这些物质以及从各类物质中提取能量的机制各不相同。Biological systems have evolved a great deal of robustness. One of the characteristics of biological systems is that they are redundant. Organs such as the liver and kidney are highly redundant: there is vastly more capacity than is necessary to do the job, so a person missing a kidney or part of a liver suffers no obvious incapacity. Biological systems are also highly degenerate: there are usually many ways to satisfy a given requirement.13 For example, if a finger is damaged, there are ways that the other fingers may be configured to pick up an object. We can obtain the necessary energy for life from a great variety of sources: we can metabolize carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, even though the mechanisms for digestion and for extraction of energy from each of these sources is quite distinct.

遗传密码本身就具有简并性，因为从密码子，即由三个核苷酸组成的序列，到氨基酸的映射不是一一对应的：64 种可能的密码子仅用于指定约 20 种可能的氨基酸 [86, 54]。因此，许多点突变，即单个核苷酸的改变，并不会改变编码区所指定的蛋白质。而且，用一种相似的氨基酸替换另一种氨基酸，往往也不会损害蛋白质的生物活性。这些简并使变异得以积累，而不产生明显的表型后果。此外，如果一个基因发生复制——这并不少见——各个副本就可以不显露效应地逐渐分化，在不影响当前生存能力的情况下，产生未来可能变得有价值的变体。另外，各个副本还可以置于不同的转录控制之下。The genetic code is itself degenerate, in that the map from codons (triples of nucleotides) to amino acids is not one-to-one: there are 64 possible codons to specify only about 20 possible amino acids [86, 54]. As a consequence, many point mutations (changes of a single nucleotide) do not change the protein specified by a coding region. Also, quite often the substitution of one amino acid with a similar one does not impair the biological activity of a protein. These degeneracies provide ways that variation can accumulate without obvious phenotypic consequences. Furthermore, if a gene is duplicated (not an uncommon occurrence), the copies may diverge silently, allowing the development of variants that may become valuable in the future, without interfering with current viability. In addition, the copies can be placed under different transcriptional controls.

简并是演化的产物，而它无疑也使演化成为可能。简并本身很可能也是选择的对象，因为只有具有显著简并程度的生物，才有足够的适应能力，在环境变化时生存下来。14 例如，假设某种生物，或某个工程系统，具有简并性，能够通过几种迥然不同且相互独立的机制实现某项基本功能。如果环境或需求发生变化，使其中一种实现基本功能的方式无法继续奏效，该生物仍能继续生存和繁殖，该系统也仍能继续满足其规范。但此时，那个已无法工作的子系统就有了发生突变或接受修复的空间，而不会影响整个系统的生存能力或当前运行。Degeneracy is a product of evolution, and it certainly enables evolution. Probably degeneracy is itself selected for, because only creatures that have significant amounts of degeneracy are sufficiently adaptable to allow survival as the environment changes.14 For example, suppose we have some creature (or engineered system) that is degenerate in that there are several very different independent mechanisms to achieve some essential function. If the environment changes (or the requirements change) so that one of the ways of achieving an essential function becomes untenable, the creature will continue to live and reproduce (the system will continue to satisfy its specifications). But the subsystem that has become inoperative is now open to mutation (or repair), without impinging on the viability (or current operation) of the system as a whole.

物理学的理论结构具有深刻的简并性。例如，经典力学问题可以通过多种方式处理：既有矢量力学的牛顿表述，也有变分力学的拉格朗日表述和哈密顿表述。如果矢量力学和变分力学的任一种形式都适用，它们就会产生等价的运动方程。在分析具有摩擦力等耗散力的系统时，矢量力学很有效；变分方法则不太适合这类系统。在处理具有刚性约束的系统时，拉格朗日力学远优于矢量力学；而哈密顿力学则提供了正则变换这一有力工具，帮助我们利用相空间的结构来理解系统。拉格朗日表述和哈密顿表述，都能让我们深刻洞察对称性与守恒量的作用。描述一个力学系统有三种相互重叠的方法，并且当它们都适用时会彼此一致；这一事实为我们处理任何问题都提供了多条途径 [121]。The theoretical structure of physics is deeply degenerate. For example, problems in classical mechanics can be approached in multiple ways. There is the Newtonian formulation of vectoral mechanics and the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations of variational mechanics. If both vectoral mechanics and either form of variational mechanics are applicable, they produce equivalent equations of motion. For analysis of systems with dissipative forces like friction, vectoral mechanics is effective; variational methods are not well suited for that kind of system. Lagrangian mechanics is far better than vectoral mechanics for dealing with systems with rigid constraints, and Hamiltonian mechanics provides the power of canonical transformations to help understand systems using the structure of phase space. Both the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations help us with deep insights into the role of symmetries and conserved quantities. The fact that there are three overlapping ways of describing a mechanical system, which agree when they are all applicable, gives us multiple avenues of attack on any problem [121].

在失效代价极其高昂的关键系统中，工程系统可能会引入一些冗余。但它们几乎从不有意引入生物系统中那种简并，除非简并是非最优设计的副作用。15Engineered systems may incorporate some redundancy, in critical systems where the cost of failure is extreme. But they almost never intentionally incorporate degeneracy of the kind found in biological systems, except as a side effect of designs that are not optimal.15

简并可以为我们的系统增添价值：与冗余一样，我们可以交叉核对简并计算的答案，以提高稳健性。但简并计算不仅仅是冗余，它们彼此还各不相同，这意味着其中一个计算中的错误不太可能影响其他计算。这一特点不仅有利于可靠性，也有利于安全性，因为一次成功的攻击必须攻破多个简并部件。Degeneracy can add value to our systems: as with redundancy, we can cross-check the answers of degenerate computations to improve robustness. But degenerate computations are not just redundant but different from one another, meaning that a bug in one is unlikely to affect the others. This is a positive characteristic not only for reliability but also for security, as a successful attack must compromise multiple degenerate parts.

当简并部件产生部分信息时，它们组合后的结果可能优于任何一个单独结果。有些导航系统利用这一思想，将多个位置估计结合起来，产生高度精确的结果。我们将在第 7 章探讨组合部分信息的思想。When degenerate parts generate partial information, the result of their combination can be better than any individual result. Some navigation systems use this idea to combine several positional estimates to generate a highly accurate result. We will explore the idea of combining partial information in chapter 7.

1.4 探索行为1.4 Exploratory behavior

探索行为是生物系统中实现稳健性的最强大机制之一。16 其思想是，通过生成并检验的机制产生所需结果（见图 1.2）。这种组织方式允许生成机制保持通用，并独立于负责接受或拒绝某个生成结果的检验机制而工作。One of the most powerful mechanisms of robustness in biological systems is exploratory behavior.16 The idea is that the desired outcome is produced by a generate-and-test mechanism (see figure 1.2). This organization allows the generator mechanism to be general and to work independently of the testing mechanism that accepts or rejects a particular generated result.

例如，支撑细胞形状的刚性骨架，其重要组成部分之一是一组微管。每根微管都由聚集在一起的蛋白质单元组成。在活细胞中，微管不断形成和解体；它们形成时朝各个方向生长。然而，只有遇到动粒或细胞膜中其他稳定结构的微管才能保持稳定，从而支撑由这些稳定结构的位置所决定的形状 [71]。因此，使某种形状长成并得以维持的机制，相对独立于规定该形状的机制。这种机制部分决定了复杂生物体中许多种细胞的形状，而且在动物中几乎普遍存在。For example, an important component of the rigid skeleton that supports the shape of a cell is an array of microtubules. Each microtubule is made up of protein units that aggregate to form it. Microtubules are continually created and destroyed in a living cell; they are created growing out in all directions. However, only microtubules that encounter a kinetochore or other stabilizer in the cell membrane are stable, thus supporting the shape determined by the positions of the stabilizers [71]. So the mechanism for growing and maintaining a shape is relatively independent of the mechanism for specifying the shape. This mechanism partly determines the shapes of many types of cells in a complex organism, and it is almost universal in animals.

探索行为出现在生物系统的各个细节层级。发育中胚胎的神经系统会产生远多于成年后所保留数量的神经元。能在其他神经元、感觉器官或肌肉中找到适当靶标的神经元会存活下来，找不到靶标的则会自行死亡。手的形成，是先产生一个垫状结构，再通过细胞凋亡，即程序性细胞死亡，去除手指之间的物质 [131]。我们的骨骼不断受到成骨细胞和破骨细胞的重塑，前者构建骨，后者分解骨。骨骼的形状和大小由其环境施加的约束决定：也就是它们必须与之相联的部分，例如肌肉、韧带、肌腱和其他骨骼。Exploratory behavior appears at all levels of detail in biological systems. The nervous system of a growing embryo produces a vastly larger number of neurons than will persist in the adult. Those neurons that find appropriate targets in other neurons, sensory organs, or muscles will survive, and those that find no targets kill themselves. The hand is fashioned by production of a pad and deletion, by apoptosis (programmed cell death), of the material between the fingers [131]. Our bones are continually being remodeled by osteoblasts (which build bone) and osteoclasts (which destroy bone). The shape and size of the bones is determined by constraints determined by their environment: the parts that they must be associated with, such as muscles, ligaments, tendons, and other bones.

由于生成器不必知道检验器如何接受或拒绝它的提案，而检验器也不必知道生成器如何提出提案，这两个部分就可以独立发展。这使适应和演化更有效率，因为两个子系统中的一个发生突变时，不必伴随另一个子系统的配套突变。不过，这种隔离可能代价高昂，因为生成失败提案并将其拒绝，会浪费许多精力。17Because the generator need not know about how the tester accepts or rejects its proposals, and the tester need not know how the generator makes its proposals, the two parts can be independently developed. This makes adaptation and evolution more efficient, because a mutation to one or the other of these two subsystems need not be accompanied by a complementary mutation to the other. However, this isolation can be expensive because of the wasted effort of generation and rejection of failed proposals.17

事实上，生成并检验是整个演化过程的一个比喻。生物变异的机制是随机突变，即遗传指令的修改。由于系统中的简并，大多数突变是中性的，不直接影响适合度。自然选择就是检验阶段。它不依赖于变异的方法，而变异的方法也不会预见选择的效果。Indeed, generate and test is a metaphor for all of evolution. The mechanisms of biological variation are random mutations: modifications of the genetic instructions. Most mutations are neutral in that they do not directly affect fitness because of degeneracy in the systems. Natural selection is the test phase. It does not depend on the method of variation, and the method of variation does not anticipate the effect of selection.

还有更惊人的现象：即使在亲缘关系很近的生物中，有些组成部分在成年个体中几乎完全相同，却是在胚胎中由全然不同的机制构建出来的。18 对于亲缘关系较远的生物，用不同机制构建共同结构，可以归因于“趋同演化”；但对于近亲，这更可能表明细节层级彼此分离：结果的规定方式，在一定程度上独立于其实现方式。There are even more striking phenomena: even in closely related creatures some components that end up almost identical in the adult are constructed by entirely different mechanisms in the embryo.18 For distant relationships, divergent mechanisms for constructing common structures may be attributed to “convergent evolution,” but for close relatives it is more likely evidence for separation of levels of detail, in which the result is specified in a way that is somewhat independent of the way it is accomplished.

工程系统也可能呈现类似的结构。我们努力将规范与实现分离：满足一项规范往往有多种方式，不同设计可以选择不同实现。对数据集排序的最佳方法，取决于数据集的预期规模，以及元素比较的计算成本。多项式的恰当表示方式，取决于它是稀疏的还是稠密的。但即使这些选择是动态作出的——这种系统并不常见——它们仍是确定性的：我们很少看到有系统同时尝试多种方式解决一个问题，并采用最先收敛的那一种结果——那些处理器核心到底是干什么用的呢？甚至顺序尝试多种方法的系统也很少见：一种方法失败，就试另一种。第 4 章将考察如何在模式匹配中利用回溯实现生成并检验机制。第 5 章将学习如何在语言中内置自动回溯。第 7 章则将学习如何构建依赖关系引导的回溯机制，尽可能从失败中提取信息。Engineered systems may show similar structure. We try to separate specification from implementation: there are often multiple ways to satisfy a specification, and designs may choose different implementations. The best method to use to sort a data set depends on the expected size of the data set, as well as the computational cost of comparing elements. The appropriate representation of a polynomial depends on whether it is sparse or dense. But if choices like these are made dynamically (an unusual system) they are deterministic: we do not see many systems that simultaneously try several ways to solve a problem and use the one that converges first (what are all those cores for, anyway?). It is even rare to find systems that try multiple methods sequentially: if one method fails try another. We will examine use of backtracking to implement generate-and-test mechanisms in pattern matching in chapter 4. We will learn how to build automatic backtracking into languages in chapter 5. And we will learn how to build a dependency-directed backtracking mechanism that extracts as much information as possible from failures in chapter 7.

1.5 灵活性的成本1.5 The cost of flexibility

Lisp 程序员知道一切事物的价值，却不知道任何事物的成本。Lisp programmers know the value of everything but the cost of nothing.

Alan Perlis 仿 Oscar Wilde 的话Alan Perlis paraphrasing Oscar Wilde

我们已经指出，使用泛型、分层、冗余、简并和探索行为，可以增强系统的通用性与可演化性。孤立地看，每一种方法都代价高昂。一个能够处理广泛输入的机制，要得到同样的结果，必须比专门针对某种输入的机制做更多工作。冗余机制比与之等效的非冗余机制具有更多部件。简并机制看起来更加奢侈。通过生成并检验进行探索的机制，则很容易陷入不可行的指数级搜索。然而，这些却是可演化系统的关键要素。也许，要构建真正稳健的系统，我们就必须愿意为看起来相当复杂而昂贵的基础设施付出代价。We have noted that generality and evolvability are enhanced in systems that use generics, layers, redundancy, degeneracy, and exploratory behavior. Each of these is expensive, when looked at in isolation. A mechanism that works over a wide range of inputs must do more to get the same result than a mechanism specialized to a particular input. A redundant mechanism has more parts than an equivalent nonredundant mechanism. A degenerate mechanism appears even more extravagant. And a mechanism that explores by generate-and-test methods can easily get into an infeasible exponential search. Yet these are key ingredients in evolvable systems. Perhaps to make truly robust systems we must be willing to pay for what appears to be a rather elaborate and expensive infrastructure.

部分问题在于，我们思考成本的角度不对。时间和空间的使用固然重要，但对于这些成本来自何处，我们的直觉却并不可靠。每位工程师都知道，评估系统的实际性能，需要进行大量细致的测量，而测量结果往往表明，成本出现在出人意料的地方。随着复杂性增加，这件事只会更加困难。然而，我们仍执意在程序的各个层次上进行过早优化，却并不知道它的真正价值。Part of the problem is that we are thinking about cost in the wrong terms. Use of time and space matters, but our intuition about where those costs come from is poor. Every engineer knows that evaluating the real performance of a system involves extensive and careful measurements that often show that the cost is in surprising places. As complexity increases, this will only get harder. But we persist in doing premature optimization at all levels of our programs without knowing its real value.

假设我们把系统中必须快速的部分，与必须聪明的部分分离。按照这一方针，通用性和可演化性的成本，就可以局限在必须聪明的部分。在计算系统中，这是不常见的视角，但在我们的生活经验中，它却无处不在。例如，尝试学习一种新技能，比如演奏乐器时，最初阶段需要有意识的活动，将预期效果与产生该效果所需的身体动作联系起来。但随着技能得到掌握，大部分工作无需有意识地关注就能完成。要快速演奏，这一点至关重要，因为有意识的活动太慢了。Suppose we separate the parts of a system that have to be fast from the parts that have to be smart. Under this policy, the cost of generality and evolvability can be confined to the parts that have to be smart. This is an unusual perspective in computing systems, yet it is ubiquitous in our life experience. When we try to learn a new skill, for example to play a musical instrument, the initial stages involve conscious activity to connect the intended effect to the physical movements required to produce it. But as the skill is mastered, most of the work is done without conscious attention. This is essential to being able to play at speed, because the conscious activity is too slow.

在硬件与软件的区分中，也能找到类似的论证。硬件以接口固定为代价，换取效率。然后，人们可以在该接口之上用软件构建软件，实际上就是创建一台虚拟机。众所周知，额外的抽象层会带来成本，但它所获得的通用性，完全值得这种权衡。（否则，我们就仍在用汇编语言编程！）这里的要点是，这种分层结构提供了一种兼顾效率与灵活性的方法。我们认为，要求整个系统都以尽可能高效的方式实现，会适得其反，阻碍系统为适应未来需求而保有灵活性。一个系统的真正成本，是程序员在设计、理解、维护、修改和调试它时所花费的时间。因此，增强适应性的价值可能更加巨大。一个易于调整和维护的系统，能够消除最大的成本之一：为了让新程序员知道应当从哪里着手修改代码，必须把现有系统的工作方式及其所有繁杂细节教给他们。事实上，无论从灾难造成的成本，还是从重新设计和重建所耗时间导致的机会损失来看，我们脆弱的基础设施所带来的成本，很可能都远远超过灵活设计的成本。而如果能够让系统自行适应新情境，取代为满足新需求而重新编程所需时间中的很大一部分，收益还会更大。A similar argument is found in the distinction between hardware and software. Hardware is designed for efficiency, at the cost of having a fixed interface. One can then build software on top of that interface—in effect creating a virtual machine—using software. That extra layer of abstraction incurs a well-known cost, but the tradeoff is well worth the generality that is gained. (Otherwise we'd still be programming in assembly language!) The point here is that this layered structure provides a way to have both efficiency and flexibility. We believe that requiring an entire system to be implemented in the most efficient possible way is counterproductive, preventing the flexibility for adapting to future needs. The real cost of a system is the time spent by programmers—in designing, understanding, maintaining, modifying, and debugging the system. So the value of enhanced adaptability may be even more extreme. A system that is easily adapted and maintained eliminates one of the largest costs: teaching new programmers how the existing system works, in all its gory detail, so that they know where to reach in and modify the code. Indeed, the cost of our brittle infrastructure probably greatly exceeds the cost of flexible design, both in the cost of disasters and in the lost opportunity costs due to the time of redesign and rebuilding. And if a significant fraction of the time spent reprogramming a system for a new requirement is replaced by having that system adapt itself to the new situation, that can be an even bigger win.

正确性带来的问题The problem with correctness

在乐观者看来，杯子半满。在悲观者看来，杯子半空。在工程师看来，杯子的容量是所需的两倍。To the optimist, the glass is half full. To the pessimist, the glass is half empty. To the engineer, the glass is twice as big as it needs to be.

作者不详author unknown

不过，以某种方式构建系统，使其适用范围超出我们在设计时考虑过的情境集合，可能还会带来更大的成本。因为我们打算在系统并非为之设计的上下文中使用它，所以我们无法确信它们能够正确工作！But there may be an even bigger cost to building systems in a way that gives them a range of applicability greater than the set of situations that we have considered at design time. Because we intend to be willing to apply our systems in contexts for which they were not designed, we cannot be sure that they work correctly!

在计算机科学中，我们受到的教导是，软件的“正确性”至高无上；要实现正确性，就应为组件及其构成的系统建立形式化规范，并给出证明，表明组件的规范及其组合模式能够满足组件组合体的规范。19 我们断言，这种规训会使系统更加脆弱。事实上，要构建真正稳健的系统，我们就必须放弃如此严格的规训。In computer science we are taught that the “correctness” of software is paramount, and that correctness is to be achieved by establishing formal specification of components and systems of components and by providing proofs that the specifications of a combination of components are met by the specifications of the components and the pattern by which they are combined.19 We assert that this discipline makes systems more brittle. In fact, to make truly robust systems we must discard such a tight discipline.

要求证明的问题在于，证明通用机制的一般性质，通常比证明在受限情境中使用的专用机制的特殊性质更困难。这就促使我们把部件及其组合设计得尽可能专用，以简化证明。但高度专用部件的组合是脆弱的——它没有任何容纳变化的余地！20The problem with requiring proofs is that it is usually harder to prove general properties of general mechanisms than it is to prove special properties of special mechanisms used in constrained circumstances. This encourages us to make our parts and combinations as special as possible so we can simplify our proofs. But the combination of tightly specialized parts is brittle—there is no room for variation!20

我们并不反对证明。能得到证明时，它们当然很好。事实上，对于垃圾收集器或核糖体等关键系统组件而言，证明至关重要。21 然而，即使对于自动驾驶仪等安全关键系统，将其适用范围限制在能够证明系统符合规范、正确工作的情境内，也可能反而导致不必要的失效。事实上，我们希望：即使飞机以设计者未曾预料到的方式受损，自动驾驶仪也能尽其所能，尝试让飞机安全飞行！We are not arguing against proofs. They are wonderful when available. Indeed, they are essential for critical system components, such as garbage collectors (or ribosomes).21 However, even for safety-critical systems, such as autopilots, the restriction of applicability to situations for which the system is provably correct as specified may actually contribute to unnecessary failure. Indeed, we want an autopilot to make a good-faith attempt to safely fly an airplane that is damaged in a way not anticipated by the designer!

我们反对的是强求证明的规训：要求一切事物在被允许用于某种情境之前，必须先证明其适用于该情境，会过分抑制那些能够增强设计稳健性的技术的使用。尤其受到抑制的，是允许在严格控制下将某种方法用于其已获证明的适用域之外的技术，以及为未来扩展提供支持、却不限制扩展方式的技术。We are arguing against the discipline of requiring proofs: the requirement that everything must be proved to be applicable in a situation before it is allowed to be used in that situation excessively inhibits the use of techniques that could enhance the robustness of designs. This is especially true of techniques that allow a method to be used, on a tight leash, outside of its proven domain, and techniques that provide for future expansion without putting limits on the ways things can be extended.

不幸的是，我们提倡的许多技术，会使证明问题变得困难得多，甚至在实践中不可能完成。另一方面，有时处理一个问题的最佳方法，就是将其推广，直到证明变得简单。Unfortunately, many of the techniques we advocate make the problem of proof much more difficult, if not practically impossible. On the other hand, sometimes the best way to attack a problem is to generalize it until the proof becomes simple.

But a parti combines both abstract and concrete components, while a Java interface is wholly abstract. Not to mention that over-use of interfaces is considered a “code smell” by many programmers.
5 《面向设计工程师的 TTL 数据手册》[123] 是数字系统组件规格说明取得成功的经典范例。TTL 为小规模和中规模集成电路组件规定了若干内部一致的“系列”。这些系列在速度、功耗等特性上有所不同，但功能相同。规格说明描述了各系列的静态和动态特性、各系列提供的功能，以及组件的物理封装。各系列不仅内部一致，彼此之间也一致：每种功能在每个系列中都能找到，封装相同，描述所用的命名体系也一致。因此，设计者可以先设计复合功能，随后再选择用于实现的系列。每一位优秀的工程师（还有生物学家！）都应熟悉 TTL 带来的启示。5 The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers [123] is a classic example of a successful set of specifications for digital-system components. TTL specifies several internally consistent “families” of small-scale and medium-scale integrated-circuit components. The families differ in such characteristics as speed and power dissipation, but not in function. The specification describes the static and dynamic characteristics of each family, the functions available in each family, and the physical packaging for the components. The families are cross-consistent as well as internally consistent in that each function is available in each family, with the same packaging and a consistent nomenclature for description. Thus a designer may design a compound function and later choose the family for implementation. Every good engineer (and biologist!) should be familiar with the lessons of TTL.

As noted on page 7, it is easy to specify that a chess player must play legal chess, but how would we specify that it plays well? And unlike chess, whose rules do not change, the specifications of most systems are dynamically changing as the conditions of their usage change. How do we specify an accounting system in the light of rapidly changing tax codes?

But if we keep such subsystems simple and small they can be specified and even proved “correct” with a tractable amount of work.

2 领域专用语言2 

Domain-Specific Languages

为编程项目赋予灵活性的一项强大策略，是创建一种领域专用语言，捕捉待开发程序所涉及主题的概念结构。领域专用语言是一种抽象，其中的名词和动词直接对应问题领域。这样的语言允许应用程序直接用该领域的概念来编写。领域专用语言就其本性而言，实现的是一个相当完整的领域模型，超出了某个特定应用的需要。1 这看似是当前具体问题并不必需的额外工作，但其工作量往往比编写一个单体程序更少，而产生的程序也更容易修改、调试和扩展。One powerful strategy for building flexibility into a programming project is to create a domain-specific language that captures the conceptual structure of the subject matter of the programs to be developed. A domain-specific language is an abstraction in which the nouns and verbs of the language are directly related to the problem domain. Such a language allows an application program to be written directly in terms of the domain. By its nature, a domain-specific language implements a fairly complete model of the domain, in excess of what is needed for a particular application.1 Although this may seem like extra work that is not essential to the particular problem at hand, it is often less work than writing a monolithic program, and the resulting program is much easier to modify, debug, and extend.

因此，构建领域专用语言层，所支持的不只是某个特定程序的开发。它为构建共享同一论域的各种相关程序提供了通用框架，简化了扩展该领域中现有应用的过程，还提供了使相关应用得以协作的基础。So a domain-specific language layer is built to support more than just the development of a particular program. It provides a general framework for the construction of a variety of related programs that share the domain of discourse. It simplifies the process of extending an existing application in that domain. And it provides a substrate that allows related applications to cooperate.

本章首先介绍组合子系统，这是构建领域专用语言层的一项强大的组织策略。我们将展示如何把用于字符串匹配的、丑陋混乱的正则表达式，重新组织成一种嵌入 Scheme 的、基于组合子的优雅领域专用语言，以此证明这项策略的有效性。但有时，我们手中的组件不容易融入一个整洁的系统——有时我们需要一个适配器系统。我们用一种为过程制作单位换算包装器的领域专用语言来说明这一点：它使原本假定使用某一单位制编写的过程，可以在另一单位制下使用。最后，我们考察棋盘游戏这个广泛的领域，看看如何通过为游戏规则构建解释器来抽象领域细节。In this chapter we first introduce systems of combinators, a powerful organizational strategy for the erection of domain-specific language layers. We will demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy by showing how to reformulate the ugly mess of regular expressions for string matching into a pretty combinator-based domain-specific language embedded in Scheme. But sometimes we have components that do not easily fit into a clean system— sometimes we need a system of adapters. We illustrate this with a domain-specific language for making unit-conversion wrappers for procedures, allowing procedures written assuming one unit system to be used with a different unit system. Finally, we consider the broad domain of board games. We see how it is possible to abstract the details of the domain by building an interpreter for the rules of the game.

2.1 组合子2.1 Combinators

生物系统的适应能力很大程度上来自使用非常通用的部件（细胞）：这些部件经过动态配置，因而能够随着环境的变化而调整。计算系统通常不采用这种策略，而是依赖由定制部件及其组合构成的层次结构。近年来，由规格明确的较高层次部件组成的大型程序库，提升了这类活动的抽象层次。但除了作为“模式”，组合手段本身很少被抽象或共享。2Biological systems achieve much of their adaptability through the use of very general parts (cells) that are dynamically configured and consequently able to adjust as their environment changes. Computational systems usually do not use this strategy, instead relying on a hierarchy of custom parts and combinations. In recent years, large libraries of well-specified higher-level parts have raised the abstraction level of this activity. But the means of combination are rarely abstracted or shared, other than as “patterns.”2

在某些情形下，我们可以用促进共享组合机制的简单策略来改进这种做法。如果所构建的系统由某个可以“混搭”的组件族的成员组成，而组件组合后仍形成该族的新成员，那么需求发生扰动时，有时只需重新排列组件就能应对。In some situations we can improve on this practice by simple strategies that promote the use of shared combination mechanisms. If the systems we build are made up from members of a family of “mix-and-match” components that combine to make new members of the family, perturbations of the requirements can sometimes be addressed by rearrangement of components.

组合子系统包含一组基本部件，以及一组组合部件的手段，而且组合结果的接口规格与基本部件相同。这样就能在构建过程中避免部件之间发生意外的相互作用。TTL [123] 是一个类似组合子系统的经典例子：它是一个历史悠久的标准部件及其组合的库，用于构建复杂的数字系统。A system of combinators is a set of primitive parts and a set of means of combining parts such that the interface specifications of the combinations are the same as those of the primitives. This enables construction without accidental interactions between the parts. A classic example of a combinator-like system is TTL [123], which is a historic library of standard parts and combinations for building complex digital systems.

组合子系统为领域专用语言提供了一种设计策略。系统中的元素就是语言中的词，而组合子则用来将它们组合成短语。组合子系统的显著优点是易于构建、易于推理，但也存在局限，我们将在第 3.1.5 节讨论。只要适合该领域，它们就是极好的策略选择。Combinator systems provide a design strategy for domain-specific languages. The elements of the system are words in the language, and the combinators are used to combine them into phrases. Combinator systems have the significant advantage that they are easy to build and to reason about, but they have limitations, which we will discuss in section 3.1.5. When they fit the domain, they are an excellent strategic choice.

但是，怎样才能通过组合一个可混搭组件族中的元素来构建系统呢？我们必须确定一组基本组件和一组组合子，由组合子将组件组合成复合组件，而复合组件的接口必须与基本组件相同。这样的组合子集合在数学记法中有时是显式的，但更多时候是隐含的。But how do we arrange to build our systems by combining elements of a family of mix-and-match components? We must identify a set of primitive components and a set of combinators that combine components so as to make compound components with the same interface as the primitive components. Such sets of combinators are sometimes explicit, but more often implicit, in mathematical notation.

2.1.1 函数组合子2.1.1 Function combinators

数学中使用函数记法，本身就是一种遵循组合子规则的做法。函数有一个定义域，实参从中选取，还有一个由可能取值构成的值域（或陪域）。某些组合子能通过组合其他函数来产生新函数。例如，函数 f 和 g 的复合 f ○ g 是一个新函数，它接受 g 定义域中的实参，产生 f 陪域中的值。如果两个函数的定义域和陪域相同，而且其共同的陪域上定义了算术运算，那么就可以定义这两个函数的和（或积）：给定共同定义域中的一个实参，新函数的值就是原来两个函数在该实参处取值的和（或积）。允许过程作为一等对象的语言，提供了支持这种组合手段的机制，但真正重要的是拥有一个良好的部件族。The use of functional notation in mathematics is a combinator discipline. A function has a domain, from which its arguments are selected, and a range (or codomain) of its possible values. There are combinators that produce new functions as combinations of others. For example, the composition f ○ g of functions f and g is a new function that takes arguments in the domain of g and produces values in the codomain of f. If two functions have the same domain and codomain, and if arithmetic is defined on their common codomain, then we can define the sum (or product) of the functions as the function that when given an argument in their common domain, is the sum (or product) of the values of the two functions at that argument. Languages that allow first-class procedures provide a mechanism to support this means of combination, but what really matters is a good family of pieces.

围绕组合子组织系统有几个优点。构造出的部件可以任意混搭。任何组合都会得到合法程序，其行为清晰地仅取决于各部件的行为以及它们的组合方式。部件所处的上下文不会改变它的行为：始终可以把一个复合部件拿到新的上下文中使用，而不用担心它在那里的行为。因此，这样的程序易于编写、易于阅读，也易于验证。基于组合子构建的程序具有可扩展性，因为引入新部件或新组合子不会影响现有程序的行为。Organizing a system around combinators has several advantages. The parts that are made can be arbitrarily mixed and matched. Any combination yields a legal program, whose behavior transparently depends only on the behaviors of the parts and the ways that they are combined. The context in which a part appears does not change the behavior of the part: it is always acceptable to pick up a compound part to use it in a new context, without worry about its behavior in that context. Thus such programs are easy to write, easy to read, and easy to verify. A program built on combinators is extensible, because introduction of new parts or new combinators does not affect the behavior of existing programs.

可以把函数组合子看作接线图的实现，接线图规定了如何组合部件来构造函数。例如，函数复合表示由两个子盒组成的盒子，第一个子盒的输出馈入第二个子盒的输入，如图 2.1 所示。实现这个想法的程序很直接：We can think of function combinators as implementing wiring diagrams that specify how a function is built by combining its parts. For example, functional composition represents a box made of two subboxes so that the output of the first feeds the input of the second, as shown in figure 2.1. A program that implements this idea is straightforward:

(define (compose f g)

  (lambda args

    (f (apply g args))))

（如果想检查元数是否匹配，事情就会更有趣：过程 f 所表示的函数应当只接受一个实参，以匹配 g 的输出。如果 g 能返回多个值，而 f 必须接受这些实参，那就更有趣了。我们可能还想检查，传给复合函数的实参数量是否符合 g 的要求。不过，这些细节留待后面处理。）(It gets more exciting if we want to check that the arities match: that the function represented by procedure f takes only one argument, to match the output of g. It gets even more fun if g can return multiple values and f must take those arguments. We may also want to check that the arguments passed to the composition are the right number for g. But these are fine points that we will deal with later.)
