我们可以用一个简单的例子来演示复合：We can demonstrate composition with a simple example:

((compose (lambda (x) (list ’foo x))

          (lambda (x) (list ’bar x)))

 ’z)

(foo (bar z))

有时，为组合子所返回的过程取个名字会更好。例如，可以将 compose 写成：It is sometimes nicer to name the procedure that is being returned by a combinator. For example, we could write compose as

(define (compose f g)

  (define (the-composition . args)

    (f (apply g args)))

  the-composition)

名字 the-composition 在 compose 定义的作用域之外并没有定义，所以用这种方式编写 compose 过程没有明显的优势。我们经常在程序中使用由 lambda 表达式定义的匿名过程，就像上面第一个版本的 compose 那样。因此，选择哪种写法主要是风格问题。3The name the-composition is not defined outside of the scope of the definition of compose, so there is no obvious advantage to this way of writing the compose procedure. We often use anonymous procedures defined by lambda expressions in our programs, as in the first version of compose above. So the choice of how to write the program is mostly a matter of style.3

即使只有 compose 这个组合子，我们也能写出相当优雅的代码。考虑计算函数的第 n 次迭代的问题：f(x) = f(f−1(x))。可以把它优雅地写成程序：Even with just this compose combinator we can write some rather elegant code. Consider the problem of computing the nth iterate of a function f(x) = f(f−1(x)). We can write this elegantly as a program:

(define ((iterate n) f)

  (if (= n 0)

      identity

      (compose f ((iterate (- n 1)) f))))



(define (identity x) x)

((iterate n) f) 的结果是一个与 f 同类型的新函数，凡是可以使用 f 的地方都可以使用它。因此，(iterate n) 本身也是一个函数组合子。现在可以用它来求对一个数反复平方的结果：The result of ((iterate n) f) is a new function, of the same type as f. It can be used wherever f can be used. So (iterate n) is itself a function combinator. Now we can use this to determine the result of repeatedly squaring a number:

(((iterate 3) square) 5)

390625

注意这个类比：函数复合类似于乘法，所以函数迭代就类似于乘方。Notice the analogy: function composition is like multiplication, so function iteration is like exponentiation.

有许多简单的组合子在编程中普遍有用。这里仅介绍几个，让大家感受一下可能性的广度。There are many simple combinators that are generally useful in programming. We will present just a few here to give a feeling for the range of possibilities.

我们可以让两个函数并行使用，再用指定的合并函数组合它们的结果（见图 2.2）。这种并行组合用以下过程实现：We can arrange to use two functions in parallel, then combine their results with a specified combiner function (see figure 2.2). This parallel combination is implemented with the procedure

(define (parallel-combine h f g)

  (define (the-combination . args)

    (h (apply f args) (apply g args)))

  the-combination)



((parallel-combine list

                   (lambda (x y z) (list ’foo x y z))

                   (lambda (u v w) (list ’bar u v w)))

 ’a ’b ’c)

((foo a b c) (bar a b c))

parallel-combine 组合子可以用于组织复杂的处理过程。例如，假设我们有一个蔬菜局部图像的来源。一个过程可以根据图像估计蔬菜的颜色，另一个过程可以描述其形状（叶、根、茎等）。还可以有第三个过程，将这些描述组合起来辨认蔬菜。使用 parallel-combine，便能将这些过程整洁地组合起来。The parallel-combine combinator can be useful in organizing a complex process. For example, suppose we have a source of images of pieces of vegetable. We may have one procedure that given the image can estimate the color of the vegetable, and another that can give a description of the shape (leaf, root, stalk, ...). We may have a third procedure that can combine these descriptions to identify the vegetable. These can be neatly composed with parallel-combine.

元数Arity

编程中有整族的组合子可用，而我们通常并不会想到它们。其中许多出现在常见的数学语境中。例如，张量将线性代数扩展到了具有多个实参的线性算子。但这个想法还要更普遍：两个过程的“张量组合”不过是一个新过程，它接受一种汇集了原来两个过程所需实参的数据结构，将这些实参分配给两个过程，再产生一种汇集两个过程取值的数据结构。拆开数据结构、分别处理各部分、再将结果重新打包，这种需求在编程中无处不在。图 2.3 的接线图展示了 spread-combine。它是多重线性代数中张量积的推广。在数学的张量积中，f 和 g 是其输入的线性函数，而 h 是对某些共同指标取迹；不过，张量只是启发这一组合子的特殊情形。There are entire families of combinators that we can use in programming that we don't normally think of. Many of these appear in common mathematical contexts. For example, tensors are an extension of linear algebra to linear operators with multiple arguments. But the idea is more general than that: the “tensor combination” of two procedures is just a new procedure that takes a data structure combining arguments for the two procedures. It distributes those arguments to the two procedures, producing a data structure that combines the values of the two procedures. The need to unbundle a data structure, operate on the parts separately, and rebundle the results is ubiquitous in programming. The wiring diagram in figure 2.3 shows spread-combine. It is a generalization of the tensor product in multilinear algebra. In the mathematical tensor product, f and g are linear functions of their inputs, and h is a trace over some shared indices; but tensors are just the special case that inspired this combinator.

实现 spread-combine 的程序比 parallel-combine 稍复杂一些，因为它必须将正确的实参分配给 f 和 g。下面是代码的初稿：The program to implement spread-combine is a bit more complicated than parallel-combine, because it must distribute the correct arguments to f and g. Here is a first draft of that code:

(define (spread-combine h f g)

  (let ((n (get-arity f)))

    (define (the-combination . args)

      (h (apply f (list-head args n))

         (apply g (list-tail args n))))

    the-combination))

这段代码需要一种确定过程接受多少个实参（即其元数）的方法，因为它必须先选出 f 的实参，再将余下的实参传给 g。This code requires a way of determining how many arguments a procedure takes (its arity), because it has to pick out the arguments for f and then pass the rest to g.

这个版本的 spread-combine 不太好。最严重的问题是，the-combination 接受任意数量的实参，因此没有明确定义的数值元数，也就无法传给另一个需要知道其元数的组合子。例如，某个 spread-combine 的结果不能作为第二个实参 f 传给另一个 spread-combine。所以，我们必须设法为 the-combination 附上适当的元数。下面是第二稿：This version of spread-combine is not very good. The most egregious problem is that the-combination takes any number of arguments, so it does not have a well-defined numerical arity, and thus it cannot be passed to another combinator that needs its arity. For example, the result of a spread-combine cannot be passed as the second argument f to another spread-combine. So, somehow, we have to decorate the-combination with an appropriate arity. Here is a second draft:

(define (spread-combine h f g)

  (let ((n (get-arity f)) (m (get-arity g)))

    (let ((t (+ n m)))

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (h (apply f (list-head args n))

           (apply g (list-tail args n))))

      (restrict-arity the-combination t))))

这里，返回的过程 the-combination 已经指明了元数，因此可以作为某个需要元数的其他组合子的输入。restrict-arity 过程接受一个过程，为它加上注记，使 get-arity 能获取其元数，然后返回带注记的过程。Here, the procedure the-combination that is returned has its arity specified, so it can be the input to some other combinator that requires an arity. The restrict-arity procedure takes a procedure, annotates it so that its arity can be obtained by get-arity, and returns the annotated procedure.

这已经相当不错，但最好的程序是偏执狂写出来的！我们希望尽早捕获错误，赶在它们变得难以定位或引发严重问题之前。因此，让我们采用“偏执式编程风格”，给这段代码加上一个断言，检查传给组合结果的实参数量是否正确。This is pretty good, but the best programs are written by paranoids! We want to catch errors as early as possible, before they become hard to locate or cause serious trouble. So let's annotate this code with an assertion in Paranoid Programming Style, to check that we have the right number of arguments to our combination.

(define (spread-combine h f g)

  (let ((n (get-arity f)) (m (get-arity g)))

    (let ((t (+ n m)))

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (assert (= (length args) t))

        (h (apply f (list-head args n))

           (apply g (list-tail args n))))

      (restrict-arity the-combination t))))



((spread-combine list

                 (lambda (x y) (list ’foo x y))

                 (lambda (u v w) (list ’bar u v w)))

 ’a ’b ’c 'd ’e)

((foo a b) (bar c d e))

特殊形式 assert 只是在其实参不为真值时发出错误信号的一种便捷方式。The special form assert is just a convenient way to signal an error if its argument does not have a true value.

restrict-arity 和 get-arity 的一种写法如下：One way to write restrict-arity and get-arity is as follows:

(define (restrict-arity proc nargs)

  (hash-table-set! arity-table proc nargs)

  proc)



(define (get-arity proc)

  (or (hash-table-ref/default arity-table proc #f)

      (let ((a (procedure-arity proc))) ;arity not in table

        (assert (eqv? (procedure-arity-min a)

                      (procedure-arity-max a)))

        (procedure-arity-min a))))

(define arity-table (make-key-weak-eqv-hash-table))

这里，我们用散列表给过程贴上一张“便条”。4 这是向现有对象添加信息的一种简单技巧，但它依赖被注记对象的唯一性，因此应谨慎使用。Here we are using a hash table to attach a “sticky note” to the procedure.4 This is a simple trick for adding information to an existing object, but it depends on the uniqueness of the object being annotated, so it should be used carefully.

如果过程 get-arity 无法在 arity-table 中找到显式的值，就使用底层 MIT/GNU Scheme 系统的基本过程来计算。这里有些棘手，因为这些基本过程支持更一般的元数概念：一个过程要求至少接受一定数量的实参，还可能有一个可选的实参数量上限。我们的元数代码假定元数是固定的实参数量，因此 get-arity 无法处理其他种类的过程。不幸的是，这就排除了像 + 这样接受任意数量实参的过程。修改元数代码以使用更一般的元数概念会增加其复杂性，而我们在这里的目标是清晰地阐述，而非给出通用解法（见练习 2.2）。If the procedure get-arity is unable to find an explicit value in arity-table, it computes one using primitives from the underlying MIT/GNU Scheme system. This involves some hair, because those primitives support a more general idea of arity: that a procedure requires a minimum number of arguments, and may have an optional maximum number of arguments. Our arity code expects an arity to be a fixed number of arguments, and so get-arity cannot work with any other kind of procedure. Unfortunately, this excludes procedures like + that take any number of arguments. Changing the arity code to use a more general notion of arity would complicate it, and our goal here is to have a clear exposition rather than a general solution (see exercise 2.2).

练习 2.1：修正元数Exercise 2.1: Arity repair

我们介绍的过程 compose 和 parallel-combine 不符合公布组合结果元数的要求。因此，它们还算不上组合子家族中的好成员。修正上面给出的 compose 和 parallel-combine 的实现，使它们满足：The procedures compose and parallel-combine that we have introduced do not obey the requirement that they advertise the arity of the combination. Thus they would not be good citizens of our family of combinators. Fix the implementations of compose and parallel-combine shown above, so that

  • 检查各组件，确保元数兼容；they check their components to make sure that the arities are compatible;
  • 构造出的组合在被调用时，检查收到的实参数量是否正确；the combination they construct checks that it is given the correct number of arguments when it is called;
  • 组合向 get-arity 正确地公布其元数。the combination advertises its arity correctly for get-arity.

练习 2.2：扩展元数Exercise 2.2: Arity extension

我们对实用组合子的阐述有个缺陷：展示的元数机制无法处理 MIT/GNU Scheme 所使用的更一般的元数机制。例如，加法过程，即 + 的值，可以接受任意数量的实参：Our exposition of useful combinators is flawed in that the arity mechanism we displayed cannot handle the more general arity mechanism used by MIT/GNU Scheme. For example, the addition procedure, which is the value of +, can take any number of arguments:

(procedure-arity-min (procedure-arity +)) = 0

(procedure-arity-max (procedure-arity +)) = #f

而反正切过程可以接受 1 个或 2 个实参：and the arctangent procedure can take either 1 or 2 arguments:

(procedure-arity-min (procedure-arity atan)) = 1

(procedure-arity-max (procedure-arity atan)) = 2

扩展元数的处理方式，使组合子能够应对这些更复杂的情况，是很有用的。It is useful to extend the handling of arities so that combinators can work with these more complex situations.

  1. a. 概述一个扩展组合子的方案，使其使用更一般的元数。注意，你不一定总能对元数进行算术运算。重新设计 spread-combine 时，你必须作出哪些选择？例如，在 spread-combine 中，需要对过程 f、g 和 h 施加哪些限制？a. Sketch a plan for how to extend the combinators to use the more general arities. Note that you may not always be able to use arithmetic on the arities. What choices will you have to make in reformulating spread-combine? For example, what kinds of restrictions will be needed on the procedures f, g, and h in spread-combine?
  2. b. 实施你的方案，让一切正常运转！b. Apply your plan and make it all work!

任何语言都有基本元素、组合手段和抽象手段。组合子语言定义基本元素和组合手段，并从底层编程语言继承抽象手段。在我们的例子中，基本元素是函数，组合手段则是组合子 compose、parallel-combine、spread-combine，以及我们可能引入的其他组合子。For any language there are primitives, means of combination, and means of abstraction. A combinator language defines primitives and means of combination, inheriting its means of abstraction from the underlying programming language. In our example, the primitives are functions, and the means of combination are the combinators compose, parallel-combine, spread-combine, and others we may introduce.

多值Multiple values

注意，parallel-combine 和 spread-combine 有一个共同点：二者都将合并函数 h 应用于 f 和 g 的结果。但我们构造这些组合子时，没有使用 compose。要抽象出这一模式，就必须能够从 f 和 g 的组合中返回多个值，再将这些值作为 h 的实参。可以通过返回一个复合数据结构做到这一点，但更好的办法是使用 Scheme 的多值返回机制。有了多值，就能把 spread-combine 定义为两部分的复合：h，以及 f 和 g 的这一组合：5Notice that parallel-combine and spread-combine are similar in that each is the application of a combiner h to the results of f and g. But we did not use compose to construct these combinators. To abstract this pattern we need to be able to return multiple values from the combination of f and g and then use those multiple values as arguments for h. We could do this by returning a compound data structure, but a better way is to use the Scheme multiple-value return mechanism. Given multiple values we can define spread-combine as a composition of two parts, h and this combination of f and g:5

(define (spread-apply f g)

  (let ((n (get-arity f)) (m (get-arity g)))

    (let ((t (+ n m)))

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (assert (= (length args) t))

        (values (apply f (list-head args n))

                (apply g (list-tail args n))))

      (restrict-arity the-combination t))))

Scheme 过程 values 返回分别应用 f 和 g 所得的结果。6The Scheme procedure values returns the results of applying both f and g.6

下面，我们将推广 compose，以便如下直接实现图 2.4 所示的抽象：Below we will generalize compose so that we can directly implement the abstraction shown in figure 2.4 as follows:

(define (spread-combine h f g)

  (compose h (spread-apply f g)))

它与最初版本的行为相同：This has the same behavior as our original version:

((spread-combine list

                 (lambda (x y) (list ’foo x y))

                 (lambda (u v w) (list ’bar u v w)))

 ’a ’b ’c 'd ’e)

((foo a b) (bar c d e))

为此，我们推广 compose，使多个值能够在参与复合的过程之间传递：To make this work, we generalize compose to allow multiple values to pass between the composed procedures:

(define (compose f g)

  (define (the-composition . args)

    (call-with-values (lambda () (apply g args))

      f))

  (restrict-arity the-composition (get-arity g)))

这里，传给 compose 的第二个实参返回两个值：Here the second argument to compose returns two values:

((compose (lambda (a b)

            (list ’foo a b))

          (lambda (x)

            (values (list ’bar x)

                    (list ’baz x))))

 ’z)

(foo (bar z) (baz z))

现在还可以进一步推广：允许所有被组合的函数都返回多个值。如果 f 和 g 都返回多个值，我们就可以将这些值汇集成 the-combination 可以返回的多个值：Now we can generalize even further. We can allow all of the functions we are combining to return multiple values. If f and g both return multiple values we can combine those values into multiple values that the-combination can return:

(define (spread-apply f g)

  (let ((n (get-arity f)) (m (get-arity g)))

    (let ((t (+ n m)))

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (assert (= (length args) t))

        (let-values ((fv (apply f (list-head args n)))

                     (gv (apply g (list-tail args n))))

          (apply values (append fv gv))))

      (restrict-arity the-combination t))))

((spread-combine list

                 (lambda (x y) (values x y))

                 (lambda (u v w) (values w v u)))

 ’a ’b ’c 'd ’e)

(a b e d c)

唯一的限制是，返回值的总数必须符合 h 的元数要求。The only restriction is that the total number of values returned must be appropriate for the arity of h.

练习 2.3：一道快题Exercise 2.3: A quickie

将 parallel-combine 改写为两部分的复合，并允许各部分返回多个值。Reformulate parallel-combine to be a composition of two parts and to allow the parts to return multiple values.

一个小型程序库A small library

许多常见的使用模式都可以提炼为组合子，使用这类技术往往能够构造出非常优雅的程序。揭示并抽象这些常见模式对我们大有裨益。下面再给出几个供大家思考。Many common patterns of usage can be captured as combinators, and very pretty programs are often constructed using such techniques. It is to our advantage to expose and abstract such common patterns. Here are a few more to think about.

我们常常会有一个接口，其通用程度超出了某一具体情形的需要。这时，我们可能希望保留该接口，但调用一个更专门化的过程，它不需要一般情况下可以提供的全部参数；于是，我们选择为这个专门化过程制作一个忽略某些实参的版本。Often we have an interface that is more general than necessary in a particular situation. In such a case we may want to preserve the interface, but call some more specialized procedure that does not need all of the parameters we can supply in the general case; so we choose to make a version of our specialized procedure that ignores some arguments.

过程 discard-argument 接受要丢弃的实参的索引 i，并返回一个组合子。这个组合子接受一个有 n 个实参的函数 f，返回一个有 n + 1 个实参的新函数 the-combination；新函数从给定的 n + 1 个实参中删去第 i 个实参，再将 f 应用于剩下的 n 个实参。图 2.5 说明了这个想法。该组合子的代码如下：The procedure discard-argument takes the index, i, of the argument to be discarded and returns a combinator. The combinator takes a function, f, of n arguments and returns a new function the-combination of n + 1 arguments that applies f to the n arguments resulting from deleting the ith argument from the n + 1 given arguments. Figure 2.5 illustrates this idea. The code for this combinator is:

(define (discard-argument i)

  (assert (exact-nonnegative-integer? i))

  (lambda (f)

    (let ((m (+ (get-arity f) 1)))

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (assert (= (length args) m))

        (apply f (list-remove args i)))

      (assert (< i m))

      (restrict-arity the-combination m))))



(define (list-remove lst index)

  (let lp ((lst lst) (index index))

    (if (= index 0)

        (cdr lst)

        (cons (car lst) (lp (cdr lst) (- index 1))))))



(((discard-argument 2)

  (lambda (x y z) (list ’foo x y z)))

 ’a ’b ’c 'd)

(foo a b d)

可以推广这个组合子，使其丢弃多个实参。与 discard-argument 相反的情况也经常出现。图 2.6 的接线图展示了如何通过预先指定除一个实参以外的所有实参，来专门化一个过程，而留下的那个实参由调用时传入。这种做法传统上称为柯里化，以纪念逻辑学家 Haskell Curry；他是组合逻辑的早期研究者。7One can generalize this combinator to discard multiple arguments. The opposite of the situation of discard-argument also commonly occurs. In figure 2.6 we see a wiring diagram for specializing a procedure by specifying all but one argument in advance, leaving one to be passed in the call. This is traditionally called currying in honor of the logician Haskell Curry, who was an early investigator of combinatory logic.7

curry-argument 的代码没有什么出人意料之处：The code for curry-argument poses no surprises:

(define ((curry-argument i) . args)

  (lambda (f)

    (assert (= (length args) (- (get-arity f) 1)))

    (lambda (x)

      (apply f (list-insert args i x)))))



(define (list-insert lst index value)

  (let lp ((lst lst) (index index))

    (if (= index 0)

        (cons value lst)

        (cons (car lst) (lp (cdr lst) (- index 1))))))



((((curry-argument 2) ’a ’b ’c)

  (lambda (x y z w) (list ’foo x y z w)))

 'd)

(foo a b d c)

注意，这里不需要使用 restrict-arity，因为返回的过程恰好只有一个实参。8 在练习 2.5 中，我们将推广这个柯里化组合子，让它留下多个实参待提供。Note that here we do not need to use restrict-arity because the returned procedure has exactly one argument.8 In exercise 2.5 we generalize this combinator for currying, to leave multiple arguments to be supplied.

有时，我们想使用一个库过程，但其实参顺序不同于当前应用采用的标准。与其为这个过程制作专用接口，不如用一个通用的置换过程来重新排列，如图 2.7 所示。这个程序也很简单，但请注意：组合子返回的、实际处理 args 的过程 the-combination，不必再解释置换规格——这项工作只在包围 the-combination 的 let 中做一次，内部只需引用其结果。一般来说，这种写法允许通过提前计算进行某些深度优化，即使绑定发生得非常晚也一样！Sometimes we want to use a library procedure that has a different order of arguments than the standard that we are using in the current application. Rather than make a special interface for that procedure, we can use a general permutation procedure to rearrange things, as in figure 2.7. This program is also simple, but notice that the procedure the-combination that is returned from the combinator and actually runs on args does not have to interpret the permutation specification—this is done once in the let surrounding the-combination and referred to within. In general, writing code this way allows some deep optimizations by early computation, even in the light of very late binding!

(define (permute-arguments . permspec)

  (let ((permute (make-permutation permspec)))

    (lambda (f)

      (define (the-combination . args)

        (apply f (permute args)))

      (let ((n (get-arity f)))

        (assert (= n (length permspec)))

        (restrict-arity the-combination n)))))



(((permute-arguments 1 2 0 3)

  (lambda (x y z w) (list ’foo x y z w)))

 ’a ’b ’c 'd)

(foo b c a d)

过程 make-permutation 很简单，但效率不高：The procedure make-permutation is simple, but it is not efficient:

(define (make-permutation permspec)

  (define (the-permuter lst)

    (map (lambda (p) (list-ref lst p))

         permspec))

  the-permuter)

2.1.2 组合子与构型2.1.2 Combinators and body plans

这一讨论的一个启示是：由组合子的组合所构成的结构就是一种构型，很像动物的构型，或超外差无线电接收机这样的工程模式（第 10 页图 1.1）。考虑 compose 组合子。它安排了若干局部区域，即过程 f 和 g。这些局部区域通过标准连接方式相连，而这就是对 f 和 g 的全部要求。事实上，这些组件可以是任何能接受正确数量的实参并返回正确数量的值的东西。因此，组合子是一种组织原则，就像 Hox 基因一样：它们规定局部区域及其相互关系，却不强制规定每个局部区域内部要发生什么。A moral of this story is that a structure composed of combinations of combinators is a body plan, much like the body plans of animals or engineering patterns like the superheterodyne radio receiver (figure 1.1 on page 10). Consider the compose combinator. It provides an arrangement of locales, the procedures f and g. The locales are connected by a standard interconnect, but that is all that is required of f and g. Indeed, these components may be anything that can take the right number of arguments and can return the right number of values. So the combinators are organizing principles, like Hox genes: they specify locales and their relationship without mandating what happens inside each locale.

练习 2.4：写成复合？Exercise 2.4: As compositions?

你可能已经注意到，discard-argument、curry-argument 和 permute-arguments 生成的组合子，都可以看作一次实参变换与一个过程的复合。利用多值返回机制，将这些组合子重新构建为复合。You may have noticed that the combinators made by discard-argument, curry-argument, and permute-arguments can each be thought of as a composition of an argument manipulation and a procedure. Rebuild these combinators as compositions using the multiple-value return mechanism.

练习 2.5：实用组合子Exercise 2.5: Useful combinators

现在该把这个小型程序库再充实一些了。It is time to fill out this small library a bit more.

  1. a. 可以推广组合子 discard-argument 和 curry-argument，允许忽略多个实参，或者预先指定多个实参来进行专门化。为 permute-arguments 指定置换的方法，似乎是一种相当通用的方式，可以按实参在调用中的顺序来指定它们（从零开始计数）。构造这些过程的推广版本，采用这样的接口，将其命名为 discard-arguments 和 curry-arguments。让你的代码与正文中的代码兼容：你的（curry-arguments 2）应该与（curry-argument 2）的作用完全相同。a. The combinators discard-argument and curry-argument could be generalized to allow ignoring or prespecializing on more than one argument. The method of specifying the permutation for permute-arguments seems to be a pretty general way to specify arguments by their order in a call (zero-based). Build generalized versions of these procedures that have such an interface. Name them discard-arguments and curry-arguments. Make your code compatible with the code in the text: your (curry-arguments 2) should do exactly what (curry-argument 2) does.
  2. b. 你觉得还有哪些组合子会有用？列一张清单，并配上你在实际代码中可能遇到的适当用例。为你的程序库实现这些组合子。b. What other combinators would you find useful? Make up a list, with appropriate use cases that you might encounter in actual code. Write implementations of them for your library.
  3. c. 进一步推广 compose，使其接受任意数量的函数实参。表达式（compose f g h）等价于（compose f (compose g h)）。注意，它也应当等价于（compose (compose f g) h）。小心：零个实参的复合是什么？c. Further generalize compose so that it can take any number of functional aguments. The expression (compose f g h) is equivalent to (compose f (compose g h)). Note that it should also be equivalent to (compose (compose f g) h). Be careful: what is the composition of zero arguments?

2.2 正则表达式2.2 Regular expressions

正则表达式广泛用于字符串匹配。尽管正则表达式系统源自一种完全良好的数学形式体系，实现者为了将它扩充为实用的软件系统所作的具体选择，却往往是灾难性的：采用的引用约定极不规则；对括号的严重滥用——既用来分组，又用来向后引用——更是令人叹为观止。此外，为增强表达能力、弥补早期设计的缺陷所作的尝试，又导致了大量互不兼容的派生语言。Regular expressions are widely used for string matching. Although regular-expression systems are derived from a perfectly good mathematical formalism, the particular choices made by implementers to expand the formalism into useful software systems are often disastrous: the quotation conventions adopted are highly irregular; the egregious misuse of parentheses, both for grouping and for backward reference, is a miracle to behold. In addition, attempts to increase the expressive power and address shortcomings of earlier designs have led to a proliferation of incompatible derivative languages.

表面上看，正则表达式像是一种组合子语言，因为表达式片段可以组合成更复杂的表达式。但片段的含义高度依赖于它所嵌入的表达式。例如，如果想在方括号表达式 [...] 中包含脱字符 ∧，脱字符就不能位于第一个字符的位置：如果它出现在第一个字符之后，就只是普通字符；但如果它是第一个字符，就会对方括号表达式的含义取反。因此，方括号表达式中不能只有一个脱字符。On the surface, regular expressions look like a combinator language, because expression fragments can be combined to make more complex expressions. But the meaning of a fragment is highly dependent on the expression it is embedded in. For example, if we want a caret, ∧, in a bracket expression, [...], the caret must not be in the first character position, because if the caret appears after the first character it is just an ordinary character, but if it appears as the first character it negates the meaning of the bracket expression. Thus a bracket expression may not contain just a caret.

所以，正则表达式语言的语法很糟糕；这种语言有各种互不兼容的形式；引用约定也繁复怪诞 [sic]。尽管正则表达式语言属于领域专用语言，却是糟糕的领域专用语言。考察正则表达式的价值之一，就是体会事情究竟能糟糕到什么程度。So the syntax of the regular-expression language is awful; there are various incompatible forms of the language; and the quotation conventions are baroquen [sic]. While regular expression languages are domain-specific languages, they are bad ones. Part of the value of examining regular expressions is to experience how bad things can be.

尽管如此，仍有大量实用软件（例如 grep）使用正则表达式来指定所需行为。我们将设计一种更好的领域专用组合子语言来描述正则表达式，并提供一种方法，将其翻译为传统的正则表达式语法。我们将使用 POSIX 基本正则表达式（BRE）语法作为翻译器的目标 [96]，因为它是大多数其他正则表达式语法的子集。POSIX 还定义了一种功能更强的扩展正则表达式（ERE）语法，我们将在一道练习中考虑它。Nevertheless, there is a great deal of useful software, for example grep, that uses regular expressions to specify the desired behavior. We will invent a better domain-specific combinator language for specifying regular expressions and a means of translating this language to conventional regular-expression syntax. We will use the POSIX Basic Regular Expression (BRE) syntax as a target for our translator [96], since it is a subset of most other regular-expression syntaxes. POSIX also defines a more powerful Extended Regular Expression (ERE) syntax, which we will consider in an exercise.

有了这套机制，就能在 Scheme 环境内部使用 grep 这类系统的能力。我们将获得组合子语言的所有优点：既有清晰、模块化的描述，又保留使用现有工具的能力。这种语言的使用者将没什么好抱怨的，除非他们更看重表达简短而非可读性。With this machinery we will be able to use the capabilities of systems like grep from inside the Scheme environment. We will have all the advantages of a combinator language. It will have a clean, modular description while retaining the ability to use existing tools. Users of this language will have nothing to grep about, unless they value concise expression over readability.

与任何语言一样，这里也有基本元素、组合手段和抽象手段。我们的语言允许构造模式，grep 这类工具可以用它们来匹配字符串数据。由于这门语言嵌入在 Scheme 中，我们便继承了 Scheme 的能力：可以使用 Scheme 构造来组合模式，使用 Scheme 过程来抽象模式。As with any language there are primitives, means of combination, and means of abstraction. Our language allows the construction of patterns that utilities like grep can match against character-string data. Because this language is embedded in Scheme, we inherit Scheme's power: we can use Scheme constructs to combine patterns and use Scheme procedures to abstract them.

2.2.1 一种正则表达式组合子语言2.2.1 A regular expression combinator language

模式由下列基本模式构成：Patterns are built out of these primitive patterns:

(r:dot) 匹配换行符以外的任意字符。(r:dot) matches any character except newline

(r:bol) 只匹配行首。(r:bol) matches only the beginning of a line

(r:eol) 只匹配行尾。(r:eol) matches only the end of a line

(r:quote string) 匹配该字符串。(r:quote string) matches the string

(r:char-from string) 匹配该字符串中包含的一个字符。(r:char-from string) matches one character that is in the string

(r:char-not-from string) 匹配该字符串中不包含的一个字符。(r:char-not-from string) matches one character that is not in the string

模式可以组合成复合模式：Patterns can be combined to make compound patterns:

(r:seq pattern ...)(r:seq pattern ...)

这个模式从左到右依次匹配作为实参的各个模式。This pattern matches each argument pattern in sequence, from left to right.

(r:alt pattern ...)(r:alt pattern ...)

这个模式从左到右尝试作为实参的各个模式，直到其中一个备选项匹配成功。如果没有任何一个匹配成功，那么整个模式也不匹配。This pattern tries each argument pattern from left to right, until one of these alternatives matches. If none matches then this pattern does not match.

(r:repeat min max pattern)(r:repeat min max pattern)

这个模式尝试匹配作为实参的模式，至少 min 次，至多 max 次。如果 max 给为 #f，则不指定上限。如果 max 等于 min，给定模式就必须恰好匹配这么多次。This pattern tries to match the argument pattern a minimum of min times but no more than a maximum of max times. If max is given as #f then no maximum is specified. If max equals min the given pattern must be matched exactly that many times.

下面是一些模式示例：Here are some example patterns:

(r:seq (r:quote "a") (r:dot) (r:quote "c"))

匹配任何以 a 开头、以 c 结尾的三字符字符串。例如，它会匹配 abc、aac 和 acc。matches any three-character string beginning with a and ending with c. For example, it will match abc and aac and acc.

(r:alt (r:quote "foo") (r:quote "bar") (r:quote "baz"))

匹配 foo、bar 或 baz。matches either foo, bar, or baz.

(r:repeat 3 5 (r:alt (r:quote "cat") (r:quote "dog"))) 匹配 catdogcat、catcatdogdog 和 dogdogcatdogdog，但不匹配 catcatcatdogdogdog。(r:repeat 3 5 (r:alt (r:quote "cat") (r:quote "dog"))) matches catdogcat and catcatdogdog and dogdogcatdogdog but not catcatcatdogdogdog.

我们将用 Scheme 表达式实现模式。因此，可以将它们与任意 Scheme 代码自由混用，从而获得这门编程语言的全部能力。We will implement patterns as Scheme expressions. Thus we can freely mix them with any Scheme code, giving us all the power of the programming language.

2.2.2 翻译器的实现2.2.2 Implementation of the translator

来看看这门语言是如何实现的。正则表达式将表示为采用 POSIX 基本正则表达式语法的字符串。Let's look at how this language is implemented. Regular expressions will be represented as strings in the POSIX Basic Regular Expression syntax.

(define (r:dot) ".")

(define (r:bol) "∧")

(define (r:eol) "$")

这些与正则表达式语法直接对应。These directly correspond to regular-expression syntax.

接下来，r:seq 实现了一种将给定的一组正则表达式片段视为一个独立完整元素的方法：Next, r:seq implements a way to treat a given set of regular-expression fragments as a self-contained element:

(define (r:seq . exprs)

  (string-append "\\(" (apply string-append exprs) "\\)"))

在结果中使用括号，可以将给定表达式片段的内容与周围上下文隔离开来。不幸的是，翻译输出中必须使用 \。在基本正则表达式中，括号字符被视为表示自身的字符。这里需要它们起分组运算的作用，为此必须在每个括号前加上反斜杠。雪上加霜的是，把这个正则表达式放入 Scheme 字符串时，又必须用另一个反斜杠转义每个反斜杠字符。因此，示例 (r:seq (r:quote "a") (r:dot) (r:quote "c")) 被翻译为 \(\(a\).\(c\)\)，或者写成 Scheme 字符串就是 "\\(\\(a\\).\\(c\\)\\)"。真糟糕。The use of parentheses in the result isolates the content of the given expression fragments from the surrounding context. Unfortunately, the use of \ in the translated output is necessary. In basic regular expressions, the parenthesis characters are treated as self-quoting characters. Here we need them to act as grouping operations, which is done by preceding each with a backslash. Adding insult to injury, when this regular expression is put into a Scheme string, it is necessary to quote each backslash character with another backslash. So our example (r:seq (r:quote "a") (r:dot) (r:quote "c")) translates to \(\(a\).\(c\)\), or as a Scheme string "\\(\\(a\\).\\(c\\)\\)". Ugh.

r:quote 的实现稍难一些。在正则表达式中，大多数字符都表示自身。但某些字符是正则表达式运算符，必须显式转义。我们用 r:seq 包装结果，以确保转义后的字符串是独立完整的。The implementation of r:quote is a bit harder. In a regular expression, most characters are self-quoting. However, some characters are regular-expression operators and must be explicitly quoted. We wrap the result using r:seq to guarantee that the quoted string is self-contained.

(define (r:quote string)

  (r:seq

    (list->string

      (append-map (lambda (char)

                    (if (memv char chars-needing-quoting)

                        (list #\\ char)

                        (list char)))

                  (string->list string)))))



(define chars-needing-quoting

  ’(#\. #\[ #\\ #\∧ #\$ #\*))

为实现备选子表达式，我们在子表达式之间插入竖线，并用 r:seq 包装结果：To implement alternative subexpressions, we interpolate a vertical bar between subexpressions and wrap the result using r:seq:

(define (r:alt . exprs)

  (if (pair? exprs)

      (apply r:seq

             (cons (car exprs)

                   (append-map (lambda (expr)

                                 (list "\\|" expr))

                               (cdr exprs))))

      (r:seq)))

(r:alt (r:quote "foo") (r:quote "bar") (r:quote "baz")) 被翻译为 \(\(foo\)\|\(bar\)\|\(baz\)\)。除了转义括号字符外，还必须转义竖线字符，否则它在这种语法中就是一个表示自身的字符。注意，与这里支持的其他正则表达式不同，BRE 语法不支持备选表达式：这是 GNU grep 定义的一种扩展，许多实现都支持它。（ERE 语法支持备选项。）(r:alt (r:quote "foo") (r:quote "bar") (r:quote "baz")) translates to \(\(foo\)\|\(bar\)\|\(baz\)\). In addition to quoting the parenthesis characters, we must also quote the vertical bar character, which is otherwise a self-quoting character in this syntax. Note that alternative expressions, unlike the rest of the regular expressions supported here, are not supported by BRE syntax: they are an extension defined by GNU grep that is supported by many implementations. (Alternatives are supported by ERE syntax.)

使用给定正则表达式的副本来实现重复，是很直接的：It is straightforward to implement repetition by using copies of the given regular expression:

(define (r:repeat min max expr)

  (apply r:seq

         (append (make-list min expr)

                 (cond ((not max) (list expr "*"))

                       ((= max min) ’())

                       (else

                        (make-list (- max min)

                                   (r:alt expr "")))))))

这会生成 min 份 expr，后面再接 (- max min) 份可选副本；每份可选副本都是该表达式与空表达式之间的备选。如果没有上限，9 就在表达式之后加上星号，以匹配任意次数。因此，(r:repeat 3 5 (r:alt (r:quote "cat") (r:quote "dog"))) 会被翻译成一个庞然大物，读者看了恐怕都要抽搐。This makes min copies of expr, followed by (- max min) optional copies, where each optional copy is an alternative of the expression and an empty expression. If there is no maximum,9 the expression is followed by an asterisk to match any number of times. So (r:repeat 3 5 (r:alt (r:quote "cat") (r:quote "dog"))) translates to something large that might cause seizures in the reader.

r:char-from 和 r:char-not-from 的实现因为需要繁复的转义处理而变得复杂。最好将其组织成两部分：第一部分处理二者的差异，第二部分处理二者共有的转义操作：The implementation of r:char-from and r:char-not-from is complicated by the need for baroque quotation. This is best organized in two parts, the first to handle the differences between them, and the second for the quotation handling that they have in common:

(define (r:char-from string)

  (case (string-length string)

    ((0) (r:seq))

    ((1) (r:quote string))

    (else

     (bracket string

              (lambda (members)

                (if (lset= eqv? ’(#\- #\∧) members)

                    ’(#\- #\∧)

                    (quote-bracketed-contents members)))))))



(define (r:char-not-from string)

  (bracket string

           (lambda (members)

             (cons #\∧ (quote-bracketed-contents members)))))



(define (bracket string procedure)

  (list->string

   (append ’(#\[)

           (procedure (string->list string))

           ’(#\]))))

r:char-from 的特殊分支专门处理空字符集和单字符集，从而简化一般情形。另有一个特殊分支处理只含脱字符和连字符的集合。但 r:char-not-from 没有这些特殊分支。The special cases for r:char-from handle empty and singleton sets of characters specially, which simplifies the general case. There is also a special case for a set containing only caret and hyphen. But r:char-not-from has no such special cases.

一般情形通过将三个在方括号内具有特殊含义的字符放在不被视为运算符的位置，来实现对它们的转义。（我们早说过这很丑陋！）The general case handles the quotation of the three characters that have special meaning inside a bracket by placing them in positions where they are not operators. (We told you this was ugly!)

(define (quote-bracketed-contents members)

  (define (optional char)

    (if (memv char members) (list char) ’()))

  (append (optional #\])

          (remove

            (lambda (c)

              (memv c chars-needing-quoting-in-brackets))

            members)

          (optional #\∧)

          (optional #\-)))



(define chars-needing-quoting-in-brackets

  ’(#\] #\∧ #\-))

为了测试这段代码，可以打印出对应的 grep 命令，再通过剪切粘贴在 shell 中运行。由于不同 shell 使用不同的引用约定，我们不仅需要引用正则表达式，还要选择使用哪种 shell。Bourne shell 随处可见，其引用约定也相对简单。In order to test this code, we can print the corresponding grep command and use cut and paste to run it in a shell. Because different shells use different quoting conventions, we need to not only quote the regular expression, but also choose which shell to use. The Bourne shell is ubiquitous, and has a relatively simple quoting convention.

(define (write-bourne-shell-grep-command expr filename)

  (display (bourne-shell-grep-command-string expr filename)))



(define (bourne-shell-grep-command-string expr filename)

  (string-append "grep -e "

                 (bourne-shell-quote-string expr) 

                 " "

                 filename))

Bourne 的引用约定用单引号包围字符串，可以引用字符串中除单引号外的任何内容；单引号会终止被引用的字符串。因此，要引用单引号字符，必须先结束字符串，用反斜杠显式转义该单引号，再开始另一个被引用的字符串。shell 会把这种拼接解释为单个词元。（现在觉得好玩了吗？）The Bourne quoting convention uses single-quote characters surrounding a string, which quotes anything in the string other than a single-quote, which ends the quoted string. So, to quote a single-quote character, we must end the string, quote the single quote explicitly using backslash, and then start another quoted string. The shell interprets this concatenation as a single token. (Are we having fun yet?)

(define (bourne-shell-quote-string string)

  (list->string

   (append (list #\’)

           (append-map (lambda (char)

                         (if (char=? char #\’)

                             (list #\’ #\\ char #\’)

                             (list char)))

                       (string->list string))

           (list #\’))))

这段讨论的启示The moral of this story

我们的翻译器非常复杂，因为大多数正则表达式都不能直接组合成更大的正则表达式，除非采取极端手段将各部分隔离开来。翻译器完成了这项工作，但也因此生成了带有大量不必要样板内容的正则表达式。人类并不这样编写正则表达式，因为他们只在必要的地方使用样板内容——但也往往漏掉确实需要的地方，从而引入难以发现的错误。Our translator is very complicated because most regular expressions are not composable to make larger regular expressions unless extreme measures are taken to isolate the parts. Our translator does this work, but consequently the regular expressions that it generates have much unnecessary boilerplate. Humans don't write regular expressions this way, because they use boilerplate only where necessary—but they often miss instances where it is necessary, causing hard-to-find bugs.

这段讨论的启示是：正则表达式是一个绝好的反面教材，展示了不该如何构建系统。使用可组合的部件和组合子，通过组合已有部件来构造新部件，能够得到更简单、更健壮的实现。The moral of this story is that regular expressions are a beautiful example of how not to build a system. Using composable parts and combinators to make new parts by combining others leads to simpler and more robust implementations.

练习 2.6：为正则表达式添加 * 和 +Exercise 2.6: Adding * and + to regular expressions

在传统的正则表达式语言中，位于子模式之后的星号（*）运算符表示该子模式出现零次或多次。这门语言的一种常见扩展加入了加号（+）运算符。子模式之后的加号表示该子模式出现一次或多次。In the traditional regular expression language the asterisk (*) operator following a subpattern means zero or more copies of the subpattern. A common extension to the language adds the plus-sign (+) operator. A plus sign following a subpattern means one or more copies of the subpattern.

定义 Scheme 过程 r:* 和 r:+，使它们接受一个模式，并按要求重复该模式。这可以用 r:repeat 来实现。Define Scheme procedures r:* and r:+ to take a pattern and iterate it as necessary. This can be done in terms of r:repeat.

在复杂模式中，使用真实数据演示你的过程。Demonstrate your procedures on real data in complex patterns.

练习 2.7：一个错误、一个烂笑话、两处微调，以及一个顿悟Exercise 2.7: A bug, one bad joke, two tweaks, and a revelation

Ben Bitdiddle 注意到，我们对 (r:repeat min max expr) 的实现存在一个问题。Ben Bitdiddle has noticed a problem with our implementation of (r:repeat min max expr).

在 r:repeat 过程的末尾使用（r:alt expr ""）有些不可靠。这段代码会被翻译成 \(expr\|\)，其中 expr 是 expr 的值。这依赖于这样一个事实：在某个东西与空之间进行备选，就等于说“一个或没有”。（在接下来的说明中，我们将省略那些必需却令人困惑的反斜杠。）也就是说，(expr|) 表示 expr 出现一次或零次。不幸的是，这依赖于正式 POSIX 正则表达式标准之外的一项未记载的 GNU 扩展。The use of (r:alt expr "") at the end of the r:repeat procedure is a bit dodgy. This code fragment translates to \(expr\|\), where expr is the value of expr. This relies on the fact that alternation with something and nothing is the equivalent of saying “one or none.” (We will omit the required but confusing backslashes in the rest of this explanation.) That is: (expr|) denotes one or no instances of expr. Unfortunately, this depends on an undocumented GNU extension to the formal POSIX standard for REs.

具体来说，POSIX 标准10 的第 9.4.3 节规定，竖线紧接在右括号之前（或紧接在左括号之后）会产生未定义行为。实质上，正则表达式不得是空序列。Specifically, section 9.4.3 of the POSIX standard10 states that a vertical line appearing immediately before a close parenthesis (or immediately after an open parenthesis) produces undefined behavior. In essence, an RE must not be a null sequence.

GNU grep 碰巧在遇到 (x|) 时“做了正确的事”。并非所有 grep 实现都如此宽容。GNU grep just happens to “do the right thing” when presented with (x|). Not all grep implementations are as tolerant.

因此，Ben 请团队中的三位代码高手（Louis、Alyssa 和 Eva）提出其他变通方案。最后，他自己也提出了一项补丁，你将实现它。Therefore, Ben asks his team of three code hackers (Louis, Alyssa, and Eva) to propose alternative workarounds. Ultimately, he proposes his own patch, which you will implement.

  • Louis Reasoner 提议，一个简单、优雅的修正办法，是把代码片段（r:alt expr ""）换成对（r:repeat 0 1 expr）的直接调用。Louis Reasoner suggests that a simple, elegant fix would be to replace the code fragment (r:alt expr "") with a straightforward call to (r:repeat 0 1 expr).
  • Alyssa P. Hacker 提议重写 r:repeat 的 else 分支，将（r:repeat 3 5 x）翻译成等价于 (xxx|xxxx|xxxxx) 的表达式，而不是我们的代码所生成的、糟糕的 xxx(x|)(x|)——这种正则表达式不符合 POSIX 标准，行为未定义。她引用的是 POSIX 正则表达式文档的第 9.4.7 节。11Alyssa P. Hacker proposes to rewrite the else clause of r:repeat to translate (r:repeat 3 5 x) into the equivalent of (xxx|xxxx|xxxxx) instead of the naughty xxx(x|)(x|) non-POSIX-compliant undefined regular expression that our code produces. She refers to section 9.4.7 of the POSIX regular expression documentation.11
  • Eva Lu Ator 指出了第 9.4.6.4 节12 的问号（?）运算符，提出更好的修正办法是实现一个 r:? 运算符，并将（r:alt expr ""）替换为（r:? expr）。Eva Lu Ator points to the question mark (?) operator in section 9.4.6.412 and proposes that a better fix would be to implement an r:? operator and replace (r:alt expr "") with (r:? expr).
  • 与此同时，Ben 仔细研究正则表达式规格说明后有了顿悟。他建议重新实现 r:repeat，使其输出区间表达式。参见 POSIX 文档第 9.3.6.5 节。13Meanwhile, Ben looks closely at the RE spec and has a revelation. He proposes that r:repeat be reimplemented to emit Interval Expressions. See section 9.3.6.5 of the POSIX documentation.13

    请尽量忍住，别吐。Please try not to get sick.

我们来逐一考察这些提议：Let's consider each proposal:

  1. a. 大家都被 Louis 的傻笑话逗笑了。它究竟好笑在哪里？也就是说，这个想法有什么问题？a. Everyone giggles at Louis's silly joke. What's so funny about it? That is, what's wrong with this idea?

    用一句话点出笑点即可。A one-sentence punchline will do.

  2. b. 从代码和数据两方面看，Eva 的提议相比 Alyssa 的提议有什么优点？b. What advantages does Eva's proposal have over Alyssa's in terms of both code and data?

    简洁而有说服力地回答几句话即可。A concise yet convincing few sentences suffice.

  3. c. Ben 的提议相比所有其他提议有什么优势？具体来说，想一想他引用的是 POSIX 文档的哪一节，而其他人引用的又是哪几节；然后快速看一下后面的练习 2.10，考虑其中的含义。此外，还要考虑新代码输出字符串的大小，以及代码整体的清晰程度。c. What advantage does Ben's proposal have over all the others? Specifically, ponder which section of the POSIX document he cites versus which sections the others cite, then take a quick peek at exercise 2.10 below and consider the implications. Also, consider the size of the output strings in this new code as well as the overall clarity of the code.

    同样，简要回答一两句话即可。Again, a brief sentence or two is sufficient.

  4. d. 按照 Ben 的提议，重新实现 r:repeat，使其输出区间表达式。提示：Scheme 的 number->string 过程应当能派上用场。注意：小心反斜杠。d. Following Ben's proposal, reimplement r:repeat to emit Interval Expressions. Hint: Scheme's number->string procedure should be handy. Caveat: Beware the backslashes.

    选取几个恰当的示例输入，展示 r:repeat 生成的输出。在一些复杂模式中，使用真实数据演示你的过程。Show the output generated by r:repeat on a few well-chosen sample inputs. Demonstrate your procedure on real data in some complex patterns.

练习 2.8：嵌套过多Exercise 2.8: Too much nesting

我们的程序产生的正则表达式嵌套过多：即使不需要，也会创建分组。例如，下面这个简单模式就导致了一个过于复杂的正则表达式：Our program produces excessively nested regular expressions: it makes groups even when they are not necessary. For example, the following simple pattern leads to an overly complex regular expression:

(display (r:seq (r:quote "a") (r:dot) (r:quote "c")))

\(\(a\).\(c\)\)

另一个问题是，BRE 可能涉及反向引用。（见 POSIX 正则表达式文档第 9.3.6.3 节。14）反向引用指向前面某个带括号的子表达式。因此，带括号的子表达式应当由模式的作者显式指定，这一点很重要。（啊！这是我们听过的最糟糕的主意之一——将迭代所必需的分组，与供以后引用的命名混为一谈！）Another problem is that BREs may involve back-references. (See section 9.3.6.3 of the POSIX regular expression documentation.14) A back-reference refers to a preceding parenthesized subexpression. So it is important that the parenthesized subexpressions be ones explicitly placed by the author of the pattern. (Aargh! This is one of the worst ideas we have ever heard of—grouping, which is necessary for iteration, was confused with naming for later reference!)

任务：修改我们的程序，尽可能消除不必要的嵌套。注意：这里有一些微妙情形，必须留心。举出一个这样的情形。演示你改进后的程序版本，并展示它如何处理这些微妙之处。To do: Edit our program to eliminate as much of the unnecessary nesting as you can. Caution: There are subtle cases here that you have to watch out for. What is such a case? Demonstrate your better version of our program and show how it handles the subtleties.

提示：我们的程序既用字符串作为中间表示，也用它作为结果。你可以考虑采用另一种中间表示。Hint: Our program uses strings as its intermediate representation as well as its result. You might consider using a different intermediate representation.

练习 2.9：反向引用Exercise 2.9: Back-references

添加一个构造反向引用的过程。（见练习 2.8。）尽情享受被 BRE 搞糊涂的乐趣吧。Add a procedure for constructing back-references. (See exercise 2.8.) Have fun getting confused about BREs.

练习 2.10：标准？Exercise 2.10: Standards?

标准最妙的地方在于，有那么多种可供选择。The best thing about standards is that there are so many to choose from.

Andrew S. TannenbaumAndrew S. Tannenbaum

除了基本正则表达式（BRE），POSIX 正则表达式文档 [96] 还定义了扩展正则表达式（ERE）。一些软件（如 egrep）使用这个版本的正则表达式。不幸的是，ERE 并不是 BRE 的保守扩展：ERE 语法实际上与 BRE 语法不一致！扩展我们的 Scheme 模式语言，使翻译目标既可以是 BRE，也可以是 ERE，会是一个有趣的项目。In addition to Basic Regular Expressions (BREs), there are Extended Regular Expressions (EREs) defined in the POSIX regular expression documentation [96]. Some software, such as egrep, uses this version of regular expressions. Unfortunately EREs are not a conservative extension of BREs: ERE syntax is actually inconsistent with BRE syntax! It is an interesting project to extend our Scheme pattern language so that the target can be either BREs or EREs.

  1. a. BRE 和 ERE 之间有哪些重要差异，使这件事变得棘手？列出必须处理的差异。a. What are the significant differences between BREs and EREs that make this a pain? List the differences that must be addressed.
  2. b. 如何分解我们的翻译器，使这门语言能够根据需要翻译成任一种正则表达式？如何保持一个独立于目标正则表达式语言的抽象层？说明你的策略。b. How can our translator be factored so that our language can translate into either kind of regular expression, depending on what is needed? How can we maintain the abstract layer that is independent of the target regular expression language? Explain your strategy.
  3. c. 实现你在 b 部分设计的策略。通过演示来验证你的成果：确保既能运行 egrep，也能运行 grep，并在检验 a 部分所发现差异的各种情况下得到等价的结果。c. Implement the strategy you devised in part b. Demonstrate your work by making sure that you can run egrep as well as grep, with equivalent results in cases that test the differences you found in part a.

2.3 包装器2.3 Wrappers

有时，只需包装现有程序而不必重写，就可以将其改作他用。考虑这样一个问题：在保持压强不变的情况下，计算一团球形气体的半径如何随温度变化。理想气体定律为：Sometimes we can repurpose an existing program by wrapping it rather than rewriting it. Consider the problem of computing how the radius of a sphere of gas varies with the temperature, keeping the pressure constant. The ideal gas law is

其中，P 是压强，V 是体积，n 是气体的物质的量，R 是气体常量，T 是温度。因此，体积可用以下方式计算：where P is the pressure, V is the volume, n is the amount of the gas, R is the gas constant, and T is the temperature. So the volume is computed by

(define (gas-law-volume pressure temperature amount)

  (/ (* amount gas-constant temperature) pressure))



(define gas-constant 8.3144621)         ;J/(K*mol)

而球的半径可用以下方式计算：and the radius of a sphere is computed by

(define (sphere-radius volume)

  (expt (/ volume (* 4/3 pi)) 1/3))



(define pi (* 4 (atan 1 1)))

（注意：4/3 和 1/3 是有理数常量——斜杠不是中缀除法运算符。）所选用的气体常量使这个程序采用 SI 单位，因此压强以牛顿每平方米计，温度以开尔文计，物质的量以摩尔计，体积以立方米计，半径以米计。(Note: 4/3 and 1/3 are rational constants—the slash is not an infix division operator.) The choice of gas constant makes this program use SI units, so the pressure is in newtons per square meter, the temperature is in kelvins, the amount is in moles, the volume is in cubic meters, and the radius is in meters.

这看起来很直接，但使用其他单位就可能让事情变得复杂。假设我们想用华氏度测量温度，用磅每平方英寸测量压强，用英寸测量半径。确定正确公式比算出数值答案更复杂。可以修改这个简单公式，把单位考虑进去，但这样会掩盖程序的思想，并让它专门针对这个特定问题。另一种做法是，以模块化的方式进行单位换算。This looks straightforward, but use of other units can make things complicated. Suppose we want to measure the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, the pressure in pounds per square inch, and the radius in inches. Determining the correct formula is more complicated than computing the numerical answer. We could modify the simple formula to account for the units, but this obscures the idea of the program and specializes it to the particular problem. Alternatively, we could arrange to have a modular way to convert the units.

一个单位换算是与其逆过程相关联的过程。我们可以编写常规温标（如华氏和摄氏温标）之间的温度换算，也可以编写 SI 单位与常规单位之间的换算。A unit conversion is a procedure that is linked to its inverse. We can write temperature conversions between conventional units, such as Fahrenheit and Celsius temperatures, and between SI and conventional units.

(define fahrenheit-to-celsius

  (make-unit-conversion (lambda (f) (* 5/9 (- f 32)))

                        (lambda (c) (+ (* c 9/5) 32))))



(define celsius-to-kelvin

  (let ((zero-celsius 273.15)) ;kelvins

    (make-unit-conversion (lambda (c) (+ c zero-celsius))

                          (lambda (k) (- k zero-celsius)))))

可以用 unit:invert 访问逆过程。例如：We can access the inverse procedure using unit:invert. For example,

(fahrenheit-to-celsius -40)

-40

(fahrenheit-to-celsius 32)

0

((unit:invert fahrenheit-to-celsius) 20)

68

我们可以复合单位换算：We can compose unit conversions:

((compose celsius-to-kelvin fahrenheit-to-celsius) 80)

299.81666666666666

也可以定义复合单位的换算。例如，压强可以用磅每平方英寸或牛顿每平方米来表示。15And we can define compound unit conversions. For example, pressure can be expressed in in pounds per square inch or newtons per square meter.15

(define psi-to-nsm

  (compose pound-to-newton

           (unit:invert inch-to-meter)

           (unit:invert inch-to-meter)))

现在，我们就能以英寸为单位，计算 1 摩尔理想气体在 68◦F、14.7 psi 条件下占据的球体的半径。So now we can compute, in inches, the radius of a sphere occupied by 1 mole of an ideal gas at 68◦F and 14.7 psi.

((unit:invert inch-to-meter)

 (sphere-radius

  (gas-law-volume

   (psi-to-nsm 14.7)

   ((compose celsius-to-kelvin fahrenheit-to-celsius) 68)

   1)))

7.049624635839811

真是一团糟！这种单位换算实现虽然编写起来简单，却难读又难用。另一方面，它很好地分离了几个关注点：气体定律的物理内容与球体的几何性质以及测量单位彼此分离。物理描述和几何描述都没有杂乱内容，各自很容易阅读。This is a mess! This implementation of unit conversions, while simple to program, is hard to read and hard to use. On the other hand, it nicely separates several concerns. The physics of the gas law is separated from the geometry of the sphere and the units of measurement. The physical and geometric descriptions are uncluttered and each is easy to read.

我们可以做得更好。可以构建一个小型领域专用语言，其领域就是单位。这将简化构造新换算器的工作，并使所得换算器更易读。We can do better. We can build a small domain-specific language, where the domain is units. This will simplify the job of constructing new converters, and make the resulting converters more readable.

2.3.1 专门化包装器2.3.1 Specialization wrappers

一种做法是构造一个通用的包装器家族，接受像 gas-law-volume 这样的过程，再通过对其输出和输入进行单位换算，生成该过程的专门化版本。虽然我们将展示如何用它进行单位换算，但代码足够通用，能够为任意数据变换构建包装器。One way to proceed is to make a general family of wrappers that can take a procedure like gas-law-volume and produce a version of that procedure specialized by unit conversions for its output and inputs. Although we will show how to do this for unit conversions, the code will be general enough to build wrappers for arbitrary transformations of data.

针对当前问题，可以为 gas-law-volume 过程构造一个专门化器，让它知道该过程的原生单位（SI）。这个专门化器用一种简单语言来定义，该语言会被编译成基本单位换算的适当组合。这有些像组合子系统，不同之处在于组合子由编译器根据高层规格生成。我们将在第 4 章再次看到这一技术，用它将模式编译成模式匹配过程的组合。For the problem at hand we can construct a specializer for the gas-law-volume procedure that knows its native units (SI). The specializer is defined by a simple language that is compiled into the appropriate combinations of primitive unit conversions. This is somewhat like a combinator system except that the combinators are generated by the compiler according to a high-level specification. We will see this technique again in chapter 4, where we use it to compile combinations of pattern-matching procedures from patterns.

(define make-specialized-gas-law-volume

  (unit-specializer

    gas-law-volume

    ’(expt meter 3)                    ; output (volume)

    ’(/ newton (expt meter 2))         ; pressure

    ’kelvin                            ; temperature

    'mole))                            ; amount

要制作一个使用其他单位的 gas-law-volume 过程版本，只需提供想使用的单位：To make a version of the gas-law-volume procedure that uses other units we supply the units that we want to use:

(define conventional-gas-law-volume

  (make-specialized-gas-law-volume

    ’(expt inch 3)                     ; output (volume)

    ’(/ pound (expt inch 2))           ; pressure

    ’fahrenheit                        ; temperature

    ’mole))                            ; amount

然后便可用这个过程得到以立方英寸表示的体积，进而得到以英寸表示的半径。This procedure can then be used to produce the volume in cubic inches, and therefore we can get the radius in inches.

(sphere-radius (conventional-gas-law-volume 14.7 68 1))

7.04962463583981

2.3.2 实现专门化器2.3.2 Implementing specializers

怎样使它运转起来呢？这分成两部分：过程 unit-specializer，为给定过程包装所需的单位换算；以及一种将给定单位表达式翻译成适当单位换算的方法。第一部分如下：How can we make this work? There are two parts: a procedure unit-specializer that wraps a given procedure with the necessary unit conversions, and a means of translating the given unit expressions into the appropriate unit conversion. The first part is

(define (unit-specializer procedure implicit-output-unit

                          . implicit-input-units)

  (define (specializer specific-output-unit

                       . specific-input-units)

    (let ((output-converter

           (make-converter implicit-output-unit

                           specific-output-unit))

          (input-converters

           (map make-converter

                specific-input-units

                implicit-input-units)))

      (define (specialized-procedure . arguments)

        (output-converter

         (apply procedure

                (map (lambda (converter argument)

                       (converter argument))

                     input-converters

                     arguments))))

      specialized-procedure))

  specializer)

过程 unit-specializer 接受一个待专门化的过程及其隐含的原生单位，返回一个专门化器；后者接受指定的单位，并创建给定过程的专门化版本。唯一需要小心的地方，是确保将单位表达式按正确的顺序传给 make-converter。The procedure unit-specializer takes a procedure to be specialized and its implicit native units, and returns a specializer that takes specific units and creates a specialized version of the given procedure. The only tricky part is making sure that unit expressions are passed to make-converter in the correct order.

解法的第二部分是 make-converter，它接受两个单位表达式，返回一个换算器过程，将以第一个单位表示的数据换算成第二个单位。针对这个问题，我们将制作一个非常笨的 make-converter 版本：把单位表达式视为可用 equal? 比较的字面常量。经过这一简化，make-converter 可以通过查表找到适当的换算器；这意味着必须显式提供每一种所需换算，而不是从基本单位换算中推导它们。下面是创建这张表的示例：The second part of the solution is make-converter, which takes two unit expressions, and returns a converter procedure that converts data in the first unit to the second unit. For this problem, we will make a version of make-converter that's really dumb: it treats the unit expressions as literal constants that can be compared with equal?. With that simplification, make-converter can use a table lookup to find the appropriate converter, which means we have to explicitly provide every necessary conversion rather than deriving them from primitive unit conversions. Here's an example of how the table is created:

(register-unit-conversion ’fahrenheit ’celsius

                          fahrenheit-to-celsius)



(register-unit-conversion ’celsius ’kelvin

                          celsius-to-kelvin)

这就注册了前面定义的换算。注册以后，便可以通过传给 make-converter 的实参顺序，查找任一方向的换算。This registers the conversions we defined earlier. Once these conversions are registered, we can look up either conversion direction by the order of arguments passed to make-converter.

不过，我们需要的不是这两种换算中的任何一种，而是从 fahrenheit 到 kelvin 的换算。由于我们不想从现有定义中推导这一换算——那是一种有趣但复杂得多的实现——因此必须用现有换算来构造复合换算。为方便做到这一点，我们将引入如下的单位换算“代数”：However, what we need isn't either of these conversions, but instead the conversion from fahrenheit to kelvin. Since we don't want to infer this from the existing definitions—an interesting but much more complex implementation—we will have to build compound conversions from the existing ones. To make that easy, we will introduce an “algebra” of unit conversions, as follows:

(define (unit:* u1 u2)

  (make-unit-conversion (compose u2 u1)

                        (compose (unit:invert u1)

                                 (unit:invert u2))))

过程 unit:* 与 unit:invert 结合，便提供了组合单位换算的通用能力。为方便起见，我们再添加以下操作，它们很容易从 unit:* 和 unit:invert 推导出来：The procedure unit:*, combined with unit:invert, provides us with a general ability to combine unit conversions. For convenience, we will add the following, which are easily derived from unit:* and unit:invert:

(unit:/ u1 u2)

(unit:expt u n)

有了这套代数，就可以写出所需的换算：With this algebra, we can write the conversions we want:

(register-unit-conversion ’fahrenheit ’kelvin

    (unit:* fahrenheit-to-celsius celsius-to-kelvin))



(register-unit-conversion ’(/ pound (expt inch 2))

                          ’(/ newton (expt meter 2))

    (unit:/ pound-to-newton

            (unit:expt inch-to-meter 2)))



(register-unit-conversion ’(expt inch 3) ’(expt meter 3)

    (unit:expt inch-to-meter 3))

2.3.2 适配器2.3.2 Adapters

这里展示的是一种可能的技术：扩大现有程序的适用范围，却不改变原始程序。所得的“适配器”机制本身也是可扩展的，还可用来推广许多其他种类的程序。What we have shown here is one possible technique for taking an existing program and broadening its applicability without changing the original program. The resulting “adapter” mechanism is itself extensible and can be used to generalize many other kinds of programs.

这是一条重要原则：与其重写程序来适应新用途，不如从一个简单、通用的基础程序开始，用包装将其专门化，以适合特定用途。程序完全不知道包装器的存在，而包装器对底层程序所作的假设也很少。unit-specializer 过程对两者所知都甚少。正因为这些部分的耦合如此松散，才可以各自推广，用于许多用途，包括我们在这里未曾想到的用途。这是一种分层策略，我们将在第 6 章进一步阐述。This is an important principle: rather than rewriting a program to adapt it to a new purpose, it's preferable to start with a simple and general base program and wrap it to specialize it for a particular purpose. The program doesn't know anything about the wrappers, and the wrappers make few assumptions about the underlying program. And the unit-specializer procedure knows very little about either. Because these parts are so loosely coupled, they can each be generalized for many purposes, including those we aren't thinking about here. This is a kind of layering strategy, which we will expand upon in chapter 6.

练习 2.11：实现单位换算Exercise 2.11: Implementing unit conversions

这里请你补全让这个系统正常运作所需的细节。Here we ask you to fill in the details that make this system work.

  1. a. 作为热身，编写过程 register-unit-conversion 和 make-converter。a. As a warmup, write the procedures register-unit-conversion, and make-converter.
  2. b. 编写过程 unit:/ 和 unit:expt。b. Write the procedures unit:/ and unit:expt.
  3. c. 充实一个将常规单位换算成 SI 单位的程序库。这需要质量和长度的换算。（两种单位制中的时间都以秒计。不过，你也许会对分、时、日、周、年等感兴趣。不要为了做到无所不包而陷入困境。）c. Fill out a library of conversions for conventional units to SI units. This requires conversions for mass and length. (Time is in seconds in both systems. However, you may be interested in minutes, hours, days, weeks, years, etc. Don't get stuck trying to make this universal.)
  4. d. 制作一些有用的复合单位换算，如速度和加速度的换算。d. Make some useful compounds, like velocity and acceleration.
  5. e. 作为一个实际项目，扩展这个专门化器系统，为其他某个程序处理另一种与单位无关的数据转换。e. For a real project, extend this specializer system for some other data conversion of some other program, having nothing to do with units.
  6. f. 另一项大的扩展是构建 make-converter，让它可以根据需要，从先前注册的换算中推导出复合换算。这将需要图搜索。f. Another big extension is to build make-converter so that it can derive compound conversions, as required, from previously registered conversions. This will require a graph search.

2.4 抽象一个领域2.4 Abstracting a domain

来看看如何创建一个领域专用语言层，作为棋盘游戏软件的基础。棋盘游戏有许多共同特征；每种游戏都将其中一些特征组合起来。可以用描述棋盘游戏的抽象概念，例如棋子、可能的位置，以及移动和吃子等基本行为，构建一个领域模型，捕捉某一类棋盘游戏的共同结构。Let's look at how a domain-specific language layer can be created as a basis for software about board games. There are many common features of board games; each game combines some of those features. A domain model can be built that captures the common structure of a class of board games, in terms of the abstract concepts that describe board games, such as pieces, potential locations, and primitive behaviors such as moving and capturing.

某个具体棋盘游戏的程序，可以完全用领域模型来构建。如果领域模型足够通用，它便能支持未来的变化，而无须改变模型本身。A particular board game program may be constructed entirely in terms of the domain model. If the domain model is sufficiently general, it will support future variation without change to the model itself.

考虑国际象棋和西洋跳棋这样的棋盘游戏。二者都是在矩形网格棋盘上进行的双人游戏。双方的棋子排列在棋盘上。棋盘上任何位置都不会有多于一枚棋子。双方交替走棋。每一着中，玩家选择一枚棋子，将它移到棋盘上的另一个位置。有时会吃掉对方的棋子。这是对某类棋盘游戏领域模型的非正式描述。Let's consider board games such as chess and checkers. They are both two-person games played on a board that is a rectangular grid. The players have pieces that are arrayed on the board. There is never more than one piece at any position on the board. The players alternate moves. On each move a player chooses a piece and moves it to some other location on the board. Sometimes an opponent's piece is captured. This is an informal description of a domain model for a class of board games.

我们将基于这种领域模型，构造一个西洋跳棋裁判程序，计算在给定局面下某一方所有的合法走法。领域模型的实现相当复杂，要提供棋子、坐标和棋盘的实现。为简化讲解，我们仅限于裁判程序所需要的内容。Based on this kind of domain model we will construct a referee for checkers that will compute all legal moves for a player at a given state of play. The domain model's implementation is fairly complex, providing implementations of pieces, coordinates, and the board. In order to simplify our presentation we will restrict ourselves to just what is needed by the referee.

裁判程序的大体组织方式是：分别生成每枚棋子的全部合法走法，再将它们汇总。为此，最好有一种抽象来记录移动棋子带来的影响。例如，一种影响可能改变棋子的位置，另一种可能改变它的类型（如西洋跳棋中的“升王”），还有一种可能吃掉对方的棋子。每种合法走法都由一系列这类变化构成，它们依次作用于这一着的初始状态。The general organization of the referee is that it will generate all the legal moves for each piece separately and then aggregate them. In order to do this, it's helpful to have an abstraction that keeps track of the effects of moving a piece. For example, one effect might change a piece's position, another might change its type (e.g., “kinging” in checkers), and yet another might capture an opponent's piece. Each legal move consists of a sequence of such changes applied to the initial state of the move.

好的程序必须反复编写多次。我们展示的程序也是如此。初稿可能还不能清晰地分离各个关注点，但通过编写初稿，程序员能了解问题的结构。我们将展示两种不同的实现，揭示当我们发现初稿中的不足时，程序如何随之演进。A good program must be written many times. This is true of the programs we show. The first draft may not clearly separate out the concerns, but by making that draft the programmer learns the structure of the problem. We will show two different implementations, which will reveal the evolution of the program as we identify shortcomings in our draft.

2.4.1 单体式实现2.4.1 A monolithic implementation

先从一个简单版本的裁判程序开始，人们可能会先写出这样的版本，以理解究竟需要做些什么。Let's start with a simple version of the referee that one might write to understand what really has to be done.

一个西洋跳棋领域模型A checkers domain model

第一种实现将基于一个专用于西洋跳棋、相当简单的领域模型。在后面的实现中，我们会将西洋跳棋专有的部分抽象出去，并隐藏领域模型的许多细节。最终的领域模型将支持其他类似的棋盘游戏，甚至可能支持其他领域。The first implementation will be built on a domain model that is specific to checkers and fairly simple. In the later implementation we will abstract away the checkers-specific parts and hide many of the details of the domain model. The final domain model will support other similar board games, and perhaps other domains.

我们将使用的领域模型有三种抽象类型。棋盘记录尚在场上的棋子，以及下一步走棋方（当前玩家）的颜色。可以查询某个位置上是否有棋子，以及是哪枚棋子。棋子具有颜色、位置，以及是否为王的信息。位置由相对于当前走棋方的坐标指定。下面是对棋盘的操作：The domain model we will use has three abstract types. A board tracks the live pieces and the color of the player to move next (the current player). It can be asked what piece, if any, is in a particular position. A piece has a color, a position, and whether it is a king. A position is specified by coordinates that are relative to the player to move. Here are the operations on boards:

(current-pieces board)(current-pieces board)

获取一个列表，其中包含属于当前玩家的棋子。gets a list of the pieces belonging to the current player.

(is-position-on-board? coords board)(is-position-on-board? coords board)

检查给定的 coords 是否指定了 board 上的一个位置。不满足这个谓词的坐标，在用于其他操作时会引发错误。tests whether the given coords specify a position on board. Coordinates that do not satisfy this predicate will cause errors when used with other operations.

(board-get coords board)(board-get coords board)

获取 coords 所指定位置上的棋子。如果该位置没有棋子，就返回 #f。gets the piece that is at the position specified by coords. If there is no piece in that position it returns #f.

(position-info coords board)(position-info coords board)

描述 board 中位置 coords 的占用情况。如果该位置为空，值为 unoccupied；如果放着当前玩家的一枚棋子，值为 occupied-by-self；如果放着对手的一枚棋子，值为 occupied-by-opponent。describes what occupies the position coords in board. If the position is empty the value is unoccupied; if it contains one of the current player's pieces the value is occupied-by-self; if it contains an opponent's piece the value is occupied-by-opponent.

(is-position-unoccupied? coords board)(is-position-unoccupied? coords board)

等价于 position-info 返回 unoccupied。is equivalent to position-info returning unoccupied.

(is-position-occupied-by-self? coords board)(is-position-occupied-by-self? coords board)

等价于 position-info 返回 occupied-by-self。is equivalent to position-info returning occupied-by-self.

(is-position-occupied-by-opponent? coords board)(is-position-occupied-by-opponent? coords board)

等价于 position-info 返回 occupied-by-opponent。is equivalent to position-info returning occupied-by-opponent.

对棋子的操作同样只有很少几种：There is a similarly small set of operations on pieces:

(piece-coords piece)(piece-coords piece)

获取 piece 的坐标。gets the coordinates of piece.

(should-be-crowned? piece)(should-be-crowned? piece)

检查 piece 是否应当升王——具体来说，它是否尚未成为王，且位于对手的底线。tests whether piece should be crowned—specifically, if it is not already a king and is on the opponent's home row.

(crown-piece piece)(crown-piece piece)

获取一枚与 piece 相同的新棋子，唯一的区别是它已成为王。gets a new piece identical to piece except that it is a king.

(possible-directions piece)(possible-directions piece)

获取一个方向列表，列出 piece 走棋时可以考虑的方向。这并不考虑向该方向移动是否被允许。gets a list of directions that piece may consider for a move. This does not take into account whether moving in that direction is permissible.

坐标系很简单：行和列都是整数。当我们提到坐标或 coords 时，指的是棋盘上的绝对坐标。我们用偏移量一词表示相对坐标。可以将偏移量加到某个坐标上，得到新的坐标；反过来，也可以将两个坐标相减，得到一个偏移量。方向是行、列分量取值为 0、1 或 −1 的偏移量。对于西洋跳棋，可能的方向是向前的两条对角线，行分量为 1，列分量为 −1 或 1。一枚棋子升为王后，还可以沿行分量为 −1 的向后对角线移动。在国际象棋中，不同棋子的可能走法还会使用其他方向，而马的走法需要更复杂的定义。我们不会定义操作坐标的过程；它们的含义应该不言自明。The coordinate system is simple: just row and column integers. When we refer to coordinates or coords, we mean absolute coordinates on the board. We use the term offset for relative coordinates. An offset can be added to some coordinates to produce new coordinates, or inversely two coordinates can be subtracted to produce an offset. A direction is an offset in which the row and column are 0, 1, or −1; For checkers, the possible directions are the two forward diagonals, with the row 1 and the column either −1 or 1. Once a piece becomes a king, it can additionally use the backward diagonals, with row −1. In chess, the possible moves use additional directions, depending on the piece, while a knight move needs a more complex definition. We won't define the procedures for manipulating coordinates; they should be self-explanatory.

一个西洋跳棋裁判程序A checkers referee

我们需要一种数据结构来表示每一着。由于某一着可能需要多次改变棋子的位置，我们将使用一个步骤对象列表；每个步骤对象都指定该步之前的棋子、该步之后的棋子、该步之后的棋盘，以及这一步是否为跳跃。我们将这样的列表称为路径，它按从最新步骤到最早步骤的顺序排列。当一着可以有多种续走方式时，这种排序有利于共享可能出现的公共子路径。We need a data structure to represent each move. Since any given move may require changing a piece's position multiple times, we will use a list of step objects, each of which specifies the piece prior to the step, the piece after the step, the board after the step, and whether the step is a jump. Such a list, which we will call a path, is ordered from newest step to oldest. This ordering facilitates sharing of common subpaths that may occur when a move can be continued in multiple ways.

(step-to step)(step-to step)

获取执行 step 之后的棋子。gets the piece after step is taken.

(step-board step)(step-board step)

获取执行 step 之后的棋盘。gets the board after step is taken.

(make-simple-move new-coords piece board)(make-simple-move new-coords piece board)

获取一个步骤，将 board 上的 piece 移到 new-coords。gets a step that moves piece to new-coords on board.

(make-jump new-coords jumped-coords piece board)(make-jump new-coords jumped-coords piece board)

获取一个步骤，将 board 上的 piece 移到 new-coords，并移除 jumped-coords 处的对方棋子。gets a step that moves piece to new-coords on board and removes the opponent's piece at jumped-coords.

(replace-piece new-piece old-piece board)(replace-piece new-piece old-piece board)

获取一个步骤，将 board 上的 old-piece 替换为 new-piece。gets a step that replaces old-piece with new-piece on board.

(path-contains-jumps? path)(path-contains-jumps? path)

检查 path 中是否有任何步骤是跳跃。tests whether any of the steps in path are jumps.

现在来构建裁判程序。我们先描述从给定起点沿给定方向，可能采取哪些单步行动。过程 try-step 找出一个可能的下一步，并扩展给定路径。如果没有这样的步骤，就返回 #f。Let's build our referee. We will start by describing what simple steps are possible from a given starting point in a given direction. The try-step procedure identifies a potential next step, augmenting the given path. If there is no such step, it returns #f.

(define (try-step piece board direction path)

  (let ((new-coords

         (coords+ (piece-coords piece) direction)))

    (and (is-position-on-board? new-coords board)

         (case (position-info new-coords board)

           ((unoccupied)

            (and (not (path-contains-jumps? path))

                 (cons (make-simple-move new-coords

                                         piece

                                         board)

                       path)))

           ((occupied-by-opponent)

            (let ((landing (coords+ new-coords direction)))

             (and (is-position-on-board? landing board)

                  (is-position-unoccupied? landing board)

                  (cons (make-jump landing

                                   new-coords 

                                   piece

                                   board)

                        path))))

          ((occupied-by-self) #f)

          (else (error "Unknown position info"))))))

这个过程检查沿给定方向前进一步的位置；如果没有棋子占据，就可以移到那里。（我们显式检查这是否接在一次跳跃之后，因为西洋跳棋不允许这样续走。）如果该位置被己方棋子占据，就无法移动。但如果该位置被对方棋子占据，而同一方向再下一个位置没有棋子占据，就可以跳过对方棋子并将其吃掉。The procedure looks at the position one step along the given direction; if it's unoccupied, then it's possible to move there. (We explicitly test whether this is a continuation of a jump, as that is not allowed in checkers.) If the position is occupied by one of the player's pieces, no move is possible. But if the position is occupied by an opponent's piece, and the next position in that direction is unoccupied, then we can jump over the opponent's piece and capture it.

必须尝试该棋子的每个可能方向。过程 compute-next-steps 通过在现有路径上增加一步，返回一个由可能的后续路径组成的列表。We must try each possible direction for the piece. The procedure compute-next-steps returns a list of possible next paths by augmenting an existing path by one step.

(define (compute-next-steps piece board path)

  ;; filter-map drops false values

  (filter-map (lambda (direction)

                (try-step piece board direction path))

              (possible-directions piece)))

西洋跳棋规则规定，只要存在一种或多种跳跃走法，就必须选择跳跃：The rules of checkers mandate choosing a jump when one or more is possible:

(define (evolve-paths piece board)

  (let ((paths (compute-next-steps piece board ’())))

    (let ((jumps (filter path-contains-jumps? paths)))

      (if (null? jumps)

          paths

          (evolve-jumps jumps)))))

而且，首次跳跃之后，还必须检查是否可以继续跳跃：And after an initial jump, we must test for other possible jumps:

(define (evolve-jumps paths)

  (append-map (lambda (path)

                (let ((paths

                       (let ((step (car path)))

                         (compute-next-steps (step-to step)

                                             (step-board step)

                                             path))))

                  (if (null? paths)

                      (list path)

                      ;; continue jumping if possible

                      (evolve-jumps paths))))

              paths))

这就是为单枚棋子生成走法的逻辑。裁判程序必须对每枚棋子都这样处理，并汇总结果：That is the logic for generating the moves for a single piece. The referee must do this for every piece and aggregate the results:

(define (generate-moves board)

  (crown-kings

    (mandate-jumps

      (append-map (lambda (piece)

                    (evolve-paths piece board))

                  (current-pieces board)))))

除了生成走法，这个过程还做了两件事。首先，汇总的走法中可能有些棋子可以跳跃，有些只能普通移动，这时只有跳跃才是合法走法。This procedure does two things in addition to generating the moves. First, the aggregated moves may contain jumps for some pieces and ordinary moves for others, in which case only the jumps are legal moves.

(define (mandate-jumps paths)

  (let ((jumps (filter path-contains-jumps? paths)))

    (if (null? jumps)

        paths

        jumps)))

其次，如果有棋子到达了对手的底线，就必须将它升为王。Second, if any piece reaches the opponent's home row, it must be made a king.

(define (crown-kings paths)

  (map (lambda (path)

         (let ((piece (step-to (car path))))

           (if (should-be-crowned? piece)

               (cons (replace-piece (crown-piece piece)

                                    piece

                                    (step-board (car path)))

                     path)

               path)))

       paths))

评析Critique

这段代码相当不错；它出奇地紧凑，而且是用领域模型来编写的。然而，西洋跳棋的规则分散在整个代码中。能否跳跃是在过程 try-step 中判定的，但允许连续跳跃这一事实却体现在 evolve-jumps 中。另外，“有跳必跳”的规则被拆分在过程 evolve-paths 和 mandate-jumps 之间。更微妙的问题是，裁判程序的控制结构与规则交织在一起。例如，变化的累积（路径中的各个步骤）内置于控制结构中，连续多次跳跃也是如此。强制跳跃的逻辑之所以出现在两处，就是因为控制结构的分布迫使我们这样做。This code is quite nice; it is surprisingly compact, and it is written in terms of the domain model. However, the rules of checkers are distributed throughout the code. The availability of a jump is discovered in the procedure try-step, but the fact that jumps may chain is in evolve-jumps. Also, the rule that if a jump is available a jump must be taken is split between the procedures evolve-paths and mandate-jumps. A more subtle problem is that the control structure of the referee is interwoven with the rules. For example, the accumulation of changes (steps in the path) is built into the control structure, as is chaining of a multiple jump. The reason why the logic for mandating jumps is in two places is that it is required by the distribution of the control structure.

2.4.2 分离领域2.4.2 Factoring out the domain

让我们尝试改善前一实现中指出的问题。能否将领域模型和控制结构，与西洋跳棋规则分离开来？Let's try to ameliorate the problems noted in the previous implementation. Can we separate the domain model and control structure from the rules of checkers?

一个领域模型A domain model

可以复用单体式实现中的坐标、棋子和棋盘，因为它们基本不变。不过，我们将去掉王和非王棋子这样的专有概念，改用符号类型。这会引入两个新操作：We can reuse the coordinates, pieces, and board from our monolithic implementation, since they are largely unchanged. However, we will eliminate the specific idea of king and non-king pieces, instead using a symbolic type. This introduces two new operations:

(piece-type piece)(piece-type piece)

获取 piece 的类型。gets the type of piece.

(piece-new-type piece type)(piece-new-type piece type)

获取一枚与 piece 相同的新棋子，唯一的区别是它具有给定的类型。gets a new piece identical to piece except that it has the given type.

我们重新定义 should-be-crowned? 和 crown-piece，让它们使用棋子类型，因此它们的行为与之前相同，但不再属于核心领域模型的一部分。We redefine should-be-crowned? and crown-piece to use the piece type, so they behave the same as before, but they are no longer part of the core domain model.

虽然过程 possible-directions 是西洋跳棋专用的，我们仍将在这里使用它，但仅用于定义西洋跳棋规则。它不属于新的领域模型。Although the procedure possible-directions is specific to checkers, we will use it here, but only when defining the rules of checkers. It is not part of the new domain model.

步骤数据结构也是西洋跳棋专用的，因为它指定了一个步骤是否为跳跃。我们将用一种更通用的结构来替代它，称为变化：The step data structure is also specific to checkers, because it specifies whether a step is a jump. We will replace it with a more general structure called a change:

(make-change board piece flags)(make-change board piece flags)

创建一个新的变化对象。实参 flags 是一个符号列表，可以用来指示吃子等状态变化。选择器 get-board、get-piece 和 get-flags 可用于获取变化对象中相应的部分。creates a new change object. The flags argument is a list of symbols that we can use to indicate changes of state such as capture of a piece. The selectors get-board, get-piece, and get-flags can be used to get the corresponding parts of a change.

与棋子类型一样，变化标志提供了一种向领域模型添加游戏特有功能的方法，而不必将这些功能固化在模型中。Like the piece type, the change flags provide a way to add game-specific features to the domain model without baking them in.

我们将用一个更抽象的概念代替路径，称为部分走法。部分走法由初始棋盘和棋子，以及零个或多个变化组成。代码中用标识符 pmove 表示部分走法。We will replace the path idea with a more abstract notion called a partial move. A partial move consists of an initial board and piece, together with zero or more changes. Our code uses the identifier pmove for a partial move.

(initial-pmove board piece)(initial-pmove board piece)

创建一个没有变化、也没有标志的 pmove。creates a pmove with no changes and no flags.

(is-pmove-empty? pmove)(is-pmove-empty? pmove)

检查 pmove 是否为空，也就是说，它是否不含任何变化。tests whether pmove is empty: in other words, if it has no changes.

(is-pmove-finished? pmove)(is-pmove-finished? pmove)

检查 pmove 是否已被标记为完成。tests whether pmove has been flagged as finished.

(current-board pmove)(current-board pmove)

返回 pmove 中最近一次变化所包含的棋盘；如果没有变化，则返回作为实参传给 initial-pmove 的棋盘。returns the board from the most recent change in pmove; if there are no changes, it returns the board passed as an argument to initial-pmove.

(current-piece pmove)(current-piece pmove)

返回 pmove 中最近一次变化所包含的棋子；如果没有变化，则返回作为实参传给 initial-pmove 的棋子。returns the piece from the most recent change in the pmove; if there are no changes, it returns the piece passed as an argument to initial-pmove.

接下来的操作以不同方式扩展 pmove。当我们说“通过 foo 扩展 pmove”时，指的是“添加一个执行 foo 的变化对象来扩展 pmove”。The next operations extend a pmove in different ways. When we say “extends pmove by foo” we mean “extends pmove by adding a change object that does foo.”

(new-piece-position coords pmove)(new-piece-position coords pmove)

通过将其棋子移到 coords 来扩展 pmove。extends pmove by moving its piece to coords.

(update-piece procedure pmove)(update-piece procedure pmove)

通过将其棋子替换为对该棋子调用 procedure 所得的结果，来扩展 pmove。extends pmove by replacing its piece with the result of calling procedure on its piece.

(finish-move pmove)(finish-move pmove)

添加一个变化对象来扩展 pmove，该对象带有指明这一着已经完成的标志。结果始终满足谓词 is-pmove-finished?。extends pmove by adding a change object with a flag that specifies that the move is complete. The result always satisfies the predicate is-pmove-finished?.

在以下一节的实现中：In the implementation of 第 2.4.1 节section 2.4.1，我们将“跳跃”和“吃子”两个词混用。但吃子是更一般的概念：例如，在国际象棋中，吃子是通过占据对方棋子的位置来完成的，而不是跳过它。我们用一个变化标志来编码吃子的动作，并用以下过程管理该标志：, we used the terms jumping and capturing interchangeably. But capturing is a more general idea: for example, in chess, capturing is done by displacing a piece rather than jumping over it. We use a change flag to encode the act of capturing a piece, and the following procedures to manage that flag:

(captures-pieces? pmove)(captures-pieces? pmove)

检查 pmove 是否吃掉了任何棋子。tests whether any pieces are captured by pmove.
