(capture-piece-at coords pmove)(capture-piece-at coords pmove)

通过移除 coords 处的棋子来扩展 pmove。coords 指定的位置必须有一枚对方棋子。该操作还会在新的变化对象中设置一个标志，表明有棋子被吃掉；所得的 pmove 始终满足 captures-pieces?。extends pmove by removing the piece at coords. The position specified by coords must contain an opponent's piece. The operation also sets a flag in the new change object saying that a piece was captured; the resulting pmove always satisfies captures-pieces?.

一个执行器An executive

为了帮助将控制结构与西洋跳棋规则分离，我们构建一个规则执行器，捕捉控制结构，却不包含规则的具体内容。这类游戏中有两种规则。一种称为演进规则，用来扩展一个 pmove，可能返回多个派生的 pmove。另一种称为汇总规则，作用于一个 pmove 集合，剔除其中不允许的走法，或扩展某些走法以纳入变化，例如升王。To help separate the control structure from the rules of checkers we build a rule executive that captures the control structure without incorporating the specific content of the rules. In this kind of game there are two kinds of rule. One kind, which we will call an evolution rule, augments a pmove, possibly returning multiple derived pmoves. The other kind, an aggregate rule, acts on a set of pmoves, eliminating some that are not allowed or extending some to incorporate changes, such as crowning a king.

下面的执行器从若干空 pmove 开始，玩家的每枚棋子对应一个，然后将它们演进为表示完整走法的 pmove 集合。随后，它对这些已完成的 pmove 应用汇总规则，最终返回一个合法走法集合。Here is an executive that starts with some empty pmoves, one for each of the player's pieces, and evolves these into a collection of pmoves that represent finished moves. It then applies the aggregate rules to the collection of finished pmoves, ultimately returning a collection of the legal moves.

演进规则实现为一个过程，将给定的 pmove 转换成一组新的 pmove，其中一些可能已经完成（满足 is-pmove-finished?）。执行器对 pmove 集合递归地应用所有演进规则，直到它们全部完成。An evolution rule is implemented as a procedure that transforms a given pmove into a collection of new pmoves, some of which may be finished (satisfy is-pmove-finished?). The executive recursively applies all of the evolution rules to the collection of pmoves until all of them are finished.

汇总规则实现为一个过程，接受一个已完成的 pmove 集合，并产生一个新集合。每条汇总规则只应用一次，而且汇总规则之间没有顺序约束，因此执行器可以将它们复合成一个过程，作为复合汇总规则。如果没有汇总规则，这个复合过程就直接返回其实参。An aggregate rule is implemented as a procedure that accepts a collection of finished pmoves and produces a new collection. Each aggregate rule is applied once, and there are no ordering constraints between aggregate rules, so the executive can compose them together into a single procedure that is the composite aggregate rule. If there are no aggregate rules, then the composite simply returns its argument.

(define (execute-rules initial-pmoves evolution-rules

                       aggregate-rules)

  ((reduce compose (lambda (x) x) aggregate-rules)

   (append-map (lambda (pmove)

                 (evolve-pmove pmove evolution-rules))

               initial-pmoves)))



(define (evolve-pmove pmove evolution-rules)

  (append-map (lambda (new-pmove)

                (if (is-pmove-finished? new-pmove)

                    (list new-pmove)

                    (evolve-pmove new-pmove evolution-rules)))

             (append-map (lambda (evolution-rule)

                           (evolution-rule pmove))

                         evolution-rules)))

通过过程 define-evolution-rule 注册演进规则，供执行器使用；通过过程 define-aggregate-rule 注册汇总规则。每条规则都有一个名称、它所注册到的游戏，以及实现其行为的过程。An evolution rule is registered for use in the executive by the procedure define-evolution-rule and an aggregate rule is registered by the procedure define-aggregate-rule. Each rule has a name, the game that it is registered in, and a procedure implementing its behavior.

西洋跳棋规则Rules of checkers

下面是一条普通移动规则。它沿可能的方向寻找任何未被占据的相邻位置，并扩展 pmove，将移动到该位置纳入其中。在这样一次移动之后，就不能合法地继续移动了，所以我们将该 pmove 标记为完成。Here is a rule for simple moves. This looks for any unoccupied adjacent position in a possible direction, and extends the pmove to include a move to that position. After such a move, it is not legal to continue moving, so we mark that pmove as finished.

(define-evolution-rule 'simple-move checkers

  (lambda (pmove)

    (if (is-pmove-empty? pmove)

        (get-simple-moves pmove)

        ’())))



(define (get-simple-moves pmove)

  (filter-map

   (lambda (direction)

     (let ((landing (compute-new-position direction 1 pmove))

           (board (current-board pmove)))

       (and (is-position-on-board? landing board)

            (is-position-unoccupied? landing board)

            (finish-move (new-piece-position landing pmove)))))

   (possible-directions (current-piece pmove))))

在 get-simple-moves 中，过程 compute-new-position 根据该次移动的 direction 和 distance，求出可能被移动的棋子的拟定落点。过程 offset* 将一个偏移量与一个数相乘，得到按该数缩放后的新偏移量。In get-simple-moves, the procedure compute-new-position gets the proposed landing site of the piece possibly being moved, given the direction and distance for the move. The procedure offset* multiplies an offset and a number to get a new offset scaled by the number.

(define (compute-new-position direction distance pmove)

  (coords+ (piece-coords (current-piece pmove))

           (offset* direction distance)))

跳吃规则与此类似，只是它必须在给定方向上寻找一个被占据的位置，其后紧接一个空位置。当无法再跳吃时，一个 pmove 就完成了。The rule for jumps is similar, except that it must look for an occupied position followed by an unoccupied position in a given direction. When no jumps are possible, a pmove is finished.

(define-evolution-rule ’jump checkers

  (lambda (pmove)

    (let ((jumps (get-jumps pmove)))

      (cond ((not (null? jumps))

             jumps)

            ((is-pmove-empty? pmove)

             ’()) ; abandon this pmove

            (else

             (list (finish-move pmove)))))))



(define (get-jumps pmove)

  (filter-map

   (lambda (direction)

     (let ((possible-jump

            (compute-new-position direction 1 pmove))

           (landing (compute-new-position direction 2 pmove))

           (board (current-board pmove)))

       (and (is-position-on-board? landing board)

            (is-position-unoccupied? landing board)

            (is-position-occupied-by-opponent? possible-jump

                                               board)

            (capture-piece-at possible-jump

                              (new-piece-position landing

                                                  pmove)))))

   (possible-directions (current-piece pmove))))

升王与其他规则无关：只需查看所有已经完成的走法，把其中位于对方底线上的非王棋子加冕为王即可。Making kings is independent of other rules: just look at all the completed moves and crown any non-king that is on the opponent's home row.

(define-aggregate-rule ’coronation checkers

  (lambda (pmoves)

    (map (lambda (pmove)

           (let ((piece (current-piece pmove)))

             (if (should-be-crowned? piece)

                 (update-piece crown-piece pmove)

                 pmove)))

         pmoves)))

最后，如果有一个或多个跳吃机会就必须跳吃，这条规则在最后处理：检测这种情况，并丢弃所有不跳吃的走法。And finally, the rule mandating that a jump be taken when one or more is available is done at the end by detecting that case and throwing away all the non-jump moves.

(define-aggregate-rule 'require-jumps checkers

  (lambda (pmoves)

    (let ((jumps (filter captures-pieces? pmoves)))

      (if (null? jumps)

          pmoves

          jumps))))

评析Critique

基于规则的裁判实现解决了我们先前指出的问题。它把控制结构从程序中抽离出来，集中到执行器里。因此，各条规则都很明确：每条跳棋规则都由一条过程式规则表达，不再像先前的实现那样分散各处。The rule-based implementation of our referee solves the problems we identified earlier. It removes the control structure from our program and localizes it in the executive. As a consequence, the rules are specific: each checkers rule is expressed by a single procedural rule. The rules are not diffused as they were in the earlier implementation.

不过，这样做也有代价：我们必须为每条规则添加适用条件，防止它应用于不合适的 pmove。16 例如，simple-move 规则必须排除传给它的所有非空 pmove，因为非空 pmove 可能包含一次或多次跳吃，而跳吃之后不能接着进行普通移动。这是基于规则的系统普遍存在的一项缺陷：每条规则都必须能够接受任何规则的输出；通常的处理办法是把控制状态编码到规则所作用的数据中。However, this comes at a cost: we must add applicability conditions to each rule to prevent it being applied to pmoves for which it is inappropriate.16 For example, the simple-move rule must exclude any nonempty pmoves that it is given, because a nonempty pmove might include one or more jumps, which cannot be continued with a simple move. This is a general mis-feature of rule-based systems: every rule must be able to accept the output of any rule; this is normally handled by encoding the control state in the data the rules are applied to.

练习 2.12：一点国际象棋Exercise 2.12: A bit of chess

利用我们为跳棋使用的同一个领域模型，也可以表达国际象棋的规则。除了国际象棋有多种不同棋子之外，还有几个重要区别。一个区别是，车、象和后的移动范围只受阻挡限制。另一个区别是，吃子靠占据对方棋子的位置，而不是跳过它。在本练习中，我们只考虑车和马；其余棋子留到练习 2.13 中讨论。Using the same domain model we used for checkers, it is possible to capture the rules of chess. There are several important differences, besides the fact that chess involves many types of pieces. One difference is that the range of motion of rooks, bishops, and queens is limited only by obstruction. Another difference is that capture is by displacement rather than jump. In this exercise we will consider only rooks and knights; the remaining pieces are addressed in exercise 2.13.

  1. a. 构造一个类似的裁判，生成车的合法走法。不要尝试实现王车易位规则。a. Construct an analogous referee to generate the legal moves for a rook. Don't try to implement the castling rule.
  2. b. 扩充你的裁判，使其能够模拟马的行为。b. Augment your referee to model the behavior of a knight.

练习 2.13：更多国际象棋Exercise 2.13: More chess

完整实现国际象棋的规则。Make a full implementation of the rules of chess.

练习 2.14：一个进阶项目Exercise 2.14: An advanced project

选择另一个并非棋类游戏的领域，使用规则执行器以及你自行设计的领域模型，实现某个过程的规则。这并不容易。Choose some other domain, not a board game, and build an implementation of the rules of some process using the rule executive and a domain model of your design. This is not easy.

2.5 小结2.5 Summary

本章展示并详细阐述的技术，有助于任何大型系统的设计和开发。使用接口定义明确、可以混搭的可互换部件来构建系统，几乎总是有利的。The techniques displayed and elaborated on in this chapter can be helpful in the design and development of every large-scale system. It is almost always to our advantage to build our systems using mix-and-match interchangeable parts with well-defined interfaces.

对于 Scheme 或 Java 这样具有高阶过程和词法作用域的语言，很容易为可互换部件库构造一套组合子，也就是诸如 compose 这样的标准组合手段。构造共享同一接口规范的参数化部件也很方便。例如，如果我们的接口规范要求过程接收一个参数并返回一个值，那么In languages with higher-order procedures and lexical scoping, like Scheme or Java, it is easy to make systems of combinators— standard means of combination, such as compose—for a library of interchangeable parts. And it is convenient to make parametric parts that share a common interface specification. For example, if our interface specification is procedures that take one argument and return one value, then

(define (make-incrementer dx)

  (lambda (x) (+ x dx)))

就定义了一组可互换的递增器。对于 C 这样没有词法作用域高阶过程的语言，构造组合子系统以及可组合部件库就困难得多。不过，只要周密规划并付出一些努力，还是可以做到的。defines a set of interchangeable incrementers. It is much harder to make systems of combinators and libraries of combinable parts with languages like C that do not have lexically scoped higher-order procedures. But with careful planning and some effort it can be done.

当我们遇到一个由难以干净组合的部件构成的系统时，例如正则表达式，往往可以通过元编程来缓解困难。在那个例子里，我们构造了一门新的基于组合子的语言，并将其编译成正则表达式语言，得到了一种用起来舒适但略显冗长的替代方案。对于需要匹配字符串的程序，我们的正则表达式组合子语言是一门很好的领域专用中间语言；但作为供用户键入的脚本语言，它就不那么理想了。为此，我们会希望设计一种清晰而更简洁的字符串匹配语法，并将其编译成基于组合子的中间语言。17When we are confronted with a system based on parts that do not compose cleanly, such as regular expressions, it is often possible to ameliorate the difficulties by metaprogramming. In that case we built a new combinator-based language that we compiled to the regular expression language, making a pleasant but longwinded alternative. Our regular-expressions combinator language is a fine domain-specific intermediate language for programs that need to match strings, but it is not so nice as a scripting language for a user to type. For that purpose we would want to design a clean and more concise syntax for matching strings that can be compiled to a combinator-based intermediate language.17

包装器是让旧代码适用于新环境的一种常见策略。我们展示了如何构造一套自动完成必要单位换算的包装器系统，使假定采用特定单位制的程序也能使用其他单位制。为此，我们构造了一门表达单位换算的小型领域专用语言，并将其编译成相应的包装器。Wrappers are a common strategy for making old code useful in a new context. We showed how programs that assumed a particular unit system could be used with other unit systems, by building a system of wrappers that automatically did the necessary unit conversions. To do this we made a small domain-specific language for expressing unit conversions that compiled into the appropriate wrapper.

但包装器的用途并不限于充当旧代码的适配器。我们可以用包装器包住一个过程，检查输入参数是否合理，并检查对于给定输入，输出是否像是一个合理的结果。如果检查失败，包装器就可以发出错误信号。这种“偏执式编程风格”是一种非常有力的工具，既能保护系统免遭误用，也有助于调试。But wrappers can be used for more than just adapters for old code. We can wrap a procedure with a wrapper that checks input arguments for reasonableness and checks that the output is a plausible result given the inputs. If such checks fail, the wrapper can raise an error signal. This “paranoid programming style” is a very powerful tool for protecting a system from misuse and for debugging.

正则表达式和单位换算的例子说明，解决某一类问题的最佳办法，往往是发明一门能轻松表达其解法的领域专用语言。为了探索这一策略，我们把生成棋类游戏合法走法的问题拆分成三个可以独立扩展的部分：领域模型、控制结构执行器，以及游戏的具体规则。领域模型提供一组基本构件，将它们组合起来就能构成规则，从而为我们提供一门表达规则的语言。控制结构执行器负责安排规则的应用顺序。这样的组合构成了一门领域专用语言的核心，用来表达类似跳棋的棋类游戏规则。As illustrated with regular expressions and with unit conversions, often the best way to attack a class of problems is to invent a domain-specific language in which the solutions are easy to express. To explore this strategy we divided the problem of generating the legal moves for a board game into three individually extensible pieces: a domain model, a control-structure executive, and the specific rules of the game. The domain model provides a set of primitives that are combined to make the rules, giving us a language for expressing the rules. The application of the rules is sequenced by the control-structure executive. This combination forms the essence of a domain-specific language for expressing the rules of checkers-like board games.

每一门好的语言都有基本构件、组合这些基本构件的手段，以及对组合进行抽象的手段。本章展示的例子嵌入在 Scheme 中，因此能够利用 Scheme 强大的组合与抽象手段。但这只是开始。在第 5 章中，我们将运用元语言抽象这一强大思想，超越这种嵌入策略。Every good language has primitives, means of combination of those primitives, and means of abstraction for the combinations. The examples shown in this chapter are embedded in Scheme, and thus are able to use Scheme's powerful means of combination and abstraction. But this is only the start. In chapter 5 we will transcend this embedding strategy, using the powerful idea of metalinguistic abstraction.
