3.3 示例：自动微分3.3 Example: Automatic differentiation

自动微分是可扩展泛型过程的一项非凡应用。14 这是一种优美的方法，可以获得一个程序，用来计算给定程序所计算函数的导数。15 如今，自动微分已经是机器学习应用的重要组成部分。One remarkable application of extensible generic procedures is automatic differentiation.14 This is a beautiful way to obtain a program that computes the derivative of the function computed by a given program.15 Automatic differentiation is now an important component in machine learning applications.

我们将看到，实现自动微分的一种简单方法，是扩展泛型算术基本过程，使其能够处理微分对象这一新的复合数据类型。这将使我们既能对数值函数，也能对符号函数进行自动微分。它还将使自动微分能够用于高阶过程，也就是将其他过程作为值返回的过程。We will see that a simple way to implement automatic differentiation is to extend the generic arithmetic primitives to work with differential objects, a new compound data type. This will enable the automatic differentiation of symbolic as well as numerical functions. It will also enable us to make automatic differentiation work with higher-order procedures—procedures that return other procedures as values.

下面是一个简单的自动微分示例，用来说明我们讨论的内容：Here is a simple example of automatic differentiation to illustrate what we are talking about:

((derivative (lambda (x) (expt x 3))) 2)

12

注意，计算参数立方的函数的导数，是一个新函数；当以 2 为参数调用它时，它返回的值是 12。Note that the derivative of the function that computes the cube of its argument is a new function, which when given 2 as its argument returns 12 as its value.

如果把算术扩展为能够处理符号表达式，并对结果做一些代数化简，就得到：If we extend the arithmetic to handle symbolic expressions, and we do some algebraic simplification on the result, we get:

((derivative (lambda (x) (expt x 3))) ’a)

(* 3 (expt a 2))

而且，编程语言的全部能力都可使用，包括高阶过程。这种系统对于处理有趣的物理问题中出现的巨大表达式很有用。16And the full power of the programming language is available, including higher-order procedures. This kind of system is useful in working with the very large expressions that occur in interesting physics problems.16

让我们看一个简单的应用：用 Newton 法计算方程的根。其思路是寻找满足 f (x) = 0 的 x 值。如果 f 足够光滑，而且我们已有一个足够接近的猜测值 x0，就可以按下式计算新猜测值 x1，从而改进猜测：Let's look at a simple application: the computation of the roots of an equation by Newton's method. The idea is that we want to find values of x for which f (x) = 0. If f is sufficiently smooth, and we have a sufficiently close guess x0, we can improve the guess by computing a new guess x1 by the formula:

必要时，可以反复进行这一过程，以得到足够精确的结果。完成这一任务的一个基本程序如下：This can be repeated, as necessary, to get a sufficiently accurate result. An elementary program to accomplish this is:

(define (root-newton f initial-guess tolerance)

  (let ((Df (derivative f)))

    (define (improve-guess xn)

      (- xn (/ (f xn) (Df xn))))

    (let loop ((xn initial-guess))

      (let ((xn+1 (improve-guess xn)))

        (if (close-enuf? xn xn+1 tolerance)

            xn+1

            (loop xn+1))))))

注意，root-newton 中名为 Df 的局部过程，会计算作为 f 传入的过程所计算函数的导数。Notice that the local procedure named Df in root-newton is a procedure that computes the derivative of the function computed by the procedure passed in as f.

例如，假设我们想知道第一象限中满足 cos(θ) = sin(θ) 的角 θ。（答案是 π/4 ≈ .7853981633974484。）我们可以写：For example, suppose we want to know the angle θ in the first quadrant for which cos(θ) = sin(θ). (The answer is π/4 ≈ .7853981633974484) We can write:

(define (cs theta)

  (- (cos theta) (sin theta)))



(root-newton cs 0.5 1e-8)

.7853981633974484

这一结果达到了机器所能提供的全部精度。This result is correct to full machine accuracy.

3.3.1 自动微分如何工作3.3.1 How automatic differentiation works

自动微分程序直接从导数的定义推导而来。假设给定一个函数 f 及其定义域中的一点 x，我们想知道它在邻近点处的函数值 f (x + Δx)，其中 Δx 是一个小增量。函数 f 的导数定义为函数 Df，它在特定参数 x 处的值可以与参数增量 Δx“相乘”，从而得到 f 的函数值增量的最佳线性近似：The program for automatic differentiation is directly derived from the definition of the derivative. Suppose that given a function f and a point x in its domain, we want to know the value of the function at a nearby point f (x + Δx), where Δx is a small increment. The derivative of a function f is defined to be the function Df whose value for particular arguments x is something that can be “multiplied” by an increment Δx of the argument to get the best possible linear approximation to the increment in the value of f:

我们用一种称为微分对象的数据类型来实现这个定义。微分对象 [x, δx] 可以看作带有一个小增量的数，即 x + δx。但我们将其视为一种类似复数的新数值量：它有两个分量，一个有限部分和一个无穷小部分。17 我们扩展每个基本算术函数，使其能够处理微分对象：每个基本算术函数 f 都必须知道自己的导函数 Df，从而有：We implement this definition using a data type that we call a differential object. A differential object [x, δx] can be thought of as a number with a small increment, x + δx. But we treat it as a new numerical quantity similar to a complex number: it has two components, a finite part and an infinitesimal part.17 We extend each primitive arithmetic function to work with differential objects: each primitive arithmetic function f must know its derivative function Df , so that:

注意，f 在点 x 处的导数 Df (x)，就是所得微分对象的无穷小部分中 δx 的系数。Note that the derivative of f at the point x, Df (x), is the coefficient of δx in the infinitesimal part of the resulting differential object.

现在，强大的思想来了：如果接着把 f ([x, δx]) 的结果（方程 3.5）传入另一个函数 g，我们就会得到所期望的链式法则结果：Now here is the powerful idea: If we then pass the result of f ([x, δx]) (equation 3.5) through another function g, we obtain the chain-rule answer we would hope for:

因此，只要能计算所有基本函数作用于微分对象的结果，就能计算所有函数组合在微分对象上的结果。得到这样的结果后，我们就可以提取组合函数的导数：导数就是所得微分对象中无穷小增量的系数。Thus, if we can compute the results of all primitive functions on differential objects, we can compute the results of all compositions of functions on differential objects. Given such a result, we can extract the derivative of the composition: the derivative is the coefficient of the infinitesimal increment in the resulting differential object.

要扩展泛型算术运算符，使其能够对微分对象进行计算，我们只需提供一个过程，用来计算该运算符所指的基本算术函数的导数。接着，就可以使用普通的 Scheme 组合方式，得到任意基本函数组合的导数。18To extend a generic arithmetic operator to compute with differential objects, we need only supply a procedure that computes the derivative of the primitive arithmetic function that the operator names. Then we can use ordinary Scheme compositions to get the derivative of any composition of primitive functions.18

给定一个实现一元函数 f 的过程，过程 derivative 会生成一个新过程 the-derivative，用于计算 f 所计算函数的导数。19 当把这个导数过程应用于某个参数 x 时，它会创建一个新的无穷小增量 dx，再将其加到参数上，得到表示 x + δx 的新微分对象 [x, δx]。然后，将过程 f 应用于该微分对象，并从所得值中提取无穷小增量 dx 的系数，从而得到 f 的导数：Given a procedure implementing a unary function f, the procedure derivative produces a new procedure the-derivative that computes the derivative of the function computed by f.19 When applied to some argument, x, the derivative creates a new infinitesimal increment dx and adds it to the argument to get the new differential object [x, δx] that represents x + δx. The procedure f is then applied to this differential object and the derivative of f is obtained by extracting the coefficient of the infinitesimal increment dx from the value:

(define (derivative f)

  (define (the-derivative x)

    (let* ((dx (make-new-dx))

           (value (f (d:+ x (make-infinitesimal dx)))))

      (extract-dx-part value dx)))

  the-derivative)

过程 make-infinitesimal 构造一个有限部分为零、无穷小部分为 dx 的微分对象。过程 d:+ 用于将微分对象相加。细节将在The procedure make-infinitesimal makes a differential object whose finite part is zero and whose infinitesimal part is dx. The procedure d:+ adds differential objects. The details will be explained in 第 3.3.3 节中解释。section 3.3.3.

扩展基本过程Extending the primitives

我们需要构造处理过程，扩展基本算术泛型过程，使其能够操作微分对象。对于每个一元过程，我们都要构造结果的有限部分和无穷小部分，并按照方程 3.5 将它们组合起来。因此，对于计算函数 f 的一元基本算术过程，其处理过程由 diff:unary-proc 构造，输入是计算 f 的过程 f，以及计算其导数 Df 的过程 df。我们使用微分对象专用的加法和乘法过程 d:+ 与 d:* 将它们粘合起来，其细节将在后文说明。We need to make handler procedures that extend the primitive arithmetic generic procedures to operate on differential objects. For each unary procedure we have to make the finite part of the result and the infinitesimal part of the result, and we have to put the results together, as expressed in equation 3.5. So the handler for a unary primitive arithmetic procedure that computes function f is constructed by diff:unary-proc from the procedure f for f and the procedure df for its derivative Df. These are glued together using special addition and multiplication procedures d:+ and d:* for differential objects, to be explained in 第 3.3.3 节中解释。section 3.3.3.

(define (diff:unary-proc f df)

  (define (uop x)       ; x is a differential object

      (let ((xf (finite-part x))

            (dx (infinitesimal-part x)))

        (d:+ (f xf) (d:* (df xf) dx))))

  uop)

例如，针对微分对象的 sqrt 过程的处理过程就是：For example, the sqrt procedure handler for differential objects is just:

(define diff:sqrt

  (diff:unary-proc sqrt (lambda (x) (/ 1 (* 2 (sqrt x))))))

diff:unary-proc 的第一个参数是 sqrt 过程，第二个参数是计算 sqrt 的导数的过程。The first argument of diff:unary-proc is the sqrt procedure and the second argument is a procedure that computes the derivative of sqrt.

我们使用下面的方式，将新处理过程加入泛型 sqrt 过程We add the new handler to the generic sqrt procedure using

(assign-handler! sqrt diff:sqrt differential?)

其中，differential? 是一个仅对微分对象为真的谓词。过程 assign-handler! 只是一种有用模式的简写：where differential? is a predicate that is true only of differential objects. The procedure assign-handler! is just shorthand for a useful pattern:

(define (assign-handler! procedure handler . preds)

  (define-generic-procedure-handler procedure

    (apply match-args preds)

    handler))

而过程 match-args 则根据一系列谓词构造适用性规范。And the procedure match-args makes an applicability specification from a sequence of predicates.

其他一元基本过程的处理过程都很直接：20Handlers for other unary primitives are straightforward:20

(define diff:exp (diff:unary-proc exp exp))



(define diff:log (diff:unary-proc log (lambda (x) (/ 1 x))))



(define diff:sin (diff:unary-proc sin cos))



(define diff:cos

        (diff:unary-proc cos (lambda (x) (* -1 (sin x)))))

⋮

二元算术运算稍微复杂一些。Binary arithmetic operations are a bit more complicated.

其中，∂0f 和 ∂1f 是 f 分别对两个参数的偏导函数。设 f 是一个二元函数，那么 ∂0f 就是一个新的二元函数，用于计算 f 对第一个参数的偏导数：where ∂0f and ∂1f are the partial derivative functions of f with respect to the two arguments. Let f be a function of two arguments; then ∂0f is a new function of two arguments that computes the partial derivative of f with respect to its first argument:

因此，二元运算的规则为So the rule for binary operations is

要实现二元运算，我们可能会认为，只需遵循一元运算的方案即可，其中 d0f 和 d1f 是两个偏导函数：To implement binary operations we might think that we could simply follow the plan for unary operations, where d0f and d1f are the two partial derivative functions:

(define (diff:binary-proc f d0f d1f)

  (define (bop x y)

    (let ((dx (infinitesimal-part x))

          (dy (infinitesimal-part y))

          (xf (finite-part x))

          (yf (finite-part y)))

      (d:+ (f xf yf)

           (d:+ (d:* dx (d0f xf yf))

                (d:* (d1f xf yf) dy)))))

  bop)

这是一个不错的方案，但还不完全正确：它无法确保为两个参数选择有限部分和无穷小部分时保持一致。我们需要更谨慎地选择这些部分。我们将在后文解释这一技术细节并加以修正This is a good plan, but it isn't quite right: it doesn't ensure that the finite and infinitesimal parts are consistently chosen for the two arguments. We need to be more careful about how we choose the parts. We will explain this technical detail and fix it in 第 3.3.3 节中解释。section 3.3.3，不过，眼下先使用这段大体正确的代码。, but let's go with this approximately correct code for now.

加法和乘法很直接，因为其偏导数很简单；而除法和幂运算则更有意思。我们只展示 diff:+ 的处理过程指派，因为其他情形都与此类似。Addition and multiplication are straightforward, because the partial derivatives are simple, but division and exponentiation are more interesting. We show the assignment of handlers only for diff:+ because all the others are similar.

(define diff:+

  (diff:binary-proc +

                    (lambda (x y) 1)

                    (lambda (x y) 1)))



(assign-handler! + diff:+ differential? any-object?)

(assign-handler! + diff:+ any-object? differential?)



(define diff:*

  (diff:binary-proc *

                    (lambda (x y) y)

                    (lambda (x y) x)))



(define diff:/

  (diff:binary-proc /

                    (lambda (x y)

                      (/ 1 y))

                    (lambda (x y)

                      (* -1 (/ x (square y))))))

幂运算 f (x, y) = x 的处理过程稍微复杂一些。对第一个参数的偏导数很简单：∂0f (x, y) = yx−1。但对第二个参数的偏导数通常为 ∂1f (x, y) = x log x，下面这些特殊情况除外：The handler for exponentiation f (x, y) = x is a bit more complicated. The partial with respect to the first argument is simple: ∂0f (x, y) = yx−1. But the partial with respect to the second argument is usually ∂1f (x, y) = x log x, except for some special cases:

(define diff:expt

  (diff:binary-proc expt

    (lambda (x y)

      (* y (expt x (- y 1))))

    (lambda (x y)

      (if (and (number? x) (zero? x))

          (if (number? y)

              (if (positive? y)

                  0

                  (error "Derivative undefined: EXPT"

                         x y))

              0)

          (* (log x) (expt x y))))))

提取导数值Extracting the derivative's value

为了计算一个函数的导数值，我们将该函数应用于一个微分对象，得到一个结果。我们必须从这一结果中提取导数值。有几种可能情况需要处理。如果结果是微分对象，就必须从该对象中取出导数值。如果结果不是微分对象，导数值就是零。还有一些情况我们尚未提及。因此，这里需要一个泛型过程，其默认处理过程产生零。To compute the value of the derivative of a function, we apply the function to a differential object and obtain a result. We have to extract the derivative's value from that result. There are several possibilities that must be handled. If the result is a differential object, we have to pull the derivative's value out of the object. If the result is not a differential object, the derivative's value is zero. There are other cases that we have not mentioned. This calls for a generic procedure with a default that produces a zero.

(define (extract-dx-default value dx) 0)



(define extract-dx-part

  (simple-generic-procedure ’extract-dx-part 2

                            extract-dx-default))

如果返回的是微分对象，dx 的系数就是所需的导数。实际情况会稍微复杂一些，但基本思想可以表达如下：In the case where a differential object is returned, the coefficient of dx is the required derivative. This will turn out to be a bit complicated, but the basic idea can be expressed as follows:

(define (extract-dx-differential value dx)

  (extract-dx-coefficient-from (infinitesimal-part value) dx))



(define-generic-procedure-handler extract-dx-part

  (match-args differential? diff-factor?)

  extract-dx-differential)

这还不完全正确，因为出于一些技术原因，微分对象的结构比我们已经展示的更复杂。后文将对此作完整解释。The reason this is not quite right is that for technical reasons the structure of a differential object is more complex than we have already shown. It will be fully explained in 第 3.3.3 节中解释。section 3.3.3.

注意：我们把提取器设计为泛型过程，是为了日后能够扩展到返回函数或复合对象的函数，例如返回向量、矩阵和张量的函数。（见第 124 页的练习 3.12。）Note: We made the extractor generic to enable future extensions to functions that return functions or compound objects, such as vectors, matrices, and tensors. (See exercise 3.12 on page 124.)

除了可能还需纳入更多基本运算符和数据结构之外，实现自动微分真正需要的就只有这些了！处理过程中引用的所有过程，都是通常的泛型算术过程；它们可以包括符号算术和函数算术。Except for the fact that there may be more primitive operators and data structures to be included, this is all that is really needed to implement automatic differentiation! All of the procedures referred to in the handlers are the usual generic procedures on arithmetic; they may include symbolic arithmetic and functional arithmetic.

3.3.2 n 元函数的导数3.3.2 Derivatives of n-ary functions

对于具有多个参数的函数，我们需要能够计算它对每个参数的偏导数。一种做法如下：21For a function with multiple arguments we need to be able to compute the partial derivatives with respect to each argument. One way to do this is:21

(define ((partial i) f)

  (define (the-derivative . args)

    (if (not (< i (length args)))

        (error "Not enough arguments for PARTIAL" i f args))

    (let* ((dx (make-new-dx))

           (value

            (apply f (map (lambda (arg j)

                            (if (= i j)

                                (d:+ arg

                                     (make-infinitesimal dx))

                                arg))

                          args (iota (length args))))))

      (extract-dx-part value dx)))

  the-derivative)

这里，我们把所提供参数中的第 i 个参数增加 dx，再将 f 应用于这些参数，并从所得结果中提取无穷小量 dx 的系数。22Here we are extracting the coefficient of the infinitesimal dx in the result of applying f to the arguments supplied with the ith argument incremented by dx.22

现在考虑一个二元函数 g。展开方程 3.6，我们发现导数 Dg 与一个由各参数增量组成的向量相乘：Now consider a function g of two arguments. Expanding on equation 3.6 we find that the derivative Dg is multiplied by a vector of increments to the arguments:

g 在点 x, y 处的导数 Dg，是方括号中的那一对偏导数。这个由偏导数组成的协向量与增量向量的内积，就是函数 g 的增量。general-derivative 过程计算的正是这个结果：The derivative Dg of g at the point x, y is the pair of partial derivatives in square brackets. The inner product of that covector of partials with the vector of increments is the increment to the function g. The general-derivative procedure computes this result:

(define (general-derivative g)

  (define ((the-derivative . args) . increments)

    (let ((n (length args)))

      (assert (= n (length increments)))

      (if (= n 1)

          (* ((derivative g) (car args))

             (car increments))

          (reduce (lambda (x y) (+ y x))

                  0

                  (map (lambda (i inc)

                         (* (apply ((partial i) g) args)

                             inc))

                       (iota n)

                       increments)))))

  the-derivative)

遗憾的是，general-derivative 并不返回偏导数所组成的结构。在许多场合，若有一个真正给出偏导数协向量的求导过程 gradient，会很有用。（见练习 3.10。）Unfortunately general-derivative does not return the structure of partial derivatives. It is useful in many contexts to have a derivative procedure gradient that actually gives the covector of partial derivatives. (See exercise 3.10.)

练习 3.8：偏导数Exercise 3.8: Partial derivatives

理解偏导数的另一种方式，是从 λ 演算中的柯里化入手。画一幅图，说明数据必须如何流动。用柯里化固定那些保持不变的参数，生成一个单参数过程，再对它应用普通的求导运算。编写这个版本的偏导数过程。Another way to think about partial derivatives is in terms of λ-calculus currying. Draw a diagram of how the data must flow. Use currying to fix the arguments that are held constant, producing a one-argument procedure that the ordinary derivative will be applied to. Write that version of the partial derivative procedure.

练习 3.9：添加处理过程Exercise 3.9: Adding handlers

有些基本算术函数，我们尚未为其添加处理微分对象的处理过程，例如 tan。There are primitive arithmetic functions for which we did not add handlers for differential objects, for example tan.

  1. a. 为 tan 和 atan1 添加处理过程（atan1 是一个单参数函数）。a. Add handlers for tan and atan1 (atan1 is a function of one argument).
  2. b. 如果能让 atan 像 Scheme 报告 [109] 中那样，也可以接受两个参数，那就太好了，因为我们通常希望保留所在象限的信息。修改泛型过程 atan，使它正确地做到这一点：只有一个参数时使用 atan1，给出两个参数时使用 atan2。另外，为微分量安装一个 atan2 处理过程。记住，它必须与 atan1 处理过程共存。b. Remember, it must coexist with the atan1 handler.

如上所述，导数的概念可以推广到多参数函数。多参数函数的 gradient 是由相对于每个参数的偏导数组成的协向量。As described above, the idea of derivative can be generalized to functions with multiple arguments. The gradient of a function of multiple arguments is the covector of partial derivatives with respect to each of the arguments.

  1. a. 设计向量和协向量的数据类型，使 Dg(x, y) 的值为偏导数的协向量。编写一个给出该值的 gradient 过程。记住，向量与协向量的乘积应当是它们的内积，即各对应分量乘积之和。a. 3.3.3 一些技术细节3.3.3 Some technical details

虽然自动微分背后的思想并不复杂，但要使它正确工作，还必须处理一些微妙的技术细节。Although the idea behind automatic differentiation is not complicated, there are a number of subtle technical details that must be addressed for it to work correctly.

微分代数Differential algebra

如果要计算二阶导数，就必须对导函数求导。对这样的函数求值时，会有两个无穷小量参与其中。为了计算多阶导数以及多变量函数的导数，我们在“无穷小空间”中定义一种微分对象的代数。这些对象是多元幂级数，其中任何无穷小增量的指数都不大于一。23If we want to compute a second derivative we must take a derivative of a derivative function. The evaluation of such a function will have two infinitesimals in play. To enable the computation of multiple derivatives and derivatives of functions of several variables we define an algebra of differential objects in “infinitesimal space.” The objects are multivariate power series in which no infinitesimal increment has exponent greater than one.23

微分对象用一个带标记的列表表示，列表中存放幂级数的各项。每一项都有一个系数和一个无穷小增量因子列表。各项按阶数降序排列。（阶数就是增量因子的个数。因此，δxδy 的阶数高于 δx 或 δy。）下面是一个简陋但可用的实现：24A differential object is represented by a tagged list of the terms of a power series. Each term has a coefficient and a list of infinitesimal incremental factors. The terms are kept sorted, in descending order. (Order is the number of incrementals. So δxδy is higher order than δx or δy.) Here is a quick and dirty implementation:24

(define differential-tag 'differential)



(define (differential? x)

  (and (pair? x) (eq? (car x) differential-tag)))



(define (diff-terms h)

  (if (differential? h)

      (cdr h)

      (list (make-diff-term h ’()))))

项列表就是微分对象的 cdr。不过，如果给定的对象不是显式的微分对象，例如一个数，我们就将它强制转换为只有一项、且不含增量因子的微分对象。根据一个（预先排好序的）项列表构造微分对象时，我们总是尽量返回简化后的形式；它可能只是一个数，而不是显式的微分对象：The term list is just the cdr of the differential object. However, if we are given an object that is not explicitly a differential object, for example a number, we coerce it to a differential object with a single term and with no incremental factors. When we make a differential object from a (presorted) list of terms, we always try to return a simplified version, which may be just a number, which is not explicitly a differential object:

(define (make-differential terms)

  (let ((terms                       ; Nonzero terms

         (filter

          (lambda (term)

            (let ((coeff (diff-coefficient term)))

              (not (and (number? coeff) (= coeff 0)))))

          terms)))

    (cond ((null? terms) 0)

          ((and (null? (cdr terms))

                ;; Finite part only:

                (null? (diff-factors (car terms))))

           (diff-coefficient (car terms)))

          ((every diff-term? terms)

           (cons differential-tag terms))

          (else (error "Bad terms")))))

在这个实现中，各项也用带标记的列表表示，每个列表包含一个系数和一个有序的因子列表。In this implementation the terms are also represented as tagged lists, each containing a coefficient and an ordered list of factors.

(define diff-term-tag 'diff-term)



(define (make-diff-term coefficient factors)

  (list diff-term-tag coefficient factors))



(define (diff-term? x)

  (and (pair? x) (eq? (car x) diff-term-tag)))



(define (diff-coefficient x)

  (cadr x))



(define (diff-factors x)

  (caddr x))

要计算导数，我们需要能够对微分对象做加法和乘法：To compute derivatives we need to be able to add and multiply differential objects:

(define (d:+ x y)

  (make-differential

   (+diff-termlists (diff-terms x) (diff-terms y))))



(define (d:* x y)

  (make-differential

   (*diff-termlists (diff-terms x) (diff-terms y))))

我们还需要这个：and we also need this:

(define (make-infinitesimal dx)

  (make-differential (list (make-diff-term 1 (list dx)))))

在项列表的加法中，我们确保并利用各项的排序，让高阶项位于列表前面。只有因子相同的两项才能相加。如果系数之和为零，就不把所得的项包括在结果中。Addition of term lists is where we enforce and use the sorting of terms, with higher-order terms coming earlier in the lists. We can add two terms only if they have the same factors. And if the sum of the coefficients is zero we do not include the resulting term.

(define (+diff-termlists l1 l2)

  (cond ((null? l1) l2)

        ((null? l2) l1)

        (else

         (let ((t1 (car l1)) (t2 (car l2)))

           (cond ((equal? (diff-factors t1) (diff-factors t2))

                  (let ((newcoeff (+ (diff-coefficient t1)

                                     (diff-coefficient t2))))

                    (if (and (number? newcoeff)

                             (= newcoeff 0))

                        (+diff-termlists (cdr l1) (cdr l2))

                        (cons

                         (make-diff-term newcoeff

                                         (diff-factors t1))

                         (+diff-termlists (cdr l1)

                                          (cdr l2))))))

                 ((diff-term>? t1 t2)

                  (cons t1 (+diff-termlists (cdr l1) l2)))

                 (else

                  (cons t2

                        (+diff-termlists l1 (cdr l2)))))))))

只要能对单独的项做乘法，项列表的乘法就很直接。两个项列表 l1 和 l2 的乘积，是将 l1 中的每一项与 l2 中的每一项相乘，再把所得的各个项列表相加得到的项列表。Multiplication of term lists is straightforward, if we can multiply individual terms. The product of two term lists l1 and l2 is the term list resulting from adding up the term lists resulting from multiplying every term in l1 by every term in l2.

(define (*diff-termlists l1 l2)

  (reduce (lambda (x y)

            (+diff-termlists y x))

          ’()

          (map (lambda (t1)

                 (append-map (lambda (t2)

                               (*diff-terms t1 t2))

                             l2))

               l1)))

一项具有一个系数和一个因子列表（即那些无穷小量）。微分对象中，任何一项都不能含有指数大于一的无穷小量，因为 δx2 = 0。因此，将两项相乘时，必须检查要合并的因子列表是否没有共同的因子。这就是 *diff-terms 返回只含乘积项的列表或空列表的原因，这些列表随后在 *diff-termlists 中被拼接起来。合并两个因子列表时，我们保持因子的有序性；这样更容易对各项排序。A term has a coefficient and a list of factors (the infinitesimals). In a differential object no term may have an infinitesimal with an exponent greater than one, because δx2 = 0. Thus, when we multiply two terms we must check that the lists of factors we are merging have no factors in common. This is the reason that *diff-terms returns a list of the product term or an empty list, to be appended in *diff-termlists. We keep the factors sorted when we merge the two lists of factors; this makes it easier to sort the terms.

(define (*diff-terms x y)

  (let ((fx (diff-factors x)) (fy (diff-factors y)))

    (if (null? (ordered-intersect diff-factor>? fx fy))

        (list (make-diff-term

               (* (diff-coefficient x) (diff-coefficient y))

               (ordered-union diff-factor>? fx fy)))

        ’())))

有限部分与无穷小部分Finite and infinitesimal parts

微分对象具有有限部分和无穷小部分。第 109 页的 diff:binary-proc 过程，对于含有多个无穷小量的微分对象并不正确。为了确保以一致的方式选取参数 x 和 y 的各个部分，我们实际使用的是：A differential object has a finite part and an infinitesimal part. Our diff:binary-proc procedure on page 109 is not correct for differential objects with more than one infinitesimal. To ensure that the parts of the arguments x and y are selected consistently we actually use:

(define (diff:binary-proc f d0f d1f)

  (define (bop x y)

    (let ((factor (maximal-factor x y)))

      (let ((dx (infinitesimal-part x factor))

            (dy (infinitesimal-part y factor))

            (xe (finite-part x factor))

            (ye (finite-part y factor)))

        (d:+ (f xe ye)

             (d:+ (d:* dx (d0f xe ye))

                  (d:* (d1f xe ye) dy))))))

  bop)

其中，factor 由 maximal-factor 选出，使 x 和 y 都在一个因子数最多的项中含有它。where factor is chosen by maximal-factor so that both x and y contain it in a term with the largest number of factors.

微分对象的有限部分，是除去那些含有最高阶项中最大因子的项后所剩的所有项；无穷小部分则是其余的项，它们都含有该因子。The finite part of a differential object is all terms except for terms containing the maximal factor in a term of highest order, and the infinitesimal part is the remaining terms, all of which contain that factor.

考虑下面的计算：Consider the following computation:

最高阶项是 ∂0∂1f (x, y) · δxδy。它关于 x 和 y 是对称的。关键在于，我们可以选择任意一个最大因子（这里是 δx 或 δy）作为主因子，并按任何与这一选择一致的方式把微分对象分成两部分。选哪一个并不重要，因为 R → R 的混合偏导数可以交换求导次序。25The highest-order term is ∂0∂1f (x, y) · δxδy. It is symmetrical with respect to x and y. The crucial point is that we may break the differential object into parts in any way consistent with any one of the maximal factors (here δx or δy) being primary. It doesn't matter which is chosen, because mixed partials of R → R commute.25

(define (finite-part x #!optional factor)

  (if (differential? x)

      (let ((factor (default-maximal-factor x factor)))

        (make-differential

         (remove (lambda (term)

                   (memv factor (diff-factors term)))

                 (diff-terms x))))

      x))



(define (infinitesimal-part x #!optional factor)

  (if (differential? x)

      (let ((factor (default-maximal-factor x factor)))

        (make-differential

         (filter (lambda (term)

                   (memv factor (diff-factors term)))

                 (diff-terms x))))

      0))



(define (default-maximal-factor x factor)

  (if (default-object? factor)

      (maximal-factor x)

      factor))

提取操作究竟如何工作How extracting really works

如第 114 页所述，为了能够求多阶导数，或者处理有多个参数的函数，微分对象用多元幂级数表示，其中任何无穷小增量的指数都不大于一。级数的每一项都有一个系数和一个无穷小增量因子列表。这使得提取相对于任意一个增量因子的导数变得复杂。实际情况如下：As explained on page 114, to make it possible to take multiple derivatives or to handle functions with more than one argument, a differential object is represented as a multivariate power series in which no infinitesimal increment has exponent greater than one. Each term in this series has a coefficient and a list of infinitesimal incremental factors. This complicates the extraction of the derivative with respect to any one incremental factor. Here is the real story:

如果返回的是微分对象，我们必须在结果中找出含有无穷小因子 dx 的那些项，这个因子对应于正在计算的导数。我们收集这些项，并从每一项中去掉 dx。如果取出含有 dx 的项并作上述处理后没有留下任何项，导数的值就是零。如果恰好剩下一项，而且它不含微分因子，那么这一项的系数就是导数的值。但如果剩余的项仍含有微分因子，就必须把由这些剩余项构成的微分对象作为导数的值返回。In the case where a differential object is returned we must find those terms of the result that contain the infinitesimal factor dx for the derivative we are evaluating. We collect those terms, removing dx from each. If there are no terms left after taking out the ones with dx, the value of the derivative is zero. If there is exactly one term left, which has no differential factors, then the coefficient of that term is the value of the derivative. But if there are remaining terms with differential factors, we must return the differential object with those residual terms as the value of the derivative.

(define (extract-dx-differential value dx)

  (let ((dx-diff-terms

         (filter-map

          (lambda (term)

            (let ((factors (diff-factors term)))

              (and (memv dx factors)

                   (make-diff-term (diff-coefficient term)

                                   (delv dx factors)))))

          (diff-terms value))))

    (cond ((null? dx-diff-terms) 0)

          ((and (null? (cdr dx-diff-terms))

                (null? (diff-factors (car dx-diff-terms))))

           (diff-coefficient (car dx-diff-terms)))

          (else (make-differential dx-diff-terms)))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler extract-dx-part

  (match-args differential? diff-factor?)

  extract-dx-differential)

高阶函数Higher-order functions

在许多应用中，我们希望自动微分器能够正确处理返回函数值的函数：For many applications we want our automatic differentiator to work correctly for functions that return functions as values:

(((derivative

   (lambda (x)

     (lambda (y z)

       (* x y z))))

  2)

 3

 4)

;Value: 12

再加上字面函数和偏导数，情况就更有趣了。Including literal functions and partial derivatives makes this even more interesting.

((derivative

  (lambda (x)

    (((partial 1) (literal-function ’f))

     x ’v)))

 ’u)

(((partial 0) ((partial 1) f)) u v)

情况甚至还会更加复杂：And things can get even more complicated:

(((derivative

   (lambda (x)

     (derivative

      (lambda (y)

        ((literal-function ’f)

         x y)))))

  ’u)

 ’v)

(((partial 0) ((partial 1) f)) u v)

要使这些情况正常工作，过程 extract-dx-part 就会变得相当复杂。Making this work introduces serious complexity in the procedure extract-dx-part.

如果将函数应用于微分对象所得到的结果是一个函数，例如导数的导数，我们就需要推迟提取操作，直到那个函数被传入参数并调用时再进行：If the result of applying a function to a differential object is a function—a derivative of a derivative, for example—we need to defer the extraction until that function is called with arguments:

在返回函数的情况下，例如In a case where a function is returned, as in

(((derivative

   (lambda (x)

     (derivative

      (lambda (y)

        (* x y)))))

  ’u)

 ’v)

1

我们无法在函数应用于参数之前提取导数。因此，我们推迟提取，直到获得这次应用所产生的值。我们扩展泛型提取器：we cannot extract the derivative until the function is applied to arguments. So we defer the extraction until we get the value resulting from that application. We extend our generic extractor:

(define (extract-dx-function fn dx)

  (lambda args

    (extract-dx-part (apply fn args) dx)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler extract-dx-part

  (match-args function? diff-factor?)

  extract-dx-function)

遗憾的是，这一版 extract-dx-function 有一个微妙的错误。26 我们的修补办法是，用一段重新映射因子 dx 的代码包裹新的延迟过程的过程体，以避免这种麻烦的冲突。因此，我们把函数的处理过程改为：Unfortunately, this version of extract-dx-function has a subtle bug.26 Our patch is to wrap the body of the new deferred procedure with code that remaps the factor dx to avoid the unpleasant conflict. So, we change the handler for functions to:

(define (extract-dx-function fn dx)

  (lambda args

    (let ((eps (make-new-dx)))

       (replace-dx dx eps

        (extract-dx-part

         (apply fn

           (map (lambda (arg)

                  (replace-dx eps dx arg))

                args))

         dx)))))

这会创建一个全新的因子 eps，并在参数中用它代表 dx，从而避免与其他任何 dx 实例发生冲突。This creates a brand-new factor eps and uses it to stand for dx in the arguments, thus preventing collision with any other instances of dx.

因子的替换本身也稍微复杂一些，因为代码必须深入遍查数据结构。我们将把替换操作做成泛型过程，以便将它扩展到新的数据种类。默认情况下，替换只是对象上的恒等操作：Replacement of the factors is itself a bit more complicated, because the code has to grovel around in the data structures. We will make the replacement a generic procedure, so we can extend it to new kinds of data. The default is that the replacement is just the identity on the object:

(define (replace-dx-default new-dx old-dx object) object)



(define replace-dx

  (simple-generic-procedure ’replace-dx 3

                            replace-dx-default))

对于微分对象，我们必须真正进入其内部，用新因子替换旧因子，并且必须保持因子列表的有序性：For a differential object we have to actually go in and substitute the new factor for the old one, and we have to keep the factor lists sorted:

(define (replace-dx-differential new-dx old-dx object)

  (make-differential

   (sort (map (lambda (term)

                (make-diff-term

                 (diff-coefficient term)

                 (sort (substitute new-dx old-dx

                                   (diff-factors term))

                       diff-factor>?)))

              (diff-terms object))

         diff-term>?)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler replace-dx

  (match-args diff-factor? diff-factor? differential?)

  replace-dx-differential)

最后，如果对象本身是函数，我们就必须推迟操作，直到有了参数、能够计算出一个值时再进行：Finally, if the object is itself a function we have to defer it until arguments are available to compute a value:

(define (replace-dx-function new-dx old-dx fn)

  (lambda args

    (let ((eps (make-new-dx)))

      (replace-dx old-dx eps

        (replace-dx new-dx old-dx

          (apply fn

            (map (lambda (arg)

                   (replace-dx eps old-dx arg))

                 args)))))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler replace-dx

  (match-args diff-factor? diff-factor? function?)

  replace-dx-function)

这比我们可能预想的复杂得多。它实际上对微分因子做了三次替换。这是为了避免与 fn 的过程体中可能自由出现的因子发生冲突；这些因子继承自函数 fn 定义时的词法环境。27This is quite a bit more complicated than we might expect. It actually does three replacements of the differential factors. This is to prevent collisions with factors that may be free in the body of fn that are inherited from the lexical environment of definition of the function fn.27

练习 3.11：那个错误！Exercise 3.11: The bug!

在得知第 121 页脚注 26 指出的错误之前，过程 extract-dx-function 是这样写的：Before we became aware of the bug pointed out in footnote 26 on page 121, the procedure extract-dx-function was written:

(define (extract-dx-function fn dx)

  (lambda args

    (extract-dx-part (apply fn args) dx)))

构造一个函数，使其导数用这一早期版本的 extract-dx-part 计算时是错误的，而用修正后的版本计算时是正确的，以此说明为什么要使用 replace-dx 包装层。这并不容易！你可能需要阅读脚注 26 指向的参考文献。Demonstrate the reason for the use of the replace-dx wrapper by constructing a function whose derivative is wrong with this earlier version of extract-dx-part but is correct in the fixed version. This is not easy! You may want to read the references pointed at in footnote 26.

3.3.4 接受微分参数的字面函数3.3.4 Literal functions of differential arguments

对于简单参数，应用字面函数，只需构造一个表达式，表示将函数表达式应用于这些参数。但字面函数也必须能够接受微分对象作为参数。这时，字面函数必须为那些微分量参数构造（偏）导数表达式。对于一个 n 参数函数的第 i 个参数，适当的导数表达式为：For simple arguments, applying a literal function is just a matter of constructing the expression that is the application of the function expression to the arguments. But literal functions must also be able to accept differential objects as arguments. When that happens, the literal function must construct (partial) derivative expressions for the arguments that are differentials. For the ith argument of an n-argument function the appropriate derivative expression is:

(define (deriv-expr i n fexp)

  (if (= n 1)

      ‘(derivative ,fexp)

      ‘((partial ,i) ,fexp)))

有些参数可能是微分对象，因此字面函数必须为每个参数选定有限部分和无穷小部分。与二元算术处理过程一样，必须以一致的方式选取最大因子。我们的字面函数能够接受多个参数，所以这看起来可能很复杂，但我们编写的 maximal-factor 过程能够处理多个参数。这一点解释于Some arguments may be differential objects, so a literal function must choose, for each argument, a finite part and an infinitesimal part. Just as for binary arithmetic handlers, the maximal factor must be consistently chosen. Our literal functions are able to take many arguments, so this may seem complicated, but we wrote the maximal-factor procedure to handle many arguments. This is explained in 第 3.3.3 节中解释。section 3.3.3.

如果参数中没有微分对象，我们只需用 cons 构造所需的表达式。如果有微分对象，就需要求字面函数的导数。为此，我们从所有参数中找出一个最大因子，并分离出各参数的有限部分，即不含该因子的项。（无穷小部分就是含有该因子的项。）偏导数本身也是字面函数，其表达式在构造时加入了参数的索引。所得的微分对象，就是在各参数有限部分处求得的偏导数与各参数无穷小部分的内积。If there are no differential objects among the arguments we just cons up the required expression. If there are differential objects we need to make a derivative of the literal function. To do this we find a maximal factor from all of the arguments and separate out the finite parts of the arguments—the terms that do not have that factor. (The infinitesimal parts are the terms that have that factor.) The partial derivatives are themselves literal functions with expressions that are constructed to include the argument index. The resulting differential object is the inner product of the partial derivatives at the finite parts of the arguments with the infinitesimal parts of the arguments.

下面的过程将这些内容汇集在一起：This is all brought together in the following procedure:

(define (literal-function fexp)

  (define (the-function . args)

    (if (any differential? args)

        (let ((n (length args))

              (factor (apply maximal-factor args)))

          (let ((realargs

                 (map (lambda (arg)

                        (finite-part arg factor))

                      args))

                (deltargs

                 (map (lambda (arg)

                        (infinitesimal-part arg factor))

                      args)))

            (let ((fxs (apply the-function realargs))

                  (partials

                   (map (lambda (i)

                          (apply (literal-function

                                  (deriv-expr i n fexp))

                                 realargs))

                        (iota n))))

              (fold d:+ fxs

                (map d:* partials deltargs)))))

        ‘(,fexp ,@args)))

  the-function)

练习 3.12：返回结构化值的函数Exercise 3.12: Functions with structured values

我们将 extract-dx-part 过程做成了泛型过程（第 110 页），以便将它扩展到微分对象和函数以外的值。扩展 extract-dx-part，使其能够处理返回向量的函数的导数。注意：你还必须扩展提取器中的泛型过程 replace-dx（第 122 页）。We made the extract-dx-part procedure generic (page 110) so we could extend it for values other than differential objects and functions. Extend extract-dx-part to work with derivatives of functions that return vectors. Note: You also have to extend the replace-dx generic procedure (page 122) in the extractor.

3.4 高效的泛型过程3.4 Efficient generic procedures

在In 第 3.2.3 节section 3.2.3我们利用元数据中提供的分派存储，查找适用的规则，从而分派到一个处理过程： we dispatched to a handler by finding an applicable rule using the dispatch store provided in the metadata:

(define (generic-procedure-dispatch metadata args)

  (let ((handler

         (get-generic-procedure-handler metadata args)))

    (apply handler args)))

我们在第 89 页用来构造 simple-generic-procedure 构造器的分派存储实现（第 98 页）相当简陋。简单分派存储将规则集维护为一个规则列表。每条规则表示为一个适用性说明与一个处理过程组成的序对。适用性说明是由谓词列表组成的列表，这些谓词要应用于传入的参数。由 simple-generic-procedure 构造的泛型过程，通过顺序扫描规则列表、寻找参数所满足的适用性说明，来找到恰当的处理过程。The implementation of the dispatch store (on page 98) we used (on page 89) to make the simple-generic-procedure constructor was rather crude. The simple dispatch store maintains the rule set as a list of rules. Each rule is represented as a pair of an applicability and a handler. The applicability is a list of lists of predicates to apply to tendered arguments. The way a generic procedure constructed by simple-generic-procedure finds an appropriate handler is to sequentially scan the list of rules looking for an applicability that is satisfied by the arguments.

这非常低效，因为许多规则的适用性说明可能在某个给定的操作数位置上具有相同的谓词。例如，在一个兼有数值算术和符号算术的系统中，可能有许多乘法规则的第一个谓词都是 number?。因此，在找到适用规则之前，可能会多次应用 number? 谓词。如果能组织好规则，使查找适用规则时不做冗余测试，那就好了。通常可以用索引来实现这一点。This is seriously inefficient, because the applicability of many rules may have the same predicate in a given operand position: For example, for multiplication in a system of numerical and symbolic arithmetic there may be many rules whose first predicate is number?. So the number? predicate may be applied many times before finding an applicable rule. It would be good to organize the rules so that finding an applicable one does not perform redundant tests. This is usually accomplished by the use of an index.

3.4.1 前缀树3.4.1 Tries

一种简单的索引机制基于前缀树。28One simple index mechanism is based on the trie.28

前缀树通常是一种树结构，但更一般地说，它也可以是有向图。前缀树的每个节点都有连接到后继节点的边。每条边都关联着一个谓词。接受测试的数据是一个线性的特征序列，在这里就是泛型过程的参数。A trie is traditionally a tree structure, but more generally it may be a directed graph. Each node in the trie has edges connecting to successor nodes. Each edge has an associated predicate. The data being tested is a linear sequence of features, in this case the arguments to a generic procedure.

从前缀树的根节点开始，取出序列中的第一个特征，用从根节点出发的各条边上的谓词分别测试它。沿着测试成功的谓词所在的边进入下一个节点，然后对特征序列的剩余部分重复这一过程。当所有特征都用完时，当前节点中就存有相关联的值，在这里就是适用于这些参数的处理过程。Starting at the root of the trie, the first feature is taken from the sequence and is tested by each predicate on an edge emanating from the root node. The successful predicate's edge is followed to the next node, and the process repeats with the remainder of the sequence of features. When we run out of features, the current node will contain the associated value, in this case an applicable handler for the arguments.

在任意节点，都可能有多个谓词测试成功。如果发生这种情况，就必须沿所有成功的分支继续查找。因此，可能会有多个适用的处理过程，必须另有办法来决定该怎么办。It is possible that at any node, more than one predicate may succeed. If this happens, then all of the successful branches must be followed. Thus there may be multiple applicable handlers, and there must be a separate means of deciding what to do.

下面说明如何使用前缀树。对以下命令序列求值，会逐步构造出图 3.1 所示的前缀树。Here is how we can use a trie. Evaluating the following sequence of commands will incrementally construct the trie shown in figure 3.1.

(define a-trie (make-trie))

我们可以向这棵前缀树添加一条边We can add an edge to this trie

(define s (add-edge-to-trie a-trie symbol?))

其中，add-edge-to-trie 返回位于新边目标端的新节点。对符号进行匹配会到达这个节点。where add-edge-to-trie returns the new node that is at the target end of the new edge. This node is reached by being matched against a symbol.

我们可以构造由多条边组成的链，并用相应边上的谓词所组成的列表来引用这些链We can make chains of edges, which are referenced by lists of the corresponding edge predicates

(define sn (add-edge-to-trie s number?))

从根节点沿路径 (list symbol? number?) 可到达节点 sn。使用路径来构造边链，有一种比反复调用 add-edge-to-trie 更简单的方法：The node sn is reached from the root via the path (list symbol? number?). Using a path, there is a simpler way to make a chain of edges than repeatedly calling add-edge-to-trie:

(define ss (intern-path-trie a-trie (list symbol? symbol?)))

我们可以给任何节点添加一个值（这里展示的是符号值，但稍后我们将存储作为处理过程的过程值）：We can add a value to any node (here we show symbolic values, but we will later store values that are procedural handlers):

(trie-has-value? sn)

#f



(set-trie-value! sn ’(symbol number))



(trie-has-value? sn)

#t



(trie-value sn)

(symbol number)

我们也可以用基于路径的接口来设置值We can also use a path-based interface to set values

(set-path-value! a-trie (list symbol? symbol?)

                ’(symbol symbol))



(trie-value ss)

(symbol symbol)

注意，intern-path-trie 和 set-path-value! 都会尽可能重用现有的节点和边，只在必要时添加边和节点。Note that both intern-path-trie and set-path-value! reuse existing nodes and edges when possible, adding edges and nodes where necessary.

现在，我们可以将一个特征序列与目前构造出的前缀树进行匹配：Now we can match a feature sequence against the trie we have constructed so far:

(equal? (list ss) (get-matching-tries a-trie ’(a b)))

#t



(equal? (list s) (get-matching-tries a-trie ’(c)))

#t

我们还可以将匹配与取值结合起来。过程 get-a-value 找出所有匹配的节点，从中选出一个具有值的节点，并返回该值。We can also combine matching with value fetching. The procedure get-a-value finds all matching nodes, picks one that has a value, and returns that value.

(get-a-value a-trie ’(a b))

(symbol symbol)

但并非所有特征序列都有相关联的值：But not all feature sequences have an associated value:

(get-a-value a-trie ’(-4))

;Unable to match features: (-4)

我们可以逐步给前缀树中的节点添加值：We can incrementally add values to nodes in the trie:

(set-path-value! a-trie (list negative-number?)

                 ’(negative-number))

(set-path-value! a-trie (list even-number?)

                 ’(even-number))



(get-all-values a-trie ’(-4))

((even-number) (negative-number))

其中，get-all-values 找出与给定特征序列匹配的所有节点，并返回它们的值。where get-all-values finds all the nodes matching a given feature sequence and returns their values.

有了这个前缀树实现，我们就能构造一个以它为索引的分派存储：Given this trie implementation, we can make a dispatch store that uses a trie as its index:

(define (make-trie-dispatch-store)

  (let ((delegate (make-simple-dispatch-store))

        (trie (make-trie)))

    (define (get-handler args)

      (get-a-value trie args))

    (define (add-handler! applicability handler)

      ((delegate ’add-handler!) applicability handler)

      (for-each (lambda (path)

                  (set-path-value! trie path handler))

                applicability))

    (lambda (message)

      (case message

        ((get-handler) get-handler)

        ((add-handler!) add-handler!)

        (else (delegate message))))))

我们将大部分操作委托给一个简单分派存储，从而使这个分派存储保持简单。没有被委托的操作是 add-handler! 和 get-handler：前者把处理过程同时存入简单分派存储和前缀树，后者则完全使用前缀树进行访问。简单分派存储管理默认处理过程，也管理规则集，这对调试很有用。与更广为人知的继承思想不同，这是通过委托来扩展接口的一个简单例子。We make this dispatch store simple by delegating most of the operations to a simple dispatch store. The operations that are not delegated are add-handler!, which simultaneously stores the handler in the simple dispatch store and also in the trie, and get-handler, which exclusively uses the trie for access. The simple dispatch store manages the default handler and also the set of rules, which is useful for debugging. This is a simple example of the use of delegation to extend an interface, as opposed to the better-known inheritance idea.

练习 3.13：前缀树规则Exercise 3.13: Trie rules

为了便于试验不同的分派存储，我们向 generic-procedure-constructor 和 make-generic-arithmetic 提供了分派存储构造器。例如，可以像第 95 页那样构造完整的泛型算术，但改用 make-trie-dispatch-store，如下所示：To make it easy to experiment with different dispatch stores, we gave generic-procedure-constructor and make-generic-arithmetic the dispatch store maker. For example, we can build a full generic arithmetic as on page 95 but using make-trie-dispatch-store as follows:

(define trie-full-generic-arithmetic

  (let ((g (make-generic-arithmetic make-trie-dispatch-store)))

    (add-to-generic-arithmetic! g numeric-arithmetic)

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g function-extender)

    (add-to-generic-arithmetic! g

       (symbolic-extender numeric-arithmetic))

    g))



(install-arithmetic! trie-full-generic-arithmetic)
  1. a. 这是否改变了我们在下述小节中费力处理的对顺序的依赖？a. Does this make any change to the dependence on order that we wrestled with in 第 3.2.2 节section 3.2.2?
  2. b. 一般来说，谓词的哪些特征可能导致某个参数序列有多个适当处理过程的情况？b. In general, what characteristics of the predicates could produce situations where there is more than one appropriate handler for a sequence of arguments?
  3. c. 我们的泛型算术代码中是否存在这样的情况？c. Are there any such situations in our generic arithmetic code?

我们提供了一个简陋的工具，用于衡量分派策略的效果。用 with-predicate-counts 包裹任意计算，就能知道每个分派谓词在一次执行中被调用了多少次。例如，在使用基于前缀树的分派存储的泛型算术中，对 (fib 20) 求值可能产生类似下面的结果：29We have provided a crude tool to measure the effectiveness of our dispatch strategy. By wrapping any computation with with-predicate-counts we can find out how many times each dispatch predicate is called in an execution. For example, evaluating (fib 20) in a generic arithmetic with a trie-based dispatch store may yield something like this:29

(define (fib n)

  (if (< n 2)

      n

      (+ (fib (- n 1)) (fib (- n 2)))))



(with-predicate-counts (lambda () (fib 20)))

(109453 number)

(109453 function)

(54727 any-object)

(109453 symbolic)

6765

练习 3.14：分派效率：意外的陷阱！Exercise 3.14: Dispatch efficiency: gotcha!

有了这个性能工具，考察以下计算的执行情况会很有启发：Given this performance tool it is instructive to look at executions of

(define (test-stormer-counts)

  (define (F t x) (- x))

  (define numeric-s0

    (make-initial-history 0 .01 (sin 0) (sin -.01) (sin -.02)))

  (with-predicate-counts

   (lambda ()

     (x 0 ((evolver F ’h stormer-2) numeric-s0 1)))))

一方面，使用 make-simple-dispatch-store 中基于规则列表的分派，所用算术由下式得到：for the rule-list–based dispatch in make-simple-dispatch-store, in the arithmetic you get by:

(define full-generic-arithmetic

  (let ((g (make-generic-arithmetic make-simple-dispatch-store)))

    (add-to-generic-arithmetic! g numeric-arithmetic)

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g function-extender)

    (add-to-generic-arithmetic! g

            (symbolic-extender numeric-arithmetic))

    g))



(install-arithmetic! full-generic-arithmetic)

另一方面，使用基于前缀树的版本（练习 3.13），所用算术由下式得到：and the trie-based version (exercise 3.13), in the arithmetic you get by:

(install-arithmetic! trie-full-generic-arithmetic)

对于某些问题，前缀树的性能应当远好于简单的规则列表。如果有大量规则具有相同的起始片段，我们预期使用前缀树会有更好的性能。For some problems the trie should have much better performance than the simple rule list. We expect that the performance will be better with the trie if we have a large number of rules with the same initial segment.

理解这一点很重要，因为前缀树有时对性能没有帮助，这似乎有违直觉。我们引入前缀树的明确目的，就是避免冗余调用。用简短的一段话解释这一现象。Understanding this is important, because the fact that sometimes the trie does not help with the performance appears counterintuitive. We explicitly introduced the trie to avoid redundant calls. Explain this phenomenon in a concise paragraph.

要获得进一步的认识，可以考察 (fib 20) 在这两种实现中的性能。For an additional insight, look at the performance of (fib 20) in the two implementations.

当有多个处理过程适用于某个给定的参数序列时，应该如何使用它们并不明确；处理这种情况是消歧策略的职责。设计消歧策略时，需要考虑许多因素。例如，选择最特定的处理过程通常是一个好策略；不过，实现这种策略需要更多信息。有时，运行所有适用的处理过程并比较其结果是恰当的。这可以用来发现错误，并提供一种冗余。或者，如果每个处理过程提供的都是部分信息，例如数值区间，那么可以组合不同处理过程的结果，以获得更完善的信息。When more than one handler is applicable for a given sequence of arguments, it is not clear how to use those handlers; addressing this situation is the job of a resolution policy. There are many considerations when designing a resolution policy. For example, a policy that chooses the most specific handler is often a good policy; however, we need more information to implement such a policy. Sometimes it is appropriate to run all of the applicable handlers and compare their results. This can be used to catch errors and provide a kind of redundancy. Or if we have partial information provided by each handler, such as a numerical interval, the results of different handlers can be combined to provide better information.

3.4.2 缓存3.4.2 Caching

通过使用前缀树，我们消除了对参数谓词的冗余求值。我们还可以做得更好，用抽象完全消除谓词求值。谓词标识了一个对象集合，将其与其他所有对象区分开来；换句话说，谓词与它所区分出的集合实际上是同一回事。在前缀树实现中，我们利用谓词过程是否相等来避免冗余；否则，前缀树中就会出现冗余的边，它也就毫无帮助了。这也是谓词组合不太适合与前缀树实现混用的原因。With the use of tries we have eliminated redundant evaluation of argument predicates. We can do better by using abstraction to eliminate the evaluation of predicates altogether. A predicate identifies a set of objects that are distinguished from all other objects; in other words, the predicate and the set it distinguishes are effectively the same. In our trie implementation, we use the equality of the predicate procedures to avoid redundancy; otherwise we would have redundant edges in the trie and it would be no help at all. This is also why the use of combinations of predicates doesn't mix well with the trie implementation.

这里的问题是，我们想建立一个按谓词区分对象的索引，但过程的不透明性使它们作为索引键时并不可靠。我们真正想做的是，给某个谓词所区分出的集合指定一个名字。如果能够通过简单查看一个给定对象就得到这个名字，我们就完全不必计算谓词了。这个名字就是“类型”；但为避免混淆，我们将把这个名字称为标记。The problem here is that we want to build an index that discriminates objects according to predicates, but the opacity of procedures makes them unreliable when used as keys to the index. What we'd really like is to assign a name to the set distinguished by a given predicate. If we had a way to get that name from a given object by superficial examination, we could avoid computing the predicate at all. This name is a “type”; but in order to avoid confusion we will refer to this name as a tag.

有了从对象获取标记的方法，我们就能构造一个缓存，保存前一次分派得到的处理过程，并在其他参数具有相同标记模式的分派中重用它。但如果没有显式附加的标记，这种方法就有局限，因为我们只能按照实现规定的表示形式来区分对象。例如，区分数和符号很容易，但要区分素数就不容易了，因为实现通常不会对它们采用特殊表示。Given a way to get a tag from an object, we can make a cache that saves the handler resulting from a previous dispatch and reuses it for other dispatches whose arguments have the same tag pattern. But in the absence of explicitly attached tags, there are limitations to this approach, because we can only discriminate objects that share an implementation-specified representation. For example, it's easy to distinguish between a number and a symbol, but it's not easy to distinguish a prime number, because it's unusual for an implementation to represent them specially.

我们将在下述小节重新讨论显式标记的问题：We will return to the problem of explicit tagging in 第 3.5 节section 3.5，不过在此之前，仍然可以利用 Scheme 实现提供的表示标记，构造有用的缓存。给定一个实现特定的过程 implementation-type-name，用来获取对象的表示标记，我们就可以构造带缓存的分派存储：, but in the meantime it is still possible to make a useful cache using the representation tags from the Scheme implementation. Given an implementation-specific procedure implementation-type-name to obtain the representation tag of an object, we can make a cached dispatch store:

(define a-cached-dispatch-store

  (cache-wrapped-dispatch-store (make-trie-dispatch-store)

                                implementation-type-name))

这个分派存储在前缀树分派存储外包裹了一层缓存，但同样也可以用它来包裹简单分派存储。This dispatch store wraps a cache around a trie dispatch store, but it could just as well wrap a simple dispatch store.

带缓存分派存储的核心，是一个基于哈希表构建的记忆化器。哈希表的键，是由过程 implementation-type-name 从参数中提取出的表示标记列表。将 implementation-type-name 作为 get-key 传给这个分派存储包装层，就能用它为我们即将开发的更强大的标记机制构造带缓存的分派存储。The heart of the cached dispatch store is a memoizer built on a hash table. The key for the hash table is the list of representation tags extracted by the implementation-type-name procedure from the arguments. By passing implementation-type-name into this dispatch-store wrapper (as get-key) we can use it to make cached dispatch stores for more powerful tag mechanisms that we will develop soon.

(define (cache-wrapped-dispatch-store dispatch-store get-key)

  (let ((get-handler

         (simple-list-memoizer

           eqv?

           (lambda (args) (map get-key args))

           (dispatch-store ’get-handler))))

    (lambda (message)

      (case message

        ((get-handler) get-handler)

        (else (dispatch-store message))))))

对 simple-list-memoizer 的调用，会在它的最后一个参数外包裹一层缓存，生成该参数的记忆化版本。第二个参数指定如何从过程的参数中取得缓存键。eqv? 参数指定如何在缓存中判定标记是否相同。The call to simple-list-memoizer wraps a cache around its last argument, producing a memoized version of it. The second argument specifies how to get the cache key from the procedure's arguments. The eqv? argument specifies how the tags will be identified in the cache.

练习 3.15：缓存性能Exercise 3.15: Cache performance

使用我们在第 130 页为练习 3.14 引入的同一性能工具，针对练习 3.14 中考察过的那些泛型算术，测量带缓存的分派版本执行 (test-stormer-counts) 和 (fib 20) 时的情况。记录结果。比较起来如何？Using the same performance tool we introduced for exercise 3.14 on page 130, make measurements for execution of (test-stormer-counts) and (fib 20) in the cached version of dispatch with the same generic arithmetics explored in exercise 3.14. Record your results. How do they compare?

3.5 高效的用户定义类型3.5 Efficient user-defined types

在In 第 3.4.2 节section 3.4.2我们将标记作为分派缓存机制的一部分引入。每个参数都映射到一个标记，然后以标记列表为缓存键，获取处理过程。如果缓存中有与这个标记列表关联的处理过程，就使用它。否则，就利用谓词前缀树查找适当的处理过程，并将它存入缓存，与该标记列表关联起来。 we introduced tags as part of a caching mechanism for dispatch. Each argument is mapped to a tag, and the list of tags is then used as a key in a cache to obtain the handler. If the cache has a handler associated with this list of tags, it is used. If not, the trie of predicates is used to find the appropriate handler and it is entered into the cache associated with the list of tags.

这个机制相当粗糙：适用性说明中能用的谓词受到限制，对于标记相同的任意两个对象，它们必须总是给出相同的布尔值。因此，类型的区分不能比现有标记更精细。那些标记是实现特定的符号，如 pair、vector 或 procedure。这严重限制了可用的谓词。例如，我们无法制定规则，区分满足 even-integer? 的整数和满足 odd-integer? 的整数。This mechanism is pretty crude: the predicates that can be used for the applicability specifications are restricted to those that always give the same boolean value for any two objects with the same tag. So the discrimination of types cannot be any finer than the available tags. The tags were implementation-specific symbols, such as pair, vector, or procedure. So this severely limits the possible predicates. We could not have rules that distinguish between integers that satisfy even-integer? and integers that satisfy odd-integer?, for example.

我们需要一种标记系统，它既能在计算上轻易获取与数据项关联的标记，又不把标记限制为少量实现特定的值。通过显式的数据结构，或通过关联表，为每个数据项附加一个标记，就能做到这一点。What is needed is a system of tagging that makes it computationally easy to obtain the tag associated with a data item, but where the tags are not restricted to a small set of implementation-specific values. This can be accomplished by attaching a tag to each data item, either with an explicit data structure or via a table of associations.

这里有几个相互交织的问题：我们想在适用性说明中使用谓词；想要高效的分派机制；还想能够指定谓词之间的关系，并在分派中使用这些关系。例如，我们希望能够声明，谓词 integer? 是谓词 even-integer? 和 odd-integer? 的析取，还能声明 integer? 是 positive-integer?、negative-integer? 和 zero? 的析取。We have several problems interwoven here: we want to use predicates in applicability specifications; we want an efficient mechanism for dispatch; and we want to be able to specify relationships between predicates that can be used in the dispatch. For example, we want to be able to say that the predicate integer? is the disjunction of the predicates even-integer? and odd-integer?, and also that integer? is the disjunction of positive-integer?, negative-integer?, and zero?.

为表达这些关系，我们需要给谓词附加元数据；但若像第 28 页处理函数元数时那样，通过增加一次关联查找来获取谓词的元数据，就会带来过大的开销，因为元数据中会包含对其他标记的引用，而沿着这些引用进行查找必须是高效的。To capture such relationships we need to put metadata on the predicates; but adding an associative lookup to get the metadata of a predicate, as we did with the arity of a function (on page 28), adds too much overhead, because the metadata will contain references to other tags, and chasing these references must be efficient.

一种解决办法是注册所需的谓词。注册会创建一种新的标记，即与谓词关联的数据结构。这种标记很容易附加到被该谓词接受的对象上。标记也为存储元数据提供了便利的地方。One way out is to register the needed predicates. Registration creates a new kind of tag, a data structure that is associated with the predicate. The tag will be easy to attach to objects that are accepted by the predicate. The tag will provide a convenient place to store metadata.

我们将构造一个系统，其中每个独立对象只能有一个标记，而且可以声明谓词之间的关系。这看起来可能过于简单，但足以满足我们的目的。We will construct a system in which each distinct object can have only one tag and where relationships between predicates can be declared. This may appear to be overly simple, but it is adequate for our purposes.

3.5.1 用谓词表示类型3.5.1 Predicates as types

先从一些简单的谓词开始。例如，基本过程 exact-integer? 已经作为简单谓词预先注册到我们的系统中：Let's start with some simple predicates. For example, the primitive procedure exact-integer? is preregistered in our system as a simple predicate:

(predicate? exact-integer?)

#t

现在来定义一个新的、非基本的谓词。我们将以这个特别慢的素数测试为基础来构造它。Now let's define a new predicate that's not a primitive. We will build it on this particularly slow test for prime numbers.

(define (slow-prime? n)

  (and (n:exact-positive-integer? n)

       (n:>= n 2)

       (let loop ((k 2))

         (or (n:> (n:square k) n)

             (and (not (n:= (n:remainder n k) 0))

                  (loop (n:+ k 1)))))))

注意，所有算术运算符都加了 n: 前缀，以确保使用的是底层 Scheme 运算。Note that all of the arithmetic operators are prefixed with n: to ensure that we get the underlying Scheme operations.

我们构造抽象谓词 prime-number?，为其提供一个用于错误消息的名字，以及判定对象是否为素数的准则 slow-prime?：We construct the prime-number? abstract predicate, with a name for use in error messages and a criterion, slow-prime?, for an object to be considered a prime number:

(define prime-number?

  (simple-abstract-predicate ’prime-number slow-prime?))

过程 simple-abstract-predicate 创建一个抽象谓词，这是对代价高昂的谓词（这里是 slow-prime?）的结果进行记忆化的一种巧妙技巧。抽象谓词有一个相关联的构造器，用于创建带标记对象；该对象由抽象谓词的标记和一个对象组成。构造器要求待加标记的对象满足那个代价高昂的谓词。所得的带标记对象既满足抽象谓词，又携带其标记。因此，可以使用快速的抽象谓词，或等价地根据标记进行分派，来测试带标记对象是否具有那个代价高昂的谓词所定义的性质。The procedure simple-abstract-predicate creates an abstract predicate, which is a clever trick for memoizing the result of an expensive predicate (in this case slow-prime?). An abstract predicate has an associated constructor that is used to make a tagged object, consisting of the abstract predicate's tag and an object. The constructor requires that the object to be tagged satisfies the expensive predicate. The resulting tagged object satisfies the abstract predicate, as well as carrying its tag. Consequently the tagged object can be tested for the property defined by the expensive predicate by using the fast abstract predicate (or, equivalently, by dispatching on its tag).

例如，抽象谓词 prime-number? 用来给已验证为素数的对象加上标记，以便高效实现泛型分派。这一点很重要，因为我们不希望在分派过程中执行 slow-prime? 来判定一个数是否为素数。因此，我们构造一个新的带标记对象，其中既包含一个标记（prime-number? 的标记），也包含一个数据值（原始素数）。泛型过程收到带标记对象时，就能高效地取出其标记，并用它作为缓存键。For example, the abstract predicate prime-number? is used to tag objects that are verified prime numbers, for the efficient implementation of generic dispatch. This is important because we do not want to execute slow-prime? during the dispatch to determine whether a number is prime. So we build a new tagged object, which contains both a tag (the tag for prime-number?) and a datum (the raw prime number). When a generic procedure is handed a tagged object, it can efficiently retrieve its tag and use that as a cache key.

为了构造带标记对象，我们用 predicate-constructor 获取与抽象谓词相关联的构造器：In order to make tagged objects, we use predicate-constructor to get the constructor associated with the abstract predicate:

(define make-prime-number

  (predicate-constructor prime-number?))



(define short-list-of-primes

  (list (make-prime-number 2)

        (make-prime-number 7)

        (make-prime-number 31)))

构造器 make-prime-number 要求其参数必须是由 slow-prime? 判定的素数：这个构造器能加上标记的对象只能是素数。The constructor make-prime-number requires that its argument be prime, as determined by slow-prime?: the only objects that can be tagged by this constructor are prime numbers.

(make-prime-number 4)

;Ill-formed data for prime-number: 4

3.5.2 谓词之间的关系3.5.2 Relationships between predicates

用抽象谓词定义的集合之间可以存在关系。例如，素数集是正整数集的子集。正整数集、偶整数集和奇整数集都是整数集的子集。这很重要，因为任何适用于整数的操作，也适用于任一子集中的任意元素；但有些操作可以应用于子集中的元素，却不能应用于包含它的超集中所有元素。例如，偶整数除以二不会有余数，但对整个整数集而言并非如此。The sets that we can define with abstract predicates can be related to one another. For example, the primes are a subset of the positive integers. The positive integers, the even integers, and the odd integers are subsets of the integers. This is important because any operation that is applicable to an integer is applicable to any element of any subset, but there are operations that can be applied to an element of a subset that cannot be applied to all elements of an enclosing superset. For example, the even integers can be halved without leaving a remainder, but that is not true of the full integers.

定义 prime-number? 时，我们实际上定义了一个对象集合。但这个集合与 exact-integer? 定义的集合并没有关系：When we defined prime-number?, we effectively defined a set of objects. But that set has no relation to the set defined by exact-integer?:

(exact-integer? (make-prime-number 2))

#f

我们希望在这些集合之间建立恰当的关系，为此可以给谓词本身添加一些元数据：We would like these sets to be properly related, which is done by adding some metadata to the predicates themselves:

(set-predicate<=! prime-number? exact-integer?)

过程 set-predicate<=! 修改作为其参数的谓词的元数据，表明第一个参数定义的集合是第二个参数定义的集合的（非严格）子集。在这里，我们声明 prime-number? 定义的集合是 exact-integer? 定义的集合的子集。完成这一步之后，exact-integer? 就能识别我们的对象：This procedure set-predicate<=! modifies the metadata of its argument predicates to indicate that the set defined by the first argument is a (non-strict) subset of the set defined by the second argument. In our case, the set defined by prime-number? is declared to be a subset of the set defined by exact-integer?. Once this is done, exact-integer? will recognize our objects:

(exact-integer? (make-prime-number 2))

#t

3.5.3 谓词就是分派键3.5.3 Predicates are dispatch keys

我们定义的抽象谓词适合用于泛型分派。更好的是，它们可以用作缓存键，从而使分派高效。如前所述，注册谓词时，会创建一个新标记并将其与谓词关联。我们只需要一种从给定对象获取标记的方法：过程 get-tag 就能做到这一点。The abstract predicates we have defined are suitable for use in generic dispatch. Even better, they can be used as cache keys to make dispatch efficient. As we described above, when a predicate is registered, a new tag is created and associated with the predicate. All we need is a way to get the tag for a given object: the procedure get-tag does this.

如果将 get-tag 作为 get-key 参数传给 cache-wrapped-dispatch-store，就得到了一个可工作的实现。不过，由于谓词定义的集合可能有子集，我们需要考虑给定参数存在多个候选处理过程的情况。有多种方法可以解决这种情况，但最常用的方法是通过某种手段找出“最特定”的处理过程，并调用它。由于子集关系是一种偏序，哪个处理过程最特定可能并不明确，因此实现必须另用其他办法来消除歧义。If we pass get-tag to cache-wrapped-dispatch-store as its get-key argument, we have a working implementation. However, since the set defined by a predicate can have subsets, we need to consider a situation where there are multiple potential handlers for some given arguments. There are a number of possible ways to resolve this situation, but the most common is to identify the “most specific” handler by some means, and invoke that one. Since the subset relation is a partial order, it may not be clear which handler is most specific, so the implementation must resolve the ambiguity by independent means.

下面是这样的一种实现。它用过程 rule< 将匹配的规则按适当的顺序排序，然后从结果中选出一个处理过程。30Here is one such implementation. It uses a procedure rule< to sort the matching rules into an appropriate order, then chooses a handler from the result.30

(define (make-subsetting-dispatch-store-maker choose-handler)

  (lambda ()

    (let ((delegate (make-simple-dispatch-store)))

      (define (get-handler args)

        (let ((matching

               (filter (lambda (rule)

                        (is-generic-handler-applicable?

                         rule args))

                      ((delegate ’get-rules)))))

         (and (n:pair? matching)

              (choose-handler    ; from sorted handlers

               (map cdr (sort matching rule<))

               ((delegate ’get-default-handler))))))

     (lambda (message)

       (case message

         ((get-handler) get-handler)

         (else (delegate message)))))))

过程 make-most-specific-dispatch-store 将排序后的第一个处理过程选作实际使用的处理过程：The procedure make-most-specific-dispatch-store chooses the first of the sorted handlers to be the effective handler:

(define make-most-specific-dispatch-store

  (make-subsetting-dispatch-store-maker

   (lambda (handlers default-handler)

     (car handlers))))

另一种可能的选择，是构造“链式”分派存储，其中每个处理过程都获得一个参数，可用来调用排序序列中的下一个处理过程。当子集的处理过程希望扩展超集处理过程的行为，而不是覆盖它时，这会很有用。我们将在冒险游戏的时钟处理过程中看到这样的例子，见Another possible choice is to make a “chaining” dispatch store, in which each handler gets an argument that can be used to invoke the next handler in the sorted sequence. This is useful for cases where a subset handler wants to extend the behavior of a superset handler rather than overriding it. We will see an example of this in the clock handler of the adventure game in 第 3.5.4 节section 3.5.4.

(define make-chaining-dispatch-store

  (make-subsetting-dispatch-store-maker

   (lambda (handlers default-handler)

     (let loop ((handlers handlers))

       (if (pair? handlers)

           (let ((handler (car handlers))

                 (next-handler (loop (cdr handlers))))

             (lambda args

               (apply handler (cons next-handler args))))

           default-handler)))))

这两种分派存储都可以通过添加缓存包装层，变成带缓存的分派存储：Either one of these dispatch stores can be made into a cached dispatch store by adding a caching wrapper:

(define (make-cached-most-specific-dispatch-store)

  (cache-wrapped-dispatch-store

     (make-most-specific-dispatch-store)

     get-tag))



(define (make-cached-chaining-dispatch-store)

  (cache-wrapped-dispatch-store

     (make-chaining-dispatch-store)

     get-tag))

然后，我们创建相应的泛型过程构造器：Then we create the corresponding generic-procedure constructors:

(define most-specific-generic-procedure

  (generic-procedure-constructor

   make-cached-most-specific-dispatch-store))



(define chaining-generic-procedure

  (generic-procedure-constructor

   make-cached-chaining-dispatch-store))

3.5.4 示例：冒险游戏3.5.4 Example: An adventure game

为世界建模的一种传统方式是“面向对象编程”。其思想是，所建模的世界由对象构成，每个对象都有独立的局部状态，对象之间松散耦合。假定每个对象都有特定的行为。对象可以接收其他对象发来的消息，改变自身状态，并向其他对象发送消息。对于我们希望建模的行为不依赖多个信息源协作的情形，这种方式非常自然：每条消息都来自另一个对象。这对程序的组织方式是一种严格的约束。One traditional way to model a world is “object-oriented programming.” The idea is that the world being modeled is made up of objects, each of which has independent local state, and the coupling between the objects is loose. Each object is assumed to have particular behaviors. An object may receive messages from other objects, change its state, and send messages to other objects. This is very natural for situations where the behavior we wish to model does not depend on the collaboration of multiple sources of information: each message comes from one other object. This is a tight constraint on the organization of a program.

把问题分解成若干部分，还有其他方法。我们对“算术”的考察已经足以表明，一个运算符（如 *）的含义可以依赖多个参数的性质。例如，数与向量的乘积，与两个向量的乘积或两个数的乘积，是不同的运算。这类问题很自然地可以用泛型过程来表述。31There are other ways to break a problem into pieces. We have looked at “arithmetic” enough to see that the meaning of an operator, such as *, can depend on the properties of multiple arguments. For example, the product of a number and a vector is a different operation from the product of two vectors or of two numbers. This kind of problem is naturally formulated in terms of generic procedures.31

考虑用泛型过程为一个由“地点”“物品”和“人物”组成的世界建模。那些被认为是实体局部状态的状态变量，应当如何表示和封装？哪些操作适合在什么种类的实体上作为泛型操作？既然将实体归为类型（或集合），并把某些操作表述为适用于某个包含范围较广的集合中的所有成员，是很自然的，那么应当如何安排子类型关系？任何面向对象的观点都会为这些设计问题规定具体答案；在这里，我们有更多自由，也必须设计所要采用的约定。Consider the problem of modeling a world made of “places,” “things,” and “people” with generic procedures. How should the state variables that are presumed to be local to the entities be represented and packaged? What operations are appropriately generic over what kinds of entities? Since it is natural to group entities into types (or sets) and to express some of the operations as appropriate for all members of an inclusive set, how is subtyping to be arranged? Any object-oriented view will prescribe specific answers to these design questions; here we have more freedom, and must design the conventions that will be used.

为了说明这一过程，我们将为一个简单的冒险游戏构造一个世界。这里有通过通道相连的房间网络，里面住着各种生物，其中一些是自主的，也就是说它们可以四处游荡。这里有一个由玩家控制的化身。还有一些物品，其中一些可以被生物捡起并携带。生物之间可以以各种方式互动：巨魔可以咬其他生物，造成伤害；任何生物都可以拿走另一个生物携带的物品。To illustrate this process we will build a world for a simple adventure game. There is a network of rooms connected by passages and inhabited by a variety of creatures, some of which are autonomous in that they can wander around. There is an avatar that is controlled by the player. There are things, some of which can be picked up and carried by the creatures. There are ways that the creatures can interact: a troll can bite another creature and damage it; any creature can take a thing carried by another creature.

这个世界中的每个实体都有一组具名属性。其中一些是固定的，另一些则可以改变。例如，房间有通向其他房间的出口。它们表示网络的拓扑结构，不能更改。房间还容纳着一些东西，例如当前位于房间中的生物，以及可以获取的物品。随着生物四处移动、将物品带入或带离其他房间，房间容纳的内容也会改变。在计算模型中，我们将把这组具名属性表示为从名字到属性值的表。Every entity in our world has a set of named properties. Some of these are fixed and others are changeable. For example, a room has exits to other rooms. These represent the topology of the network and cannot be changed. A room also has contents, such as the creatures who are currently in the room and things that may be acquired. The contents of a room change as creatures move around and as they carry things to and from other rooms. We will computationally model this set of named properties as a table from names to property values.

有一组泛型过程适用于这个世界。例如，有些东西可以移动，如书、生物和化身。在所有情况下，移动一个东西都需要将它从来源处所容纳的内容中删除，将它加入目的地所容纳的内容，并改变它的位置属性。这一操作对于书、人和巨魔都是一样的，它们全都是“可移动物品”集合的成员。There is a set of generic procedures that are appropriate for this world. For example, some things, such as books, creatures, and the avatar, are movable. In every case, moving a thing requires deleting it from the contents of the source, adding it to the contents of the destination, and changing its location property. This operation is the same for books, people, and trolls, all of which are members of the “movable things” set.

书可以阅读；人可以说话；巨魔可以咬生物。为了实现这些行为，书具有一些不同于人或巨魔的特有属性。但这些不同种类的可移动物品也有一些共同属性，例如位置。因此，实例化这样的东西时，必须为它的全部属性建立一张表，包括从包含范围更广的集合继承的那些属性。实现 move 等运算符行为的规则，必须能够在每种情况下找到适当的处理过程来操作这些属性。A book can be read; a person can say something; a troll can bite a creature. To implement these behaviors there are specific properties of books that are different from the properties of people or those of trolls. But these different kinds of movable things have some properties in common, such as location. So when such a thing is instantiated, it must make a table for all of its properties, including those inherited from more inclusive sets. The rules for implementing the behavior of operators such as move must be able to find appropriate handlers for manipulating the properties in each case.

游戏The game

我们的游戏在一张 MIT 的粗略拓扑地图上进行。其中有各种自主智能体（非玩家角色），例如学生和管理人员。比如，教务注册主任就是一只巨魔。这里既有可移动的东西，也有不可移动的东西，可移动的东西可以由自主智能体或玩家化身拿走。虽然这个游戏细节不多，但可以把它扩展得非常有趣。Our game is played on a rough topological map of MIT. There are various autonomous agents (non-player characters), such as students and officials. The registrar, for example, is a troll. There are movable and immovable things, and movable things can be taken by an autonomous agent or the player's avatar. Although this game has little detail, it can be expanded to be very interesting.

我们创建一个游戏会话，其中名为 gjs 的化身出现在随机地点。游戏向玩家介绍化身周围的环境。We create a session with an avatar named gjs who appears in a random place. The game tells the player about the environment of the avatar.

(start-adventure ’gjs)

You are in dorm-row

You see here: registrar

You can exit: east

既然教务注册主任在这里，还是离开为妙！（他可能会咬人，咬得足够多次后，化身就会死去。）Since the registrar is here it is prudent to leave! (He may bite, and after enough bites the avatar will die.)

(go ’east)

gjs leaves via the east exit

gjs enters lobby-7

You are in lobby-7

You can see: lobby-10 infinite-corridor

You can exit: up west east

alyssa-hacker enters lobby-7

alyssa-hacker says: Hi gjs

ben-bitdiddle enters lobby-7

ben-bitdiddle says: Hi alyssa-hacker gjs

registrar enters lobby-7

registrar says: Hi ben-bitdiddle alyssa-hacker gjs

注意，几个自主智能体在化身之后到达，而且是一个接一个地到达。因此可以看出，报告描述的是一段模拟时间，而不是某个瞬间状态的概述。这是我们的实现附带产生的现象，并非刻意的设计选择。Notice that several autonomous agents arrive after the avatar, and that they do so one at a time. So we see that the report is for an interval of simulated time rather than a summary of the state at an instant. This is an artifact of our implementation rather than a deliberate design choice.

不幸的是，教务注册主任跟了过来，所以又该离开了。Unfortunately the registrar has followed, so it's time to leave again.

(say "I am out of here!")

gjs says: I am out of here!



(go ’east)

gjs leaves via the east exit

gjs enters lobby-10

You are in lobby-10

You can see: lobby-7 infinite-corridor great-court

You can exit: east south west up



(go ’up)

gjs leaves via the up exit

gjs enters 10-250

You are in 10-250

You see here: blackboard

You can exit: up down

10-250 房间是一间大讲堂，有一块大黑板。也许我们可以把它拿走？Room 10-250 is a lecture hall, with a large blackboard. Perhaps we can take it?

(take-thing ’blackboard)

blackboard is not movable

真遗憾——gjs 喜欢黑板。我们继续四处看看吧。So sad—gjs loves blackboards. Let's keep looking around.

(go ’up)

gjs enters barker-library

You are in barker-library

You can exit: up down

An earth-shattering, soul-piercing scream is heard...

显然，有一只巨魔（也许是教务注册主任）吃掉了某个人。不过，这里有一本应该可以拿走的书，于是我们拿起它，返回大讲堂。Apparently, a troll (maybe the registrar) has eaten someone. However, here is a book that should be takable, so we take it and return to the lecture hall.

(take-thing ’engineering-book)

gjs picks up engineering-book
