我们希望两位棋手看到棋盘图的不同视图：边标签的含义应当相对于棋手而定。如果执白棋的棋手看到一条从格子 A（所代表的节点）到格子 B 的 north 边，我们就希望执黑棋的棋手看到一条从格子 B 到格子 A 的 north 边。We want the two players to have different views of the board graph: we want the meanings of the edge labels to be relative to the player. If the player playing White sees a north edge from (the node representing) square A to square B we want the player playing Black to see a north edge from square B to square A.

为此，我们引入图视图。图视图是从一种边标签到另一种边标签的可逆映射。把图视图应用于一个节点时，它返回该节点的一个副本，其中的边已被重新命名。To make this work we introduce graph views. A graph view is a reversible mapping from one edge label to another. When a graph view is applied to a node, it returns a copy of that node in which the edges are renamed.

对于国际象棋，所需的视图就是把棋盘旋转 180 度：In the case of chess the relevant view is with the board rotated 180 degrees:

(define rotate-180-view

  (make-graph-view ’inverse rotate-180 rotate-180))

其中，make-graph-view 创建一个图视图。过程 graph-node-view 将视图应用于节点：where make-graph-view makes a graph view. The procedure graph-node-view applies a view to a node:

(graph-node-view node view )

白方直接看到节点，黑方则通过 rotate-180-view 看到同一节点的投影。有了这个映射，所有操作在白方和黑方看来都是一样的。White will see a node directly and Black will see the same node projected through the rotate-180-view. Given this map, all operations look the same to both White and Black.

使用图视图解决了相对寻址的问题，即查看给定节点的邻居。不过，我们还需要绝对寻址，即通过行和列指定要找的节点。双方都希望看到类似的寻址方式：己方的底线行为 0，对方的底线行为 7；同样，双方看到的最左列为 0，最右列为 7。17 默认采用白方的地址，黑方的地址则通过过程 invert-address 反转。Using a graph view takes care of relative addressing, where we are looking at neighbors of a given node. But we also need to do absolute addressing, where the node to find is specified by a row and column. Each color wants to see similar addressing, where the home row is 0, and the opponent's home row is 7; likewise each color sees the leftmost column as 0 and the rightmost as 7.17 White's addresses are the default, and Black's are inverted with the procedure invert-address.

我们来创建一个棋盘。下面的代码专用于国际象棋，因为我们并不着重于创建一个抽象领域。我们创建一个 8 × 8 的节点数组来表示格子，每个格子都有地址。我们遍历所有可能的格子地址，用带有适当标签的边把每个节点连接到它的各个邻居。然后在棋盘两侧摆上棋子。Let's make a board. The following code is specific to chess, since we're not focusing on making an abstract domain. We make an 8 × 8 array of nodes representing squares, each with an address. We iterate through all possible square addresses, connecting each node to each of its neighbors by an edge with the appropriate label. Then we populate the sides with pieces.

(define chess-board-size 8)

(define chess-board-indices (iota chess-board-size))

(define chess-board-last-index (last chess-board-indices))



(define (make-chess-board)

  (let ((board (make-chess-board-internal)))

    (for-each (lambda (address)

                (connect-up-square address board))

              board-addresses)

    (populate-sides board)

    board))

国际象棋棋盘格的所有可能地址，就是由 0 到 7 的整数组成的所有数对：The possible addresses for chess-board squares are all pairs of integers from 0 to 7:

(define board-addresses

  (append-map (lambda (y)

                (map (lambda (x)

                       (make-address x y))

                     chess-board-indices))

              chess-board-indices))

过程 make-chess-board-internal 创建表示格子的节点数组，表示形式是一个行列表，其中每一行又是该行各列的列表。它返回一个捆绑过程，其中包含少数几个用于操作棋盘的委托过程。The procedure make-chess-board-internal makes the array of nodes for squares as a list of rows, each of which is a list of columns for that row. It returns a bundle procedure with a handful of delegates to manipulate the board.

(define (make-chess-board-internal)

  (let ((nodes

         (map (lambda (x)

                (map (lambda (y)

                       (make-graph-node (string x "," y)))

                     chess-board-indices))

              chess-board-indices)))

    (let loop ((turn 0))

      See below for the delegate definitions.

      (bundle #f node-at piece-at piece-in address-of

              set-piece-at color next-turn))))

变量 turn 表示当前回合，从零开始。偶数回合由白方走，奇数回合由黑方走，如委托过程 color 所示：The turn variable is the current turn, starting with zero. Even turns are White, and odd turns are Black, as shown by the delegate procedure color:

(define (color) (if (white-move?) ’white ’black))

(define (white-move?) (even? turn))

委托过程 node-at 获取给定地址处的节点。如果当前是黑方回合，它就转换地址，并应用节点视图。The delegate procedure node-at gets the node at a given address. If this is a Black turn, it translates the address and applies the node view.

(define (node-at address)

  (define (get-node address)

    (list-ref (list-ref nodes (address-x address))

              (address-y address)))

  (if (white-move?)

      (get-node address)

      (graph-node-view (get-node (invert-address address))

                       rotate-180-view)))

node-at 的逆操作是委托过程 address-of。每个节点都有一条标签为 address 的边，以其地址为值。与 node-at 一样，如果当前是黑方走棋，返回的地址必须转换。The inverse of node-at is the delegate procedure address-of. Each node has an edge, labeled with address, with its address as the value. As with node-at, if this is a Black move the returned address must be translated.

(define (address-of node)

  (let ((address (node ’edge-value ’address)))

    (if (white-move?)

        address

        (invert-address address))))

委托过程 next-turn 在走完一步之后推进棋盘状态：The delegate procedure next-turn advances the board after a move is made:

(define (next-turn) (loop (+ turn 1)))

把格子与其邻居连接起来时，要通过地址运算处理边界情况（这里确实是棋盘边缘），在每个格子与其每个邻居之间创建一条带标签的边。它还为每个节点创建 address 边。Connecting the squares to their neighbors does address arithmetic to handle (literal) edge cases, creating a labeled edge between each square and each of its neighbors. It also creates the address edge for each node.

(define (connect-up-square address board)

  (let ((node (board ’node-at address)))

    (node ’connect! ’address address)

    (for-each-direction

     (lambda (label x-delta y-delta)

       (let ((x+ (+ (address-x address) x-delta))

             (y+ (+ (address-y address) y-delta)))

         (if (and (<= 0 x+ chess-board-last-index)

                  (<= 0 y+ chess-board-last-index))

             (node ’connect! label

                   (board ’node-at

                          (make-address x+ y+)))))))))



(define (for-each-direction procedure)

  (procedure ’north 0 1)

  (procedure ’northeast 1 1)

  (procedure ’east 1 0)

  (procedure 'southeast 1 -1)

  (procedure 'south 0 -1)

  (procedure 'southwest -1 -1)

  (procedure ’west -1 0)

  (procedure ’northwest -1 1))

地址表示为由列号和行号组成的列表：An address is represented as a list of column and row number:

(define (make-address x y) (list x y))

(define (address-x address) (car address))

(define (address-y address) (cadr address))



(define (address= a b)

  (and (= (address-x a) (address-x b))

       (= (address-y a) (address-y b))))



(define (invert-address address)

  (make-address (- chess-board-last-index

                   (address-x address))

                (- chess-board-last-index

                   (address-y address))))

棋子用包含棋子类型及其颜色的数据表示。我们的约定是：在第 n 回合，棋盘上的每个棋子都通过一条从其所在格子的节点出发、标签为 n 的边，与该节点相连。这是图不可变性带来的结果；否则，我们只需利用副作用修改那条边即可。为了在棋盘上摆放棋子，我们用标签为 0 的边，把每个棋子连接到其初始格子的节点上。A piece is represented by data incorporating its piece type and its color. Our convention is that at the nth turn, each piece on the board will be connected to the node representing the square it occupies by an edge from that node with the label n. This is a consequence of graph immutability; otherwise we could just use a side effect to modify the edge. To populate the board, we connect each piece to the node for its initial square with an edge labeled 0.

(define (populate-sides board)



  (define (populate-side color home-row pawn-row)



    (define (do-column col type)

      (add-piece col home-row type)

      (add-piece col pawn-row ’pawn))



    (define (add-piece col row type)

      ((board ’node-at (make-address col row))

        ’connect! 0 (make-piece type color)))



    (do-column 0 ’rook)

    (do-column 1 ’knight)

    (do-column 2 ’bishop)

    (do-column 3 ’queen)

    (do-column 4 ’king)

    (do-column 5 ’bishop)

    (do-column 6 ’knight)

    (do-column 7 ’rook))



  (populate-side ’white 0 1)

  (populate-side ’black 7 6))

现在我们可以开始一局棋了：We can now start a game:

(define the-board)



(define (start-chess-game)

  (set! the-board (make-chess-board))

  (print-chess-board the-board))

于是，我们得到这幅漂亮的棋盘图像：And we get this nice chessboard image:

4.5.5 国际象棋走法4.5.5 Chess moves

现在有了摆满棋子的棋盘，我们还需要一种移动这些棋子的方法。如果在某个回合，一个棋子位于某个特定格子，那么表示该格子的节点就有一条以该回合为标签的边，它的值就是这个棋子。第 218 页的 make-chess-board-internal 中，下列委托过程与此有关：Now that we have a chessboard, populated with pieces, we need a way to move those pieces around. If a piece is in a particular square at a particular turn, the node representing that square has an edge, with the turn as its label, whose value is the piece. The following delegate procedures in make-chess-board-internal on page 218 are relevant here:

(define (piece-at address)

  (piece-in (node-at address)))



(define (piece-in node)

  (and (node ’has-edge? turn)

       (node ’edge-value turn)))



(define (set-piece-at address piece)

  ((node-at address) ’connect! (+ turn 1) piece))

给定我们打算移动的棋子的地址，就可以用 piece-at 获取这个棋子。当然，检查明显的错误总是个好主意。We use piece-at to obtain a piece that we expect to move, given its address. Of course, it is always a good idea to check for obvious errors.

(define (get-piece-to-move board from)

  (let ((my-piece (board ’piece-at from)))

    (if (not my-piece)

        (error "No piece in this square:" from))

    (if (not (eq? (board ’color) (piece-color my-piece)))

        (error "Can move only one's own pieces:"

               my-piece from))

    my-piece))

真正走棋时，我们把棋子拿起来，再放到目标格中。不过，只有目标格为空，或者被一个可以吃掉的对方棋子占据时，才允许这样走。To actually make a move we pick the piece up and set it down in the target square. However, this move is allowed only if the target square is empty or if it is occupied by an opponent piece to be captured.

(define (simple-move board from to)

  (let ((my-piece (get-piece-to-move board from)))

    (let ((captured (board ’piece-at to)))

      (if (not (no-piece-or-opponent? captured my-piece))

          (error "Can't capture piece of same color:"

                 captured)))

    ;; The move looks good; make it so:

    (board 'set-piece-at to my-piece)

    ;; Now update all the unaffected pieces to

    ;; the next state of the board:

    (for-each (lambda (address)

                (if (not (or (address= from address)

                             (address= to address)))

                    (let ((p (board ’piece-at address)))

                      (if p

                          (board ’set-piece-at address p)))))

              board-addresses)

    (board ’next-turn)))

请注意，我们没有加入检查，来判断想要移动的棋子是否能按那样走。关于各类棋子合法走法的全部描述，只存在于我们在Notice that we didn't put in a check that the piece we want to move is able to make that move. Our only descriptions of the legal moves available to each kind of piece are in the graph patterns that we built in 第 4.5.3 节section 4.5.3中构建的图模式里。在第 225 页的练习 4.24 中，我们将修正这个问题。. In exercise 4.24 on page 225 we will fix this problem.

但首先，让我们用匹配器判断由这样一个路径模式描述的走法是否是在吃子：But first, let's use the matcher to determine whether a move described by such a path pattern is a capture:

(define (capture? board from path)

  (let* ((my-piece (get-piece-to-move board from))

         (dict

          (graph-match path

                       (match:extend-dict chess-board:var ;**

                                          board

                                          (match:new-dict))

                       (board ’node-at from))))

    (and dict

         (let* ((target (match:get-value 'target-node dict))

                (captured (board ’piece-in target)))

           (and captured

                ‘(capture ,my-piece

                          ,captured

                          ,(board ’address-of target)))))))

标有 ;** 的那一行在初始字典中加入一个特殊绑定，供某些需要查询棋盘的模式限制条件使用。The line marked by ;** adds a special binding in the initial dictionary, which is used by some pattern restrictions that need to interrogate the board.

为方便起见，chess-move 按一步走法更新棋盘，然后从下一位走棋者的视角打印棋盘。For convenience, chess-move updates the board with a move, then prints the board for the player who will move next.

(define (chess-move from to)

  (set! the-board (simple-move the-board from to))

  (print-chess-board the-board))

为了演示这段代码，我们可以摆出一个有趣的局面：To demonstrate this code we can make an interesting position:

(define (giuoco-piano-opening)

  (start-chess-game)

  (chess-move ’(4 1) ’(4 3))            ;W: P-K4

  (chess-move ’(3 1) ’(3 3))            ;B: P-K4

  (chess-move ’(6 0) ’(5 2))            ;W: N-KB3

  (chess-move ’(6 0) ’(5 2))            ;B: N-QB3

  (chess-move ’(5 0) ’(2 3))            ;W: B-QB4

  (chess-move ’(2 0) ’(5 3)))           ;B: B-QB4



(giuoco-piano-opening)

经过大量打印输出后，我们得到如下棋盘局面：After lots of printout, we obtain the following board position:

此时，位于王翼象线第 3 格的白马正在攻击王线第 5 格的黑兵。吃掉这个兵并不是好主意，因为它受到位于后翼象线第 6 格的黑马保护，而我们不应该用马去换兵。不过，我们可以使用马的走法中的一个图模式，检查这确实是一种可能的吃子走法：At this point the White Knight at King Bishop 3 is attacking the Black Pawn at King 5. It is not a good idea to take that piece because it is defended by the Black Knight at Queen-Bishop 6, and one should not exchange a knight for a pawn. However, we can use a graph pattern from the knight moves to check that this is a possible capture:

(capture? the-board

          (make-address 5 2)

          ‘((? source-node ,(occupied-by ’knight))

            north (?) north (?)

            west (? target-node ,maybe-opponent)))

(capture (knight white) (pawn black) (4 4))

事实上，这是这只马唯一可能的吃子走法：Indeed, it is the only possible capture for this knight:

(filter-map (lambda (path)

              (capture? the-board

                        (make-address 5 2)

                        path))

            all-knight-moves)

((capture (knight white) (pawn black) (4 4)))

练习 4.24：合法的国际象棋走法Exercise 4.24: Legal chess moves

在第 216 页的练习 4.23 中，我们为所有合法的国际象棋走法构建了一个模式库。修改 simple-move 程序（第 222 页），检查被移动的棋子是否可以按所要求的方式走。In exercise 4.23 on page 216 we made a library of patterns for all legal chess moves. Modify the simple-move program (page 222) to check that the piece being moved is allowed to move in the way requested.

4.5.6 实现图匹配4.5.6 Implementing graph matching

使用图模式的入口是：The entry point for using a graph pattern is:

(define (graph-match path dict object)

  ((gmatch:compile-path path) object dict

   (lambda (object* dict*)

     dict*)))

我们把路径模式编译成一个匹配过程，它接收作为起点的图对象（一个节点）、初始字典和成功续延。如果模式成功匹配了从该节点开始的一串边，它就调用成功续延，并传入匹配路径末端的节点（object*）以及匹配过程中积累的绑定字典，如前所述We compile the path pattern into a match procedure that takes the graph object (a node) to start from, an initial dictionary, and a success continuation. If the pattern successfully matches a sequence of edges starting with that node, it calls the success continuation, which takes the node (object*) at the end of the matched path and a dictionary of bindings accumulated in the match, as described in 第4.3节section 4.3。18 如果模式无法匹配给定对象，匹配过程就返回 #f。.18 If the pattern fails to match the given object the match procedure returns #f.

我们用来与图匹配的模式，是一种小型语言的表达式；我们希望将它们编译成匹配过程。图模式表达式的语法可以用 BNF 描述。这里，后缀 * 表示出现零次或多次，后缀 + 表示出现一次或多次，后缀 ? 表示出现零次或一次。中缀 | 表示备选项。用 " 括起来的项是字面字符串。例如，匹配单个元素的模式变量以 (? 开始，可以有名称和谓词，也可以没有，最后以 ) 结束。The patterns that we are using for matching against graphs are expressions of a small language that we want to compile into match procedures. The syntax of graph-pattern expressions can be described in BNF. Here a postfix * indicates 0 or more occurrences, postfix + indicates 1 or more, and postfix ? indicates 0 or 1 occurrence. An infix | indicates alternatives. Items surrounded in " are literal strings. For example, a pattern variable to match a single element starts with (?, has an optional name and optional predicate, and ends with ).

<edge> = <edge-label> <target>

<edge-label> = <symbol>

<target> = <node-var> | <object-var> | <constant>

<node-var> = <single-var>

<object-var> = <single-var> | <sequence-var>

<single-var> = "(?" <var-name>? <unary-predicate>? ")"

<sequence-var> = "(?*" <var-name>? <unary-predicate>? ")"

<var-name> = <symbol>



<path> = <node-var> <path-elements>

<path-elements> = <path-element>*



<path-element> =

    <edge>

  | "(*" <path-elements> ")" ; repeat any number of times

  | "(+" <path-elements> ")"  ; repeat at least once

  | "(opt" <path-elements> ")"  ; one or zero instances

  | "(or" <ppath-elements>+ ")"

  | "(and" <ppath-elements>+ ")"

<ppath-elements> = "(" <path-elements> ")"

在我们的图匹配语言中，图中的每条路径都从一个节点变量开始。节点变量是单元素变量，满足谓词 match:element-var?。我们如下编译路径：In our graph-matching language every path in a graph starts with a node variable. A node variable is a single-element variable, which satisfies the predicate match:element-var?. We compile a path as follows:

(define (gmatch:compile-path path)

  (if (and (pair? path) (match:element-var? (car path)))

      (gmatch:finish-compile-path (cdr path)

        (gmatch:compile-var (car path)))

      (error "Ill-formed path:" path)))

这里我们检查 path 的第一个元素是不是元素变量；如果是，就把它编译成变量匹配器。路径的其余部分（如果有）由 finish-compile-path 编译：19Here we check that the first element of path is an element variable; if so, we compile it into a variable matcher. The remainder of the path, if any, is compiled by finish-compile-path:19

(define (gmatch:finish-compile-path rest-elts matcher)

  (if (null? rest-elts)

      matcher

      (gmatch:seq2 matcher

                   (gmatch:compile-path-elts rest-elts))))

其中，seq2 产生一个匹配过程，依次使用作为参数传入的各个匹配过程进行匹配：where seq2 produces a match procedure that sequentially matches its match-procedure arguments:

(define (gmatch:seq2 match-first match-rest)

  (define (match-seq object dict succeed)

    (match-first object dict

                 (lambda (object* dict*)

                   (match-rest object* dict* succeed))))

  match-seq)

由 compile-var 产生的变量匹配器 match-first 将匹配路径的初始节点；然后，compile-path-elts 的结果（match-rest）使用所得字典 dict*，从边 object* 开始匹配路径的其余部分。The variable matcher match-first, produced by compile-var, will match the initial node of the path, and the resulting dictionary dict* is then used by the result of compile-path-elts (match-rest) to match the remainder of the path, starting with the edge object*.

编译路径元素模式时，只有几种情况：路径或者以边标签和目标节点开始，或者以特殊匹配形式（*、+、opt、or、and）开始：There are only a few cases for compiling path-element patterns. Either the path starts with an edge label and a target node, or it starts with a special match form (*, +, opt, or, and):

(define (gmatch:compile-path-elts elts)

  (let ((elt (car elts))

        (rest (cdr elts)))

    (cond ((and (symbol? elt) (pair? rest))

           (gmatch:finish-compile-path (cdr rest)

             (gmatch:compile-edge elt (car rest))))

          ((pair? elt)

           (gmatch:finish-compile-path rest

             (gmatch:compile-path-elt elt)))

          (else

           (error "Ill-formed path elements:" elts)))))

边的标签可以是任意符号，只要它不是图匹配器模式所用的特殊符号（*、+、opt、or、and）之一。于是，简单带标签边的匹配器可以这样编译：An edge may be labeled by any symbol that is not one of the special symbols (*, +, opt, or, and) used by graph-matcher patterns. The matcher for a simple labeled edge is then compiled by:

(define (gmatch:compile-edge label target)

  (let ((match-target (gmatch:compile-target target)))

    (define (match-edge object dict succeed)

      (and (graph-node? object)

           (object ’has-edge? label)

           (match-target (object ’edge-value label)

                         dict succeed)))

    match-edge))

边匹配器 match-edge 检查对象是否为图节点、是否有一条给定标签的边从该对象出发，以及这条边的目标（edge-value）能否（使用 match-target）匹配图匹配模式中的目标模式。match-edge 中使用的匹配过程 match-target 是由编译器 compile-target 创建的。The edge matcher, match-edge, checks that the object is a graph node, that there is an edge with the given label emanating from that object, and that the target of the edge (the edge-value) will match (using match-target) the pattern for the target in the graph-match pattern. The match procedure match-target used in match-edge is made by the compiler compile-target.

编译目标时只有两种可能：变量或常量。There are only two possibilities when compiling a target: a variable or a constant.

(define (gmatch:compile-target elt)

  (if (match:var? elt)

      (gmatch:compile-var elt)

      (let ()

        (define (match-constant object dict succeed)

          (and (eqv? elt object)

               (succeed object dict)))

        match-constant)))

特殊匹配形式由 compile-path-elt 处理：The special match forms are handled by compile-path-elt:

(define (gmatch:compile-path-elt elt)

  (let ((keyword (car elt))

        (args (cdr elt)))

    (case keyword

      ((*) (gmatch:compile-* args))

      ((+) (gmatch:compile-+ args))

      ((opt) (gmatch:compile-opt args))

      ((or) (gmatch:compile-or args))

      ((and) (gmatch:compile-and args))

      (else (error "Ill-formed path element:" elt)))))

编译带有可选路径元素的模式，工作方式如下：用那段可选路径元素序列的路径元素模式，递归调用 compile-path-elts，得到 matcher，即路径中可有可无的那些元素的匹配器。把 match-opt 应用于一个图节点对象时，就应用这些路径元素的匹配器；但如果它失败，返回 #f，则以原始对象和原始字典作为结果，使匹配成功。Compiling a pattern with optional path elements works as follows: There is a recursive call to compile-path-elts with the path element patterns for the optional sequence of path elements, to obtain matcher, the matcher for the elements that are optionally present in the path. When match-opt is applied to a graph node object, the matcher for those path elements is applied; but if it fails, returning #f, the match succeeds with the original object and the original dictionary.

(define (gmatch:compile-opt elts)

  (let ((matcher (gmatch:compile-path-elts elts)))

    (define (match-opt object dict succeed)

      (or (matcher object dict succeed)

          (succeed object dict)))

    match-opt))

含有重复路径元素的模式，例如第 215 页 basic-queen-moves 中的模式 (* north (?* ,unoccupied))，按下面的方式编译：A pattern with repeated path elements, for example the pattern (* north (?* ,unoccupied)) in basic-queen-moves on page 215, is compiled like this:

(define (gmatch:compile-* elts)

  (gmatch:* (gmatch:compile-path-elts elts)))

与要求可选路径元素序列的模式一样，编译器递归调用自身，得到可能重复出现的序列的匹配器，再将其传给 gmatch:*：As for a pattern requiring an optional sequence of path elements, the compiler is called recursively to obtain a matcher for the potentially repeated sequence, which is then passed to gmatch:*:

(define (gmatch:* matcher)

  (define (match-* object dict succeed)

    (or (matcher object dict

                 (lambda (object* dict*)

                   (match-* object* dict* succeed)))

        (succeed object dict)))

  match-*)

图模式匹配器 match-* 尝试把传给它的 matcher 应用于所提供的图节点对象。如果成功，match-* 就递归调用自身，尝试匹配从上次匹配结束处开始的那部分图。最终它会无法继续前进，此时便以 matcher 未能匹配的图对象作为结果，使匹配成功。The graph-pattern matcher match-* tries to use the matcher passed to it on the graph node object supplied. If it succeeds, match-* calls itself recursively to try the part of the graph where the last match left off. Eventually it will fail to progress, succeeding with the graph object that matcher failed on.

编译要求路径元素序列至少重复一次、也可能重复多次的模式（用 + 表示），与编译 * 类似。它像上面一样使用 gmatch:*，但要求先匹配至少一个元素：Compiling patterns requiring at least one, but possibly many, repetitions of a sequence of path elements, indicated with +, is similar to *. It uses gmatch:* as above, but requires at least one matching element first:

(define (gmatch:compile-+ elts)

  (let ((matcher (gmatch:compile-path-elts elts)))

    (gmatch:seq2 matcher (gmatch:* matcher))))

剩下的特殊路径模式是 and 和 or，每种都包含若干子路径模式。and 元素必须匹配从当前节点开始的所有子路径模式。or 元素则必须匹配从当前节点开始的至少一个子路径模式。The remaining special path patterns are and and or, each of which contains a number of subpath patterns. An and element must match all of the subpath patterns starting at the current node. An or element must match at least one of the subpath patterns starting at the current node.

(define (gmatch:compile-and elt-lists)

  (gmatch:and (map gmatch:compile-path-elts elt-lists)))



(define (gmatch:compile-or elt-lists)

  (gmatch:or (map gmatch:compile-path-elts elt-lists)))

真正的工作在过程 and 和 or 中进行：The procedures and and or are where the real work happens:

(define (gmatch:and matchers)

  (lambda (object dict succeed)

    (if (null? matchers)

        (succeed object dict)

        (let loop ((matchers matchers) (dict dict))

          ((car matchers) object dict

           (if (null? (cdr matchers))

               succeed

               (lambda (object* dict*)

                 (loop (cdr matchers) dict*))))))))



(define (gmatch:or matchers)

  (lambda (object dict succeed)

    (let loop ((matchers matchers))

      (if (pair? matchers)

          (or ((car matchers) object dict succeed)

              (loop (cdr matchers)))

          #f))))

过程 compile-var 编译模式变量。它由 compile-path 和 compile-target 调用，并用四种互斥的情况处理具有或不具有可选名称和谓词的变量：The procedure compile-var compiles a pattern variable. It is called from compile-path and compile-target, and has four mutually exclusive cases to handle variables with or without the optional name and predicate:

(define (gmatch:compile-var var)

  (cond ((match-list? var gmatch:var-type?)

         (gmatch:var-matcher (car var) #f #f))

        ((match-list? var gmatch:var-type? symbol?)

         (gmatch:var-matcher (car var) (cadr var) #f))

        ((match-list? var gmatch:var-type? symbol? procedure?)

         (gmatch:var-matcher (car var) (cadr var) (caddr var)))

        ((match-list? var gmatch:var-type? procedure?)

         (gmatch:var-matcher (car var) #f (cadr var)))

        (else

         (error "Ill-formed variable:" var))))

过程 var-type? 匹配模式变量的类型符号：? 或 ?*。为了识别这四种变量情况，compile-var 使用工具过程 match-list?；当其第一个参数是列表，且列表中的每个元素都满足对应的谓词参数时，它就为真。The procedure var-type? matches the type symbol of a pattern variable: ? or ?*. To recognize the four cases of variables, compile-var uses a utility procedure match-list?, which is true if its first argument is a list and each element of the list satisfies the corresponding predicate argument.

(define (match-list? datum . preds)

  (let loop ((preds preds) (datum datum))

    (if (pair? preds)

        (and (pair? datum)

             ((car preds) (car datum))

             (loop (cdr preds) (cdr datum)))

        (null? datum))))

既然已经解读了变量的语法，过程 var-matcher 就是变量的匹配器。The procedure var-matcher is the matcher for variables, now that we have decoded their syntax.

(define (gmatch:var-matcher var-type var-name restriction)

  (define (match-var object dict succeed)

    (and (or (not restriction)

             (restriction object dict))

         (if var-name

             (let ((dict*

                    (gmatch:bind var-type var-name object

                                 dict)))

               (and dict*

                    (succeed object dict*)))

             (succeed object dict))))

  match-var)

这里，bind 为 var-name 加入一个值为 object 的绑定，返回一个新字典。如果字典中已有这样的绑定，而其值不同于 object，那么 bind 就返回 #f，表示匹配失败。Here bind adds a binding for var-name with value object, returning a new dictionary. If the dictionary already has such a binding, and its value is different from object, bind returns #f to indicate a match failure.

至此，我们就完成了图匹配器。And with this we have finished the graph matcher.

练习 4.25：图匹配Exercise 4.25: Graph matching

这里描述的图匹配器非常有用，但有些问题并不适合用它处理。有什么有趣的问题需要扩展这个匹配器呢？找出这样一个问题，定义并实现所需的扩展，再用一些例子演示它的用法。The graph matcher described here is very useful, but there are problems for which it isn't well suited. What is an interesting problem that requires extension(s) to the matcher? Find such a problem, define and implement the extension(s), and demonstrate its use on some examples.

4.6 小结4.6 Summary

模式很有趣，但它们也是一种非常实用的方式，可以将系统各部分组织得便于添加扩展。本章中，我们看到了如何构建项重写系统。基于规则的项重写系统让我们能够轻松编写程序，不断把表达式的某些部分替换为“等价”部分，直到没有规则可再应用时才终止。这类系统是进行符号操作的大型系统的重要组成部分。代数表达式化简是一种应用，但编译器也会进行大量这样的操作，以完成优化，有时还用于生成代码。Patterns are fun, but they are also a very useful way to organize parts of a system for additivity. In this chapter we have seen how to build a term-rewriting system. A rule-based term-rewriting system makes it easy to write programs that do successive replacements of parts of an expression with “equivalent” parts, terminating when no more rules are applicable. Such systems are important components of larger systems that do symbolic manipulation. Algebraic expression simplification is one application, but compilers do huge amounts of this kind of manipulation, to compute optimizations and sometimes to generate code.

我们还看到了一种构建模式匹配器的灵活方法：把模式“编译”为简单匹配器的组合，而所有这些匹配器都具有相同的接口结构。这样既容易加入新特性，也容易使这种系统非常高效。当我们给这样的匹配器加入可匹配未指定数量元素的片段变量时，就会发现必须实现一个回溯系统，因为如果模式包含不止一个片段变量，那么对任何特定数据都可能有多个匹配结果。这使事情复杂了很多。除了回溯本身固有的复杂性之外，还必须把模式匹配器中的回溯与使用这些模式的规则执行机构中的回溯系统衔接起来。我们将在第 5.4 节研究处理回溯的更一般方法，并在第 7.5.2 节探讨更强大的回溯策略。We also saw a flexible way to construct a pattern matcher, by “compiling” a pattern into a combination of simple matchers that all have the same interface structure. This makes it easy to add new features and to make such a system very efficient. When we add segment variables, which match an unspecified number of elements, to such a matcher we find that we have to implement a backtracking system, because there may be multiple possible matches to any particular data if the pattern has more than one segment variable. This complicates matters significantly. Besides the intrinsic complexity of backtracking, the backtracking in the pattern matcher must be interfaced to the backtracking system in the rule executive that uses the patterns. We will examine more general ways of dealing with backtracking in section 5.4. We will investigate even more powerful backtracking strategies in section 7.5.2.

如果把部分指定的数据建模为带有空缺（由模式变量表示）的模式，那么我们就会发现，需要让模式相互匹配，收集数据所受的约束，从而使其规格更加明确。我们探索了合一：将这类部分信息结构合并的过程。这实际上是一种为数据中缺失的部分建立并求解符号方程的方法。合一非常强大，我们展示了如何以这种方式利用合一构建一个简单的类型推断引擎。If we model partially specified data as patterns with holes (represented by pattern variables), then we find that we need to match patterns against each other to collect the constraints on the data so that we can sharpen the specification. We explored unification: the process of merging partial information structures of this kind. This is essentially a way of setting up and solving symbolic equations for the missing parts of the data. Unification is very powerful, and we showed how to make a simple type-inference engine using unification in this way.

我们发现，模式匹配的思想可以扩展到一般的图，而不仅仅用于层次化表达式。这使处理国际象棋棋盘这样的复杂图变得容易；我们用模式指定了合法的国际象棋走法。模式和模式匹配可以成为表达计算思想的一种方式，而且在某些问题上，它们比其他编程方法更能揭示问题的本质。但要小心：模式匹配并不是解决世间所有问题的答案，所以不要沉迷于它。We found that the ideas of pattern matching can be extended to operate on general graphs rather than just hierarchical expressions. This made it easy to work with such complex graphs as chess boards, where we used patterns to specify legal chess moves. Patterns and pattern matching can be a way to express computational thought, and on some problems can be more revealing than other programming methods. But be careful: pattern matching is not the answer to all of the world's problems, so let's not become addicted to it.

 

1 当然，在假定所处理的是数的情况下，一个非常聪明的匹配器可以推导出 y=0。1 Of course, a very clever matcher could deduce that y=0, under the assumption that we are dealing with numbers.
2 关于这种成功／失败模式的更多示例与解释，见第 273 页的第 5.4.2 节。2 See section 5.4.2 on page 273 for more examples and explanation of this success/failure pattern.
3 这种构建模式匹配器的策略最早由 Carl Hewitt 在他的博士论文 [56] 中描述。3 This strategy for building pattern matchers was first described by Carl Hewitt in his PhD thesis [56].
4 对于只含元素变量的模式，合一子是唯一的。这是一个定理，我们不在这里证明。在4 The unifier is unique for patterns with only element variables. This is a theorem; we will not prove it here. In 第4.4.4节section 4.4.4中，我们将扩展合一器，使其支持片段变量。不过，当模式含有片段变量时，合一通常会产生多个匹配结果。 we will extend our unifier to include segment variables. However, when the patterns have segment variables, unification will generally yield multiple matches.
5 关于合一的全面综述，见 [6]。5 For an extensive survey of unification see [6].
6 在这个合一器的内部，发生失败时显式调用失败续延是很方便的。但在 unify:internal 中，我们转而采用另一种表示失败的约定：从成功续延返回 #f。这样做是为了让合一器的使用约定与前述匹配器的使用约定相同6 In the guts of this unifier it is convenient for a failure to make an explicit call to a failure continuation. But in unify:internal we transition to a different convention for indicating a failure: returning #f from a success continuation. This is to make the convention for use of the unifier the same as the convention for use of the matcher of 第4.3节section 4.3。这是一个有趣的转换。在.This is an interesting transition. In the rule system in 第 4.2.2 节section 4.2.2的规则系统中，我们使用了显式的成功续延和失败续延，因此，为了在规则系统中使用匹配器，我们必须进行反向转换：匹配器采用 #f 约定，所以 make-rule（第 166 页）必须实现这一转换。在回溯系统中，选择哪一种约定来实现失败通常是风格问题，但使用显式失败续延往往更容易扩展。幸运的是，在这些不同的回溯实现方式之间建立接口很容易。 we used explicit success and failure continuations, so to use the matcher in the rule system we had to make the reverse transition: the matcher used the #f convention, so make-rule (on page 166) had to implement the transition.The choice of convention for implementing failure in a backtracking system is usually a matter of style, but the use of an explicit failure continuation is often easier to extend. Luckily, it is easy to interface these disparate ways of implementing backtracking.
7 与前述模式匹配系统一样7 As in the pattern matching system described in 第4.3节section 4.3，合一匹配器围绕项列表组织，以便日后扩展到片段变量。, the unification matcher is organized around lists of terms to allow later extension to segment variables.
8 在合一的文献中，这称为“出现检查”。出现检查用于避免尝试求解 x = f(x) 这样的方程。如果我们对函数 f 有更多了解，这样的不动点方程在某些情况下或许可以求解，但这个合一器是语法匹配器。我们可以在这里设置一个钩子，请更强大的方程求解器帮忙，不过我们并没有这么做。大多数 Prolog 系统出于效率考虑，不实现出现检查。8 In the unification literature this is called the “occurs check.” The occurs check is used to prevent trying to obtain a solution to an equation like x = f(x). Such a fixed-point equation may be solvable, in some cases, if we know more about the function f, but this unifier is a syntactic matcher. One could put in a hook at this point to ask for a more powerful equation solver to help, but we are not doing that. Most Prolog systems avoid implementing the occurs check for efficiency reasons.
9 由于合一非常重要，人们在开发高效算法方面做了大量工作。使用记忆化可以带来很大的改进。关于合一算法的全面论述，见 [6]。9 Because unification is so important, there has been a great deal of work developing efficient algorithms. Memoization can be used to make large improvements. For an extensive exposition of unification algorithms see [6].
10 其他人也曾为模式匹配器或合一器加入片段变量 [5]，并取得了一定成功。看来有些 Prolog 版本支持片段变量 [34]。Kutsia 的博士论文 [79] 对一种在合一器中包含序列变量（片段变量的另一个名称）的算法进行了详细的理论论述。不过，这里我们并不打算构建完整且正确的片段合一器。我们只是想说明，为已经构建好的基本合一过程添加一些有用的新行为是多么容易。10 Others have added segment variables to pattern matchers or unifiers [5], with some success. Apparently there are versions of Prolog that have segment variables [34]. A detailed theoretical treatment of an algorithm that includes sequence variables (another name for segment variables) in a unifier can be found in Kutsia's PhD thesis [79]. However, here we are not trying to build a complete and correct segment unifier. We are just trying to show how easy it is to add some useful new behavior to the elementary unification procedure already built.
11 扩展到片段的过程非常微妙。感谢 Kenny Chen、Will Byrd 和 Michael Ballantyne 帮助我们思考这个实验。11 The extension to segments is very subtle. We thank Kenny Chen, Will Byrd, and Michael Ballantyne for helping us think about this experiment.
12 过程 complement 是谓词的组合子：complement 创建一个新谓词，它是其参数的否定。12 The procedure complement is a combinator for predicates: complement makes a new predicate that is the negation of its argument.
13 这是单向匹配，用前面的匹配器也能完成；不过，能够匹配双方都带有变量的表达式，这种能力很有用。13 This is a one-sided match that could also be done with the earlier matcher, but this ability to match expressions with variables on both sides of the match is useful.
14 图节点的使用示例，见第 210 页的 g:cons。关于捆绑过程的更完整说明，见第 395 页。14 For an example of how a graph node is used, see g:cons on page 210. For a more complete description of bundle procedures see page 395.
15 王车易位是另一种特殊情况。只有在受限条件下才允许王车易位：王和车都处于初始位置，王与车之间的格子均未被占据，王当前没有被将军，而且不必经过或落在会使其被将军的格子上。15 Castling is another special case. Castling is allowed under restricted circumstances: when the king and the rook are in their initial positions, the squares between the king and rook are unoccupied, and the king is not in check and will not have to traverse or land in a square where it would be in check.
16 还有一种兵的走法，即吃过路兵，它取决于对方上一步的走法。16 There is also a pawn move, en passant capture, that depends on the opponent's previous move.
17 我们采用从零开始的索引，这与国际象棋的传统约定不同，但除了与棋手进行输入输出之外，这一点并不重要。17 We use zero-based indexing, unlike the traditional chess conventions, but this is not important except for input and output to players.
18 但请注意，图匹配器过程的成功续延与表达式匹配器过程的成功续延不同。表达式匹配器的成功续延接收字典以及匹配器消耗的元素数量（这是为了支持片段）；图匹配器的成功续延则接收最终节点，以及匹配图中被匹配部分所得到的字典。18 But notice that the success continuation of the graph-matcher procedure is different from the success continuation of the expression-matcher procedure. The expression-matcher success continuation takes a dictionary and a number of elements eaten by the matcher (to make segments work), whereas the graph-matcher success continuation takes the final node and the dictionary resulting from matching the matched part of the graph.
19 尽管过程的实际名称是 gmatch:finish-compile-path，我们在文字说明中会缩写这样的名称，省略 gmatch: 前缀。19 Although the actual name of the procedure is gmatch:finish-compile-path, we abbreviate such names to elide the gmatch: prefix in text explanations.

5 求值5 

Evaluation

解决问题的最佳方法之一，是设计一种领域专用语言，让解决方案能够在其中轻松表达。如果你设计的语言足够强大，那么许多与你正在解决的问题相似的问题，也都能用这种语言轻松表达解决方案。如果一开始就采用灵活的机制，这种策略会尤其有效。我们在第 2、3、4 章的有限情境中探索过这个想法。这里，我们将以完全一般的方式继续探究它。One of the best ways to attack a problem is to make up a domain-specific language in which the solution is easily expressed. If the language you make up is powerful enough, many problems that are similar to the one you are attacking will have easy-to-express solutions in your language. This strategy is especially effective if you start with a flexible mechanism. We explored this idea in limited contexts in chapters 2, 3, and 4. Here we will pursue this idea in full generality.

设计一种语言时，我们必须赋予它含义。如果希望这种语言的表达式描述计算过程，就必须构建一种机制：给它这种语言的表达式，它就展开所需的过程。解释器正是这样的机制。我们将从应用序 Scheme eval/apply 解释器的一个可扩展版本开始，探索这个富有创造性的领域；它类似于 SICP [1] 第 4 章描述的解释器。When we make up a language we must give it meaning. If we want the expressions of the language to describe computational processes, we must build a mechanism that, when given expressions in the language, evolves the desired process. An interpreter is just such a mechanism. We will explore this creative realm starting with an extensible version of the applicative order Scheme eval/apply interpreter similar to the ones described in SICP [1], Chapter 4.

Scheme 过程是严格的，要求进入过程体之前先对每个参数求值。接下来，我们将推广解释器，在过程的形式参数列表中加入声明。这些声明允许过程把对应参数的求值推迟到真正需要其值的时候，从而提供惰性求值，并且可以选择是否对该值进行记忆化。这个声明机制还可以用于其他信息，例如类型和单位。Scheme procedures are strict, requiring each argument to be evaluated before the body of the procedure is entered. We next generalize our interpreter, adding declarations to the formal parameter list of a procedure. These declarations will allow a procedure to defer evaluation of the corresponding argument to when its value is actually needed, providing for lazy evaluation, with or without memoization of the value. This declaration mechanism can also be used for other information, such as types and units.

解释器的效率相当低，因为它必须分析要解释的表达式，才能知道每一步该做什么。解释器每次遇到同一个表达式，都会重复这项工作。因此，接下来我们将把解释分成两个阶段：分析与执行。分析阶段检查表达式，并编译出一个执行过程；调用该过程时，它就会完成表达式所表达的意图。执行过程运行时不需要访问编译它所依据的表达式。所有执行过程都具有相同的形式，构成一个组合子系统。An interpreter is rather inefficient, because it must analyze the expression to be interpreted in order to know what to do at each step. This effort is repeated each time the interpreter encounters the same expression. So we next separate the interpretation into two phases, analysis and execution. The analysis phase examines the expression and compiles an execution procedure, which when called will perform the intent of the expression. The execution procedure runs without access to the expression it was compiled from. The execution procedures all have the same form, and constitute a system of combinators.

接下来，我们加入 McCarthy 的 amb 运算符，以进行非确定性求值与搜索。值得注意的是，这不需要修改求值器的分析部分。唯一需要改变的是执行过程的形式，将它们改写为续延传递风格。采用续延传递风格启发我们把底层续延暴露给程序员。We next add McCarthy's amb operator to allow us to do nondeterministic evaluation and search. Remarkably, this requires no change to the analysis part of the evaluator. The only change required is in the format of the execution procedures, which are re-expressed in continuation-passing style. The use of continuation-passing style suggests exposing the underlying continuation to the programmer.

暴露底层续延的过程 call/cc 是 Scheme 的标准过程，而事实证明，只需 call/cc 就能直接在 Scheme 中实现 amb，因此，我们最后将展示如何做到这一点。The procedure call/cc that exposes the underlying continuation is a standard procedure in Scheme, and it turns out that all we need is call/cc to implement amb directly in Scheme, so we conclude by showing how to do this.

5.1 泛型 eval/apply 解释器5.1 Generic eval/apply interpreter

我们的第一个解释器将以可扩展的方式构建。所有重要部分都是泛型过程，而且我们会小心避免不必要的预先限定。开始吧。Our first interpreter is constructed to be extensible. All significant parts are generic procedures, and we are careful to avoid unnecessary commitments. Let's start.

解释器的精髓在于两个过程：eval 和 apply。过程 eval 接收表达式和环境作为输入。表达式是由子表达式通过语法粘合而成的组合。环境赋予表达式中出现的某些符号以含义。另一些符号的含义则固定在 eval 的定义中。1 不过，大多数表达式都被解释为运算符与运算对象的组合。对运算符求值应当得到一个过程，对运算对象求值应当得到实参。然后，把过程和实参传给 apply。过程通常用形式参数来命名这些实参。过程 apply 在一个把该过程的形式参数绑定到实参的环境中，对过程体（使用 eval）求值。这就是解释器的核心计算循环。The essence of the interpreter is in two procedures: eval and apply. The procedure eval takes an expression and an environment as inputs. The expression is a combination of subexpressions that are syntactically glued together. The environment gives meanings to some of the symbols that appear in the expression. There are other symbols that have meanings that are fixed in the definition of eval.1 But most expressions are interpreted as combinations of an operator and operands. Evaluation of the operator should yield a procedure and evaluation of the operands should yield arguments. The procedure and arguments are then passed to apply. The procedure usually names the arguments with formal parameters. The procedure apply evaluates the body of the procedure (using eval) in an environment in which the formal parameters of the procedure are bound to the arguments. This is the central computational loop of the interpreter.

我们刚才描述的是传统的应用序解释器方案。在我们的解释器中，我们将把尚未求值的运算对象以及对它们求值所需的环境传给 apply，从而能够实现多种求值策略，例如正则序和应用序。What we just described is the traditional applicative-order interpreter plan. In our interpreter we will pass the unevaluated operands and the environment for their evaluation to apply to make it possible to implement a variety of evaluation strategies, such as normal order as well as applicative order.

我们要实现的语言是 Lisp 的一种变体。2 这意味着代码表示为列表结构。在 Lisp 中，所有复合表达式都是列表，其中有些以特定关键字开头。具有特定关键字的复合表达式称为特殊形式。不是特殊形式的复合表达式，则被解释为将过程应用于实参。实现将按每种表达式类型的一组规则来组织，但应用除外，因为应用的识别依据恰恰是它不是特殊形式。我们在给出每条规则时，也给出相应表达式类型的语法定义。这种策略几乎可以用于实现任何语言，不过需要一个新的语法分析器。对于 Lisp，读取器把输入的字符串转换为列表结构，这些结构是该语言抽象语法树（AST）的自然表示。对于其他语言，AST 更为复杂，语法分析器也复杂得多。The language we will be implementing is a Lisp variant.2 This implies that the code is expressed as list structures. In Lisp all compound expressions are lists, some of which start with distinguished keywords. Compound expressions that have distinguished keywords are called special forms. The compound expressions that are not special forms are interpreted as applications of procedures to arguments. The implementation will be organized as a set of rules for each expression type, with the exception of applications, which are distinguished by not being special forms. With each rule we give the syntactic definition of the expression type. This strategy can be used to implement almost any language, though a new parser would be needed. With Lisp the reader converts the character-string input into list structures, which are natural representations of the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the language. With other languages the AST is more elaborate and the parser is much more complicated.

5.1.1 eval

我们把 g:eval 定义为一个具有两个参数的泛型过程。We define g:eval as a generic procedure with two arguments.

(define g:eval

  (simple-generic-procedure ’eval 2 default-eval))

eval 的默认情况是应用（有时也称为组合式）。The default case for eval is an application (sometimes described as a combination).

(define (default-eval expression environment)

  (cond ((application? expression)

         (g:apply (g:advance

                   (g:eval (operator expression)

                           environment))

                  (operands expression)

                  environment))

        (else

         (error "Unknown expression type" expression))))

在基于 Lisp 的语言中，表示应用的列表以第一个元素为运算符，其余元素为运算对象。In Lisp-based languages the operator of a list representing an application is the first element of the list and the operands are the rest of the elements of the list.

(define (application? exp) (pair? exp))

(define (operator app) (car app))

(define (operands app) (cdr app))

注意，上面的代码如何遵循我们在第 235 页描述的模式。我们同时给出了某个特定语法构造（应用）的解释方式及其语法定义。另外，正如那里所解释的，必须把应用作为泛型过程的默认情况来处理，因为 Lisp 中没有专门的关键字用来标识应用；相反，识别应用的依据是：它是一个不以任何特定关键字开头的列表。Note how the code above follows the pattern we described on page 235. We are presenting both the interpretation of a particular syntactic construct (application), and the definition of its syntax. Also as we explained there, it is necessary to handle applications as the default case of the generic procedure, because there is no special keyword identifying an application in Lisp—instead it is identified by being a list not starting with one of the distinguished keywords.

应用首先对表达式的运算符部分求值，然后把所得值与表达式的运算对象以及当前环境一起传给 g:apply。不过，对运算符求值后，我们会先把这个值传给泛型过程 g:advance。g:advance 的作用是继续那些被推迟的求值。在An application first evaluates the operator part of the expression and then passes that value to g:apply along with the operands of the expression and the current environment. However, after evaluating the operator, we pass the value to the generic procedure g:advance. The purpose of g:advance is to continue evaluations that have been postponed. We will not need to postpone evaluations until 第 5.2 节section 5.2之前，我们还不需要推迟求值，因此在那之前，g:advance 只是一个恒等函数：3, so until then g:advance is just an identity function:3

(define g:advance

  (simple-generic-procedure ’g:advance 1 (lambda (x) x)))

这不是定义 apply 的传统方式。通过传递尚未求值的运算对象以及应用所在的环境，我们保留了既引入正则序求值、也引入应用序求值的选择；同时也使形式参数声明的实现成为可能，或许还为其他选择留下了空间。This is not the traditional way that apply is defined. By passing along the unevaluated operands and the environment of the application we leave open the option to introduce normal-order evaluation as well as applicative-order evaluation; we also enable the implementation of declarations on the formal parameters, and perhaps some other options.

对于每一种非应用表达式类型，我们都提供一个处理过程。自求值表达式返回它们自身：For each non-application expression type we provide a handler. Self-evaluating expressions return themselves:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args self-evaluating? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment) expression))

在 Lisp 语言中，自求值表达式包括数、布尔值和字符串。在 Scheme 中，number? 是一个相当复杂的谓词。满足 number? 的对象包括任意大小的整数、有理分数、实数和复数。4In Lisp languages the self-evaluating expressions include the numbers, the boolean values, and strings. In Scheme, number? is a rather complicated predicate. The objects that satisfy number? include integers of arbitrary size, rational fractions, reals, and complex numbers.4

(define (self-evaluating? exp)

  (or (number? exp)

      (boolean? exp)

      (string? exp)))

还可能存在其他自求值表达式，因此，为了真正灵活地支持这种选择，我们本可以把 self-evaluating? 定义为泛型过程。不过这里没有必要，因为要定义我们可能想添加的任何其他自求值表达式类型，只需为 g:eval 再创建一个处理过程即可。There may be other self-evaluating expressions, so to make that option really flexible we could have defined self-evaluating? as a generic procedure. But here this is not necessary, because we could just make another handler for g:eval to define any other self-evaluating expression type that we might want to add.

允许操作语言自身符号表达式的语言，需要引用。5 引用是一种保护子表达式、使其不被求值的表达式。Quotations are required in languages that allow manipulation of the symbolic expressions of the language.5 A quotation is an expression that protects a subexpression from evaluation.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args quoted? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (text-of-quotation expression)))

在基于 Lisp 的语言中，引用表达式的列表结构表示，是以关键字 quote 开头的列表。Lisp 的读取器（语法分析器）会把任何以单引号字符开头的表达式（例如 ’(a b c)）展开为引用表达式（这里是 (quote (a b c))）。In Lisp-based languages the list-structure representation of a quoted expression is a list beginning with the keyword quote. The reader (parser) for Lisp expands any expression beginning with an apostrophe character (e.g., ’(a b c)) into a quoted expression (here (quote (a b c))).

(define (quoted? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’quote))

(define (text-of-quotation quot) (cadr quot))

带标签列表就是以某个给定的唯一符号开头的列表：A tagged list is just a list beginning with a given unique symbol:

(define (tagged-list? e t) (and (pair? e) (eq? (car e) t)))

对 Scheme 变量，只需在环境中查找即可。其他语言关于变量有更复杂的规则。例如，C 中有左值和右值，二者的处理方式不同。Scheme variables are just looked up in the environment. In other languages there are more complex rules about variables. For example, in C there are lvalues and rvalues, and they are handled differently.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args variable? environment?)

  lookup-variable-value)

在基于 Lisp 的语言中，变量用符号表示。6In Lisp-based languages the variables are represented by symbols.6

(define (variable? exp) (symbol? exp))

过程 lookup-variable-value 在给定环境中查找它的参数。如果没有找到该变量的值，它就到底层 Scheme 中查找。7 如果还是找不到值，就报告 Unbound variable 错误。The procedure lookup-variable-value looks up its argument in the given environment. If no value is found for that variable, it looks for a value in the underlying Scheme.7 If no value is found, an Unbound variable error is signaled.

二分支条件表达式（if-then-else）的处理过程很简单。如果表达式的谓词部分求值得到真值，就对表达式的后件部分求值，否则对表达式的替代分支部分求值。Binary conditional expressions (if-then-else) have a simple handler. If the predicate part of the expression evaluates to a true value, evaluate the consequent part of the expression, otherwise evaluate the alternative part of the expression.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args if? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (if (g:advance

         (g:eval (if-predicate expression) environment))

        (g:eval (if-consequent expression) environment)

        (g:eval (if-alternative expression) environment))))

我们必须对求值后的谓词调用 g:advance，因为需要知道它的值才能作出选择。注意，if 的求值器使用了宿主语言的 if 构造来完成这项工作！We must call g:advance on the evaluated predicate because we need to know the value to make the decision. Notice that the evaluator for if uses the if construct of the embedding language to do the work!

if 表达式的 Lisp 语法很简单。如果没有指定替代分支，那么当谓词为假时，if 表达式的值就是全局变量 the-unspecified-value 的值。The Lisp syntax for the if expression is simple. If no alternative is specified, the value of the if expression with a false predicate is the value of the global variable the-unspecified-value.

(define (if? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’if))

(define (if-predicate exp) (cadr exp))

(define (if-consequent exp) (caddr exp))



(define (if-alternative exp)

  (if (not (null? (cdddr exp)))

      (cadddr exp)

      ’the-unspecified-value))



(define (make-if pred conseq alternative)

  (list ’if pred conseq alternative))

第一个真正有趣的特殊形式，是用 lambda 表达式表示的匿名过程的描述。lambda 表达式是一种特殊形式，是过程的构造器。对 lambda 表达式求值，会利用形式参数、过程体和当前环境构造一个过程。如果语言中的变量采用词法作用域，那么过程就必须携带环境。在词法作用域语言中，lambda 表达式体内的自由变量（那些不是形式参数的变量）从词法上下文（lambda 表达式在文本中出现的位置）获得含义。The first really interesting special form is the specification of an anonymous procedure, represented by a lambda expression. A lambda expression is a special form, the constructor for procedures. Evaluation of a lambda expression constructs a procedure from the formal parameters, the body, and the current environment. The environment must be carried by the procedure if the variables in the language are lexically scoped. In a lexically scoped language the free variables in the body of the lambda expression (those that are not formal parameters) are given meanings from the lexical context (where the lambda expression appears textually).

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args lambda? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (make-compound-procedure

     (lambda-parameters expression)

     (lambda-body expression)

     environment)))

lambda 表达式的语法是：The syntax for lambda expressions is:

(define (lambda? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’lambda))



(define (lambda-parameters lambda-exp) (cadr lambda-exp))



(define (lambda-body lambda-exp)

  (let ((full-body (cddr lambda-exp)))

    (sequence->begin full-body)))



(define (make-lambda parameters body)

  (cons ’lambda

        (cons parameters

              (if (begin? body)

                  (begin-actions body)

                  (list body)))))

注意，lambda 表达式的过程体可以包含多个表达式。这些表达式应当按顺序求值，以支持具有副作用的动作，例如赋值，或输入／输出控制动作，例如打印。这由 sequence->begin 处理，它会创建一个 begin 特殊形式。Note that the body of a lambda expression may contain several expressions. These are intended to be evaluated in sequence, to allow for side-effecting actions, such as assignment, or I/O control actions, such as printing. This is handled by sequence->begin, which creates a begin special form.

(define (sequence->begin seq)

  (cond ((null? seq) seq)

        ((null? (cdr seq)) (car seq))

        (else

         (make-begin

          (append-map (lambda (exp)

                        (if (begin? exp)

                            (begin-actions exp)

                            (list exp)))

                      seq)))))

注意，过程 sequence->begin 会把嵌套的 begin 形式展平，同时保留执行顺序。begin 形式的语法与求值在第 242 页定义并说明。Notice that the procedure sequence->begin flattens nested begin forms, preserving the order of execution. The syntax and evaluation of begin forms is defined and described on page 242.

派生表达式类型Derived expression types

已经介绍的表达式类型，足以让我们方便地编写大多数程序，但有一些语法糖往往也很不错。这些可以通过把表达式变换成更简单表达式的组合来实现。宏是推广这类变换的一种方式；不过，我们选择不把宏展开器作为解释器的一部分来构建。8 这里我们明确展示，如何把 Lisp 的多分支条件表达式转换为嵌套的 if 表达式：The expression types already introduced are sufficient to conveniently write most programs, but it is often nice to have some syntactic sugar. These can be implemented by transformations of expressions into combinations of simpler ones. Macros are a way to generalize such transformations; but we choose not to build a macro expander as part of our interpreter.8 Here we explicitly show how the Lisp multi-armed conditional can be turned into a nest of if expressions:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args cond? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (g:eval (cond->if expression)

            environment)))

过程 cond->if 是一种相当简单的数据操作：The procedure cond->if is a rather simple data manipulation:

(define (cond->if cond-exp)

  (define (expand clauses)

    (cond ((null? clauses)

           (error "COND: no values matched"))

          ((else-clause? (car clauses))

           (if (null? (cdr clauses))

               (cond-clause-consequent (car clauses))

               (error "COND: ELSE not last"

                      cond-exp)))

          (else

           (make-if (cond-clause-predicate (car clauses))

                    (cond-clause-consequent (car clauses))

                    (expand (cdr clauses))))))

  (expand (cond-clauses cond-exp)))

下面是 cond 特殊形式的语法：And here is the syntax for the cond special form:

(define (cond? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’cond))



(define (cond-clauses exp) (cdr exp))



(define (cond-clause-predicate clause) (car clause))



(define (cond-clause-consequent clause)

  (sequence->begin (cdr clause)))



(define (else-clause? clause)

  (eq? (cond-clause-predicate clause) ’else))

由于 cond 允许子句的后件是一串动作，这个定义也依赖于 sequence->begin。Because cond allows a sequence of actions for the consequent of a clause, this definition also depends on sequence->begin.

局部变量可以用 let 表达式引入。它们通过翻译为带有显式 lambda 表达式的组合式来实现：Local variables can be introduced with let expressions. These are implemented by translation into a combination with an explicit lambda expression:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args let? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (g:eval (let->combination expression)

            environment)))

let 的语法是：The syntax for let is:

(define (let? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’let))



(define (let-bound-variables let-exp)

  (map car (cadr let-exp)))



(define (let-bound-values let-exp)

  (map cadr (cadr let-exp)))



(define (let-body let-exp)

  (sequence->begin (cddr let-exp)))



(define (let->combination let-exp)

  (let ((names (let-bound-variables let-exp))

        (values (let-bound-values let-exp))

        (body (let-body let-exp)))

    (cons (make-lambda names body)

          values)))

效应Effects

如果语言中存在赋值或打印这类具有效应的操作，就必须让它们按顺序进行，因为顺序至关重要。在 Scheme 中，我们用 begin 在语法上表示这样的操作序列：If there are operations in the language that have effects, like assignment or printing, they must be sequenced, because the order is essential. In Scheme we syntactically represent such sequences of operations with begin:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args begin? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (evaluate-sequence (begin-actions expression)

                       environment)))



(define (begin? exp) (tagged-list? exp ’begin))

(define (begin-actions begin-exp) (cdr begin-exp))

(define (make-begin actions) (cons ’begin actions))

真正的工作其实发生在序列求值中：The real work is actually in the sequence evaluation:

(define (evaluate-sequence actions environment)

  (cond ((null? actions)

         (error "Empty sequence"))

        ((null? (cdr actions))

         (g:eval (car actions) environment))

        (else

         (g:eval (car actions) environment)

         (evaluate-sequence (cdr actions)

                            environment))))

对非空表达式序列求值，返回的值是序列中最后一个表达式的值。但执行序列中的表达式所产生的效应，会按序列的顺序发生。The value returned by evaluating a nonempty sequence of expressions is the value of the last expression in the sequence. But effects caused by executing expressions in the sequence happen in the order of the sequence.

大多数效应通过对变量赋值来实现。（事实上，输入／输出操作在硬件中通常也是通过向地址空间中特定的敏感位置赋值来实现的。）在 Scheme 中，我们允许程序对赋值语句所在词法环境中的变量赋值：Most effects are implemented by assignment of variables. (Indeed, input/output operations are usually implemented in hardware by assignment to particular sensitive locations in the address space.) In Scheme we allow a program to assign to a variable in the lexical environment of the assignment statement:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args assignment? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (set-variable-value! (assignment-variable expression)

                         (g:eval (assignment-value expression)

                                 environment)

                         environment)))

赋值的语法是：The syntax for assignment is:

(define (assignment? exp) (tagged-list? exp 'set!))

(define (assignment-variable assn) (cadr assn))

(define (assignment-value assn) (caddr assn))

我们还允许定义，即创建一个具有给定值的新变量。定义会在定义语句所在的最局部词法环境框架中创建新变量。We also allow definition, the creation of a new variable with a given value. A definition creates a new variable in the most local lexical environment frame of the definition statement.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:eval

  (match-args definition? environment?)

  (lambda (expression environment)

    (define-variable! (definition-variable expression)

                      (g:eval (definition-value expression)

                              environment)

                      environment)

    (definition-variable expression)))

定义的语法比赋值的语法更复杂，因为我们允许用多种方式定义过程：9The syntax for definitions is more complicated than the syntax for assignment, because we allow multiple ways to define a procedure:9

(define (definition? exp) (tagged-list? exp 'define))



(define (definition-variable defn)

  (if (variable? (cadr defn))      ; (DEFINE  foo      ...)

      (cadr  defn)

      (caadr defn)))               ; (DEFINE (foo ...) ...)



(define (definition-value defn)

  (if (variable? (cadr defn))      ; (DEFINE  foo      ...)

      (caddr defn)

      (cons ’lambda                ; (DEFINE (foo p...) b...)

            (cons (cdadr defn)     ; =(DEFINE  foo

                  (cddr  defn))))) ;    (LAMBDA (p...) b...))

至此，定义这种语言语法的常见特殊形式就都列全了。当然，泛型过程实现使创建新的特殊形式变得容易，让语言能够不断成长，更方便地表达基础语言原本支持不佳的计算思想。但具有许多不同语法构造的语言，学习、编写文档和使用起来都可能很困难；这是一个经典的工程权衡（请回想第 159 页 Alan Perlis 的箴言）。This completes the usual list of special forms that define the syntax of the language. Of course, the generic procedure implementation enables creation of new special forms easily, allowing the language to grow to make it more convenient to express computational ideas that were not well supported in the base language. But a language with many different syntactic constructs may be difficult to learn, document, and use; this is a classic engineering tradeoff (remember Alan Perlis's maxim on page 159).

5.1.2 apply

传统 Scheme 的 apply 接收两个参数：要应用的过程，以及求值后准备传给该过程的实参。对 Scheme 来说，这就足够了，因为 Scheme 是一种严格的应用序语言，只具有词法作用域变量。The traditional Scheme apply takes two arguments, the procedure to be applied and the evaluated arguments to be passed to the procedure. This is sufficient for Scheme, because Scheme is a strict applicative-order language with only lexically scoped variables.

通过推广 apply 的接口，让它接收三个参数——要应用的过程、尚未求值的运算对象和调用环境——我们就能纳入某些参数要求正则序求值（例如按需求调用）的过程，或对参数作出类型、单位等声明的过程。我们将在By generalizing the interface to apply to take three arguments— the procedure to be applied, the unevaluated operands, and the calling environment—we make it possible to include procedures that require normal-order evaluation for some parameters (e.g., call by need) or procedures that make declarations on parameters, such as types and units. We will make some extensions like these in 第 5.2 节section 5.2中进行一些这样的扩展。环境参数还使我们能够容纳非词法作用域变量，但我们不会这么做；这通常不是好主意。我们将从 Scheme 的应用序开始，并预留用于扩展的泛型钩子。. The environment argument also makes it possible to accommodate non-lexically scoped variables, but we will not do so; it is generally a bad idea. We will start out with Scheme applicative order, with generic hooks for extension.

我们的 apply 是具有三个参数的泛型过程：Our apply is a generic procedure with three arguments:

(define g:apply

  (simple-generic-procedure ’apply 3 default-apply))



(define (default-apply procedure operands calling-environment)

  (error "Unknown procedure type" procedure))

我们需要针对各种过程的处理过程。有些过程，例如算术加法（通常以 + 运算符命名），是严格的：它们需要先对所有参数求值，才能计算出一个值。在 Scheme 中，所有过程都是严格的，包括原语过程（在低于语言层次的系统或硬件中实现的过程）。因此，我们需要一个针对严格原语的泛型处理过程：We will need handlers for the various kinds of procedures. Some procedures, like arithmetic addition (usually named by the + operator), are strict: they need all of their arguments evaluated before they can compute a value. In Scheme all procedures are strict, including primitive procedures (implemented in the system or hardware below the level of the language). So we need a generic handler for strict primitives:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:apply

  (match-args strict-primitive-procedure?

              operands?

              environment?)

  (lambda (procedure operands calling-environment)

    (apply-primitive-procedure procedure

      (eval-operands operands calling-environment))))

在这里的细节层次上，原语过程的应用是“魔法”。运算对象求值器与第 238 页的 if 一样，必须对求值结果调用 g:advance，以确保得到一个值。The application of a primitive procedure is “magic” at this level of detail. The operands evaluator, like if on page 238, must call g:advance on the result of evaluation to ensure a value.

(define (eval-operands operands calling-environment)

  (map (lambda (operand)

         (g:advance (g:eval operand calling-environment)))

       operands))

注意，运算对象的求值顺序由 map 的行为决定。Note that the order of evaluation of the operands is determined by the behavior of map.

通过对 lambda 表达式求值而构造的过程不是原语。在这里，我们可以拆解过程。我们可以获取形式参数规格，也就是形式参数的名称。我们还可以提取过程体，将它连同一个包含形式参数绑定的环境一起传给 eval。为了实现词法作用域，这个扩展环境以过程所携带的环境为基础；后者是在对构造该过程的 lambda 表达式求值时打包进过程的。Procedures constructed by evaluating lambda expressions are not primitive. Here we can take apart the procedure. We can grab the formal parameter specifications, which are the names of the formal parameters. We also can extract the body of the procedure, which we will pass to eval with an environment that includes the formal parameter bindings. For lexical scoping, that extended environment is built on the environment packaged with the procedure by the evaluation of the lambda expression that constructed the procedure.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:apply

  (match-args strict-compound-procedure?

              operands?

              environment?)

  (lambda (procedure operands calling-environment)

    (if (not (n:= (length (procedure-parameters procedure))

                  (length operands)))

        (error "Wrong number of operands supplied"))

    (g:eval (procedure-body procedure)

            (extend-environment

             (procedure-parameters procedure)

             (eval-operands operands calling-environment)

             (procedure-environment procedure)))))

这里，对于所有参数都不带任何声明的复合过程，strict-compound-procedure? 为真。10Here strict-compound-procedure? is true of all compound procedures that have no declarations on any of their parameters.10

驱动循环Driver loop

为了与这个求值器交互，我们需要一个读取—求值—打印循环：To interact with this evaluator we need a read-eval-print loop:

(define (repl)

  (check-repl-initialized)

  (let ((input (g:read)))

    (write-line (g:eval input the-global-environment))

    (repl)))

这里，g:read 在终端上发出提示符 eval>。它接收字符并加以解析，把得到的内容转换为 s 表达式。然后，g:eval 相对于 the-global-environment 对这个 s 表达式求值，并把结果写回终端。过程 repl 以尾递归方式调用自身。要让这一切工作，必须初始化全局环境：Here g:read issues a prompt, eval>, on the terminal. It accepts characters and parses them, converting what it gets into an s-expression. That s-expression is then evaluated with g:eval with respect to the-global-environment and the result is written back to the terminal. The procedure repl calls itself tail recursively. For this to work, the global environment must be initialized:

(define the-global-environment

  ’not-initialized)



(define (initialize-repl!)

  (set! the-global-environment (make-global-environment))

  'done)



(define (check-repl-initialized)

  (if (eq? the-global-environment ’not-initialized)

      (error

       "Interpreter not initialized. Run (init) first.")))

至此，基本求值器就完成了。This completes the elementary evaluator.

练习 5.1：未绑定变量的处理Exercise 5.1: Unbound-variable handling

在包括 Scheme 在内的 Lisp 语言中，尝试对未绑定符号求值会产生未绑定变量错误。不过，在某些代数处理中，允许未绑定符号成为自求值对象往往是合理的。例如，如果像第 3 章那样，以泛型方式扩展算术，使其能够用符号值构建代数表达式，那么有时允许下面的行为会很有用：In Lisps, including Scheme, attempting to evaluate an unbound symbol is an unbound-variable error. However, in some algebraic processes it is often sensible to allow an unbound symbol to be a self-evaluating object. For example, if we generically extend arithmetic to build algebraic expressions with symbolic values, as we did in chapter 3, it is sometimes useful to allow the following:

(+ (* 2 3) (* 4 5))

26



(+ (* a 3) (* 4 5))

(+ (* a 3) 20)

我们的泛型算术支持符号扩展：运算符 * 和 + 经过扩展，在参数不能归约为数时会构建表达式。但它不允许把未绑定变量用作字面数值。这里，符号 a 是未绑定的。我们可能希望它是自求值的。Our generic arithmetic supported symbolic extensions: the operators * and + were extended to build expressions when their arguments were not reducible to numbers. But it did not allow the use of unbound variables as literal numbers. Here the symbol a is unbound. We may want it to be self-evaluating.

  1. a. 对 eval 作一个泛型扩展，以允许这种行为。为了让它能与数值原语（+、*、-、/）配合工作，还必须扩展这些原语的行为。注意，应该修改底层 Scheme 环境中的这些运算符。与第 3 章一样，可以为泛型运算符机制提供在底层 Scheme 系统中工作的处理过程。a. Make a generic extension to eval to allow this kind of behavior. To make this work with the numerical primitives (+, *, -, /) it is necessary to extend their behavior as well. Note that these operators should be changed in the underlying Scheme environment. As in chapter 3, the generic operator mechanism may be given handlers that work in the underlying Scheme system.
  2. b. 同时扩充 apply，允许将运算符位置上的未绑定符号解释为仅知道其名称的字面函数：(+ (f 3) (* 4 5)) ==> (+ (f 3) 20)b. Also augment apply to allow unbound symbols in the operator position to be interpreted as literal functions, known only by their names: (+ (f 3) (* 4 5)) ==> (+ (f 3) 20)

这些对 eval 和 apply 的扩展通常很危险，因为它们会掩盖真正的未绑定变量错误。让它们是否生效取决于一个用户可设置的变量的值：allow-self-evaluating-symbols。These extensions to eval and apply are generally dangerous, because they hide real unbound-variable errors. Make them contingent on the value of a user-settable variable: allow-self-evaluating-symbols.

练习 5.2：n 元过程Exercise 5.2: n-ary procedures

第 246 页的脚注 10 指出，我们在 g:apply 处理过程中加入了一个讨厌的假设，它意味着对这个求值器未来的扩展施加了限制。在 Scheme 中，如果过程的 procedure-parameters 不是列表而是符号，那么这个符号就被视为一个单独的参数，并将绑定到实参列表。11Footnote 10 on page 246 points out a nasty assumption that we put into the g:apply handler that implies a restriction on the future expansion of this evaluator. In Scheme, if the procedure-parameters of a procedure is not a list but rather a symbol, then that symbol is taken as a single parameter that will be bound to the list of arguments.11

在本练习中，我们修改解释器，使它接受单个符号作为形式参数列表，从而能够定义接收不定数量实参的过程。在我们的解释器中，过程 lambda-parameters（第 239 页）完全可以返回单个符号，而且每个调用它的地方都会把结果传给 make-compound-procedure。这个值由 procedure-parameters 取出，而后者用于 g:apply。因此，看起来解释器唯一需要修改的部分是 g:apply。In this exercise we change the interpreter to accept a single symbol as the formal parameter list, so that a procedure can be defined to take an indefinite number of arguments. In our interpreter the procedure lambda-parameters (page 239) is happy to return a single symbol, and everywhere it is called the result is passed to make-compound-procedure. That value is retrieved by procedure-parameters, which is used in g:apply. So it appears that the only part of the interpreter that needs to be changed is g:apply.

修改 g:apply，使它能处理新的复合过程。可以通过重写 g:apply 现有的 strict-compound-procedure? 处理过程（第 246 页）来做到这一点；但更容易也更清晰的办法是，将该处理过程专用于 procedure-parameters 为列表的情况，并为 procedure-parameters 为符号的情况添加一个新的处理过程。Change g:apply to work with the new compound procedures. This can be done by rewriting the existing strict-compound-procedure? handler of g:apply (page 246), but it is both easier and clearer to specialize that handler for the case where the procedure-parameters is a list, and to add a new handler for the case where the procedure-parameters is a symbol.

练习 5.3：过程向量Exercise 5.3: Vectors of procedures

数学文献中一种常见的不严格记法，是把函数元组等同于返回值元组的函数。例如，如果 (cos 0.6) 产生 0.8253356149096783，而 (sin 0.6) 产生 0.5646424733950354，那么我们就期望 ((vector cos sin) 0.6) 产生 #(0.8253356149096783 0.5646424733950354)。In mathematical text a common abuse of notation is to identify a tuple of functions with a function that returns a tuple of values. For example, if (cos 0.6) produces 0.8253356149096783 and if (sin 0.6) produces 0.5646424733950354 then we expect ((vector cos sin) 0.6) to produce #(0.8253356149096783 0.5646424733950354).

虽然在练习 3.2 中，我们曾把算术扩展到向量，但那些扩展并未修改底层语言的求值器。要实现这种行为，需要扩展 g:apply，让它可以把函数向量作为一种函数来处理。实现并演示这个扩展，并展示它能与更常规的代码互操作。Although we had an exercise 3.2 to extend the arithmetic to vectors, those extensions did not modify the underlying language evaluator. This behavior needs an extension to g:apply so it can handle vectors of functions as a kind of function. Make this extension, demonstrate it, and show that it interoperates with more conventional code.

练习 5.4：轮到你了Exercise 5.4: Your turn

发明一种好玩而有趣的构造，使它利用泛型 eval/apply 就很容易实现，而若没有这种泛型支持，实现起来就相当费力。Invent a fun, interesting construct that can easily be implemented using generic eval/apply but would be rather painful without that kind of generic support.

练习 5.5：与底层系统互操作Exercise 5.5: Interoperation with the underlying system

如第 238 页所指出的，对表达式As pointed out on page 238, evaluating the expression

eval> (map (lambda (x) (* x x)) ’(1 2 3))

在我们的解释器中求值时，如果这个表达式中的 map 指的是底层 Scheme 系统中的 map 过程，就无法工作。in our interpreter does not work if the map in this expression refers to the map procedure from the underlying Scheme system.

不过，如果为我们的解释器重新定义 map，它就能工作：However, if we redefine map for our interpreter it does work:

eval> (define (map f l)

        (if (null? l)

            ’()

            (cons (f (car l)) (map f (cdr l)))))

map



eval> (map (lambda (x) (* x x)) ’(1 2 3))

(1 4 9)

为什么不能使用 map 这样接收过程参数的底层过程？请解释。概述一种修正此问题的策略，并实现你的解决方案。注意：要正确处理这件事有些微妙，所以不要为了让它完美工作而花费无穷的时间。Why does it not work to use the underlying procedures that take procedural arguments, such as map? Explain. Outline a strategy to fix the problem and implement your solution. Note: This is subtle to get right, so don't spend infinite time trying to make it work perfectly.

练习 5.6：不同的引用方式Exercise 5.6: Different quotation

曾经有一些有趣的语言，采用了非常不同的求值和引用规则。例如，在 MDL 中（见 Wikipedia [91]），符号被假定为自求值的，而需要查找的变量则用前缀字符加以区分。另外，在 MDL 中，组合式是一种特殊形式，只不过其关键字是隐含的。只需修改语法定义，就能很容易地修改我们的求值器，使其解释类似 MDL 的语法。试试看！There have been interesting languages with very different evaluation and quotation rules. For example, in MDL (see Wikipedia [91]) a symbol is assumed to be self evaluating, and variables to be looked up are distinguished with a prefix character. Also, in MDL a combination is a special form, but with an implied keyword. Our evaluator can easily be modified to interpret a MDL-like syntax, just by changing the syntax definitions. Try it!

练习 5.7：中缀记法Exercise 5.7: Infix notation

与 Lisp 不同，大多数计算机语言都使用中缀记法。如果想在 Scheme 中加入中缀表达式，我们可以写成：Unlike Lisp, most computer languages use infix notations. If we wanted to include infix expressions in Scheme we might write:

(infix

  "fact := lambda n:

            if n == 0

               then 1

               else n*fact(n-1)")



(fact 6)             ; The Lisp procedure is now defined

720



(infix "fact(5)")    ; And it can be used in infix notation.

120

这完全只是个小小的语法问题（哈！）。不过，让它工作是一个有趣的项目。你不需要修改解释器。要做的工作是解析字符串，把它编译为对应的 Lisp 表达式，方式与 cond->if 的工作方式相同。Lisp 程序员已经做过许多次这样的事，但用 Lisp 编程的人似乎都喜欢 Lisp 原生的波兰式前缀记法！12 唉，好吧……This is entirely a small matter of syntax (ha!). However, it is an interesting project to make it work. You do not need to change the interpreter. The work is parsing the character string to compile it into the corresponding Lisp expressions, in the same way that cond->if works. Lisp programmers have done this many times, but people who program in Lisp seem to like the native Lisp Polish prefix notation!12 Oh, well...

5.2 带有非严格参数的过程5.2 Procedures with non-strict arguments

本节我们将研究如何给过程的形式参数添加声明，以允许推迟对应运算对象的求值。In this section we will investigate adding declarations to the formal parameters of a procedure to allow deferred evaluation of the corresponding operands.

在 Scheme 中，过程是严格的。严格过程要求：在对过程体求值之前，先对调用表达式的所有运算对象求值，并把所得实参绑定到形式参数。但对于 if 表达式，必须先对谓词部分求值，以确定是对后件部分求值，还是对替代分支部分求值；两者不会都求值。这就是为什么 if 必须是特殊形式，而不是过程。非严格过程是会推迟某些运算对象求值的过程。怎样才能让程序员按需定义非严格过程，而不是只能使用语言定义中规定的少数特殊形式，例如 if 呢？In Scheme, procedures are strict. Strict procedures require evaluating all the operands of the calling expression and binding the resulting arguments to the formal parameters before the body of the procedure is evaluated. But for an if expression, the predicate part must be evaluated to determine whether to evaluate the consequent part or the alternative part; they won't both be evaluated. This is why if must be a special form, not a procedure. A non-strict procedure is one that defers the evaluation of some operands. How can we make it possible for a programmer to define non-strict procedures as needed, rather than just using a few special forms, such as if, that are specified in the language definition?

例如，假设我们想构造一个过程 unless，让它像特殊形式 if 一样，不对那些不需要的分支求值。13 使用 unless，我们可以写出：For example, suppose we want to make a procedure unless that works like the special form if in that it does not evaluate the alternatives that are not needed.13 Using unless we could write:

(define (fib n)

  (unless (< n 2)

          (+ (fib (- n 1)) (fib (- n 2)))

          n))

要让这个 Fibonacci 函数定义正确工作，当 n < 2 时，就不应对 unless 表达式的第二个运算对象求值；当 n ≥ 2 时，就不应对第三个运算对象求值。但是，unless 表达式的第一个运算对象必须始终求值，以确定作出哪种选择。For this definition of the Fibonacci function to work correctly, the second operand of the unless expression should not be evaluated if n < 2, and the third operand should not be evaluated if n ≥ 2. But the first operand of the unless expression must always be evaluated to determine the choice.

我们需要一种办法，确定 unless 的哪些运算对象应该求值，哪些应该推迟求值。为此，我们引入一种声明，并写成：We need a way to determine which operands of unless to evaluate, and which to defer. To do this we introduce a kind of declaration and write:

(define (unless condition (usual lazy) (exception lazy))

  (if condition exception usual))

这里，我们用特殊形式 if 来定义过程 unless，但声明第二和第三个参数为惰性参数。14 第一个参数默认是严格的。Here we define the procedure unless in terms of the special form if, but we declare that the second and third arguments are lazy.14 The first argument is, by default, strict.

我们可以对形式参数作出多种声明，描述如何处理运算对象和实参。参数可以声明为惰性并记忆化，以实现按需求调用，正如 Haskell 等语言中所有过程的参数那样；也可以声明参数，要求其实参满足给定的谓词，例如类型和单位；等等。We could have many kinds of declarations on formal parameters, describing how to handle operands and arguments. A parameter could be declared lazy and memoized, to implement call by need, as are arguments to all procedures in languages like Haskell; a parameter could be declared to require that its argument satisfy given predicates, which could be types and units; etc.

实现广义形式参数Implementing generalized formal parameters

为了实现广义形式参数，我们需要一个处理新情况的特殊应用器。只需给 g:apply 加入一个处理过程即可，它与前面处理严格复合过程的处理过程类似（见第 246 页）：To implement generalized formal parameters, we need a special applicator that handles the new cases. This is accomplished by adding a single handler to g:apply, similar to the earlier one for strict compound procedures (see page 246):

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:apply

  (match-args general-compound-procedure?

              operands?

              environment?)

  (lambda (procedure operands calling-environment)

    (if (not (n:= (length (procedure-parameters procedure))

                  (length operands)))

        (error "Wrong number of operands supplied"))

    (let ((params (procedure-parameters procedure))

          (body (procedure-body procedure)))

      (let ((names (map procedure-parameter-name params))

            (arguments

             (map (lambda (param operand)

                    (g:handle-operand param

                                      operand

                                      calling-environment))

                  params

                  operands)))

        (g:eval body

                (extend-environment names arguments

                 (procedure-environment procedure)))))))

这与严格应用器有两处不同：第一，我们必须提取参数的名称，因为它们可能被包裹在声明中；第二，我们必须根据声明，以特殊方式处理运算对象。这些由泛型过程 procedure-parameter-name 和 g:handle-operand 完成。This differs from the strict applicator in two ways: first, we must extract the names of the parameters, since they could be wrapped in declarations; second, we must handle the operands specially, depending on the declarations. This is done by the generic procedures procedure-parameter-name and g:handle-operand.

过程 procedure-parameter-name 允许我们给形式参数添加声明，同时仍能取得它的名称。默认处理过程是恒等函数，因此，没有修饰的形式参数，其名称就是它自身。The procedure procedure-parameter-name allows us to add declarations to a formal parameter and still be able to retrieve its name. The default handler is the identity function, so the name of an undecorated formal parameter is just itself.

(define procedure-parameter-name

  (simple-generic-procedure ’parameter-name 1 (lambda (x) x)))

过程 g:handle-operand 允许我们根据对应形式参数的声明，选择如何处理运算对象：The procedure g:handle-operand allows us to choose how to process an operand based on the declarations of the corresponding formal parameter:

(define g:handle-operand

  (simple-generic-procedure ’g:handle-operand 3

    (lambda (parameter operand environment)

      (g:advance (g:eval operand environment)))))

对于没有声明的运算对象，默认处理方式就是对其求值，如同之前第 245 页的 eval-operands 所做的那样。The default way to handle an operand without declarations is to evaluate the operand, as was previously done by eval-operands on page 245.
