我们需要一种语法，允许用声明修饰形式参数。这里我们选择使用以形式参数名称开头的列表：We need a syntax to allow us to decorate a formal parameter with declarations. Here we choose to use a list beginning with the name of the formal parameter:

(define-generic-procedure-handler procedure-parameter-name

  (match-args pair?)

  car)

我们先实现两种声明。第一种是 lazy，表示只有在需要运算对象的值时才对它求值，例如把它用作 if 表达式的谓词时。第二种是 lazy memo，它与 lazy 类似，但在第一次对运算对象求值时，会记住所得到的值，使后续使用不必重新求值。We will start by implementing two kinds of declarations. The first is lazy, which means the operand is evaluated only when its value is needed, for example as the predicate of an if expression. The second is lazy memo, which is like lazy except that the first time the operand is evaluated, the value is remembered so that subsequent uses do not require reevaluation.

如果参数被指定为惰性的（或惰性且记忆化的），就必须推迟对运算对象求值。被推迟求值的表达式必须与环境打包在一起；当需要它的值时，这个环境将用来确定该表达式中自由变量的值。15If a parameter is specified to be lazy (or lazy memoized) the evaluation of the operand must be postponed. The postponed expression must be packaged with the environment that will be used to give values to the free variables in that expression when its value is required.15

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:handle-operand

  (match-args lazy? operand? environment?)

  (lambda (parameter operand environment)

    (postpone operand environment)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler g:handle-operand

  (match-args lazy-memo? operand? environment?)

  (lambda (parameter operand environment)

     (postpone-memo operand environment)))

当然，我们必须扩展迄今只有默认处理过程的 g:advance（见第 236 页），以执行被推迟的求值。注意，g:advance 的结果本身也可能是一个推迟求值对象，因此可能还得继续推进它的求值。Of course, we must extend g:advance, which so far has only a default handler (see page 236), to do the postponed evaluation. Notice that the result of g:advance may itself be a postponement, so we may have to advance that.

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:advance

  (match-args postponed?)

  (lambda (object)

    (g:advance (g:eval (postponed-expression object)

                       (postponed-environment object)))))

如果推迟表达式求值时打算对结果进行记忆化，那么结果由 advance-memo! 保存：If the expression is postponed with the intent of memoizing the result, the result is saved by advance-memo!:

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:advance

  (match-args postponed-memo?)

  (lambda (object)

    (let ((value

           (g:advance

            (g:eval (postponed-expression object)

                    (postponed-environment object)))))

      (advance-memo! object value)

      value)))

记忆化后的值再也不需要求值。advance-memo! 过程改变推迟求值对象的类型，使其满足谓词 advanced-memo?，并保存该值，使其能通过 advanced-value 访问：16The memoized value never needs to be evaluated again. The advance-memo! procedure changes the type of the postponed object to satisfy the predicate advanced-memo? and saves the value, making it accessible by advanced-value:16

(define-generic-procedure-handler g:advance

  (match-args advanced-memo?)

  advanced-value)

示例：惰性序对与列表Example: Lazy pairs and lists

带有惰性参数的过程赋予我们新的能力。例如，可以定义构造过程 kons 和选择过程 kar、kdr，使我们能够在不对内容求值的情况下构建序对。17 这里，我们把 kons 实现为一个按需求调用方式接收实参（惰性且记忆化）的过程。它产生一个接收 kar 和 kdr 消息的消息接收器 the-pair。它还在 the-pair 上贴了一张“便签”，用来标识它是 kons 的结果。Procedures with lazy parameters give us new power. For example, we can define a constructor kons, and selectors kar and kdr, so that we can make pairs without evaluating their contents.17 Here we have implemented kons as a procedure that takes its arguments call by need (memoized lazy). It produces a message acceptor, the-pair, for kar and kdr. It also puts a “sticky note” on the-pair for identifying it as the result of kons.

(define (kons (x lazy memo) (y lazy memo))

  (define (the-pair m)

    (cond ((eq? m ’kar) x)

          ((eq? m ’kdr) y)

          (else (error "Unknown message – kons" m x y))))

  (hash-table-set! kons-registrations the-pair #t)

  the-pair)



(define (kar x)

  (x ’kar))



(define (kdr x)

  (x ’kdr))

我们需要这张便签，是为了能够识别 kons 序对：The reason why we need the sticky note is to be able to recognize a kons pair:

(define (kons? object)

  (hash-table-exists? kons-registrations object))

使用这种惰性序对机制，我们可以轻松实现流式处理。流与列表相似，但它们是由消费它们的过程按需构建的。18 因此，无限长的流也可以逐步处理，任何时刻都只有有限的一部分实际存在。Using this lazy pair mechanism we can easily implement stream-type processing. Streams are like lists, but they are built as needed by the processes that consume them.18 Thus a stream that is infinitely long may be processed incrementally, with only a finite portion actual at any time.

有些流是有限的，因此，为空流选择一种表示会很有用。我们就让它与空列表相同：Some streams are finite, so it is useful to choose a representation for the empty stream. Let's make it the same as the empty list:

(define the-empty-stream ’())



(define (empty-stream? thing)

  (null? thing))

我们可以将流相加：We can add streams:

(define (add-streams s1 s2)

  (cond ((empty-stream? s1) s2)

        ((empty-stream? s2) s1)

        (else

         (kons (+ (kar s1) (kar s2))

                (add-streams (kdr s1) (kdr s2))))))

我们可以查找流的第 n 个元素：We can find the nth element of a stream:

(define (ref-stream stream n)

  (if (= n 0)

      (kar stream)

      (ref-stream (kdr stream) (- n 1))))

有了这些，我们就可以创建一个（可能无限长的）Fibonacci 数流：先给出两个初始元素，其余部分则通过将这个流与其 kdr 相加来形成：Given these, we can create a (potentially infinite) stream of Fibonacci numbers with two initial entries and the rest of the stream formed by adding the stream to its kdr:

(define fibs

  (kons 0 (kons 1 (add-streams (kdr fibs) fibs))))

然后，我们可以查看几个 Fibonacci 数Then we can look at a few Fibonacci numbers

(ref-stream fibs 10)

55



(ref-stream fibs 100)

354224848179261915075

通常的双重递归 Fibonacci 程序具有指数级复杂度，因此不能指望用那种方法得到这个序列的第 100 个元素；但由于 kons 序对采用了记忆化，问题的复杂度就降为线性。注意，在序列的这个位置，两个相邻 Fibonacci 数的比值已经以完整精度收敛到黄金分割比：The usual doubly recursive Fibonacci program is exponential, so one could not expect to get the 100th entry in this sequence by that method; but the fact that the kons pairs are memoized reduces this to a linear problem. Notice that by this point in the sequence the ratio of two successive Fibonacci numbers has converged to the golden ratio in full precision:

(inexact

  (/ (ref-stream fibs 100)

     (ref-stream fibs 99)))

1.618033988749895

练习 5.8：对微分方程积分Exercise 5.8: Integrating differential equations

遗憾的是，使用 kons 本身并不能解决所有流的问题。例如，SICP [1] 第 4.2.3 节（第 411 页）提到的困难并不会自动消失。假设我们想在给定初始条件下，对一个微分方程进行积分。我们作出如下定义：Unfortunately, the use of kons does not, in itself, solve all stream problems. For example, the difficulty alluded to in SICP [1] section 4.2.3 (p. 411) does not automatically dissipate. Suppose we want to integrate a differential equation given some initial conditions. We make the following definitions:

(define (map-stream proc (items lazy memo))

  (if (empty-stream? items)

      items

      (kons (proc (kar items))

            (map-stream proc (kdr items)))))



(define (scale-stream items factor)

  (map-stream (lambda (x) (* x factor))

              items))



(define (integral integrand initial-value dt)

  (define int

    (kons initial-value

          (add-streams (scale-stream integrand dt)

                       int)))

  int)



(define (solve f y0 dt)

  (define y (integral dy y0 dt))

  (define dy (map-stream f y))

  y)

我们尝试通过对初始条件为 x(0) = 1 的方程 x!(t) = x(t) 积分，求得 e 的近似值。我们知道 e = x(1)，因此写出：We try to find an approximation to e by integrating x!(t) = x(t) with initial condition x(0) = 1. We know that e = x(1) so we write:

(ref-stream (solve (lambda (x) x) 1 0.001) 1000)

;Unbound variable: dy

我们得到了一个错误——唉！We get an error—ugh!

不过，现在我们已经有了解决这个问题的工具。要让它按预期工作，必须修改什么？修正这个程序，使它具有下面的行为：However, now we have the tools to fix this problem. What has to be changed to make this work as expected? Fix this program to get the following behavior:

(ref-stream (solve (lambda (x) x) 1 0.001) 1000)

2.716923932235896

（没错，我们知道这是对 e 的一个很糟糕的近似，但这里要说明的是编程方面的问题，而不是数值分析方面的问题！）(Yes, we know this is a terrible approximation to e, but it illustrates a programming point, not a numerical analysis point!)

练习 5.9：为什么不用 kons？Exercise 5.9: Why not kons?

kons 特殊形式相当于两个参数都采用惰性求值并进行记忆化的 cons。如果不对参数进行记忆化，上面的计算 (ref-stream fibs 100) 就会耗费很长时间。The kons special form is equivalent to a cons with both arguments lazy and memoized. If the arguments were not memoized, the computation (ref-stream fibs 100) above would take a very long time.

  1. a. 不进行记忆化会有好处吗？在什么情况下，这一点可能很重要？a. Is there ever an advantage to not memoizing? When might it matter?
  2. b. 为什么我们不能简单地把 kons 定义为b. Why could we not have defined kons simply as
(define (kons (a lazy memo) (d lazy memo))

  (cons a d))

其中使用从 Scheme 导入的原语过程 cons 呢？using the primitive procedure cons imported from Scheme?

  1. c. 更一般地说，Lisp 社群一直没有按 Friedman 和 Wise 的建议，把 cons 改成 kons（见第 254 页的脚注 17）。使用 cons 而不是 kons，避免了哪些潜在的严重问题？假设我们不在乎性能上较小的常数因子。c. More generally, the Lisp community has avoided changing cons to be kons, as recommended by Friedman and Wise (see footnote 17 on page 254). What potentially serious problems are avoided by using cons rather than kons? Assume that we do not care about small constant factors in performance.

练习 5.10：带限制的参数Exercise 5.10: Restricted parameters

一个不错的想法是把限制条件放进形式参数的声明中。我们可能希望要求某个任意谓词对一个参数为真，类似于第 4.3.2 节中在模式变量上使用限制条件的做法。例如，我们可能希望某个过程接收三个参数：第一个是任意整数，第二个必须是素数，第三个则不受限制。这可以记为：One nice idea is to build restrictions into the declaration of a formal parameter. We might want to require that an arbitrary predicate be true of a parameter, similar to our use of restrictions in pattern variables in section 4.3.2. For example, we might want a procedure to take three arguments: the first is any integer, but the second is prime, and the third is unrestricted. This might be notated:

(define (my-proc (n integer?) (p prime?) g)

  ...)

遗憾的是，这种特设设计不能很好地与 lazy、memo 等其他声明配合，除非我们规定声明的顺序，或者把它们设为保留标识符。为方便起见，假设我们将 lazy 和 memo 声明为特殊关键字，并要求其他声明都用关键字引入，例如用 restrict-to 引入谓词：Unfortunately, this kind of ad hoc design does not play well with other declarations, like lazy and memo, unless we legislate the order of the declarations or make them reserved identifiers. Suppose, for convenience, we declare lazy and memo to be special keywords, and require other declarations to be announced with a keyword, such as restrict-to for a predicate:

(define (my-proc (n restrict-to integer?)

                 (p restrict-to prime? lazy)

                 g)

...)
  1. a. 设计一种合适的语法。确保它具有可扩展性，能够按需加入新的声明类型。用 BNF 表达你的语法，并修改解释器的语法过程以实现它。a. Design an appropriate syntax. Make sure it is extensible in that new declaration types can be added as needed. Express your syntax in BNF and change the syntax procedures of your interpreter to implement it.
  2. b. 实现谓词限制。如果运行时违反了某个限制，程序应当报告错误。你可能会发现 guarantee 在这里很有用。b. Implement predicate restrictions. If a restriction is violated at run time, the program should report an error. You may find guarantee useful here.

练习 5.11：再谈 n 元过程！Exercise 5.11: n-ary procedures, again!

  1. a. 在第 248 页的练习 5.2 中，我们修改了 g:apply 处理过程，允许过程的形式参数是单个符号，并将它绑定到实参列表。遗憾的是，对于形式参数可以带有声明修饰的系统，这种指定剩余参数的方式并不自然。不过，我们可以发明一种修饰语法，允许定义带有可选参数和剩余参数的过程。a. In exercise 5.2 on page 248 we modified the g:apply handler to allow the formal parameters of a procedure to be a single symbol that is bound to a list of the arguments. Unfortunately, this way of specifying a rest argument is not natural for a system where the formal parameters may be decorated with declarations. However, we can invent a decoration syntax that allows us to define procedures with optional and rest arguments.

例如，如果我们允许用 rest 一词来修饰形式参数列表中的最后一个形式参数，那么它应当绑定到尚未匹配的实参。这个 rest 声明应当能够与该参数上的其他声明一起使用。因此，我们应当能够创建这样的过程：For example, if we allow the last formal parameter in the formal parameter list be decorated with the word rest, it should be bound to the unmatched arguments. This rest declaration should be usable with other declarations on that argument. So we should be able to create procedures like:

(lambda (x

         (y restrict-to integer? lazy)

         (z rest restrict-to list-of-integers?))

  ...)

其中，list-of-integers? 是一个对整数列表为真的谓词。rest 声明应当能够与其他声明一起使用，例如 lazy 和 restrict-to。where list-of-integers? is a predicate that is true of lists of integers. The rest declaration should be able to be used with other declarations, such as lazy and restrict-to.

让 rest 声明工作起来！Make rest declarations work!

  1. b. 允许过程具有可选参数，也可能很有用，而且还可以为它们指定默认值。例如，一个数值过程可以允许用户指定近似计算的容差，但如果用户没有提供容差，就采用指定的默认值：b. It may also be useful to allow a procedure to have optional arguments, possibly with specified default values. For example, a numerical procedure could allow the user to specify a tolerance for approximation, but specify a default value if the user does not supply the tolerance:

(lambda (x (epsilon optional flo:ulp-of-one))

  ...)

这里，flo:ulp-of-one 是全局定义的符号，它指定一个最小的 2 的幂：把它加到 1.0 上，得到的值就不再等于 1.0。在 C 库中，它称为 DBL EPSILON。（对于少数关心这个细节的读者，在 IEEE 双精度浮点数中，flo:ulp-of-one 的值为 2.220446049250313e-16。）Here flo:ulp-of-one is a globally defined symbol that specifies the smallest power of two that when added to 1.0 produces a value that is not equal to 1.0. In the C library it is called DBL EPSILON. (For those few of you who care, in IEEE double-precision floating point the value of flo:ulp-of-one is 2.220446049250313e-16.)

也让 optional 声明工作起来！确保你的扩展能够与所有其他有意义的声明混合搭配使用。Make optional declarations work too! Be sure that your extension can mix and match with all other declarations that make sense.

5.3 编译为执行过程5.3 Compiling to execution procedures

我们一直使用的求值器极其灵活且易于扩展，但它很笨：程序运行得相当慢。一个罪魁祸首是，求值器反复查看程序的语法（无论语法多么简单）。我们在第 4 章的第 4.3 节中，把每个匹配器模式变换为具有相同形式的匹配器过程的复合，即一种组合子语言，从而避免了这个问题。解释一种语言时，我们也可以类似地编译成执行过程的复合，避免反复检查语法结构。因此，在更深入地研究求值之前，让我们先完成这一转变。The evaluator that we have been working with is extremely flexible and extensible, but it is dumb: our programs run rather slowly. One culprit is that the evaluator is repeatedly looking at the syntax (however simple) of the program. We avoided this problem in chapter 4 by transforming each matcher pattern into a composition of matcher procedures that all have the same form—a combinator language—in section 4.3. In interpreting a language we can avoid reexamining the syntactic structure by similarly compiling into a composition of execution procedures. So before getting deeper into evaluation, let's make this transition.

关键思想是，把相对于环境对表达式求值的问题分成两个阶段。第一阶段分析表达式，并将它转换为执行过程。第二阶段把该执行过程应用于一个环境，产生预期的求值结果。我们直接将这一想法实现为两个阶段的复合。The critical idea is to separate the problem of evaluation of an expression relative to an environment into two phases. In the first phase the expression is analyzed and converted into an execution procedure. In the second phase that execution procedure is applied to an environment, producing the expected evaluation result. We implement this idea directly, as the composition of the two phases.

(define (x:eval expression environment)

  ((analyze expression) environment))

对表达式的分析与转换称为编译，它所做的工作被称为在编译时完成。编译器提取出不依赖表达式中自由变量值的那部分行为。这主要是语法分析，但也是进行某些可通过语法规则实现的优化的机会。所得的执行过程依赖于环境所指定的符号到值的映射；它所做的工作被称为在运行时完成。The analysis and conversion of the expression is called compilation, and the work that it does is said to be done at compile time. The compiler extracts that part of the behavior that does not depend on the values of the free variables in the expression. This is mostly syntactic analysis, but it is also a venue for some optimizations that are implementable by syntactic rules. The resulting execution procedure depends on the mapping of symbols to values specified in the environment; the work it does is said to be done at run time.

表达式分析Analysis of expressions

由于我们希望能够按需扩展语言语法，因此把分析实现为泛型过程，默认情况是把运算符应用于运算对象。对于 Lisp/Scheme，这必须是默认情况，因为没有用于区分应用的语法关键字。19Since we want to be able to extend the language syntax as needed, we implement the analysis as a generic procedure, with the default being an application of an operator to operands. This has to be a default for Lisp/Scheme because there is no syntactic keyword that distinguishes an application.19

(define x:analyze

  (simple-generic-procedure ’x:analyze 1 default-analyze))

x:analyze 的约定是：它接收一个表达式作为参数，返回一个执行过程，而这个执行过程接收一个参数，即环境。The convention for x:analyze is that it takes an expression as an argument and returns an execution procedure, which takes one argument, an environment.

过程 analyze 封装了一种常见的使用模式：The procedure analyze captures a common usage pattern:

(define (analyze expression)

  (make-executor (x:analyze expression)))

用过程 make-executor 包装执行过程，是为了辅助调试。所得的执行器也是一个过程，其参数和返回值与它所包装的执行过程相同。这个包装器的一个实用之处，是它会维护一条“执行轨迹”，有助于判断程序是如何走到某个出错点的。The purpose of wrapping the execution procedure with the procedure make-executor is to aid in debugging. The resulting executor is also a procedure, with the same arguments and returned value as the execution procedure that it wraps. One useful aspect of this wrapper is that it maintains an “execution trace” that can be helpful while determining how a program got to a point of failure.

如前所述，默认的分析对象是应用。As we said, the default analysis is of an application.

(define (default-analyze expression)

  (cond ((application? expression)

         (analyze-application expression))

        (else (error "Unknown expression type" expression))))



(define (analyze-application expression)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator expression)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (x:apply (x:advance (operator-exec environment))

               operand-execs

               environment))))

注意这里的分工：从表达式中提取运算符和运算对象，并对其进行分析，形成执行过程 operator-exec 和 operand-execs。这可能需要大量的分析工作。随后，应用表达式的执行过程就是一个接受环境并执行应用的过程（由 lambda 表达式创建）。过程 x:apply（第 265 页）类似于解释器中的 g:apply；但 x:apply 接受的是运算对象的执行过程，而不是 g:apply 所使用的运算对象表达式。引入类似于 g:advance 的过程 x:advance，也是出于同样的原因。求值器的每一部分都可以这样转换。Notice the division of labor here: the operator and the operands are extracted from the expression and analyzed to make up the execution procedures operator-exec and operand-execs. This may require significant analysis. The execution procedure for the application is then a procedure (created by the lambda expression) that takes an environment and does the application. The procedure x:apply (on page 265) is analogous to g:apply in the interpreter; but x:apply takes execution procedures for the operands, rather than the operand expressions that were used by g:apply. The procedure x:advance, analogous to g:advance, is introduced for the same reason. Every part of the evaluator can be transformed in this way.

自求值表达式（例如数、布尔值或字符串）的转换非常简单。唯一困难的部分是表达式的实际语法，而这由 Scheme 解析器处理。程序文本在送到求值器之前，就已经被解析成词法单元和 S 表达式了，因此这里不必关心这些复杂之处。The transformation of self-evaluating expressions (such as numbers, boolean values, or strings) is trivial. The only hard part of this is the actual syntax of the expressions, which is handled by the Scheme parser. The text of the programs is parsed into tokens and s-expressions before it ever gets to the evaluator, so we need not concern ourselves with those complexities here.

(define (analyze-self-evaluating expression)

  (lambda (environment) expression))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args self-evaluating?)

  analyze-self-evaluating)

引用也很容易，同样是因为困难的部分已经由解析器处理了。20Quotation is easy, again because the hard part is in the parser.20

(define (analyze-quoted expression)

  (let ((qval (text-of-quotation expression)))

    (lambda (environment) qval)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args quoted?)

  analyze-quoted)

变量也很容易。一旦识别出变量，所有工作都由执行过程完成。Variables are also easy. Once we identify the variable, all of the work is in the execution procedure.

(define (analyze-variable expression)

  (lambda (environment)

    (lookup-variable-value expression environment)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args variable?)

  analyze-variable)

过程定义在 Lisp/Scheme 中用 lambda 表达式表示，它展现了一种强有力的分工方式。在构造执行过程之前，分析器（编译器）会解析 lambda 表达式，提取形式参数规格，并编译表达式的过程体。因此，lambda 表达式的执行过程以及最终执行过程体的代码都不必再做这些工作。Procedure definitions, expressed in Lisp/Scheme by lambda expressions, are an example of a powerful division of labor. Before building the execution procedure, the analyzer (compiler) parses the lambda expression, extracting the formal parameter specifications, and compiles the body of the expression. Thus the execution procedure for the lambda expression, and the code that eventually executes the body, need not do that work.

(define (analyze-lambda expression)

  (let ((vars (lambda-parameters expression))

        (body-exec (analyze (lambda-body expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (make-compound-procedure vars body-exec environment))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args lambda?)

  analyze-lambda)

特殊形式 if 是另一个非常清楚的例子，说明了将分析与执行分离的好处。if 表达式的三个部分都在编译时分析，因此执行过程只需从谓词中取得布尔值，以决定执行结果分支还是替代分支。运行时（使用执行过程时）不必再分析这些子表达式。The special form if is another very clear example of the advantage of separating analysis from execution. The three parts of the if expression are analyzed at compile time, allowing the execution procedure to do no more work than extract the boolean value from the predicate to decide whether to do the consequent or the alternative. The analysis of the subexpressions is not necessary to do at run time (when the execution procedure is used).

(define (analyze-if expression)

  (let ((predicate-exec

         (analyze (if-predicate expression)))

        (consequent-exec

         (analyze (if-consequent expression)))

        (alternative-exec

         (analyze (if-alternative expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (if (x:advance (predicate-exec environment))

          (consequent-exec environment)

          (alternative-exec environment)))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args if?)

  analyze-if)

待求值的表达式序列尤其能说明分析与执行分离的好处。没有理由在每次进入过程体时都重新编译表达式序列；这项工作可以在编译时一劳永逸地完成。Sequences of expressions to be evaluated are an especially good example of separation of analysis and execution. There is no good reason to recompile a sequence of expressions every time we enter the body of a procedure; this work can be done once and for all at compile time.

analyze-begin 过程首先分析 begin 表达式的每个子表达式，生成一个执行过程列表（保留各表达式在 begin 表达式中的顺序）。随后，使用 reduce-right 和一个二元组合子将这些执行过程衔接起来；该组合子接受两个执行过程，生成一个按顺序执行这两个给定执行过程的执行过程。21The analyze-begin procedure first analyzes each subexpression of the begin expression, producing a list of execution procedures (preserving the order of the expressions in the begin expression). These execution procedures are then glued together using reduce-right and a pairwise combinator that takes two execution procedures and produces an execution procedure that executes the two given execution procedures in sequence.21

(define (analyze-begin expression)

  (reduce-right (lambda (exec1 exec2)

                  (lambda (environment)

                    (exec1 environment)

                    (exec2 environment)))

                #f

                (map analyze

                     (let ((exps

                            (begin-actions expression)))

                       (if (null? exps)

                           (error "Empty sequence")) 

                       exps))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args begin?)

  analyze-begin)

在没有编译器优化的情况下，处理赋值并不困难。The treatment of assignments is not problematical in the absence of compiler optimizations.

(define (analyze-assignment expression)

  (let ((var

         (assignment-variable expression))

        (value-exec

         (analyze (assignment-value expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (set-variable-value! var

                           (value-exec environment)

                           environment)

      ’ok)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args assignment?)

  analyze-assignment)

然而，如果要进行编译器优化，赋值就会带来严重的问题。事实上，赋值把时间引入了程序：有些事情发生在赋值之前，有些发生在赋值之后，而赋值会改变那些引用了被修改变量的事件。因此，例如，如果公共子表达式引用了可被赋值的变量，它们的值实际上就未必相同！However, if there are compiler optimizations to be done, assignments pose serious problems. Indeed, assignments introduce time into a program: some things happen before the assignment and some happen after the assignment, and the assignment can change the events that reference the variable that was changed. Thus, for example, common subexpressions may not really have the same value if they reference a variable that can be assigned!

定义本身不会带来问题，除非我们把它们看作赋值（并错误地当作赋值使用），从而可能干扰编译器优化。Definitions are not a problem, unless we think of them (and incorrectly use them) as assignments, potentially interfering with compiler optimizations.

(define (analyze-definition expression)

  (let ((var

         (definition-variable expression))

        (value-exec

         (analyze (definition-value expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (define-variable! var

                        (value-exec environment)

                        environment)

      var)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args definition?)

  analyze-definition)

通过表达式变换实现的特殊形式，如 cond 和 let，在这个系统中非常容易处理；只需编译变换后的表达式即可。事实上，正可以在这里接入一种非常通用的宏机制。Special forms that are implemented by transformations of expressions, such as cond and let, are really easy in this system; we simply compile the transformed expression. Indeed, this is the place where a very general macro facility could be hooked in.

(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args cond?)

  (compose analyze cond->if))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:analyze

  (match-args let?)

  (compose analyze let->combination))

过程的应用Application of procedures

应用表达式的执行过程调用运算符的执行过程，获得要应用的复合过程。（见第 260 页的 analyze-application。）运算对象也已经转换成了执行过程。The execution procedure for an application calls the execution procedure for the operator to obtain the compound procedure to be applied. (See analyze-application on page 260.) The operands have also been converted to execution procedures.

过程 x:apply 类似于基本求值器中的 g:apply（第 245 页）：The procedure x:apply is analogous to g:apply in the elementary evaluator (on page 245):

(define x:apply

  (simple-generic-procedure ’x:apply 3 default-apply))



(define (default-apply procedure operand-execs environment)

  (error "Unknown procedure type" procedure))

注意，这里的 default-apply 与 g:apply 所使用的版本相同，区别只在于那两个未使用的参数的名称。Note that the default-apply here is the same as the one used by g:apply except for the names of the two unused parameters.

与前面一样，对于具有特定种类参数的各种过程，我们需要相应的应用处理过程。严格原语过程的应用处理过程必须先强制求出实参值，然后执行原语过程。As before, we need handlers for application of the various kinds of procedures, with particular kinds of parameters. The application handler for strict primitive procedures has to force the arguments and then execute the primitive procedure.

(define-generic-procedure-handler x:apply

  (match-args strict-primitive-procedure?

              executors?

              environment?)

  (lambda (procedure operand-execs environment)

    (apply-primitive-procedure procedure

     (map (lambda (operand-exec)

            (x:advance (operand-exec environment)))

          operand-execs))))

一般过程的应用处理过程与前面展示的基本求值器中的版本只有细微差别。区别在于，我们现在处理的是执行过程，而不是运算对象表达式。The application handler for general procedures is only slightly different than in the elementary evaluator shown earlier. The difference is that we have execution procedures rather than operand expressions to work with.

(define-generic-procedure-handler x:apply

  (match-args compound-procedure? executors? environment?)

  (lambda (procedure operand-execs calling-environment)

    (if (not (n:= (length (procedure-parameters procedure))

                  (length operand-execs)))

        (error "Wrong number of operands supplied"))

    (let ((params (procedure-parameters procedure))

          (body-exec (procedure-body procedure)))

      (let ((names (map procedure-parameter-name params))

            (arguments

             (map (lambda (param operand-exec)

                    (x:handle-operand param

                                      operand-exec

                                      calling-environment))

                  params

                  operand-execs)))

        (body-exec (extend-environment names arguments

                     (procedure-environment procedure)))))))

这个复合过程的应用处理过程必须能够处理复合过程中可能出现的各种形式参数。按照惯常的做法，我们把 x:handle-operand 做成泛型过程来实现这一点。默认情况下，运算对象应在进入复合过程体之前求值，所以立即执行该运算对象的执行过程，以获得一个值。不过，惰性参数和带记忆的惰性参数需要能够适当地推迟执行。This application handler for compound procedures needs to be able to deal with the various kinds of formal parameters that may be present in the compound procedure. This is accomplished, in our usual way, by making x:handle-operand a generic procedure. The default, for an operand to be evaluated before entering the body of the compound procedure, is to immediately execute the operand execution procedure to obtain a value. However, lazy parameters and memoized lazy parameters need to be able to postpone the execution appropriately.

(define x:handle-operand

  (simple-generic-procedure ’x:handle-operand 3

    (lambda (parameter operand-exec environment)

      (operand-exec environment))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:handle-operand

  (match-args lazy? executor? environment?)

  (lambda (parameter operand-exec environment)

    (postpone operand-exec environment)))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:handle-operand

  (match-args lazy-memo? executor? environment?)

  (lambda (parameter operand-exec environment)

    (postpone-memo operand-exec environment)))

推迟运算对象执行过程的执行，与推迟运算对象表达式的求值是一样的。但泛型过程 x:advance 用来处理被推迟的运算对象执行过程的处理过程，与 g:advance 的处理过程不同：必须以保存的环境为实参调用被推迟的执行过程，而不是相对于该环境对它求值（与第 253 页的 g:advance 比较）。The postponement of an execution procedure for an operand is the same as the postponement of an operand expression. But the handlers for the generic procedure x:advance to deal with a postponed operand execution procedure are different from those for g:advance: the postponed execution procedure must be called on the postponed environment rather than evaluated relative to that environment (compare with g:advance on page 253).

(define-generic-procedure-handler x:advance

  (match-args postponed?)

  (lambda (object)

    (x:advance ((postponed-expression object)

                (postponed-environment object)))))



(define-generic-procedure-handler x:advance

  (match-args postponed-memo?)

  (lambda (object)

    (let ((value

           (x:advance ((postponed-expression object)

                       (postponed-environment object)))))

      (advance-memo! object value)

      value)))

这个 x:apply 对运算对象的处理并不高明。事实上，它在执行过程中对形式参数列表做了大量“解析”，所以我们并没有真正完整地编译复合过程。改进这种编译的一个步骤，是像前面那样将严格复合过程的处理过程单独分离出来。修正这个糟糕之处，是你在练习 5.16 中的任务。The handling of operands in this x:apply is not very clever. In fact, it does lots of “parsing” of the formal parameter list in the execution procedure, so we really did not fully compile the compound procedure. One step to improve this compilation would be to separate out the handler for strict compound procedures, as we did earlier. Fixing this nastiness is your job in exercise 5.16.

练习 5.12：实现 n 元过程Exercise 5.12: Implementing n-ary procedures

在练习 5.2 和 5.11 中，我们指出，能够接受不定数量实参的过程往往很有价值。Scheme 中的加法和乘法过程就是这样的例子。In exercises 5.2 and 5.11 we noted that it is often valuable to have procedures that can take an indefinite number of arguments. The addition and multiplication procedures in Scheme are examples of such procedures.

要在 Scheme 中定义这样的过程，我们把 lambda 表达式的形式参数指定为单个符号，而不是列表。该符号会绑定到一个由所提供实参组成的列表。例如，要构造一个接受若干实参并返回各实参平方的列表的过程，可以写成：To define such a procedure in Scheme, we specify the formal parameters of a lambda expression as a single symbol rather than a list. That symbol is bound to a list of the arguments supplied. For example, to make a procedure that takes several arguments and returns a list of the squares of the arguments, we can write:

(lambda x (map square x))

或者or

(define (ss . x) (map square x))

然后就可以写：and then we can say

(ss 1 2 3 4) ==> (1 4 9 16)

修改分析式解释器，使它支持这种构造。Modify the analyzing interpreter to allow this construct.

提示：不必修改语法定义中涉及 define 或 lambda 的代码！改动完全发生在分析器中。Hint: You do not need to change the code involving define or lambda in the syntax definitions! This is entirely a change in the analyzer.

证明你的修改支持这类过程，而且不会引发其他问题。Demonstrate that your modification allows this kind of procedure and that it does not cause other troubles.

练习 5.13：简化调试Exercise 5.13: Simplifying debugging

这个编译器的一个问题是，执行过程都是匿名的 lambda 表达式。因此，回溯信息能够报告的内容很少。不过，这很容易改善。如果把为应用构造执行过程的过程One problem with this compiler is that the execution procedures are all anonymous lambda expressions. So there is little information for a backtrace to report. However, it is easy to improve matters. If we rewrite the procedure that makes execution procedures for applications

(define (analyze-application exp)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator exp)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands exp))))

    (lambda (env)

      (x:apply (x:advance (operator-exec env))

               operand-execs

               env))))

改写为：like this:

(define (analyze-application exp)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator exp)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands exp))))

    (define (execute-application env)

      (x:apply (x:advance (operator-exec env))

               operand-execs

               env))

    execute-application))

那么（在 MIT/GNU Scheme 中），执行过程就会有一个名称，告诉我们它属于哪种执行过程。将这一想法应用到所有执行过程中。then (in MIT/GNU Scheme) the execution procedure will have a name that tells us what kind of execution procedure it is. Implement this idea in all the execution procedures.

想一想，还有哪些方法可以在不影响执行速度的情况下，改善运行时代码的可调试性，并酌情实现它们。一种做法是把表达式 exp 作为“便签”附在执行过程上。Think of, and perhaps implement, other ways we could improve the debuggability of the runtime code without impairing the execution speed. One thing you might do is add the expression exp as a “sticky note” on the execution procedure.

练习 5.14：常量折叠Exercise 5.14: Constant folding

假定我们有一种声明，可以告诉分析器某些符号具有给定的含义（例如，声明惯用的算术运算符 {+, -, *, /, sqrt} 指向已知且固定的过程）。那么，任何由这些运算符和常量组成的组合式，例如 (/ (+ 1 (sqrt 5)) 2)，都可以由分析器在编译时求值，并使用求得的结果，而不必在运行时执行计算。这种编译时优化称为常量折叠。Assume we have a declaration to tell the analyzer that certain symbols have a given meaning (for example a declaration that the conventional arithmetic operators {+, -, *, /, sqrt} refer to known constant procedures). Then any combination of constants with these operators, such as (/ (+ 1 (sqrt 5)) 2), may be evaluated by the analyzer at compile time and the result used instead of executing the computation at run time. This compile-time optimization is called constant folding.

在分析器中实现常量折叠。为了进行常量折叠，分析器需要知道，程序文本中的哪些符号可以确信绑定到了已知值。例如，它需要知道 car 是否确实绑定到了序对的原语选择器。假定分析器可以调用一个查找已知符号绑定的过程。这个过程应接受一个符号，并返回分析器可以信赖的值；如果该符号不在分析器的掌控之下，则返回 #f。Implement constant folding in the analyzer. To do constant folding, the analyzer needs to know which symbols in the program text it can count on to be bound to known values. For example, it needs to know if car is actually bound to the primitive selector of pairs. Assume that the analyzer can call a procedure that finds the bindings of known symbols. This procedure should take a symbol and return the value that the analyzer may depend on, or #f if the symbol is not under control of the analyzer.

练习 5.15：其他优化Exercise 5.15: Other optimizations

许多简单的变换都能改善程序的执行。例如，可以利用我们的模式匹配技术构造一个项重写系统，实现窥孔优化和循环不变代码外提。加入公共子表达式消除或许也不错，但要小心赋值引起的副作用。在分析过程中加入一个优化阶段，实现一些经典的编译器优化，并展示它们的效果。There are many simple transformations that can improve the execution of a program. For example, we can use our pattern-matching technology to make a term-rewriting system that implements peephole optimization and loop-invariant code motion. Perhaps it would be nice to add common subexpression elimination; but be careful about side effects due to assignments. Add a phase of optimization to the analysis, implement some classic compiler optimizations, and show their effects.

练习 5.16：编译形式参数声明Exercise 5.16: Compiling formal-parameter declarations

虽然转换成执行过程的组合非常有效，生成的代码也远快于直接解释执行，但我们给出的版本并不高明：x:apply 中用于复合过程的执行过程会解析形式参数列表，以确定如何处理运算对象。这其实应该在编译时而不是运行时完成：分析创建复合过程的 lambda 表达式时，应该生成一个知道如何处理运算对象和调用环境的执行过程。Although the transformation to compositions of execution procedures is quite effective, and produces much faster code than straight interpretation, the version we presented is not very clever: the compound-procedure execution procedure for x:apply parses the formal parameter list to determine how to handle the operands. This should really be done at compile time rather than run time: the analysis of the lambda expression that made the compound procedure should produce an execution procedure that knows what to do with the operands and calling environment.

想清楚并实现它。务必确保，调用环境只被携带到绝对必要的位置，不要传得更远。Figure this out and do it. Make sure that you do not carry the calling environment any further than is absolutely needed.

注意：这是一个大项目。Note: This is a big project.

5.4 探索性行为5.4 Exploratory behavior

我们已经遇到过在模式匹配中为匹配片段变量而进行的显式回溯搜索。不过，即使没有片段变量，项重写系统的实现也需要进行一些回溯搜索。有时，虽然规则的前件模式匹配了某段数据，但规则的后件表达式却判定，这一匹配的选择性还不够，不能用后件替换数据中匹配的部分。此时，后件表达式就返回 #f，以失败的方式回退到匹配过程，并可能尝试另一条规则。We have already encountered explicit backtracking search for matching segment variables in pattern matching. But even in the absence of segment variables, the implementation of the term-rewriting system required some backtracking search. When a rule's consequent expression determined that the match was not selective enough for the consequent to replace the matched part of the data, even though the antecedent pattern of the rule matched a piece of data, the consequent expression returned #f, failing back into the match and perhaps trying a different rule.

此外，用于优化泛型过程处理过程访问的字典树机制也需要回溯。字典树沿着一系列谓词前进，实参序列必须满足这些谓词。不过，谓词序列的初始部分可能有多种方式与实参序列的初始部分匹配，因此字典树机制中内含了隐式搜索。Also, the trie mechanism for optimizing the access to a generic procedure handler requires backtracking. The trie chases a sequence of predicates that the sequence of arguments must satisfy. But there may be multiple ways that an initial segment of predicates matches the initial segment of arguments, so there is an implicit search built into the trie mechanism.

我们通常把回溯，以及在搜索中对它的充分运用，看作一种人工智能技术。然而，也可以把回溯看作构造模块化且能够独立演化的系统的一种方法，就像生物系统的探索性行为那样。考虑一个简单而实用的例子：求解一元二次方程。一元二次方程有两个根。我们可以把两个根都返回，并假定解的使用者知道如何处理；也可以只返回一个，然后听天由命。（标准的平方根过程 sqrt 返回正平方根，尽管平方根有两个！）返回两个解的缺点是，结果的接收者必须知道要分别用两个解尝试计算，然后要么舍弃其中一个，要么返回计算得到的两个结果，而这一计算本身可能又作出了一些选择。只返回一个解的缺点是，它可能不是符合接收者目的的那个解。在物理系统仿真中，这可能是个切实的问题。We normally think of backtracking, and its extreme use in search, as an AI technique. However, backtracking can be viewed as a way of making systems that are modular and independently evolvable, as in the exploratory behavior of biological systems. Consider a simple but practical example: solving a quadratic equation. There are two roots to a quadratic. We could return both, and assume that the user of the solution knows how to deal with that, or we could return one and hope for the best. (The canonical square-root procedure sqrt returns the positive square root, even though there are two square roots!) The disadvantage of returning both solutions is that the receiver of that result must know to try the computation with both and either reject one, or return both results of the computation, which may itself have made some choices. The disadvantage of returning only one solution is that it may not be the right one for the receiver's purpose. This can be a real problem in simulations of physical systems.

语言层面隐含的搜索Linguistically implicit search

我们显式构造的搜索还不错，不过，如果将回溯机制内建于语言基础设施中，或许可以做得更好。平方根过程应该返回其中一个根，并保留改变主意的可能：如果接收者判定第一个选择不合适，就返回另一个根。判断计算所需的输入是否合适、是否可以接受，是也应该是接收者的责任。这本身可能需要复杂的计算，其中涉及的选择所带来的后果，也许要经过进一步计算才能显现；因此，这个过程是递归的。当然，这会让我们对程序中所有已作出的选择的所有可能取值进行搜索，而这样的指数级搜索可能是致命的。The searches we have explicitly built are okay, but perhaps we can do better by building a backtracking mechanism into the linguistic infrastructure. The square-root procedure should return one of the roots, with the option to change its mind and return the other one if the first choice is determined to be inappropriate by the receiver. It is, and should be, the receiver's responsibility to determine if the ingredients to its computation are appropriate and acceptable. This may itself require a complex computation, involving choices whose consequences may not be apparent without further computation; so the process is recursive. Of course, this gets us into potentially deadly exponential searches through all possible assignments to all the choices that have been made in the program.

一个重要问题是：搜索策略在多大程度上可以与程序的其他部分分离，从而无需大幅修改程序就能替换搜索策略。这里我们进一步把搜索及搜索控制下沉到语言所支持的基础设施中，根本不在程序中显式构造搜索。将搜索隐式化可能会诱使人们过度使用搜索。和往常一样，模块化所带来的灵活性也可能有危险。It is important to consider the extent to which a search strategy can be separated from the other parts of a program, so that one can interchange search strategies without greatly modifying the program. Here we take the further step of pushing search and search control into the infrastructure that is supported by the language, and not explicitly building search into our program at all. Making search implicit may encourage excessive use of search. As usual, modular flexibility can be dangerous.

这个想法颇有历史。1961 年，John McCarthy [90] 提出了非确定性运算符 amb 的想法，它可以用于表示非确定性自动机。1967 年，Bob Floyd [35] 提出将回溯搜索内建于计算机语言中，作为语言基础设施的一部分。1969 年，Carl Hewitt [56] 提出了体现这些想法的语言 PLANNER。20 世纪 70 年代初，Colmerauer、Kowalski、Roussel 和 Warren 开发了 Prolog [78]。这门语言基于一种受限的一阶谓词演算形式，使回溯搜索成为隐式机制。22This idea has considerable history. In 1961 John McCarthy [90] had the idea of a nondeterministic operator, amb, which could be useful for representing nondeterministic automata. In 1967 Bob Floyd [35] had the idea of building backtracking search into a computer language as part of the linguistic infrastructure. In 1969 Carl Hewitt [56] proposed a language, PLANNER, that embodied these ideas. In the early 1970s Colmerauer, Kowalski, Roussel, and Warren developed Prolog [78], a language based on a limited form of first-order predicate calculus, which made backtracking search implicit.22

5.4.1 amb

McCarthy 的 amb 接受任意数量的实参。amb 表达式的值是其中一个实参的值，但我们事先不知道哪一个才合适。例如，McCarthy's amb takes any number of arguments. The value of the amb expression is the value of one of the arguments, but we don't know in advance which one is appropriate. For example,

(amb 1 2 3)

产生的值可能是 1、2 或 3，具体取决于后续计算。不带实参的表达式 (amb) 没有任何可能的值：它表示计算失败，否定先前作出的选择。produces the value 1 or 2 or 3, depending on the future of the computation. The expression (amb), with no arguments, has no possible values: it is a computational failure, rejecting the choices previously made.

使用 amb 的表达式可能有许多可能的值。要查看所有可能的值，我们打印一个值，然后引发一次失败，迫使系统产生下一个值，直到再也没有值可取为止。An expression using amb may have many possible values. To see all the possible values we print one and then cause a failure, forcing the production of the next value, until there are no more to be had.

(begin

  (newline)

  (write-line (list (amb 1 2 3) (amb ’a ’b)))

  (amb))

;;; Starting a new problem (1 a)

(2 a)

(3 a)

(1 b)

(2 b)

(3 b)

;;; There are no more values

利用 amb，可以很容易地生成勾股三元组。我们用 amb 生成整数三元组，并排除其中不满足勾股关系的三元组。Using amb we can generate Pythagorean triples rather easily. We use amb to generate triples of integers and reject the ones that are not Pythagorean.

为了便于用 amb 编程，我们引入一个辅助过程。我们将 require 用作过滤器：如果作为其实参的谓词表达式不为真，它就强制引发失败并回溯。To facilitate programming with amb, we introduce a helper. We use require as a filter that will force a failure and backtrack if its argument predicate expression is not true.

(define (require p)

  (if (not p) (amb) ’ok))

要取得某个区间内的一个整数，可以写成：To obtain some integer in an interval, we write:

(define (an-integer-between low high)

  (require (<= low high))

  (amb low (an-integer-between (+ low 1) high)))

有了这些辅助过程，就可以用非常直观的形式来编写勾股三元组搜索：With these helpers we can write the search for Pythagorean triples in a very intuitive form:

(define (a-pythagorean-triple-between low high)

  (let ((i (an-integer-between low high)))

    (let ((j (an-integer-between i high)))

      (let ((k (an-integer-between j high)))

        (require (= (+ (* i i) (* j j))

                    (* k k)))

        (list i j k)))))



(begin

  (newline)

  (write-line (a-pythagorean-triple-between 1 20))

  (amb))

;;; Starting a new problem

(3 4 5)

(5 12 13)

(6 8 10)

(8 15 17)

(9 12 15)

(12 16 20)

;;; There are no more values

这似乎是一项普遍有用的功能。让我们看看如何将它纳入我们的语言。This seems like a generally useful facility. Let's see how we can make it part of our language.

5.4.2 实现 amb5.4.2 Implementing amb

幸好我们把语言表达式的分析与执行分离了，这让我们可以改变执行方式而不改变任何语法分析。因此，把非确定性搜索内建于语言中，只需修改执行过程。关键步骤是将执行过程转换为续延传递风格：除了环境实参，每个执行过程还接受两个续延实参，一个通常命名为 succeed，在计算成功时调用；另一个通常命名为 fail，在计算失败时调用。It is nice that we separated the analysis of the expressions of the language from the execution, because that allows us to change the execution without changing any of the syntactic analysis. So building nondeterministic search into the language is a matter of changing only the execution procedures. The critical step is to transform the execution procedures into continuation-passing style, where in addition to the environment argument, each execution procedure takes two continuation arguments: one, typically named succeed, that is called when the computation is successful, and the other, typically named fail, that is called when the computation is unsuccessful.

执行过程通过调用成功续延，并将候选值和一个失败续延传给它，来返回这个候选值。失败续延就是“投诉部门”：如果后续计算的某个部分不喜欢所提供的值，就可以不带实参地调用失败续延，要求一个不同的结果。（在 4.3 节中，我们用返回值 #f 表示失败。在 4.2.2 节中，我们使用了成功续延和失败续延。使用成功续延和失败续延更加灵活，还可以扩展，使其包含这个值为什么被拒绝的信息。）The execution procedure returns a proposed value by calling the success continuation with the value and a failure continuation. The failure continuation is the “complaint department”: if some future of the computation does not like the tendered value, it may call the failure continuation with no arguments to demand a different result. (In section 4.3 we used a returned value of #f as a failure indication. In section 4.2.2 we used success and failure continuations. The use of success and failure continuations is more flexible and can be expanded to include information about why the value was rejected.)

因此，执行过程的一般模式将是：So the general pattern of an execution procedure will be:

(lambda (environment succeed fail)

  ;; succeed = (lambda (value fail)

                 ;; Try this value.

                 ;; if don't like it (fail).

                 ;; ...)

  ;; fail = (lambda () ...)

  ...

  ;; Try to make a result.  If cannot, (fail).

  ...)

转换为续延传递风格有点令人不快，因为它会大幅增加代码量，但基本上是机械的。例如，第 260 页的 analyze-application 过程是：The transformation to continuation-passing style is a bit unpleasant, as it expands the code considerably, but it is basically mechanical. For example, the analyze-application procedure on page 260 is:

(define (analyze-application expression)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator expression)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands expression))))

    (lambda (environment)

      (x:apply (x:advance (operator-exec environment))

               operand-execs

               environment))))

如果把这段代码转换为续延传递风格，就得到：23If we transform this code to continuation-passing style we get:23

(define (analyze-application exp)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator exp)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (operator-exec env

                     (lambda (operator-value fail-1)

                       (a:advance operator-value

                                  (lambda (procedure fail-2)

                                    (a:apply procedure

                                             operand-execs

                                             env

                                             succeed

                                             fail-2))

                                  fail-1))

                     fail))))

这个执行过程比它所源自的过程更复杂。在原来执行过程的过程体中，表达式 (operator-exec environment) 向表达式 (x:advance ...) 返回一个值，后者再向表达式 (x:apply) 返回一个值。在新的执行过程中，这些嵌套表达式不见了。每个过程都通过调用一个接受其计算结果的过程来“返回”。This execution procedure is more complicated than the one it was derived from. In the body of the original execution procedure, the expression (operator-exec environment) returns a value to the expression (x:advance ...), which in turn returns a value to the expression (x:apply). In the new execution procedure, these nested expressions are gone. Each procedure “returns” by calling a procedure that accepts the results of its computation.

由于我们经常需要强制求出一个值，适合为这种强制求值建立一个抽象。为了确保得到一个不再被推迟的值，需要强制对被推迟的表达式求值；过程 execute-strict 隐藏了这一过程中无关紧要的细节。在上面的 analyze-application 中，它用来强制求出运算符的值，以获得一个可以应用的过程。Since we will often have to force a value, it is appropriate to make an abstraction that captures the forcing. The procedure execute-strict hides the uninteresting details associated with the process of forcing the evaluation of a postponed expression in order to ensure an unpostponed value. In analyze-application above, it is used to force the value of the operator in order to get an applicable procedure.

(define (execute-strict executor env succeed fail)

  (executor env

            (lambda (value fail-1)

              (a:advance value succeed fail-1))

            fail))

过程 execute-strict 调用给定的执行过程（executor）。得到的结果随后传给 a:advance，以进行强制求值。强制求得的值再传给 execute-strict 的成功续延（succeed），实际上就把强制求值的结果返回给了 execute-strict 的调用者。The procedure execute-strict calls the given execution procedure (executor). The result of that is then passed to a:advance to be forced. The forced value is then passed to the success continuation (succeed) of execute-strict, effectively returning the result of the forcing to the caller of execute-strict.

使用 execute-strict，可以重写 analyze-application：Using execute-strict we can rewrite analyze-application:

(define (analyze-application exp)

  (let ((operator-exec (analyze (operator exp)))

        (operand-execs (map analyze (operands exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (execute-strict operator-exec

                      env

                      (lambda (procedure fail-2)

                        (a:apply procedure

                                 operand-execs

                                 env

                                 succeed

                                 fail-2))

                      fail))))

每个执行过程都必须这样转换。我们在 analyze-if 中使用 execute-strict，强制求出条件表达式中谓词的值；没有这个值，就无法继续：Each of the execution procedures has to be transformed in this way. We use execute-strict in analyze-if to force the value of the predicate of the conditional, without which we cannot proceed:

(define (analyze-if exp)

  (let ((predicate-exec (analyze (if-predicate exp)))

        (consequent-exec (analyze (if-consequent exp)))

        (alternative-exec (analyze (if-alternative exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (execute-strict predicate-exec

                      env

                      (lambda (pred-value pred-fail)

                        ((if pred-value

                             consequent-exec

                             alternative-exec)

                         env succeed pred-fail))

                      fail))))

大多数转换都很直接，我们就不用这些细节增加正文的负担了。不过，有一个有趣的情形：赋值。在回溯系统中，我们通常需要两种不同的赋值。常规的永久赋值 set! 可用于在搜索过程中积累信息，例如某个分支被考察了多少次。还有一种可撤销赋值 maybe-set!，如果它所在的分支被撤回，就必须撤销该赋值。常规的永久赋值实现如下：Most of the transformations are straightforward, and we will not burden you with the details in this text. But there is an interesting case: assignments. Often in backtracking systems we need two different kinds of assignment. The usual permanent assignment, set!, is useful for accumulating information during a search process, such as how many times a particular branch is investigated. There is also an undoable assignment maybe-set! that must be undone if the branch it is on is retracted. The usual permanent assignment is implemented as:

(define (analyze-assignment exp)

  (let ((var (assignment-variable exp))

        (value-exec (analyze (assignment-value exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (value-exec env

                  (lambda (new-val val-fail)

                    (set-variable-value! var new-val env)

                    (succeed ’ok val-fail))

                  fail))))

可撤销赋值更复杂。赋值成功时传出的失败续延，会把被赋值变量的值恢复为原来的值。The undoable assignment is more complex. The failure continuation passed with the successful assignment reverts the value of the assigned variable to its previous value.

(define (analyze-undoable-assignment exp)

  (let ((var (assignment-variable exp))

        (value-exec (analyze (assignment-value exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (value-exec env

                  (lambda (new-val val-fail)

                    (let ((old-val

                           (lookup-variable-value var env)))

                      (set-variable-value! var new-val env)

                      (succeed ’ok

                               (lambda ()

                                 (set-variable-value! var

                                                      old-val

                                                      env)

                                 (val-fail)))))

                  fail))))

另一个、也是仅剩的有趣情形，是 amb 本身的实现。这里，如果上一次提供的备选项被拒绝，我们就必须选择下一个备选项。这由当前备选项的失败续延完成：The only other interesting case is the implementation of amb itself. Here is where we have to select the next alternative if the last one tendered is rejected. This is done by the failure continuation for the current alternative:

(define (analyze-amb exp)

  (let ((alternative-execs

         (map analyze (amb-alternatives exp))))

    (lambda (env succeed fail)

      (let loop ((alts alternative-execs))

        (if (pair? alts)

            ((car alts) env

                        succeed

                        (lambda ()

                          (loop (cdr alts))))

            (fail))))))

如果没有剩余的备选项，amb 的执行过程就调用传入的失败续延。这使程序对备选项树进行深度优先搜索。对备选项列表不断取 cdr，就能逐一检查这些备选项；因此搜索按从左到右的顺序进行。24If there are no alternatives left, the execution procedure for amb calls the failure continuation it was called with. This makes the program execute a depth-first search of the tree of alternatives. The alternatives are examined by cdring down the list of alternatives; thus the search proceeds in left-to-right order.24

除了调整读入—求值—打印循环（第 246 页），使其能配合续延传递结构工作之外，全部工作就这么多！Except for adjustments to the read-eval-print loop (page 246) to make it work with the continuation-passing structure, that is all there is to it!

练习 5.17：一道谜题Exercise 5.17: A puzzle

使用 amb 将下列谜题形式化并求解：Formalize and solve the following puzzle using amb:

两位女士（Alyssa 和 Eva）与四位男士（Ben、Louis、Cy 和 Lem）围坐在一张圆桌旁打牌。每人手中都有一手牌，任意两人的牌力都不相等。Two women (Alyssa and Eva) and four men (Ben, Louis, Cy, and Lem) are seated at a round table, playing cards. Each has a hand; no two of the hands are equally strong.

  • Ben 坐在 Eva 的正对面。Ben is seated opposite Eva.
  • Alyssa 右边那位男士的牌比 Lem 的强。The man at Alyssa's right has a stronger hand than Lem has.
  • Eva 右边那位男士的牌比 Ben 的强。The man at Eva's right has a stronger hand than Ben has.
  • Ben 右边那位男士的牌比 Cy 的强。The man at Ben's right has a stronger hand than Cy has.
  • Ben 右边那位男士的牌比 Eva 的强。The man at Ben's right has a stronger hand than Eva has.

他们在桌旁的座次是怎样的？在将整桌旋转视为相同安排的意义下，座次是否唯一？What is the arrangement at the table? Is it unique up to rotation of the table?

使用 amb 指定每次选择的可能备选项。此外，如果给出的条件不是“Ben 右边那位男士的牌比 Cy 的强”，而是“Ben 右边那位男士不是 Cy”，确定此时有多少个解。解释这一结果。Use amb to specify the alternatives that are possible for each choice. 练习 5.20：选择的顺序Exercise 5.20: Choice ordering

按目前的写法，amb 机制总是按照 amb 表达式中给出的顺序尝试各个选择。但有时，我们可以利用上下文信息来确定更好的顺序。例如，在棋盘游戏中，从合法走法中选择一步，应该取决于棋盘的状态。让我们设计一个能够提供这种灵活性的 amb 版本。假定每个选择表达式都配有一个数值权重表达式：The amb mechanism, as written, always tries the choices in the order given in the amb expression. But sometimes we can use contextual information to make a better ordering. For example, in a board game the choice of a move from the possible legal moves should depend on the state of the game board. Let's invent a version of amb that can give us this kind of flexibility. Let's assume that each choice expression is paired with a numerical weight expression:

(choose (<weight-1> <choice-1>) ... (<weight-n> <choice-n>))

我们可以对所有权重表达式求值，并据此选出下一个要进行求值并返回其结果的选择表达式。当然，一旦作出了某个选择，该选择就用尽了；如果一次失败回溯到这个 choose 形式，那么在作出下一个选择之前，必须对剩余的权重表达式重新求值。We can evaluate all the weight expressions and use them to choose the next choice expression to be evaluated and returned. Of course, after a choice is made, it is exhausted, and if a failure gets back to this choose form, the remaining weight expressions must be reevaluated before making the next choice.

  1. a. 实现 choose，使它选取权重最大的选择。a. Implement choose so that a choice with the largest weight is chosen.
  2. b. 在实际情形中，权重通常不足以唯一确定一个选择。有时，一个好的策略是随机选择，其概率与计算出的权重成正比。实现另一个选择器 pchoose，其语法与 choose 相同，按这种方式工作。b. In real situations the weights are usually not strong enough to make a unique choice. Sometimes a good strategy is to make a random choice with probability that is proportional to the computed weights. Implement an alternative chooser pchoose, with the same syntax as choose, that works in this way.

5.5 暴露底层续延5.5 Exposing the underlying continuations

现在，我们已经可以接触真正的魔法了！Now we are in a position to deal with real magic!

大多数语言，包括 Scheme，都是围绕表达式的概念组织的。表达式有一个它所“返回”的值。表达式由子表达式组成，每个子表达式都有一个值，并将这个值返回给包含它的更大表达式。表达式的本质思想是什么？Most languages, including Scheme, are organized around the notion of an expression. An expression has a value that it “returns.” An expression is made up of subexpressions, each of which has a value that it returns to the bigger expression it is a part of. What is the essential idea of an expression?

考虑复合表达式Consider the compound expression

(+ 1 (* 2 3) (/ 8 2))

当然，它的值是 11。计算方法是先对运算符和运算对象求值，再把运算符的值（过程）应用到运算对象的值（实参）上。Of course, this has the value 11. It is computed by evaluating the operator and the operands, then applying the value of the operator (the procedure) to the values of the operands (the arguments).

把这项计算改写为续延传递风格，可以使这个过程更加清晰。这里，我们引入新运算符 **、// 和 ++，分别命名续延传递风格的乘法、除法和加法过程：This process can be clarified by reformulating the computation in continuation-passing style. Here we invent new operators **, //, and ++ to name the continuation-passing style multiplication, division, and addition procedures:

(define (** m1 m2 continue)

  (continue (* m1 m2)))



(define (// n d continue)

  (continue (/ n d)))



(define (++ a1 a2 continue)

  (continue (+ a1 a2)))

这些过程与通常的 *、/ 和 + 不同：它们不返回到调用者，而是被定义为以计算出的值为实参，调用自己的最后一个实参。接收该值的实参称为续延过程。我们在 4.2.2 节和These procedures differ from the usual *, /, and + in that they do not return to their caller; rather they are defined to call their last argument with the value computed. The argument that receives the value is called the continuation procedure. We used continuation-passing style in sections 4.2.2 and 5.4.2以及第 188 页的合一器中，也使用了续延传递风格。 and also in the unifier on page 188.

以续延传递风格计算 (+ 1 (* 2 3) (/ 8 2))，形式如下：The computation of (+ 1 (* 2 3) (/ 8 2)) in continuation-passing style looks like:

(** 2 3

    (lambda (the-product)            ; A

      (// 8 2

          (lambda (the-quotient)     ; B

            (++ 1 the-product the-quotient

                k)))))

其中 k 是最终的续延过程，它接受一个实参，即该计算的值 11。26where k is the final continuation procedure, which takes one argument, which is the value 11 of the computation.26

在这个例子中，过程 ** 计算 2 与 3 的积，并以 6 为实参调用其续延过程（由注释 A 标记的 lambda 表达式）。因此，在 A 的过程体中，the-product 绑定到 6。在 A 的过程体中，过程 // 计算 8 与 2 的商，并将所得的 4 传给标记为 B 的过程，其中 the-quotient 绑定到 4。在 B 的过程体中，过程 ++ 计算 1、6 和 4 的和，并把所得的 11 传给续延过程 k。In this example the procedure ** computes the product of 2 and 3 and calls its continuation procedure (the lambda expression labeled by comment A) with 6. Thus, in the body of A, the-product is bound to 6. In the body of A the procedure // computes the quotient of 8 and 2 and passes the resulting 4 to the procedure labeled B, where the-quotient is bound to 4. In the body of B the procedure ++ computes the sum of 1, 6, and 4, and passes the resulting 11 to the continuation procedure k.

在续延传递风格中，不存在返回值的嵌套表达式。所有结果都传给续延过程。因此，不需要栈，因为没有谁在等待返回的值！我们所做的，是把表达式树线性化，就像编译器为了在顺序机器上计算表达式的值而必须做的那样。In continuation-passing style there are no nested expressions that return values. All results are passed to continuation procedures. Thus, there is no need for a stack, because there is nobody waiting for the value returned! Instead, we have linearized our expression tree in the same way that a compiler must in order to compute the value of the expression in a sequential machine.

底层续延Underlying continuations

这里的想法是：表达式中容纳子表达式的位置，只不过是某个过程的语法糖；这个过程接受子表达式的值，以供后续继续对整个表达式求值时使用。这一想法非常强大，因为续延代表了计算的全部未来。对表达式含义的这种更深入的理解，让我们能够摆脱单值表达式的编程风格，代价则是相当可观的复杂性和语法嵌套。The idea is that the slot in the expression that contains the subexpression is just syntactic sugar for a procedure that accepts the value of the subexpression for later use in continuing the evaluation of the expression. This idea is very powerful, because the continuation represents the entire future of the computation. This deeper understanding of the meaning of an expression allows us to escape from the single-valued expression style of programming, at the considerable cost of complexity and syntactic nesting.

每当对一个表达式求值时，都有一个续延等待着该表达式的结果。例如，如果在顶层对表达式求值，续延就会接收结果，把它打印到屏幕上，提示输入下一个表达式，对它求值，如此永远进行下去。大多数时候，续延包含用户代码所指定的动作。例如，一个续延会接收结果，将它乘以某个局部变量中存储的值，加上七，再把答案交给顶层续延打印。通常，这些无处不在的续延都藏在幕后，程序员并不太去想它们。Scheme 允许程序员取得表达式的底层续延。底层续延是一等对象，可以作为实参传递、作为值返回，也可以放入数据结构。大多数其他语言不支持使用一等续延。（支持它们的语言包括 SML、Ruby 和 Smalltalk。）Whenever an expression is evaluated, a continuation exists that expects the result of the expression. If the expression is evaluated at top level, for example, the continuation will take the result, print it on the screen, prompt for the next input, evaluate it, and so on, forever. Most of the time the continuation includes actions specified by user code, as in a continuation that will take the result, multiply it by the value stored in a local variable, add seven, and give the answer to the top-level continuation to be printed. Normally these ubiquitous continuations are hidden behind the scenes, and programmers don't think much about them. Scheme provides the ability for a programmer to get the underlying continuation of an expression. An underlying continuation is a first-class object that can be passed as an argument, returned as a value, and incorporated into a data structure. Most other languages do not support the use of first-class continuations. (Languages that do have them include SML, Ruby, and Smalltalk.)

显式的底层续延是程序员最强大（也最危险）的工具之一。续延让程序员可以显式控制时间。计算可以在某一时刻被捕获并挂起，再在未来的任意时刻恢复并继续。这使我们能够编写协程（协作式多任务）；再加上定时器中断机制，就能实现分时（抢占式多任务）。当你需要显式处理续延时，Scheme 允许你创建一个表示当前续延的显式过程。不过，要掌握这种力量，我们需要更深入地理解续延。Explicit underlying continuations are one of the most powerful (and most dangerous) tools of a programmer. Continuations give the programmer explicit control over time. A computation can be captured and suspended at one moment and restored and continued at any future time. This makes it possible to write coroutines (cooperative multitasking), and with the addition of a timer interrupt mechanism we get timesharing (preemptive multitasking). On the occasions that you may need to deal explicitly with continuations, Scheme lets you do so by creating an explicit procedure that is the current continuation. But before we can take charge of this power we need a deeper understanding of continuations.

续延是对计算的控制状态的一次捕获。27 如果调用一个续延，计算就从该续延所代表的位置继续。续延可以代表将子表达式的值返回给外层表达式求值过程这一动作。此时，续延就是这样一个过程：调用它时，它把自己的实参作为该子表达式的值，返回给外层表达式的求值过程。一个续延可以被调用多次，让计算在某个特定位置恢复，并由该续延返回不同的值。我们很快就会看到一个例子。A continuation is a captured control state of a computation.27 If a continuation is invoked, the computation continues at the place represented by the continuation. A continuation may represent the act of returning a value of a subexpression to the evaluation of the enclosing expression. The continuation is then a procedure that when invoked returns its argument to the evaluation of the enclosing expression as the value of the subexpression. A continuation can be invoked multiple times, allowing a computation to be resumed at a particular point with different values returned by the continuation. We will see an example shortly.

Scheme 提供了 call-with-current-continuation（缩写为 call/cc），可用来访问表达式结构背后的续延。call/cc 的实参是一个过程；这个过程会以 call/cc 表达式的续延为实参被调用。再强调一次：续延是一个一等过程，接受一个实参——调用该续延时要返回的值。28 下面是一个简单例子：Scheme provides call-with-current-continuation (abbreviated call/cc), which gives access to the continuations that underly expression structure. The argument to call/cc is a procedure that gets the continuation of the call/cc expression as its argument. Again: a continuation is a first-class procedure that takes one argument—the value to be returned when the continuation is called.28 Here is a simple example:

(define foo)



(set! foo

  (+ 1

     (call/cc

        (lambda (k)

          ;; k is the continuation

          ;; of the call/cc expression.

          ;; so if we call k with 6

          ;; then foo will get the value 11

          (k (* 2 3))))

     (/ 8 2)))



foo

11

所以，call/cc 以 call/cc 的续延为实参，调用了自己的实参。目前还不太令人兴奋！到现在为止，这与直接对 (+ 1 (* 2 3) (/ 8 2)) 求值并没有什么不同。So call/cc calls its argument with the continuation of the call/cc. Not very exciting yet! So far this is no different from the straightforward evaluation of (+ 1 (* 2 3) (/ 8 2)).

不过，Scheme 中的过程具有无限生存期。这就完全改变了局面。让我们把续延保存下来，以便再次使用。But procedures in Scheme have indefinite extent. This is a game changer. Let's save the continuation for reuse.

(define bar)

(define foo)



(set! foo

  (+ 1

     (call/cc

        (lambda (k)

          (set! bar k)

          (k (* 2 3))))

     (/ 8 2)))



foo

11



(bar -2)



foo

3

哇，看看发生了什么！我们把最终会为 foo 赋值的那项计算的未来保存在了 bar 中。当我们用另一个值调用这个续延时，对 foo 的赋值重新执行了一遍，使 foo 得到了不同的值。Wow, look what happened! We saved in bar the future of the computation that ultimately gives a value to foo. When we called that continuation with another value, the assignment of foo was redone, resulting in a different value of foo.

5.5.1 用续延实现非局部退出5.5.1 Continuations as nonlocal exits

考虑下面这个非局部退出续延的简单例子（改编自 Scheme 报告 [109]）：Consider the following simple example of a nonlocal exit continuation (adapted from the Scheme report [109]):

(call/cc

 (lambda (exit)

   (for-each (lambda (x)

               (if (negative? x) (exit x)))

             ’(54 0 37 -3 245 -19))  ; **

   (exit #t)))

-3

由于 Scheme 的 for-each 过程按从左到右的顺序遍历列表，遇到的第一个负元素是 -3，于是立即返回它。如果列表中没有负数，结果就会是 #t（因为外层 lambda 表达式的过程体是一个由两个表达式组成的序列：先是 for-each 表达式，然后返回 #t）。Because Scheme's for-each procedure walks the list in left-to-right order, the first negative element encountered is -3, which is immediately returned. Had the list contained no negative numbers, the result would have been #t (since the body of the outer lambda expression is a sequence of two expressions, the for-each expression followed by returning #t).

对 call/cc 的使用也可能出现在另一个表达式内部，如下面的定义所示。（按照惯例，绑定到底层续延的符号以字母 k 开头。）The use of call/cc might appear within some other expression, as in the following definition. (Traditionally, a symbol bound to an underlying continuation starts with the letter k.)

(define (first-negative list-of-numbers)

  (call/cc

   (lambda (k exit)

     (or (call/cc (lambda (k shortcut)

                    (for-each (lambda (n)

                                (cond ((not (number? n))

                                       (pp ‘(not-a-number: ,n))

                                       (k exit #f))

                                      ((negative? n)

                                       (k shortcut n))

                                      (else

                                       ’keep-looking)))

                              list-of-numbers)

                    #f))

         ’no-negatives-found))))

它的行为如下：This behaves as follows:

(first-negative ’(54 0 37 -3 245 -19))

-3



(first-negative ’(54 0 37 3 245 19))

no-negatives-found



(first-negative ’(54 0 37 no 245 -19))

(not-a-number: no)

#f

这展示了嵌套续延：最外层的 k exit 续延会退出对 first-negative 的整个调用，而内层的 k shortcut 续延只会退出到包围它的析取表达式，再从那里继续。This demonstrates nested continuations, where the outermost k exit continuation exits the entire call to first-negative while the inner k shortcut continuation exits only to the enclosing disjunction, then continues from there.

简言之，只要以某个值调用了由 call/cc 捕获的续延，计算就会把这个值作为捕获该续延的那次 call/cc 调用的值返回，然后从那里正常恢复执行。In short, if a continuation captured by call/cc is ever invoked with some value, then the computation will continue by returning that value as the value of the call to call/cc that captured it and resuming execution normally from there.

练习 5.21：非局部退出Exercise 5.21: Nonlocal exits

本练习应在原生 Scheme 中完成，相比在我们的嵌入式解释器中，这样更容易调试和插入监测代码。原生 Scheme 中有一个很好的 call/cc 实现。This exercise is to be done in the native Scheme, where it will be easier to debug and instrument than in our embedded interpreter. There is a good implementation of call/cc in the native Scheme.

  1. a. 定义一个简单过程 snark-hunt，29 它接受一棵树作为实参，递归地向下遍历该树，查找任意叶子处的符号 snark。如果找到，就应立即停止搜索并返回 #t；否则返回 #f。请使用 call/cc。例如：a. Define a simple procedure, snark-hunt,29 that takes a tree as its argument and recursively descends the tree looking for the symbol snark at any leaf. It should immediately stop searching and return #t if one is found; #f otherwise. Use call/cc. For example: 
    (snark-hunt ’(((a b c) d (e f)) g (((snark . "oops") h) (i . j))))

      #t

    注意，snark-hunt 的输入未必完全由正规列表组成。Note that the input to snark-hunt may not be composed solely of proper lists.

  2. b. 如何验证 snark-hunt 是立即退出的，而不是悄悄地逐层返回？定义一个新过程 snark-hunt/instrumented 来展示这一点。b. How might you verify that snark-hunt exits immediately rather than silently returning through multiple return levels? Define a new procedure, snark-hunt/instrumented, to demonstrate this.

提示：设置一个退出状态标志，然后在不该经过的返回路径上报错，若安排得当，或许可行；不过，直接用 pp 进行跟踪可能更容易。任何能奏效的简便粗糙手段都可以。这里的目标是建立对续延的直觉，而不是交付产品级的代码。简要说明你的策略。Hint: Setting an exit status flag, then signaling an error on wayward return paths might work if placed carefully, but simply tracing via pp may be easier. Any quick and dirty hack that works will do. The goal here is to build your intuition about continuations, not to ship product-quality code. Briefly explain your strategy.

5.5.2 非局部控制转移5.5.2 Nonlocal transfer of control

前面的例子有些过于简单，因为捕获的续延只用于非局部退出。但续延的能力不止于此：它们在被调用过后，还可以再次进入。下面的例子说明了这一想法：30The preceding was somewhat simplistic, because the continuations captured were used only for nonlocal exits. But continuations are more powerful than that: they can be reentered once invoked. The following example illustrates the idea:30

(define the-continuation #f)



(define (test)

  (let ((i 0))

    ;; The argument to call/cc assigns the

    ;; continuation produced by call/cc to the

    ;; global variable the-continuation.

    (call/cc (lambda (k) (set! the-continuation k)))

    ;; When the-continuation is called, execution

    ;; resumes here.

    (set! i (+ i 1))

    i))

这种行为也许令人惊讶。过程 test 创建一个局部变量 i，将其初始化为 0。它还创建一个续延，表示从 let 表达式体内的 call/cc 表达式返回时的控制状态，并将该状态存储在全局变量 the-continuation 中。随后，它递增 i，并返回 i 的新值：1。The behavior is perhaps surprising. The procedure test creates a local variable i initialized to 0. It also creates a continuation representing the control state of returning from the call/cc expression in the body of the let expression and stores that state in the global variable the-continuation. It then increments i and returns i's new value: 1.

(test)

1

调用 the-continuation 时，call/cc 就返回到 let 表达式的体中。执行继续，递增 i 并返回它的新值。这个续延可以重复使用，再次递增 i 并返回它的新值。When the-continuation is called, the call/cc returns to the body of the let expression. Execution proceeds to increment i and return its new value. The continuation can be reused to increment i again and return its new value.

(the-continuation ’OK)

2



(the-continuation ’OK)

3

（实参 OK 就是 call/cc 的值；let 的体会忽略它。）(The argument OK is the value of the call/cc; it is ignored by the let body.)

我们把这个续延保存在 another-continuation 中，这样就可以再次执行 test，创建一个新续延存入 the-continuation。对 test 的调用创建了 i 的另一个实例，并将它初始化为 0。We save the continuation in another-continuation, so we can make a new one to be stored in the-continuation by executing test again. The call to test creates another instance of i, which is initialized to 0.

(define another-continuation the-continuation)



(test)

1

这个新续延与保存在 another-continuation 中的那个续延相互独立。This new continuation is independent of the one we saved in another-continuation.

(the-continuation ’OK)

2



(another-continuation ’OK) ; uses the saved continuation

4

现在考虑下面这个稍微更有趣的情形：Now consider the following slightly more interesting scenario:

(define the-continuation #f)

(define sum #f)



(begin

  (set! sum

        (+ 2 (call/cc

              (lambda (k)

                (set! the-continuation k)

                (k 3)))))

  ’ok)

ok



sum

5



(the-continuation 4)
