请仔细注意，通过调用 the-continuation 重新进入这个被捕获的续延，会把控制权交回到加法之前的位置，因此也在对变量 sum 赋值和返回符号 ok 之前。这就是为什么调用它总会返回符号 ok。不过，sum 被赋成了 2 与我们传给 the-continuation 的实参之和。因此，当我们询问 sum 的值时，就会得到这个新的和。这展示了如何利用被捕获的续延，从中间返回点继续执行。我们将在以下一节中看到如何利用这种机制进行回溯：Note carefully how reentering this captured continuation, by calling the-continuation, returns control to the point before the addition and, therefore, before assigning variable sum and returning the symbol ok. This is why invoking it always returns the symbol ok. However, sum is assigned the sum of 2 and the argument we supplied to the-continuation. So when we ask for the value of sum we get that new sum. This demonstrates how to use a captured continuation to proceed from intermediate return points. We will see how this mechanism can be used for backtracking in 5.5.3 节section 5.5.3.

5.5.3 从续延到 amb5.5.3 From continuations to amb

事实证明，我们想做的几乎所有事情，包括实现 amb，都可以仅用 Scheme 原生的 call/cc 来完成；让我们看看如何做到。It turns out that almost anything we want to do, including implementing amb, can be done with just the Scheme native call/cc; let's see how to do that.

事实上，续延天然适合用来支持回溯。我们可以作出一个选择；如果后来发现这个选择不合适，就可以作出另一个选择，并推演其后果。（真希望现实生活也有这个功能！）在平方根的例子中，平方根程序应该返回两个平方根的 amb；其中 amb 是一个运算符，它选出并返回其中一个根，并保留在第一个根被拒绝后提供另一个根的可能。接收者只管继续使用给出的解；但如果它在某个时刻发现自己的计算不满足某项约束，就可以 fail，促使 amb 运算符修改选择，并通过它的续延返回新的选择。实质上，续延使选择的生成者能够写成一个协程，与选择的接收者／测试者交互。Indeed, continuations are a natural mechanism for supporting backtracking. A choice can be made, and if that choice turns out to be inappropriate, an alternative choice can be made and its consequences worked out. (Wouldn't we like real life to have this feature!) In our square-root example, the square-root program should return the amb of both square roots, where amb is the operator that chooses and returns one of them, with the option to provide the other if the first is rejected. The receiver can then just proceed to use the given solution; but if at some point the receiver finds that its computation does not meet some constraint, it can fail, causing the amb operator to revise its choice and return with the new choice through its continuation. In essence, the continuation allows the generator of choices to be written as a coroutine that interacts with the receiver/tester of the choices.

回溯器的核心是 amb-list，它接受一系列同级延迟过程，每个延迟过程代表 amb 表达式的一个备选值。这些延迟过程由 amb 宏生成，该宏在语法层面把 amb 表达式转换为 amb-list 表达式，如下所示：The heart of the backtracker is amb-list, which takes a sequence of sibling thunks, each representing an alternative value for the amb expression. The thunks are produced by an amb macro, which syntactically transforms amb expressions into amb-list expressions, as follows:

(amb e1 ... en) ==>

  (amb-list (list (lambda () e1) ... (lambda () en)))

amb 宏（用可移植的 syntax-rules 形式编写）如下：The amb macro (written in portable syntax-rules form) is:

(define-syntax amb

  (syntax-rules ()

    ((amb exp ...)

     (amb-list (list (lambda () exp) ...)))))

例如：For example:

(pp (syntax ’(amb a b c) user-initial-environment))

(amb-list (list (lambda () a) (lambda () b) (lambda () c)))

搜索过程维护一个搜索调度表，其中安排着一些延迟过程；当需要让 amb 表达式返回一个新的备选值时，就可以调用这些延迟过程。过程 amb-list 首先把各个备选值对应的延迟过程加入搜索调度表，然后把控制权让给调度表中第一个待执行的延迟过程。如果没有备选项（表达式仅仅是 (amb)），amb-list 就不向搜索调度表加入任何东西而直接让出控制权，并递增一个用于统计搜索情况的全局计数器。The search maintains a search schedule, an agenda of thunks that can be called when it is necessary for an amb expression to return with a new alternative value. The procedure amb-list first adds the thunks for its alternative values to the search schedule and then yields control to the first pending thunk on the schedule. If there are no alternatives (the expression was just (amb)) then the amb-list yields control without adding anything to the search schedule and increments a global counter for auditing the search.

(define (amb-list alternatives)

  (if (null? alternatives)

      (set! *number-of-calls-to-fail*

            (+ *number-of-calls-to-fail* 1)))

  (call/cc

   (lambda (k)

     ((add-to-search-schedule)

      (map (lambda (alternative)

             (lambda ()

               (within-continuation k alternative)))

           alternatives))

     (yield))))

对于某个特定的 amb 表达式，备选项的延迟过程被构造成：利用在其外层 amb-list 的入口处捕获的续延 k，从该 amb 表达式返回。31For a particular amb expression the thunks for the alternatives are constructed so as to return from that amb expression, using the continuation, k, captured at the entrance to their enclosing amb-list.31

让出控制权的方法，是从搜索调度表中取出一个指定某个备选项的延迟过程（如果有的话），然后执行它。搜索调度表既是栈也是队列；我们很快就会看到原因。The way to yield control is to retrieve a thunk specifying an alternative, if any, from the search schedule and execute it. The search schedule is both a stack and a queue; we will see why shortly.

(define (yield)

  (if (deque-empty? (*search-schedule*))

      ((*top-level*) ’no-more-alternatives)

      ((pop! (*search-schedule*)))))

我们调用 *top-level* 和 add-to-search-schedule 来取得实际执行工作的过程，这也许会让你感到困惑。我们还调用 *search-schedule* 来取得搜索调度表对象。这种间接方式的原因是，它们是 Scheme 参数对象（见第 394 页）。之所以这样定义，是因为我们将把它们动态绑定到不同的值，稍后就会展示。我们将 *search-schedule* 初始化为空：You may be puzzled by the fact that we call *top-level* and add-to-search-schedule to get the procedures that do the work. We also call *search-schedule* to get the search schedule object. The reason for this indirection is that these are Scheme parameter objects (see page 394). We have defined them this way because we will be dynamically binding them to different values, as will be shown shortly. We initialize the *search-schedule* to be empty:

(define *search-schedule*

  (make-parameter (empty-search-schedule)))

魔法就在 amb-list 中的 call/cc。amb-list（因而也是 amb）执行了 yield。对于这个 amb 的每个备选项，这个 call/cc 的续延，因而也是这个 amb 的续延，都会被放到搜索调度表上。从搜索调度表弹出的某个备选项被执行时，它的值会由当初把它放入搜索调度表的那个 amb 表达式返回。The magic is the call/cc in amb-list. The amb-list (and thus the amb) executes the yield. The continuation of this call/cc, and thus of this amb, is put onto the search schedule for each alternative of this amb. When an alternative popped from the search schedule is executed, its value is returned by whatever amb expression put that alternative into the search schedule.

让搜索调度表同时支持栈和队列，就可以实现深度优先和广度优先搜索，因为两者的区别仅在于调度顺序。如下所示，这通过把参数 add-to-search-schedule 动态绑定为所需的排序方式来实现。By making the search schedule both a stack and a queue, we can implement both depth-first and breadth-first search, because they differ only in the order of the schedule. This is done by dynamically binding the add-to-search-schedule parameter to the ordering desired, as shown below.

默认采用深度优先：The default is depth first:

(define add-to-search-schedule

  (make-parameter add-to-depth-first-search-schedule))

下面两个过程通过动态绑定 add-to-search-schedule，控制一个延迟过程执行时的搜索顺序；这个延迟过程封装了待求解的问题。其使用示例见第 293 页的练习 5.22。The following two procedures can be used to control the search order in the execution of a thunk that encapsulates a problem to be solved, by dynamically binding add-to-search-schedule. For an example of their use, see exercise 5.22 on page 293.

(define (with-depth-first-schedule problem-thunk)

  (call/cc

   (lambda (k)

     (parameterize ((add-to-search-schedule

                     add-to-depth-first-search-schedule)

                    (*search-schedule*

                     (empty-search-schedule))

                    (*top-level* k))

       (problem-thunk)))))



(define (with-breadth-first-schedule problem-thunk)

  (call/cc

   (lambda (k)

     (parameterize ((add-to-search-schedule

                     add-to-breadth-first-search-schedule)

                    (*search-schedule*

                     (empty-search-schedule))

                    (*top-level* k))

       (problem-thunk)))))

这些过程还会通过动态绑定，在局部重新初始化 *search-schedule* 和 *top-level*，提供的是生存期而非作用域上的控制。如果 yield 找不到更多备选项，就可以终止这次搜索，并向 with-...-first-schedule 的调用者返回值 no-more-alternatives。例如：These procedures also locally reinitialize the *search-schedule* and the *top-level* by dynamically binding them, providing control in extent rather than scope. If yield finds no more alternatives it can cause this search to terminate and return the value no-more-alternatives to the caller of with-...-first-schedule. For example:

(define search-order-demo

  (lambda ()

    (let ((x (amb 1 2)))

      (pp (list x))

      (let ((y (amb ’a ’b)))

        (pp (list x y))))

    (amb)))



(with-depth-first-schedule search-order-demo)

(1)

(1 a)

(1 b)

(2)

(2 a)

(2 b)

no-more-alternatives



(with-breadth-first-schedule search-order-demo)

(1)

(2)

(1 a)

(1 b)

(2 a)

(2 b)

no-more-alternatives

这些排序方式利用底层的栈和队列修改操作实现。深度优先时，把备选项放到调度表的前端；广度优先时，则放到末尾。两种情况下，它们在调度表中的排列顺序都与传给 amb 的顺序一致。The orderings are implemented in terms of the low-level stack and queue mutators. For depth first the alternatives are put onto the front of the schedule, and for breadth first they are put onto the end of the schedule. In both cases they appear on the schedule in the order in which they were supplied to amb.

(define (add-to-depth-first-search-schedule alternatives)

  (for-each (lambda (alternative)

              (push! (*search-schedule*) alternative))

            (reverse alternatives)))



(define (add-to-breadth-first-search-schedule alternatives)

  (for-each (lambda (alternative)

              (add-to-end! (*search-schedule*) alternative))

            alternatives))

参数 *top-level* 的初始化方式使得：找不到备选项时，系统会携带给定的 result 继续执行读入—求值—打印循环。（在上面的代码中，yield 把符号 no-more-alternatives 传给顶层。）注意，with-...-first-schedule 会重新绑定 *top-level*。The parameter *top-level* is initialized so that when no alternatives are found, the system continues in the read-eval-print loop with the given result. (In the code above, yield passes the symbol no-more-alternatives to the top level.) Note that with-...-first-schedule rebinds *top-level*.

(define *top-level*

  (make-parameter

    (lambda (result)

      (abort->nearest

       (cmdl-message/active

        (lambda (port)

          (fresh-line port)

          (display "; " port)

          (write result port)))))))

要启动整个系统，还需要：To start everything up we also need:

(define (init-amb)

  (reset-deque! (*search-schedule*))

  (set! *number-of-calls-to-fail* 0)

  'done)

最后，几乎每个使用 amb 的程序都需要 require：And finally, almost every program using amb will need require:

(define (require p)

  (if (not p) (amb) ’ok))

全部内容就这么多！借助 call/cc 能做到的事情真是惊人。因此，要实现 amb，不必再构造一个嵌入式系统（就像我们在That is all there is to it! It is amazing what one can do with call/cc. So we do not need to make an embedded system to implement amb (as we did in 5.4.2 节section 5.4.2中所做的那样），只要原生环境中有 call/cc 就行。), if we have call/cc in our native environment.

尝试备选项的其他方法Other ways to try alternatives

如果一个子问题有多种可能的解法，而其中只有一些适合解决更大的问题，那么，像生成并测试那样按顺序逐一尝试，只是可行方法之一。例如，如果某些选择会使测试过程进行非常漫长（甚至无限）的计算，而另一些选择可能很快成功或失败，那么，把每个选择分配给一个可以并发运行的线程就是合适的做法。这需要一种线程通信方式，也可能需要让成功的线程终止其同级线程。所有这些都可以用续延来安排，并围绕事务来组织线程间通信。If there are multiple possible ways to solve a subproblem, and only some of them are appropriate for solving the larger problem, sequentially trying them as in generate-and-test is only one way to proceed. For example, if some of the choices lead to very long (perhaps infinite) computations in the tester while others may succeed or fail quickly, it is appropriate to allocate each choice to a thread that may run concurrently. This requires a way for threads to communicate and perhaps for a successful thread to kill its siblings. All of this can be arranged with continuations, with the thread-to-thread communications organized around transactions.

练习 5.22：广度与深度Exercise 5.22: Breadth versus depth

回想一下寻找勾股三元组的那个笨办法（第 272 页）。我们在搜索器中加入一个计数器，记录尝试过多少个三元组：Recall the dumb way to find Pythagorean triples (on page 272). We instrument the searcher with a counter of the number of triples tried:

(define (a-pythagorean-triple-between low high)

  (let ((i (an-integer-between low high)))

    (let ((j (an-integer-between i high)))

      (let ((k (an-integer-between j high)))

        (set! triples-tested (+ triples-tested 1))

        (require (= (+ (* i i) (* j j))

                    (* k k)))

        (list i j k)))))



(define triples-tested 0)

考虑下面的实验。首先尝试广度优先搜索：Consider the following experiment. First we try breadth-first search:

(begin (init-amb)       ; to reset failure counter

       (set! triples-tested 0)

       (with-breadth-first-schedule

        (lambda ()

          (pp (a-pythagorean-triple-between 10 20)))))

(12 16 20)

然后尝试深度优先搜索：And then we try depth-first search:

      (pp (a-pythagorean-triple-between 10 20)))))

  1. a. 解释深度优先搜索与广度优先搜索的 triples-tested 为何不同（只需大致解释，不必说明精确计数）。a. Explain the difference in triples-tested between depth-first and breadth-first search (in rough terms, not the exact counts).

Considering that the breadth-first search does more work, why is the following a-pythagorean-triple-from search not usable under the depth-first search strategy, although it works fine under the breadth-first strategy?

    (let ((j (an-integer-from i)))

      (let ((k (an-integer-from j)))

        (require (= (+ (* i i) (* j j)) (* k k)))

        (list i j k)))))

练习 5.23：更不确定的非确定性Exercise 5.23: Less deterministic nondeterminism

Eva Lu Ator 指出，我们的 amb 实现有时还不够非确定。具体来说，给定 amb 形式中的一个备选项列表，我们总是先选最左边的备选项，然后选左起第二个，依次从左到右。Eva Lu Ator points out that our amb implementation is not as nondeterministic as one might sometimes like. Specifically, given a list of alternatives in an amb form, we always choose the leftmost alternative first, then the second leftmost, and so on, in left-to-right order.

她建议，人们可能希望改变这种选择顺序，例如从右到左，甚至随机选择。具体来说，她想要类似下面这样的东西：She suggests that one might wish to override this choice, say, by going from right to left, or even in random order. Specifically, she would like something like:

(with-left-to-right-ordering problem-thunk)

(with-right-to-left-ordering problem-thunk)

(with-random-ordering problem-thunk)

她马上指出，备选项的这种排序选择，与搜索顺序（深度优先、广度优先或其他顺序）相互独立。She's quick to point out that this choice of ordering is independent of the search order (depth-first, breadth-first, or other).

  2. b. 实现这三种选择顺序，并分别给出一个使用示例。为求简单和统一，请仿照 with-depth-first-schedule、add-to-depth-first-search-schedule 等过程的代码编写。提示：可以使用 Scheme 内建的 random 过程。b. Implement these three choice orders and give an example use of each. For simplicity and uniformity, model your code after that for with-depth-first-schedule, add-to-depth-first-search-schedule, etc. Hint: Feel free to use Scheme's built-in random procedure.

练习 5.24：嵌套策略Exercise 5.24: Nesting strategies

我们的本意是让广度优先和深度优先搜索策略能够在搜索中任意嵌套。按当前的实现，深度优先和广度优先调度的嵌套能否正确工作？具体来说，请设计一个实验：如果存在缺陷，就暴露该缺陷；如果确实正确工作，就用实例展示这一点。解释你的理由。We intended that the breadth-first and depth-first search strategies could be arbitrarily nested within searches. Does the nesting of depth-first and breadth-first scheduling work correctly as currently implemented? Specifically, design an experiment that exposes the bug (if there is one) or that demonstrates anecdotally that it does work correctly (if it does). Explain your rationale.

这需要设计能区分深度优先与广度优先搜索策略的实验，再以有趣的方式组合它们，展示对嵌套搜索的局部控制。This involves crafting experiments that distinguish between depth-first and breadth-first search strategies, then composing them in interesting ways to demonstrate local control over nested searches.

找出一类自然的问题，使这种灵活性确实有用，而不是仅仅为了证明某个观点而拼凑出来的问题。Identify a natural class of problems for which this flexibility is useful— not just hacked together to prove a point.

练习 5.25：可撤销赋值Exercise 5.25: Undoable assignment

在前面 amb 的嵌入式解释器版本中，In the embedded interpreter version of amb in 5.4.2 节section 5.4.2我们展示了如何使用两种赋值：由 set! 表示的常规永久赋值，以及由 maybe-set! 表示、会在回溯时撤销的可撤销赋值。在本节的原生代码实现中，我们可以为可撤销的作用实现一个通用包装过程： we showed how to use two kinds of assignment: the usual permanent assignment, indicated by set!, and the undoable assignment, indicated by maybe-set!, which gets undone by backtracking. We can implement a general wrapper for undoable effects in the native-code implementation of this section:

(define (effect-wrapper doer undoer)

  (force-next

   (lambda () (undoer) (yield)))

  (doer))



(define (force-next thunk)

  (push! (*search-schedule*) thunk))

然后，可以将 maybe-set! 实现为一个宏：And we can then implement maybe-set! as a macro:

(define-syntax maybe-set!

  (syntax-rules ()

    ((maybe-set! var val)

     (let ((old-val var))

       (effect-wrapper

        (lambda ()

          (set! var val))

        (lambda ()

          (set! var old-val)))))))

遗憾的是，这只对深度优先搜索有意义，对广度优先搜索却没有意义。解释原因。这可以修复吗？Unfortunately, this makes sense only for depth-first search; it makes no sense for breadth-first search. Explain why. Is this fixable?

练习 5.26：嵌入式系统中的搜索控制Exercise 5.26: Search control in the embedded system

我们如何修改前面那个嵌入式系统How could we change the embedded system of 5.4.2 节section 5.4.2——它通过分析生成带有成功续延和失败续延的组合子——使其既支持深度优先搜索（目前的方式），又支持广度优先搜索？解释你的策略。编写一个新的实现，加入这种控制搜索顺序的能力。注意：这是一次相当大的改造。, with analysis to combinators that have success and failure continuations, to enable both depth-first search (as it is now) and breadth-first search? Explain your strategy. Make a new implementation that incorporates this ability to control the search order. Note: This is a rather large transformation.

5.6 能力与责任5.6 Power and responsibility

在本章中，我们看到，计算的丘奇—图灵通用性赋予了我们强大的能力。我们永远不能抱怨：“我无法用必须使用的语言来表达这个。”如果掌握了解释和编译的技巧，我们总能突破任何语言的束缚，因为总可以为手头的问题构造一种合适的领域专用语言。这里的讲解使用 Scheme 作为底层语言，并在其上构造基于 Lisp 的强大语言。这里采用 Lisp 语法，是因为它极大地简化了这些思想的阐述。（参见关于中缀记法的练习 5.7。如果必须在一种语法复杂的语言中完成这些工作，讲解的篇幅会长上许多倍，也会乏味得多。）不过，任何图灵通用的语言都具备解释所带来的这种能力。In this chapter we have seen that we have great power from the Church-Turing universality of computation. We can never complain: “I cannot express this in the language I must use.” If we know the tricks of interpretation and compilation we can always escape from the confines of any language because it is always possible to build an appropriate domain-specific language for the problem at hand. The exposition here uses Scheme as the underlying language and builds powerful Lisp-based languages on top of Scheme. The reason we use Lisp syntax here is because it greatly simplifies the exposition of these ideas. (See exercise 5.7 on infix notations. If we had to do this in a language with a complicated syntax the exposition would be many times longer and more tedious.) But the power of interpretation is available in any Turing-universal language.

为了保留未来的灵活性，我们构造的语言必须简单而通用。它们应当只有极少的机制：原语、组合手段和抽象手段。我们希望能够按需扩展它们，并能将程序的各个部分混合搭配。最重要的是，当我们拥有多种语言、每种语言分别适合问题的某个部分时，必须有良好的方式让这些语言互操作。It is important for future flexibility that the languages we build be simple and general. They must have very few mechanisms: primitives, means of combination, and means of abstraction. We want to be able to extend them as needed and to be able to mix and match the parts of programs. And, most important, when we have multiple languages, each of which is appropriate for some part of a problem, there must be good ways for those languages to interoperate.

能力越大，责任越大。每次创建一种语言，都必须为它编写文档，以便传授给别人。今天编写的程序，将来会由其他人阅读和修改。（事实上，即使明年再读去年写的代码，我们也已大不相同，不会记得当时所做事情的细节。）因此，必须十分克制地使用这种能力，并在使用时极其仔细地记录结果。否则，我们就会给下一位程序员（或者自己！）留下一团无法理解的乱麻，等着他们清理和重写。不要参与建造“巴别塔”。With great power comes even greater responsibility. Every time we create a language we must also document it so that it can be taught to others. The programs we write today will be read and modified by others in the future. (Indeed, even when we read next year what we wrote last year, we will be very different and we will not remember the details of what we did.) So it is important that we use this power very sparingly, and that when we do so we document the result very carefully. Otherwise we will be leaving an incomprehensible mess for the next programmer (or for ourselves!) to clean up and rewrite. Don't participate in the creation of a “Tower of Babel.”

源自 UNIX 的系统展现了这个问题的好坏两面。每条命令都有自己的语言。如果你了解 awk、sed 和 grep，就知道它们各有自己的语言，其中包括我们在 2.2 节讨论过的那种非常丑陋、定义糟糕的正则表达式语言。当然，这些语言各自都让眼前的问题更容易解决。但它们没有一种一致的底层思想，能让人容易学习和理解。只要想一想 shell 的引用约定如何与 grep 的引用约定相互作用，你就能体会这一点。要成为 UNIX 高手，就必须学会许多恼人的特殊情况。另一方面，UNIX 本身有一种极其简单而优雅的方式将各种东西连接起来：流。每个基本的 UNIX 工具都从流中获取输入，并输出流。将输出流通过管道接到输入流，就能把它们连接起来。这一经验非常值得深思。The systems that derive from UNIX show both the good and the bad sides of this issue. The commands all have their own languages. If you know about awk and sed and grep you know that each has its own language, including the really ugly and badly defined regular-expression language we discussed in section 2.2. Certainly each of those languages helped make the immediate problems easier to solve. But they do not have a consistent underlying idea that makes them easy to learn and understand. Just think about how the quotation conventions of the shell interact with the quotation conventions of grep and you will appreciate this point. To become a UNIX guru you have to learn lots of nasty special-case stuff. On the other hand, UNIX itself has a wonderfully simple and elegant way to glue stuff together: streams. Each of the basic UNIX utilities takes input from streams and puts out streams. They can be connected by piping output streams to input streams. This lesson is very worth contemplating.

11 在 Scheme 中，接收显式声明的参数之后所有实参的参数，称为剩余参数。如果有显式声明的参数，可以用不正规列表（一串序对，其中最后一个 cdr 不是空列表）作为参数列表。例如，(lambda (a b . c) ...) 是一个至少接受两个实参的过程，这两个实参分别绑定到 a 和 b；另外提供的任何实参（前两个之后的实参）都组成一个列表，作为 c 的值。如果没有显式声明的参数，只有一个剩余参数，就用单个符号作为该剩余参数的名称。例如，在 Scheme 中，可以写 (lambda xs ...) 来定义一个接受任意数量实参的过程，并把参数 xs 绑定为这些实参组成的列表。11 In Scheme, a parameter that takes all the arguments after the explicitly declared ones is called a rest parameter. If there are explicitly declared parameters we can use an improper list (a chain of pairs in which the last cdr is not the empty list) as our parameter list. For example (lambda (a b . c) ...) is a procedure that takes at least two arguments, which will be bound to a and b; any additional arguments supplied (after the first two) are made into a list that is the value of c. If there are no explicitly declared parameters and just a rest parameter we use a single symbol to be the name of the rest parameter. For example, in Scheme we can write (lambda xs ...) to define a procedure that takes any number of arguments and binds the parameter xs to be the list of arguments.

6 分层6 

Layering

在 1.1 节中，我们曾提到，编程可以向建筑实践学习。程序员可以先从一个可执行的骨架方案（parti）着手，以便试验一个想法。当这个骨架方案看起来不错时，再用更多信息加以充实。In section 1.1 we alluded to the idea that programming could learn from the practice of architecture. A programmer might start with an executable skeleton plan (a parti ) to help try out an idea. When the parti looks good the programmer could elaborate it with more information.

例如，声明实现所用的类型，可以支持编译生成高效代码，并抑制类型错误的发生。可以添加量纲和单位声明，以避免某些缺陷，并为文档提供支持。谓词断言可以帮助定位运行时发生的错误，也可以支持自动或手动构造“正确性”证明。声明某些数值量和运算所需的精度，可以让数值分析问题更加清晰。提出备选实现方案，可以在实现中引入有用的简并。通过携带依赖关系，可以追踪结果的来源。For example, declared implementation types may enable the compilation of efficient code and inhibit the occurrence of type errors. Declared dimensions and units may be added to prevent some bugs and support documentation. Assertions of predicates can help with the localization of errors that occur at run time and they could support the automatic or manual construction of proofs of “correctness.” Declarations of how much precision is needed for some numerical quantities and operations can give clarity to numerical analysis problems. Suggestions of alternative implementations can enable useful degeneracy in an implementation. We can track the provenance of a result by carrying dependencies.

然而，把这些重要而强大的功能添加到程序文本中的通常做法，会使程序文本变成一团纠缠不清的乱麻。继续借用建筑的类比，这种做法没有把被服务空间与服务空间分开。如何将程序的“本质”特征（定义其行为的代码）与“附带”特征（例如供编译器使用的类型信息或日志记录代码）分离，一直是一个重要问题。面向方面编程 [67] 试图通过显式识别日志记录等“横切关注点”，解决这个问题的一部分。分层则是实现这种分离的另一种方法。能够用其他数据或代码为任何数据或代码片段加上注解，是构造灵活系统的一项关键机制。对值的这种修饰，是对支持可扩展泛型运算所用标记机制的推广。这里，我们引入分层编程的思想。数据及处理数据的过程都将由多个层组成，允许以添加的方式附加注解，而不使结构杂乱。But the usual way of adding these important and powerful features to the text of a program turns the program text into a tangled mess. To continue with the architecture analogy, it does not separate the served spaces from the servant spaces. The separation of the “essential” features of a program (the code that defines its behavior) from the “accidental” ones (e.g., type information for a compiler or code for logging) has been an important issue. Aspect-oriented programming [67] was an attempt to address part of this problem, by explicitly identifying “cross-cutting concerns” such as logging. Layering is another way to effect the separation. The ability to annotate any piece of data or code with other data or code is a crucial mechanism in building flexible systems. The decoration of a value is a generalization of the tagging used to support extensible generic operations. Here we introduce the idea of layered programming. Both the data and the procedures that process it will be made up of multiple layers that enable additive annotation without introducing clutter.

6.1 使用层6.1 Using layers

层让我们能够先勾勒计算的轮廓，再用元数据加以充实，并在计算过程中一并处理这些元数据。让我们考虑一些在许多场合可能有价值的注解。例如，假定我们想使用牛顿万有引力定律：Layers give us the ability to sketch out a computation and then elaborate that computation with metadata that is processed along with the computation. Let's consider some annotations that we think may be valuable in many situations. For example, suppose we are interested in using Newton's force law for gravity:

(define (F m1 m2 r)

  (/ (* G m1 m2) (square r)))

这是一项简单的数值计算，但我们可以扩充它，使其携带支持信息和单位。This is a simple numerical calculation, but we can elaborate it to carry support information and units.

我们查阅 NIST 近期公布的测量结果，找到牛顿引力常量 G：We find Newton's constant G by looking up a recent measurement published by NIST:

(define G

  (layered-datum 6.67408e-11

    unit-layer (unit 'meter 3 ’kilogram -1 'second -2)

    support-layer (support-set ’CODATA-2018)))

这里展示了测量的数值、测量的单位（m3/(kg s2)），以及数据的来源（即它的支持信息）。我们还可以扩展它，在另一个层中以范围的形式携带测量的不确定性，不过这里不这样做。Here we show the numerical value of the measurement, the units of that measurement (m3/(kg s2)), and the source of the data (its support). We could extend this to also carry the uncertainty in the measurement as a range in another layer, but we won't do that here.

我们还可以从其他来源查到地球的质量、月球的质量，以及到月球的距离（半长轴）：We can also find the mass of the Earth, the mass of the Moon, and the distance to the Moon (semimajor axis) from other sources:

(define M-Earth

  (layered-datum 5.9722e24

                 unit-layer (unit ’kilogram 1)

                 support-layer

                 (support-set ’Astronomical-Almanac-2016)))



(define M-Moon

  (layered-datum 7.342e22

                 unit-layer (unit ’kilogram 1)

                 support-layer

                 (support-set ’NASA-2006)))



(define a-Moon

  (layered-datum 384399e3

                 unit-layer (unit 'meter 1)

                 support-layer

                 (support-set ’Wieczorek-2006)))

现在可以提出问题：“在这一距离下，地球与月球之间的引力有多大？”我们将得到答案：Now we can ask the question, “What is the gravitational force of attraction between the Earth and the Moon at that distance?” and we will get the answer:

(pp (F M-earth M-Moon a-moon))

#[layered-datum 1.9805035857209e20]

(base-layer 1.9805035857209e20)

(unit-layer (unit kilogram 1 meter 1 second -2))

(support-layer

 (support-set Wieczorek-2006

              NASA-2006

              Astronomical-Almanac-2016

              CODATA-2018))

结果给出了数值、该结果的单位，以及它所依赖的数据来源。The result gives the numerical value, the units of that result, and the sources that the result depended upon.

6.2 分层的实现6.2 Implemention of layering

分层包含两个部分。首先，必须能够创建包含多层信息的数据。在我们的例子中，使用 layered-datum 来完成这件事。其次，必须能够增强一个过程，使它能够（在一定程度上）独立处理每一层。以这种方式增强的过程称为分层过程。There are two parts to layering. The first is that it must be possible to create a datum that contains multiple layers of information. In our example, we used layered-datum to do this. The second part is that we need to be able to enhance a procedure so that it can process each layer (somewhat) independently. A procedure enhanced in this way is called a layered procedure.

我们还需要一种给层命名的方法。每一层都必须有名称，才能指定数据中的某一层。分层过程也使用这个名称，将该层的处理与输入数据中相应的层连接起来。在示例中，我们使用变量来指代层名，例如 unit-layer，它绑定到单位层的名称。这使用户接口不依赖于层名指定方式的细节；我们会看到，这很有用。We also need a way to assign names to layers. Every layer must have a name, so that the layer in a datum can be specified. The name is also used by a layered procedure to connect the processing for that layer to the corresponding layers in the incoming data. We have written our example to use variables to refer to layer names, as in unit-layer, which is bound to the name for the unit layer. This makes the user interface independent of the details of how a layer name is specified; this will turn out to be useful.

层命名的另一个方面是，必须有一个特殊的基层，表示所执行的底层计算。在使用 layered-datum 的示例中，基层的值通过两个特点加以区分：它是第一个实参，而且没有关联的名称。Another aspect of layer naming is that there must be a distinguished base layer, which represents the underlying computation being performed. In our example using layered-datum, the base layer's value is distinguished by being the first argument and by not having an associated name.

分层数据可以用简单的数据结构来构造。任何方便的数据结构都可以，只要它能将层名与值关联起来，并允许存在多组这样的关联。可以使用一个特殊名称来标识基层，使数据结构简单而统一。Layered data can be built from simple data structures. We can use any convenient data structure that can associate a layer name with a value and that permits many such associations. A special name can be used to identify the base layer, making the data structure simple and uniform.

构造分层过程则更复杂，因为大多数层的处理都需要基层计算中的某些信息。例如，假定要将两个携带支持信息的数相乘。通常，结果的支持信息是两个实参支持信息的并集。但假定其中一个实参的基层值为零，那么，结果的支持信息就只是这个零的支持信息，而另一个实参的支持信息无关紧要。Building layered procedures is more complicated, because the processing for most layers will need some information from the computation in the base layer. For example, suppose we are multiplying two numbers that carry support information. Normally, the support of the result is the union of the supports of the arguments. But suppose one argument has a base-layer value of zero; then the support of the result is the support of the zero, and the support of the other argument is irrelevant.

基层不能依赖任何非基层，因为那会违背基层的理念：基层是一项独立的计算，其他层只是对它加以增强。而且，一个非基层也不应该依赖另一个非基层。一般来说，非基层之间不应共享信息，因为否则，它的行为就会因另一个层存在与否而有所不同。这与我们构造添加式程序的总体方法不一致。The base layer must not depend on any non-base layer because that violates the idea of the base layer: that it is an independent computation that the other layers enhance. And a non-base layer should not depend on another non-base layer. A non-base layer generally shouldn't share information with another non-base layer since its behavior would be different depending on the presence or absence of the other layer. This would be inconsistent with our general approach of building additive programs.

因此，构造分层过程需要取得平衡：既要把基层的信息共享给非基层，又要在其他大多数情况下隔离各层。在接下来几节探索分层实现的细节时，我们将处理这一问题。So building a layered procedure involves a balance between sharing information from the base layer to the non-base layers and isolating layers in most other cases. We will address this in the next sections as we explore the details of implementing layering.

6.2.1 分层数据6.2.1 Layered data

一个分层数据项，是一个附有额外信息注解的基础值，这些信息描述该值。注解就是层名与层值之间的关联。例如，数字 2 可以是许多数据项的基础值：如果我们经营土豆生意，一袋 2 磅重的土豆上可能贴着 2 美元的价签。这些数字 2 的每个实例都必须是不同的数据项，其单位层的值也不同（美元或磅）。还可以有其他层：2 美元的价格上可以附有信息，说明该价格如何根据支付给农民的价格，以及运输和加工成本推导而来。A layered data item is a base value annotated with extra information about that value. The annotation is an association of layer names with their values. For example, the number 2 may be the base value in many data items: if we are dealing in potatoes there may be a 2-dollar price tag on a 2-pound bag of potatoes. Each of these instances of the number 2 must be a distinct data item, with different values (dollars or pounds) for the units layer. There may be other layers as well: the 2-dollar price may have information saying how it was derived from the price paid to the farmer and the cost of transportation and processing.

为解决这个问题，我们引入分层数据。一个分层数据表示为一个 bundle，其中包含各层与其值的关联。因此，2 磅土豆这一数量和土豆 2 美元这一价格，是两个独立的分层数据项：To address this issue we introduce the layered datum. A layered datum is represented as a bundle that contains an association of layers and their values. So a 2-pound quantity of potatoes and a 2-dollar price for potatoes will be separate layered data items:

(define (make-layered-datum base-value alist)

  (if (null? alist)

      base-value

      (let ((alist

             (cons (cons base-layer base-value)

                   alist)))

        (define (has-layer? layer)

          (and (assv layer alist) #t))

        (define (get-layer-value layer)

          (cdr (assv layer alist)))

        (define (annotation-layers)

          (map car (cdr alist)))

        (bundle layered-datum?

                has-layer? get-layer-value

                annotation-layers))))

层与其值之间的关联表示为关联列表，简称 alist，即键值对的列表。The associations between layers and their values are represented as an association list, or alist—a list of key–value pairs.

为方便起见，我们提供 layered-datum，它以属性列表形式接受各层的实参（层和值交替出现，如第 300 页的示例所示），然后用相应的 alist 调用 make-layered-datum。For convenience, we provide layered-datum, which takes its layer arguments in property-list form (alternating layer and value, as in the examples on page 300) and calls make-layered-datum with the corresponding alist.

(define (layered-datum base-value . plist)

  (make-layered-datum base-value (plist->alist plist)))

这种设计提供了极大的灵活性。可以存在许多不同种类的分层数据，而且对每一种数据，都不必预先确定任何特定的层或层数。唯一的共同特征是，每个分层数据都有一个特殊的层，即 base-layer；其中包含一个对象，其他所有层的值都是对这个对象的注解。This design provides great flexibility. There may be many different kinds of layered data, and for each there is no a priori commitment to any particular layer or number of layers. The only common feature is that each layered datum has a distinguished layer, the base-layer, which contains the object that all the other layer values are annotations on.

每个层都由一个 bundle 表示，其中封装着该层的具体细节。最简单的是基层：Each layer is represented by a bundle that embodies the specifics of that layer. The simplest is the base layer:

(define base-layer 

  (let ()

    (define (get-name) ’base)

    (define (has-value? object) #t)

    (define (get-value object)

      (if (layered-datum? object)

          (object ’get-layer-value base-layer)

          object))

    (bundle layer? get-name has-value? get-value)))

这里展示了层的主要操作：get-value 操作。若层值存在，它就取得该值；否则返回默认值。对于基层，默认值就是对象本身。This shows the primary operation of a layer: the get-value operation that fetches the layer value, if present, or returns a default. In the case of the base layer, the default is the object itself.

注解层稍微复杂一些。除了上述内容，它们还管理一组有名称的过程；我们将在讨论分层过程时探索它们。过程 make-annotation-layer 提供了所有注解层共用的基础设施；它调用自己的 constructor 实参，提供各层专有的部分。The annotation layers have a little more complexity. In addition to the above, they also manage a set of named procedures that will be explored when we look at layered procedures. The make-annotation-layer procedure provides the common infrastructure used by all annotation layers; it calls its constructor argument to supply the layer-specific parts.

(define (make-annotation-layer name constructor)

  (define (get-name) name)

  (define (has-value? object)

    (and (layered-datum? object)

         (object ’has-layer? layer)))

  (define (get-value object)

    (if (has-value? object)

        (object ’get-layer-value layer)

        (layer ’get-default-value)))

  (define layer

    (constructor get-name has-value? get-value))

 layer)

我们使用 make-annotation-layer 构造单位层：We use make-annotation-layer to construct the units layer:

(define unit-layer

  (make-annotation-layer ’unit

    (lambda (get-name has-value? get-value)

      (define (get-default-value)

        unit:none)

      (define (get-procedure name arity)

        See definition on page 308.)

      (bundle layer?

              get-name has-value? get-value

              get-default-value get-procedure))))

这个实现展示了层结构的其余部分：一个默认值提供过程，以及过程 get-procedure；后者实现该层对分层过程的支持，我们将在下一节（第 308 页）考察它。This implementation shows the rest of the layer structure: a provider for the default value, and the procedure get-procedure that implements this layer's support for layered procedures, which we will examine in the next section (page 308).

为了方便一种常见用法，layer-accessor 会创建一个访问过程，其作用等价于调用某层的 get-value 委托过程：As a convenience for a common use case, layer-accessor creates an accessor procedure that is equivalent to calling a layer's get-value delegate:

(define (layer-accessor layer)

  (lambda (object)

    (layer ’get-value object)))



(define base-layer-value

  (layer-accessor base-layer))

6.2.2 分层过程6.2.2 Layered procedures

过程也是可以分层的数据。分层过程类似于泛型过程，泛型过程为不同的实参类型配有处理过程。不同的是，分层过程为输入数据中的各个层分别提供实现，并处理所有这些层，生成一个分层的结果。1 例如，将数值层与单位层组合时，过程可以利用自己的数值层处理实参中的数值部分，同时利用自己的单位层处理实参中的单位部分。Procedures are also data that can be layered. A layered procedure is similar to a generic procedure, in which there are handlers for different argument types. A layered procedure instead provides implementations for separate layers in the incoming data, and processes all of them to produce a layered result.1 For example, when combining a numeric layer with a units layer, the procedure can process the numeric parts of the arguments using its numeric layer, and also process the units parts of the arguments using its units layer.

在以下一节展示的数值示例中：In the numerical example shown in 6.1 节section 6.1，计算牛顿引力的代码 F 代表了 parti，即所要进行的计算的基本方案。它对数进行运算；单位则是数的注解。实现乘法等算术运算符的分层泛型过程，有一个对基层中的数进行运算的基础组成部分，此外还有其他组成部分，分别对应可能为数值基层提供注解的各个层。单位层是一个注解层，提供有关数据和计算的更多信息，但并非计算所必需的。, the code F for Newton's force represents the parti, the essential plan for the computation to be performed. It operates on numbers; the units annotate the numbers. The layered generic procedures that implement the arithmetic operators, such as multiplication, have a base component that operates on the numbers in the base layer and they have other components, one for each layer that might annotate the numerical base layer. The units layer is an annotation layer that gives more information about the data and the computation, but is not essential to the computation.

在分层系统中，基层必须能够不借助其他层而进行计算。不过，注解层可能需要访问基层中的值。如果某个实参缺少某个注解层，过程的相应注解层可以使用默认值，或者干脆不运行。无论如何，基层始终都会运行。In a layered system the base layer must be able to compute without reference to the other layers. But the annotation layers may need access to the values that are in the base layer. If an annotation layer of an argument is missing, the procedure's annotation layer may use a default value or simply not run. In any case, the base layer always runs.

要构造一个分层过程，我们需要为该过程提供唯一的 name 和 arity，以及用于实现基础计算的 base-procedure：To construct a layered procedure, we need a unique name and arity for the procedure, and a base-procedure to implement the base computation:

(define (make-layered-procedure name arity base-procedure)

  (let* ((metadata

          (make-layered-metadata name arity base-procedure))

         (procedure

          (layered-procedure-dispatcher metadata)))

    (set-layered-procedure-metadata! procedure metadata)

    procedure))

分层过程的有关信息保存在该过程的元数据中。元数据还负责管理基础层和各注释层的处理过程。Information about the layered procedure is kept in metadata for that procedure. The metadata also manages the handlers for the base layer and the annotation layers.

分层过程的元数据实现为一个束。创建它时，需要提供分层过程的 name、它的 arity，以及 base-procedure（基础层的处理过程）。元数据提供了访问这几项的方式，还提供 set-handler!，用于为某个注释层指定处理过程，以及 get-handler，用于取得某个注释层的处理过程。The metadata for a layered procedure is implemented as a bundle. It is created with the name of the layered procedure, its arity, and the base-procedure (the handler for the base layer). The metadata provides access to each of these. It also provides set-handler! for assigning a handler for an annotation layer and get-handler for retrieving the handler for an annotation layer.

每个注释层，例如 unit-layer，都提供 get-procedure；给定过程名称和元数，它就返回该层中适用于这一过程名称和元数的处理过程。分层元数据提供的 get-handler 首先检查自己是否具有该层的处理过程。如果有，就返回它；否则就返回该层的 get-procedure 的结果。Each annotation layer, for example the unit-layer, provides get-procedure that when given a procedure name and arity returns the appropriate handler for that procedure name and arity for that layer. The get-handler provided by the layered metadata first checks if it has a handler for that layer. If so it returns that handler; otherwise it returns the result of the layer's get-procedure.

(define (make-layered-metadata name arity base-procedure)

  (let ((handlers (make-weak-alist-store eqv?)))

    (define (get-name) name) (define (get-arity) arity)

    (define (get-base-procedure) base-procedure)

    (define has? (handlers ’has?))

    (define get (handlers ’get))

    (define set-handler! (handlers ’put!))

    (define (get-handler layer)

      (if (has? layer)

          (get layer)

          (layer ’get-procedure name arity)))

    (bundle layered-metadata?

            get-name get-arity get-base-procedure

            get-handler set-handler!)))

应用分层过程的实际工作由 layered-procedure-dispatcher 完成。分派器必须能够访问并应用与该分层过程关联的基础过程和各注释层过程。所有这些信息都由元数据提供。The actual work of applying a layered procedure is done by layered-procedure-dispatcher. The dispatcher must be able to access and apply the base procedure and the annotation layer procedures that are associated with the layered procedure. All of this information is provided by the metadata.

(define (layered-procedure-dispatcher metadata)

  (let ((base-procedure (metadata ’get-base-procedure)))

    (define (the-layered-procedure . args)

      (let ((base-value

             (apply base-procedure

                    (map base-layer-value args)))

            (annotation-layers

             (apply lset-union eqv?

                    (map (lambda (arg)

                           (if (layered-datum? arg)

                               (arg ’annotation-layers)

                               ’()))

                         args))))

        (make-layered-datum base-value

          (filter-map        ; drops #f values

           (lambda (layer)

             (let ((handler (metadata ’get-handler layer)))

               (and handler

                    (cons layer

                          (apply handler base-value args)))))

           annotation-layers))))

    the-layered-procedure))

调用分层过程时，它首先以各实参的基础层值为参数调用 base-procedure，得到基础值。它还会检查每个实参，确定哪些注释层适用；如果没有任何注释层具有处理过程，那么结果就只是基础层值，因为第 303 页的 make-layered-datum 会返回不带注释的基础值。否则，就调用每个适用层的处理过程，生成该层的值。各层专用的处理过程可以访问计算出的 base-value 和分层过程的各实参；它不需要本层和基础层以外的任何层的值。一般来说，结果是一个分层数据项，其中包含基础值和各个适用的注释层处理过程所产生的值。When called, a layered procedure first calls base-procedure on the base-layer values of the arguments to get the base value. It also determines which annotation layers are applicable by examining each of the arguments; if there are no annotation layers that have handlers, then the result is just the base-layer value, because make-layered-datum (on page 303), will return the unannotated base value. Otherwise, each applicable layer's handler is called to produce a value for that layer. The layer-specific handler is given access to the computed base-value and the arguments to the layered procedure; it does not need any layer values other than its own and those of the base layer. Generally, the result is a layered datum containing the base value and the values of the applicable annotation layer handlers.

为了看看这在实际中如何工作，我们来考察单位层的实现（第 304 页）。如果分层过程的名称是算术运算符，单位层的 get-procedure 处理过程（见下文）就按名称查找该层专用的过程，然后用各实参的单位调用它。（expt 是个特例，它的第二个实参不带单位修饰——它是一个数。）对于其他过程，单位的处理方式未定义，因此 get-procedure 返回 #f 来表明这一点。To see how this works in practice, let's look at the implementation for the units layer (on page 304). The get-procedure handler of the units layer (below) looks up the layer-specific procedure by name if the layered procedure's name is an arithmetic operator, and then calls the layer-specific procedure with the units from each argument. (There is a special exception for expt, whose second argument is not decorated with units—it is a number.) For other procedures, the units handling is undefined, so get-procedure returns #f to indicate that.

(define (get-procedure name arity)

  (if (operator? name)

      (let ((procedure (unit-procedure name)))

        (case name

          ((expt)

           (lambda (base-value base power)

             (procedure (get-value base)

                        (base-layer-value power))))

          (else

           (lambda (base-value . args)

             (apply procedure (map get-value args))))))

      #f))

注意，由于 get-procedure 是 unit-layer 的内部过程，它能够访问单位层从第 304 页的 make-annotation-layer 继承的 get-value。我们在讨论单位实现时会看到 unit-procedure，具体见Notice that because get-procedure is an internal procedure of unit-layer, it has access to the units layer get-value inherited from make-annotation-layer (on page 304). We will see unit-procedure when we talk about the units implementation in 第 6.3.1 节section 6.3.1.

来看一个例子。考虑一个简单的过程 square，它计算实参的平方。Let's look at an example. Consider the simple procedure square that squares its argument.

(define (square x) (* x x))

我们为平方过程创建一个分层版本，把数值版本交给基础层。We make a layered version of our square procedure, giving the numerical version to the base layer.

(define layered-square

  (make-layered-procedure 'square 1 square))

这个分层平方过程的行为与基础版本相同：This layered squaring procedure behaves the same as the base version:

(layered-square 4)

16



(layered-square 'm)

(* m m)

不过，如果我们提供带有单位层的实参，那么基础层和单位层就会分别处理，再在输出中组合起来：However, if we provide an argument with a units layer, both the base layer and units layer will be processed separately and combined in the output:

(pp (layered-square

     (layered-datum ’m

                    unit-layer (unit ’kilogram 1))))

#[layered-datum (* m m)]

(base-layer (* m m))

(unit-layer (unit kilogram 2))

6.3 分层算术6.3 Layered arithmetic

既然已经知道如何创建分层过程，我们就可以为算术系统添加层。所需做的只是构建一个算术系统，其中基础算术系统提供的每个运算都对应一个分层过程。我们从一个好用的算术系统开始Now that we know how to make layered procedures, we can add layers to an arithmetic. All that is required is to build an arithmetic with a layered procedure for each operation supplied in the base arithmetic. We start with a pleasant arithmetic

(define (generic-symbolic)

  (let ((g (make-generic-arithmetic

             make-simple-dispatch-store)))

    (add-to-generic-arithmetic! g numeric-arithmetic)

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g function-extender)

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g symbolic-extender)

    g))

并构建一个扩展器，在这个基础之上处理各层：and build an extender to handle the layers on that substrate:

(define generic-with-layers

  (let ((g (generic-symbolic)))

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g layered-extender)

    g))

分层扩展器需要做一些工作。它会创建一个作用于分层数据的分层扩展算术系统。这个分层扩展算术系统的定义域谓词是 layered-datum?。分层运算的基础谓词就是底层算术系统的定义域谓词，但额外要求它必须拒绝分层数据项。2 常量就是基础常量；对于每个算术运算符，其运算都是一个分层过程，只要有任意一个实参是分层的就适用，而它的基础过程继承自底层算术系统。The layered extender has to do a bit of work. It makes a layered extension arithmetic that operates on layered data. The domain predicate of the layered extension arithmetic is layered-datum?. The base predicate for the layered operations is just the domain predicate of the underlying arithmetic, with the extra provision that it must reject layered data items.2 The constants are the base constants, and for each arithmetic operator the operation is a layered procedure applicable if any argument is layered, with the base procedure inherited from the underlying arithmetic.

(define (layered-extender base-arith)

  (let ((base-pred

         (conjoin (arithmetic-domain-predicate base-arith)

                  (complement layered-datum?))))

    (make-arithmetic (list ’layered

                           (arithmetic-name base-arith))

                     layered-datum?

                     (list base-arith)

      (lambda (name base-value)

        base-value)

      (lambda (operator base-operation)

        (make-operation operator

          (any-arg (operator-arity operator)

                   layered-datum?

                   base-pred)

          (make-layered-procedure operator

            (operator-arity operator)

            (operation-procedure base-operation)))))))

这里几乎都是例行代码，包括保持常量对象不变，以及要求运算至少有一个实参是分层的。唯一有意思的是最后三行，它们把基础算术系统的运算过程包装成一个分层过程。运算符被用作分层过程的名称，这样，每个层都可以在该运算需要时提供特殊处理。Nearly all of this is boilerplate, including leaving the constant objects alone and requiring that at least one argument to an operation be layered. The only interesting part is the final three lines, in which the base arithmetic's operation procedure is wrapped in a layered procedure. The operator is used as the name of the layered procedure, so that each layer can provide special handling should that operation need it.

6.3.1 单位算术6.3.1 Unit arithmetic

要在算术系统上实现单位注释层，我们需要一套单位算术。单位规格包含具名的基本单位，以及每个基本单位的指数。3 在单位算术中，单位规格的乘积是一个新的单位规格，其中每个基本单位的指数，等于各实参中相应基本单位的指数之和。We need an arithmetic of units for the units annotation layer on an arithmetic. A unit specification has named base units, and an exponent for each base unit.3 In the units arithmetic, the product of unit specifications is a new unit specification where the exponent of each base unit is the sum of the exponents of the corresponding base units in the arguments.

(unit:* (unit ’kilogram 1 ’meter 1 ’second -1)

        (unit ’second -1))

(unit kilogram 1 meter 1 second -2)

这里我们假定基本单位仅用符号命名，例如 kilogram。Here we assume that the base units are just named by symbols, such as kilogram.

单位规格的表示Representation of unit specifications

为了便于创建单位规格，我们对外将其表示为一个由基本单位名称和指数组成的属性表（键和值交替出现）。To make it easy to create a unit specification, we represent it externally as a property list (with alternating keys and values) of base unit names and exponents.

但在内部，用带标记的关联表表示单位规格更方便；因此，我们必须使用 plist->alist，把原始的属性表转换为关联表表示。我们让这些关联表按基本单位名称排序。转换过程中会进行一些错误检查。unit 的实参列表必须具有属性表的形式。每个基本单位名称所关联的指数必须是精确有理数（通常是整数）。同一个具名基本单位重复出现是错误的。如果基本单位名称不是符号，按基本单位名称排序时就会报告错误。But internally, it is convenient to represent a unit specification as a tagged alist; so we must convert a raw property list to the alist representation, using plist->alist. We keep the alists sorted by the base unit name. In this conversion we do some error checking. The argument list to unit must be in the form of a property list. The exponent associated with each base unit name must be an exact rational number (usually an integer). It is an error if a named base unit is duplicated. The sort by base unit names will signal an error if the base unit name is not a symbol.

(define (unit . plist)

  (guarantee plist? plist ’unit)

  (let ((alist

         (sort (plist->alist plist)

               (lambda (p1 p2)

                 (symbol<? (car p1) (car p2))))))

    (if (sorted-alist-repeated-key? alist)

        (error "Base unit repeated" plist))

    (for-each (lambda (p)

               (guarantee exact-rational? (cdr p)))

              alist)

    (alist->unit alist)))



(define (sorted-alist-repeated-key? alist)

  (and (pair? alist)

       (pair? (cdr alist))

       (or (eq? (caar alist) (caadr alist))

           (sorted-alist-repeated-key? (cdr alist)))))

过程 alist->unit 只是给关联表附加一个唯一标记；unit->alist 则从单位规格中提取关联表：The procedure alist->unit just attaches a unique tag to an alist; and unit->alist extracts the alist from a unit specification:

(define (alist->unit alist)

  (cons %unit-tag alist))



(define (unit->alist unit)

  (guarantee unit? unit ’unit->alist)

  (cdr unit))

这里，%unit-tag 的值只是一个唯一的符号，我们将它放在单位规格关联表的表头。为使单位规格的打印输出看起来像我们传给 unit 以创建单位规格的属性表，我们安排 Scheme 打印器以属性表形式打印单位规格。这一神奇的安排（此处未展示）由列表开头的 unit-tag 符号触发。Here, the value of %unit-tag is just a unique symbol that we use to head a unit specification alist. To make the printed output of unit specifications look like the property lists that we give to unit to make a unit specification, we arrange that the Scheme printer prints unit specifications in property list form. This magic arrangement (not shown here) is triggered by the unit-tag symbol at the head of the list.

当实参是合法的单位规格时，谓词 unit? 为真：The predicate unit? is true if its argument is a legitimate unit specification:

(define (unit? object)

  (and (pair? object)

       (eq? (car object) %unit-tag)

       (list? (cdr object))

       (every (lambda (elt)

                (and (pair? elt)

                     (symbol? (car elt))

                     (exact-rational? (cdr elt))))

              (cdr object))))

单位算术运算Unit arithmetic operations

我们将单位算术构造为运算符名称与实现所需行为的运算之间的映射。像 π 这样的纯数没有单位。一个有单位的量乘以一个无单位的数时，结果的单位就是这个有单位量的单位。因此，单位算术需要一个用于无单位数的乘法单位元——这就是 unit:none。过程 simple-operation 将运算符、适用性测试和实现该运算的过程组合起来：We construct the unit arithmetic as a mapping between the operator name and the operation that implements the required behavior. Pure numbers, like π, are unitless. When a quantity with units is multiplied by a unitless number, the result is the units of the quantity with units. So the unit arithmetic needs a multiplicative identity for unitless numbers—this is unit:none. The procedure simple-operation combines the operator, the test for applicability, and the procedure that implements the operation:

(define (unit-arithmetic)

  (make-arithmetic ’unit unit? ’()

    (lambda (name)

      (if (eq? name 'multiplicative-identity)

          unit:none

          (default-object)))

    (lambda (operator)

      (simple-operation operator

                        unit?

                        (unit-procedure operator)))))

我们调用 unit-procedure，取得每个运算符所对应的过程：We call unit-procedure to get the appropriate procedure for each operator:

(define (unit-procedure operator)

  (case operator

    ((*) unit:*)

    ((/) unit:/)

    ((remainder) unit:remainder)

    ((expt) unit:expt)

    ((invert) unit:invert)

    ((square) unit:square)

    ((sqrt) unit:sqrt)

    ((atan) unit:atan)

    ((abs ceiling floor negate round truncate)

     unit:simple-unary-operation)

    ((+ - max min)

     unit:simple-binary-operation)

    ((acos asin cos exp log sin tan)

     unit:unitless-operation)

    ((angle imag-part magnitude make-polar make-rectangular

            real-part)

     ;; first approximation:

     unit:unitless-operation)

    (else

     (if (eq? ’boolean (operator-codomain operator))

         (if (n:= 1 (operator-arity operator))

             unit:unary-comparison

             unit:binary-comparison)

         unit:unitless-operation))))

对于上述每一种情况，我们都必须提供相应的运算。例如，要将两个单位量相乘，就必须把对应的指数相加，并省去所有指数为零的基本单位：For each case above we must provide the appropriate operation. For example, to multiply two unit quantities we must add corresponding exponents and elide any base unit that has zero exponent:

(define (unit:* u1 u2)

  (alist->unit

   (let loop ((u1 (unit->alist u1)) (u2 (unit->alist u2)))

     (if (and (pair? u1) (pair? u2))

         (let ((factor1 (car u1)) (factor2 (car u2)))

           (if (eq? (car factor1) (car factor2)) ; same unit

               (let ((n (n:+ (cdr factor1) (cdr factor2))))

                 (if (n:= 0 n)

                     (loop (cdr u1) (cdr u2))

                     (cons (cons (car factor1) n)

                           (loop (cdr u1) (cdr u2)))))

               (if (symbol<? (car factor1) (car factor2))

                   (cons factor1 (loop (cdr u1) u2))

                   (cons factor2 (loop u1 (cdr u2))))))

         (if (pair? u1) u1 u2)))))

某些运算符，例如 remainder、expt、invert、square、sqrt 和 atan，需要特殊处理。其余运算符则可以归入几个简单的类别。像 negate 这样的简单一元运算，只是把实参的单位传播给结果：Some operators, such as remainder, expt, invert, square, sqrt, and atan, require special treatment. The rest of the operators fit into a few simple classes. Simple unary operations, like negate, just propagate the units of their argument to their result:

(define (unit:simple-unary-operation u)

  u)

但有些运算，例如加法的实现，会检查自己是否在“把苹果和橙子混为一谈”：But some, like the implementation of addition, check that they are not “combining apples and oranges:”

(define (unit:simple-binary-operation u1 u2)

  (if (not (unit=? u1 u2))

      (error "incompatible units:" u1 u2))

  u1)

练习 6.1：导出单位Exercise 6.1: Derived units

尽管上面给出的单位计算是正确的，而且相当完整，但用起来并不十分方便。例如，动能的单位规格（如第 316 页所示）是：Although the unit computation given above is correct and reasonably complete, it is not very nice to use. For example, the unit specification for kinetic energy (as shown on page 316) is:

(unit kilogram 1 meter 2 second -2)

按国际单位制（SI）的基本单位 {kilogram, meter, second} 来说，这样是正确的；但若用焦耳——SI 中能量的导出单位——来表示，就会好得多：This is correct in terms of the International System of Units (SI) base units {kilogram, meter, second}, but it would be much nicer if expressed in terms of joules, the SI derived unit of energy:

(unit joule 1)

完整的 SI 基本单位体系是 {kilogram, meter, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela}，此外还有一组获认可的导出单位。例如：The full system of SI base units is {kilogram, meter, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela}, and there is an approved set of derived units. For example:

  • newton = kilogram·meter·second−2newton = kilogram·meter·second−2
  • joule = newton·meterjoule = newton·meter
  • coulomb = ampere·secondcoulomb = ampere·second
  • watt = joule·second−1watt = joule·second−1
  • volt = watt·ampere−1volt = watt·ampere−1
  • ohm = volt·ampere−1ohm = volt·ampere−1
  • siemens = ohm−1siemens = ohm−1
  • farad = coulomb·volt−1farad = coulomb·volt−1
  • weber = volt·secondweber = volt·second
  • henry = weber·ampere−1henry = weber·ampere−1
  • hertz = second−1hertz = second−1
  • tesla = weber·meter−2tesla = weber·meter−2
  • pascal = newton·meter−2pascal = newton·meter−2
  1. a. 编写一个过程，接受用 SI 基本单位表示的单位描述，并在可能时使用导出单位生成更简单的描述。a. Make a procedure that takes a unit description in terms of SI base units and, if possible, makes a simpler description using derived units.
  2. b. 用导出单位表示单位描述的方式并不唯一——可能有许多种这样的等价描述。这类似于代数化简问题，但“更简单”的标准并不明显。制作一个你喜欢的好用版本，并解释你为什么喜欢它。b. The expression of a unit description in terms of the derived units is not unique—there may be many such equivalent descriptions. This is similar to a problem of algebraic simplification, but the criterion of “simpler” is not obvious. Make a nice version that you like and explain why you like it.
  3. c. 能够使用单位的标准缩写和倍率会很方便。例如，1 mA 就是 0.001 A 或 1/1000 ampere 的简洁写法。设计并实现一个简单、可扩展的系统，允许在输入和输出中都使用这些便捷的记法。但请记住，“语法糖会导致分号癌”。c. It is nice to be able to use the standard abbreviations and multipliers for the units. For example, 1 mA is the nice way to write 0.001 A or 1/1000 ampere. Design and implement a simple extensible system that allows the use of these notational conveniences for both input and output. But remember that “syntactic sugar causes cancer of the semicolon.”

6.4 用依赖关系注释值6.4 Annotating values with dependencies

依赖关系跟踪是程序员可能希望在程序的某些部分采用的一种注释。每一项数据（或过程）都有来处。它要么以一个前提的身份进入计算，并可用其外部来源加以标记；要么由其他数据组合而成。我们可以为系统的基本运算提供注释层，使其在处理带有依据的数据时，能够为结果附上适当的依据。One kind of annotation that a programmer may want to deploy in some parts of a program is the tracking of dependencies. Every piece of data (or procedure) came from somewhere. Either it entered the computation as a premise that can be labeled with its external provenance, or it was created by combining other data. We can provide primitive operations of the system with annotation layers that, when processing data with justifications, can annotate the results with appropriate justifications.

依据可以有不同的详尽程度。最简单的依据就是对新数据有所贡献的那些前提的集合。像加法这样的过程可以生成一个和，其依据就是所提供的各加数的依据所包含的前提的并集。乘法与之类似，但只要有一个乘数为零，就足以使乘积为零，因此零乘积的依据不必包含其他因子的依据。Justifications can be at differing levels of detail. The simplest kind of justification is just a set of those premises that contributed to the new data. A procedure such as addition can form a sum with a justification that is just the union of the premises of the justifications of the addends that were supplied. Multiplication is similar, but a zero multiplicand is sufficient to force the product to be zero, so the justifications of the other factors do not need to be included in the justification of the zero product.

计算和携带这种简单依据，几乎只需常数级的额外开销，但对于复杂过程的调试，以及确定计算结果的功过归属，它们可能极有价值。仅仅这些，就足以支持依赖关系驱动的回溯。（参见第 7.5 节。）Such simple justifications can be computed and carried without much more than a constant overhead, but they can be invaluable in debugging complex processes and in the attribution of credit or blame for outcomes of computations. Just this much is sufficient to support dependency-directed backtracking. (See section 7.5.)

外部提供的数据可以用一个标识其来源的前提加以注释。更一般地说，任何数据值都可以用一组前提加以注释，这组前提称为它的支持集。注释某个数据项的支持集通常简称为它的支持。当一个能处理支持信息的过程应用于多个实参时，它必须组合各实参的支持集，以表示结果的支持。Externally supplied data can be annotated with a premise that identifies its origin. More generally, any data value can be annotated with a set of premises, which is called its support set. The support set annotating a datum is usually referred to as its support. When a support-aware procedure is applied to multiple arguments, it must combine the support sets of the arguments to represent the support of the result.

管理支持集是对我们的分层数据机制的一种直接应用。我们给泛型算术系统添加一个支持层，用来处理支持集。它与单位层等其他层共存。因此，这是一项以添加方式引入的功能。Managing support sets is a straightforward application of our layered data mechanism. We add a support layer to our generic arithmetic to handle support sets. It coexists with other layers, such as the units layer. So this is an additive feature.

在第 309 页，我们构建了一个支持分层数据和过程的算术系统：On page 309 we built an arithmetic that supports layered data and procedures:

(define generic-with-layers

  (let ((g (generic-symbolic)))

    (extend-generic-arithmetic! g layered-extender)

    g))



(install-arithmetic! generic-with-layers)

我们不必指定 layered-extender 要支持哪些层，因为它会自动使用每个分层过程实参中包含的层。因此，例如，当以带有单位的实参调用 + 时，结果也将带有单位。但如果各实参都没有单位，那么结果也没有单位，而且不会调用单位加法过程。同样，如果各实参具有支持，结果也会具有支持。但如果各实参没有支持，结果就不会有支持，也不会调用支持加法过程。We don't need to specify what layers are to be supported by layered-extender, since it automatically uses the layers in each layered procedure's arguments. So if, say, + is called with arguments that have units, then the result will also have units. But if none of the arguments have units, then neither does the result, and the unit addition procedure is not invoked. Similarly, if the arguments have support, then the result will have support. But if the arguments do not have support, the result will not have support, and the support addition procedure is not invoked.

例如，我们可以定义质量为 m、速度为 v 的粒子的动能：For example, we can define the kinetic energy of a particle with mass m and velocity v:

(define (KE m v)

  (* 1/2 m (square v)))

现在，我们可以看看在一些实参上求值动能所得到的结果：Now we can see the result of evaluating the kinetic energy on some arguments:

(pp (KE (layered-datum ’m

                       unit-layer (unit ’kilogram 1)

                       support-layer (support-set ’cph))

        (layered-datum ’v

                       unit-layer (unit ’meter 1 ’second -1)

                       support-layer (support-set ’gjs))))

#[layered-datum (* (* 1/2 m) (square v))]

(base-layer (* (* 1/2 m) (square v)))

(unit-layer (unit kilogram 1 meter 2 second -2))

(support-layer (support-set gjs cph))

我们为每个实参都提供单位层和支持层的注释。对于支持层，我们给出一个前提集合（支持集）。这里，每个实参分别由单个前提 cph 和 gjs 支持。得到的值是一个具有三层的分层对象：基础泛型算术层的值是相应的代数表达式；单位是正确的；支持集则是对该值有所贡献的具名前提的集合。We supply each argument with annotations for the units layer and the support layer. For the support layer we give a set of premises (the support set). Here, each argument is supported by a single premise, cph and gjs respectively. The value is a layered object with three layers: the base generic arithmetic layer value is the appropriate algebraic expression; the units are correct; and the support set is the set of named premises that contributed to the value.

这里，我们接受了 KE 的定义，却没有为该过程提供显式的支持。更一般地说，我们可能希望添加这种支持。例如，我们可能希望声明 KE 由前提 KineticEnergy-classical 支持。这样，当我们发现某个复杂计算的结果似乎不正确时，除了可以查明使用了哪些数值或符号输入值，还能查明哪些过程对错误答案有所贡献。我们将在练习 6.2 中着手解决这个问题。Here we accepted the definition of KE without supplying explicit support for that procedure. More generally, we might want to add such support. For example, we may want to say that KE is supported by a premise KineticEnergy-classical. Then if we find a result of some complex computation that seems wrong, we can find out which procedures contributed to the wrong answer, as well as the numerical or symbolic input values that were used. We will attack this problem in exercise 6.2.

计算实参中出现的前提不一定都需要出现在结果中。例如，如果乘积的一个因子为零，那么无论其他有限因子是什么，这都足以成为乘积为零的理由。提供一个零质量便能说明这一点：Not all premises that appear in the arguments to a computation need to appear in a result. For example, if a factor contributing to a product is zero, that is sufficient reason for the product to be zero, independent of any other finite factors. This is illustrated by supplying a zero mass:

(pp (KE (layered-datum 0

                       unit-layer (unit ’kilogram 1) support-layer

                       (support-set ’jems))

        (layered-datum ’v

                       unit-layer (unit 'meter 1 'second -1)

                       support-layer (support-set ’gjs))))

#[layered-datum 0]

(base-layer 0)

(unit-layer (unit kilogram 1 meter 2 second -2))

(support-layer (support-set jems))

这里，结果的数值为零这一事实的支持，仅仅是为质量零值所提供的支持。Here the support for the numeric value of the result being zero is just the support supplied for the zero value for the mass.

6.4.1 支持层6.4.1 The support layer

现在来看支持层的实现。它与单位层有些不同，因为单位的组合完全不必参考基础层，而支持层在某些运算中需要查看基础层。Now we will see how the support layer is implemented. It is somewhat different from the units layer, because units can be combined without any reference to the base layer, whereas the support layer needs to look at the base layer for some operations.

支持层比单位层稍微简单一些，因为除了三个算术运算符外，其余都采用默认方式：结果的支持集是各实参支持集的并集。The support layer is somewhat simpler than the units layer, because all but three of the arithmetic operators use the default: the support set of the result is the union of the support sets of the arguments.

(define support-layer

  (make-annotation-layer 'support

    (lambda (get-name has-value? get-value)

      (define (get-default-value)

        (support-set))

      (define (get-procedure name arity)

        (case name

          ((*) support:*)

          ((/) support:/)

          ((atan2) support:atan2)

          (else support:default-procedure)))

      (bundle layer?

              get-name has-value? get-value

              get-default-value get-procedure))))



(define support-layer-value

  (layer-accessor support-layer))



(define (support:default-procedure base-value . args)

  (apply support-set-union (map support-layer-value args)))

乘法是第一个有意思的情形。支持层需要查看基础算术实参的值，以确定如何计算支持。如果任一实参为零，那么结果的支持就只是这个零实参的支持。Multiplication is the first interesting case. The support layer needs to look at the values of the base arithmetic arguments to determine the computation of support. If either argument is zero, then the support for the result is only the support for the zero argument.

(define (support:* base-value arg1 arg2)

  (let ((v1 (base-layer-value arg1))

        (v2 (base-layer-value arg2))

        (s1 (support-layer-value arg1))

        (s2 (support-layer-value arg2)))

    (if (exact-zero? v1)

        (if (exact-zero? v2)

            (if (< (length (support-set-elements s1))

                   (length (support-set-elements s2)))

                s1

                s2)   ;arbitrary

            s1)

        (if (exact-zero? v2)

            s2

            (support-set-union s1 s2)))))

除法（以及此处未展示的反正切）也必须检查基础层，以处理零实参。如果被除数为零，就足以支持商为零这一结果。除数绝不会为零，因为在这种情况下，基础层的计算早已报告错误，这段代码不会执行。Division (and arctangent, not shown) also has to examine the base layer to deal with zero arguments. If the dividend is zero, that is sufficient to support the result that the quotient is zero. The divisor won't ever be zero because the base-layer computation will have signaled an error and this code won't be run.

(define (support:/ base-value arg1 arg2)

  (let ((v1 (base-layer-value arg1))

        (s1 (support-layer-value arg1))

        (s2 (support-layer-value arg2)))

    (if (exact-zero? v1)

        s1

        (support-set-union s1 s2))))

对于 * 和 / 的这些优化，只有当我们能够证明某个实参确实为零，而不是一个尚未化简的符号表达式时，才有意义。（不过，如果一个表达式能够化简为精确的零，我们就可以利用这一事实！）These optimizations for * and / make sense only when we can prove that an argument is really zero, not an unsimplified symbolic expression. (But if an expression simplifies to exact zero we can use that fact!)

(define (exact-zero? x)

  (and (n:number? x) (exact? x) (n:zero? x)))

支持集抽象实现为一个以符号 support-set 开头的列表The support-set abstraction is implemented as a list starting with the symbol support-set

(define (%make-support-set elements)

  (cons ’support-set elements))



(define (support-set? object)

  (and (pair? object)

       (eq? ’support-set (car object))

       (list? (cdr object))))



(define (support-set-elements support-set)

  (cdr support-set))

再加上一些辅助工具，以使这一抽象完整。along with a few extra utilities to complete the abstraction.

(define (make-support-set elements)

  (if (null? elements)

      %empty-support-set

      (%make-support-set (delete-duplicates elements))))



(define (support-set . elements)

  (if (null? elements)

      %empty-support-set

      (%make-support-set (delete-duplicates elements))))



(define %empty-support-set

  (%make-support-set ’()))



(define (support-set-empty? s)

  (null? (support-set-elements s)))

我们需要能够计算支持集的并集，并向其中添加新元素。既然我们选择把元素保存在列表中，就可以使用 Scheme 的 lset 库。4We need to be able to compute the union of support sets and adjoin new elements to them. Since we chose to keep our elements in a list, we can use the lset library from Scheme.4

(define (support-set-union . sets)

  (make-support-set

   (apply lset-union eqv?

          (map support-set-elements sets))))



(define (support-set-adjoin set . elts)

  (make-support-set

   (apply lset-adjoin eqv? (support-set-elements set) elts)))

练习 6.2：过程的责任Exercise 6.2: Procedural responsibility

建立在算术基础上的支持层极为底层。每个基本算术运算都能处理支持信息，而在常见情况下没有办法绕过这项工作。这里需要一种抽象手段。例如，假设我们有一个过程，用来计算函数的数值定积分。积分数值的单位，是被积函数数值的单位与积分限数值的单位的乘积。（上限与下限的单位必须相同！）但是，让单位计算贯穿积分过程中进行的全部细致算术运算，并不是个好主意。应该能够为积分器添加注释，使结果具有正确的单位，而不必要求每一次内部加法和乘法都是作用于分层数据的分层过程。The support layer based on arithmetic is extremely low level. Every primitive arithmetic operation is support-aware, and there is no way to bypass that work for common conditions. There needs to be a means of abstraction. For example, suppose we have a procedure that computes the numerical definite integral of a function. The units of the numerical value of the integral is the product of the units of the numerical value of the integrand and the units of the numerical value of the limits of integration. (The units of the upper and lower limit must be the same!) However, it is not a good idea to carry the units computation through all of the detailed arithmetic going on in the integration process. It should be possible to annotate the integrator so that the result has the correct units without requiring every internal addition and multiplication to be a layered procedure operating on layered data.

  1. a. 使复合过程能够通过添加一个前提（例如“made by George”）来修改其结果的支持；这些复合过程可能由基本算术过程构建而成，也可能不是。a. Make it possible to allow compound procedures that may be built out of the primitive arithmetic procedures (or possibly not) to modify the support of their results by adding a premise (such as “made by George”).
  2. b. 允许以一种对支持层隐藏过程体的方式执行复合过程。这样，例如，一个可信的库过程可以为结果附上适当的支持，但其过程体中的运算不会承担计算中间结果支持的额外开销。b. Allow compound procedures to be executed in a way that hides their bodies from the support layer. Thus, for example, a trusted library procedure may annotate its result with appropriate support, but the operations in its body will not incur the overhead of computing the support of intermediate results.
  3. c. 支持层是围绕算术系统的运算符组织的。但有时，区分某个运算符的具体出现位置会很有用。例如，在处理数值精度时，仅仅说有效数字的损失源于对几乎相等的量做减法，并没有多大帮助。指出究竟是哪一次减法造成了问题，会更有用。有没有办法为支持层添加识别运算符具体实例的能力？c. The support layer is organized around the operators of an arithmetic system. But sometimes it is useful to distinguish the specific occurrences of an operator. For example, when dealing with numerical precision it is not very helpful to say that a loss of significance is due to subtraction of almost equal quantities. It would be more helpful to show the particular instance of subtraction that is the culprit. Is there some way to add the ability to identify instances of an operator to the support layer?

练习 6.3：多疑式编程Exercise 6.3: Paranoid programming

有时，我们并不确信某个库过程会按预期工作。这时，谨慎的做法是用一个检查其结果的测试来“包装”这个库过程。例如，我们可能正在使用一个名为 solve 的程序，它接受一组方程和一组可能出现在这些方程中的未知量作为输入，产生一组对未知量的替换，使这些方程成立。我们可能希望用一个包装器包装 solve 程序，检查将输出代入输入方程后，是否确实使它们成为恒真式。但我们不希望这种多疑式包装器成为程序总体设计构思的一部分。如何将这类东西实现为一个层？解释你的设计并实现它。Sometimes we are not confident that a library procedure does what we expect. In that case it is prudent to “wrap” the library procedure with a test that checks its result. For example, we may be using a program solve that takes as inputs a set of equations and a set of unknowns, that may occur in the equations, producing a set of substitutions for the unknowns that satisfy the equations. We might want to wrap the solve program with a wrapper that checks that the result of substituting the outputs into the input equations indeed makes them tautologies. But we don't want such a paranoia wrapper to appear as part of our parti. How can this sort of thing be implemented as a layer? Explain your design and implement it.

练习 6.4：分层程序的 IDEExercise 6.4: IDE for layered programs

本练习是一项大型设计项目：构思并开发一个用于分层系统的 IDE（集成开发环境）。This exercise is a major design project: the invention of and development of an IDE (Integrated Development Environment) for layered systems.

使用分层数据和分层过程来构建分层程序，是一个非常好的想法。目标是能够用有用且可执行的元数据——例如类型声明、断言、单位和支持——注释程序，而不使基础程序的文本杂乱无章。不过，程序文本必须与注释文本相互关联，这样，在编辑程序的任何部分时，相关层也会随之编辑。例如，假设需要编辑某个分层过程的基础过程。各层可能包含类型声明，或如何处理单位和支持集之类的信息。如果编辑器能够在需要时向我们展示这些层，以及它们与基础程序文本之间的联系，就会很方便。对基础程序文本的编辑，可能意味着也要编辑注释层。有时这可以自动完成，但通常必须由程序员来编辑各层。The idea of layered programs, using layered data and layered procedures, is a very nice idea. The goal is to be able to annotate programs with useful and executable metadata—such as type declarations, assertions, units, and support—without cluttering the text of the base program. However, the text of the program must be linked with the text of the annotations, so that as any part of the program is edited, the related layers are also edited. For example, suppose it is necessary to edit the base procedure of some layered procedure. The layers may be information like type declarations or how it handles units and support sets. It would be nice for the editor to show us these layers and how they are connected to the text of the base program, when necessary. Perhaps edits to the text of the base program entail edits to the annotation layers. Sometimes this can be done automatically, but often the programmer must edit the layers.

  1. a. 设想一下，为了支持分层系统的开发，你希望 IDE 提供什么。你希望在屏幕上看到什么？你将如何使被编辑的各部分保持同步？a. Imagine what you would like to see in an IDE to support the development of layered systems. What would you like to see on a screen? How would you keep the parts that are edited synchronized?
  2. b. Emacs 是构建这种 IDE 的强大基础设施。它支持多窗口，并且每个窗口可有各自的编辑模式。它为包括 Scheme 在内的许多计算机语言提供语法支持。Emacs 的一些子系统，例如 org-mode，具有文档分层结构的意味。能否扩展它以帮助分层编程？概述一种用 Emacs 构建你的 IDE 的方法。b. Emacs is a powerful infrastructure for building such an IDE. It supports multiple windows and per-window editing modes. It has syntactic support for many computer languages, including Scheme. There are Emacs subsystems, like org-mode, that have the flavor of a layered structure for documents. Can this be extended to help with layered programming? Sketch out a way to build your IDE using Emacs.
  3. c. 以 Emacs 为基础构建一个小型但可扩展的原型，并试用它。你遇到了什么问题？Emacs 确实提供了一个良好的起点吗？如果没有，为什么？报告你的实验。c. Build a small but extensible prototype on the Emacs base, and try it out. What problems do you encounter? Did Emacs really provide a good place to start? If not, why not? Report on your experiment.
  4. d. 如果你的原型前景不错，就开发一个稳健的系统，并将其制作成可加载的 Emacs 库，这样我们都能使用你的出色系统。d. If your prototype was promising, develop a solid system and make it into a loadable Emacs library, so we can all use your great system.

6.4.2 携带依据6.4.2 Carrying justifications

更复杂的依据还可以记录用于生成数据的具体运算。这类注释可用于提供解释（证明），但它本质上有很高的空间开销——可能与所执行的运算次数成线性关系。不过，有时适宜附加一份描述数据项推导过程的详细审计历史，以便后续的某个过程能利用这一推导来达成某种目的，或者为调试而评估推导的有效性。5More complex justifications may also record the particular operations that were used to make the data. This kind of annotation can be used to provide explanations (proofs), but it is intrinsically expensive in space—potentially linear in the number of operations performed. However, sometimes it is appropriate to attach a detailed audit history describing the derivation of a data item, to allow some later process to use the derivation for some purpose or to evaluate the validity of the derivation for debugging.5

对于法律论证等许多用途，必须知道数据的来源：在哪里收集、如何收集、由谁收集、收集是如何获得授权的，等等。一项证据的详细推导，给出了每一份贡献的来源，可能是判定它在审判中能否被采纳的关键。For many purposes, such as legal arguments, it is necessary to know the provenance of data: where it was collected, how it was collected, who collected it, how the collection was authorized, etc. The detailed derivation of a piece of evidence, giving the provenance of each contribution, may be essential to determining if it is admissable in a trial.

我们在第 3.1 节构建的符号算术，是实现这一点的一种方法。事实上，如果把符号算术用作数值算术之上的一层，那么每个数值都会附带其推导过程作为注释。符号算术注释可能代价很高，因为数值运算符的一次应用所对应的符号表达式，包含其各输入的符号表达式。不过，因为我们只需包含指向每个输入的指针，为每次运算添加注释的时空开销往往可以接受。6 因此，可以在需要提供解释时叠加这类依据，甚至可以临时叠加它，以追踪一个难以捕捉的缺陷。The symbolic arithmetic that we built in section 3.1 is one way this can be done. In fact, if symbolic arithmetic is used as a layer on numeric arithmetic, then every numerical value is annotated with its derivation. The symbolic arithmetic annotation could be very expensive, because the symbolic expression for an application of a numerical operator includes the symbolic expressions of its inputs. However, because we need only include a pointer to each input, the space and time cost of annotating each operation is often acceptable.6 So one may overlay this kind of justification when it is necessary to provide an explanation, or even temporarily, to track a difficult-to-catch bug.

练习 6.5：依据Exercise 6.5: Justifications

概述为数据携带依据所涉及的问题。注意，一个值的理由取决于它由哪些值推导而来，以及那些值如何组合。如果某个值的理由是许多因素按数值权重组合的结果，如深度神经网络中的情形，我们该怎么办？这是一个我们需要研究的问题，以便让影响我们的系统能够被追究责任。Sketch out the issues involved in carrying justifications for data. Notice that the reason for a value depends on the values that it was derived from and the way those values were combined. What do we do if the reason for a value is some numerically weighted combination of many factors, as in a deep neural network? This is a research question that we need to address to make the systems that affect us accountable.

6.5 分层的前景6.5 The promise of layering

通过一种简单方便的数据和程序分层机制所能实现的事情，我们仅仅触及了皮毛。这是一个开放的研究领域。开发支持这种分层的系统，可能对未来产生巨大影响。We have only scratched the surface of what can be done with an easy and convenient mechanism for layering of data and programs. It is an open area of research. The development of systems to support such layering can have huge consequence for the future.

灵敏度分析是利用带注释的数据和分层过程可以构建的一项重要功能。例如，在力学中，如果我们有一个系统，能够从某些初始条件出发演化微分方程组的解，那么了解环绕某条参考轨迹的轨迹管如何变形，往往很有价值。通常的做法是在沿参考轨迹积分的同时，对一个变分系统进行积分。类似地，在某些分析中，或许可以在携带算出的标称值的同时，也携带其周围各值的概率分布。实现方式可以是用分布注释各个值，并为运算配备叠加过程，以标称值为指导组合这些分布，或许由此实现贝叶斯分析。当然，要把这件事做好并不容易。Sensitivity analysis is an important feature that can be built using annotated data and layered procedures. For example, in mechanics, if we have a system that evolves the solution of a system of differential equations from some initial conditions, it is often valuable to understand the way a tube of trajectories that surround a reference trajectory deforms. This is usually accomplished by integrating a variational system along with the reference trajectory. Similarly, it may be possible to carry a probability distribution of values around a nominal value along with the nominal value computed in some analyses. This may be accomplished by annotating the values with distributions and providing the operations with overlaying procedures to combine the distributions, guided by the nominals, perhaps implementing Bayesian analysis. Of course, to do this well is not easy.

一个与此相关、甚至更令人兴奋的想法是扰动式编程。类比微分方程的例子，我们能否编写符号系统，让它携带环绕参考轨迹的一个变化“管”，从而使我们能够考虑查询的微小变化？例如，考虑搜索问题。给定一组关键词，系统施展一番魔法，找出与关键词匹配的文档列表。假设我们逐步改变其中一个关键词。搜索对这个关键词有多敏感？更重要的是，在这次略有不同的搜索中，能否重用为得到上一次结果而做过的某些工作？我们不知道这些问题的答案，但如果可能，我们希望能够通过一种叠加在基础程序之上的扰动式程序来表达这些方法。An even more exciting but related idea is that of perturbational programming.
