amb-choose 过程使用前提禁配集来确定，支持真值的前提或支持假值的前提是否可以被相信。一个前提的 premise-nogoods 中，每个元素都是一个前提集合；如果其中所有前提都被相信，那么该前提就不能被相信。因此，如果 amb-choose 为某个前提找到任何一个得到完全支持的前提禁配集，该前提就不能被相信。The amb-choose procedure uses the premise nogoods to determine whether the premise supporting the true value or the premise supporting the false value may be believed. Each element of the premise-nogoods of a premise is a set of premises such that if they are all believed, the premise cannot be believed. So if amb-choose finds any fully supported premise nogood for a premise, that premise cannot be believed.

如果支持真值的前提或支持假值的前提可以被相信，amb-choose 就相应地断言真或假。如果两者都不可相信，它就交由更高层的矛盾处理（process-contradictions）来处理，希望在其他前提的相信状态经过调节后，当这个传播子重新激活时，就能断言真或假。传给 process-contradictions 的参数由 pairwise-union 构造，是一组禁配集。其中每个禁配集都是一个排除真值选择的前提集合与一个排除假值选择的前提集合的并集。因此，这些禁配集中的任何一个都会阻止对任一备选项的选择。14If the premise supporting the true value or the premise supporting the false value is believable, amb-choose asserts true or false respectively. If neither is believable, it defers to higher-level contradiction processing (process-contradictions) in the hope that after the beliefs in other premises are modulated, it may be possible to assert true or false when this propagator is reactivated. The argument given to process-contradictions, constructed by pairwise-union, is a set of nogoods. Each of these nogoods is the union of a set of premises that rule out the choice of true and a set of premises that rule out a choice of false. Thus, any one of these nogoods would prevent the choice of either alternative.14

(define (pairwise-union nogoods1 nogoods2)

  (append-map (lambda (nogood1)

                (map (lambda (nogood2)

                       (support-set-union nogood1 nogood2))

                     nogoods2))

              nogoods1))

从矛盾中学习Learning from contradictions

过程 process-contradictions 保存它收到的所有禁配集，将其中的信息分发到各个前提的前提禁配集中。然后，如果存在假设性前提，它就通过撤回其中一个假设性前提，选择一个禁配集使其不再被完全相信。The procedure process-contradictions saves all of the nogoods it received, distributing the information in the nogoods to the premise nogoods of the premises. It then chooses a nogood to disbelieve by retracting one of its hypothetical premises, if there are any.

(define (process-contradictions nogoods complaining-cell)

  (update-failure-count!)

  (for-each save-nogood! nogoods)

  (let-values (((to-disbelieve nogood)

                (choose-premise-to-disbelieve nogoods)))

    (maybe-kick-out to-disbelieve nogood complaining-cell)))

过程 save-nogood! 把给定 nogood 集合中每个前提所不相容的其他前提组成的集合，添加到该前提的 premise-nogoods 中。这就是系统从过去的失败中学习的方式。正在更新的前提不会包含在它自身的前提禁配集中，因为一个前提不可能与其自身不相容。The procedure save-nogood! augments the premise-nogoods of each premise in the given nogood set with the set of other premises it is incompatible with. This is how the system learns from its past failures. The premise being updated is not included in its own premise nogood sets, because a premise may not be incompatible with itself.

(define (save-nogood! nogood)

  (for-each (lambda (premise)

              (set-premise-nogoods! premise

                (adjoin-support-with-subsumption

                 (support-set-remove nogood premise)

                 (premise-nogoods premise))))

            (support-set-elements nogood)))

新的前提禁配集可能涵盖某个已有前提禁配集，也可能被其涵盖；极小的前提禁配集最有用。The new premise nogood may either subsume or be subsumed by one of the existing premise nogoods; minimal premise nogoods are most useful.

消解矛盾Resolving the contradiction

要消解一个矛盾，可以从支持该矛盾的禁配集中撤回一个前提。唯一可以撤回的是那些“为了讨论起见”而断言的假设性前提。如果有多个禁配集支持一个矛盾，我们就选择假设性前提数量最少的一个，因为使一个小禁配集不再被完全相信，比使一个含有更多假设性前提的禁配集不再被完全相信，能排除更多可能性。A contradiction is resolved by retracting one of the premises in the nogood set that supports the contradiction. The only premises that can be retracted are the hypotheticals, which are asserted “for the sake of argument.” If there is more than one nogood set supporting a contradiction, we choose one with the smallest number of hypotheticals, because disbelieving a small nogood set rules out more possiblities than disbelieving a nogood set with a larger number of hypotheticals.

(define (choose-premise-to-disbelieve nogoods)

  (choose-first-hypothetical

   (car (sort-by nogoods

          (lambda (nogood)

            (count hypothetical?

                   (support-set-elements nogood)))))))

不过，应当拒绝所选禁配集中的哪一个假设性前提，并不显而易见。这里，我们任意选择禁配集中第一个可用的假设性前提。However, the choice of which hypothetical from the selected nogood set to reject is not apparent. Here we arbitrarily choose the first hypothetical premise available in the nogood set.

(define (choose-first-hypothetical nogood)

  (let ((hyps (support-set-filter hypothetical? nogood)))

    (values (and (not (support-set-empty? hyps))

                 (car (support-set-elements hyps)))

            nogood)))

过程 maybe-kick-out 完成消解矛盾的最后工作。如果选择器找到了一个适合不再相信的假设，就撤回该假设，传播照常继续。否则，传播过程停止，并向用户报告矛盾。The procedure maybe-kick-out finishes the job of resolving the contradiction. If the chooser was able to find a suitable hypothesis to disbelieve, then that hypothesis is retracted and propagation continues normally. Otherwise, the propagation process is stopped and the user is informed about the contradiction.

(define (maybe-kick-out to-disbelieve nogood cell)

  (if to-disbelieve

      (mark-premise-out! to-disbelieve)

      (abort-process (list ’contradiction cell))))

在单元中发现的矛盾Contradictions discovered in a cell

如果在向单元添加内容的过程中发现矛盾，这个出问题的单元就以自身为参数调用 handle-cell-contradiction。此时，单元中的最强值是矛盾对象，而矛盾对象的支持就是造成麻烦的禁配集。可以将它交给 process-contradictions 处理。If in the process of adding content to a cell a contradiction is discovered, the unhappy cell calls handle-cell-contradiction with itself as the argument. At that moment the strongest value in the cell is the contradiction object, and the support of the contradiction object is the irritating nogood set. This can be handed off to process-contradictions to deal with.

(define (handle-cell-contradiction cell)

  (let ((nogood (support-layer-value (cell-strongest cell))))

    (process-contradictions (list nogood) cell)))

要支持依赖导向回溯，所需做的就是这些。This is all that needs to be done to support dependency-directed backtracking.

非二元 ambNon-binary amb

尽管 binary-amb 可用于表述许多问题，但大多数选择并非二元的。可以通过构建一个条件传播子电路，从 binary-amb 构造出一种 n 元选择机制；电路由一些单元控制，这些单元的真假值由 binary-amb 传播子调节。但这种方法效率很低，还引入了大量额外机制。因此，我们通过 p:amb 提供一种原生的 n 元选择机制。过程 p:amb 与 binary-amb 类似。对于 binary-amb，单元中的值恰好有两个选择：#t 或 #f，各自由一个假设性前提支持。当把 p:amb 应用于一个单元和一个可能值列表时，过程 make-hypotheticals 将这些值添加到单元中，每个值都由一个新的假设性前提支持。Although binary-amb can be used in the formulation of many problems, most choices are not binary. It is possible to construct an n-ary choice mechanism from binary-amb by building a circuit of conditional propagators controlled by cells whose true or false values are modulated by binary-amb propagators, but this is very inefficient and introduces lots of extra machinery. So we provide a native n-ary choice mechanism with p:amb. The procedure p:amb is analogous to binary-amb. For binary-amb there are exactly two choices, #t or #f, for the value in the cell, and each is supported by a hypothetical premise. When p:amb is applied to a cell and a list of possible values, the procedure make-hypotheticals adds those values to the cell, each supported by a new hypothetical premise.

当 p:amb 构造的传播子被激活时，会调用过程 amb-choose。它先尝试在自己的假设性前提中找到一个未被其 premise-nogoods 排除的前提。如果找到，就把该前提标记为 in，把其他所有前提标记为 out，从而选择与该前提关联的值作为单元的值。如果所有假设性前提都不能被相信，就把自己的所有前提标记为 out，并构造一组新的禁配集，传给 process-contradictions；后者将在可能时从其中一个禁配集中撤回一个假设性前提。将过程 pairwise-union 推广到可接收两个以上集合，就得到 cross-product-union。与之前一样，这也是一个归结步骤。When the propagator constructed by p:amb is activated, the procedure amb-choose is called. It first tries to find a hypothetical premise, among its hypotheticals, that is not ruled out by its premise-nogoods. If there is one, it marks that premise in and marks all of the other premises out, thus choosing the value associated with that premise as the value of the cell. If none of the hypothetical premises can be believed, it marks all of its premises out and makes a new set of nogoods to pass to process-contradictions, which will retract a hypothetical premise from one of those nogoods, if possible. The generalization of the procedure pairwise-union to take more than two setsis cross-product-union. As before, this is a resolution step.

(define (p:amb cell values)

  (let ((premises (make-hypotheticals cell values)))

    (define (amb-choose)

      (let ((to-choose

             (find (lambda (premise)

                     (not (any all-premises-in?

                               (premise-nogoods premise))))

                   premises)))

        (if to-choose

            (for-each (lambda (premise)

                        (if (eq? premise to-choose)

                            (mark-premise-in! premise)

                            (mark-premise-out! premise)))

                      premises)

            (let ((nogoods

                   (cross-product-union

                    (map (lambda (premise)

                           (filter all-premises-in?

                             (premise-nogoods premise)))

                         premises))))

              (for-each mark-premise-out! premises)

              (process-contradictions nogoods cell)))))

      (let ((me (propagator (list cell) (list cell)

                            amb-choose ’amb)))

        (set! all-amb-propagators

              (cons me all-amb-propagators))

        me)))

用 p:amb 构建的选择传播子引入的假设性前提，数量恰好等于选项数量。对于 n > 2 个选项，基于 binary-amb 的构造会引入大约两倍的前提。Choice propagators built with p:amb introduce only as many hypothetical premises as there are choices. Constructions for n > 2 choices based on binary-amb introduce about twice that many premises.

7.5.2 求解组合谜题7.5.2 Solving combinatorial puzzles

为了展示如何使用依赖导向回溯高效求解组合谜题，考虑著名的“多户住宅”谜题：[29]To demonstrate the use of dependency-directed backtracking to solve combinatorial puzzles efficiently, consider the famous “multiple dwelling” puzzle:[29]

Baker、Cooper、Fletcher、Miller 和 Smith 住在一栋只有五层的公寓楼里，分别住在不同楼层。Baker 不住顶层。Cooper 不住底层。Fletcher 既不住顶层，也不住底层。Miller 住得比 Cooper 高。Smith 所住楼层与 Fletcher 的不相邻。Fletcher 所住楼层与 Cooper 的不相邻。每个人分别住在哪一层？Baker, Cooper, Fletcher, Miller, and Smith live on different floors of an apartment house that has only five floors. Baker does not live on the top floor. Cooper does not live on the bottom floor. Fletcher does not live on either the top or the bottom floor. Miller lives on a higher floor than does Cooper. Smith does not live on a floor adjacent to Fletcher's. Fletcher does not live on a floor adjacent to Cooper's. Where does everyone live?

可以把它设为一个传播子问题。下面是对此问题的一种非常朴素的表述：We can set this up as a propagator problem. Here is a very unsophisticated formulation of the problem:

(define (multiple-dwelling)

  (let-cells (baker cooper fletcher miller smith)

    (let ((floors ’(1 2 3 4 5)))

      (p:amb baker floors)  (p:amb cooper floors)

      (p:amb fletcher floors)  (p:amb miller floors)

      (p:amb smith floors)

      (require-distinct

       (list baker cooper fletcher miller smith))

      (let-cells ((b=5 #f)   (c=1 #f)   (f=5 #f)

                  (f=1 #f)   (m>c #t)   (sf #f)

                  (fc  #f)   (one 1)    (five 5)

                  s-f   as-f   f-c    af-c)

        (p:= five baker b=5)  ;Baker is not on 5.

        (p:= one cooper c=1)  ;Cooper is not on 1.

        (p:= five fletcher f=5)  ;Fletcher is not on 5.

        (p:= one fletcher f=1)  ;Fletcher is not on 1.

        (p:> miller cooper m>c)  ;Miller is above Cooper.

        (c:+ fletcher s-f smith)  ;Fletcher and Smith

        (c:abs s-f as-f)  ; are not on

        (p:= one as-f sf)  ; adjacent floors.

        (c:+ cooper f-c fletcher) ;Cooper and Fletcher

        (c:abs f-c af-c)  ; are not on

        (p:= one af-c fc)  ; adjacent floors.

        (list baker cooper fletcher miller smith)))))

这里规定 Baker、Cooper、Fletcher、Miller 和 Smith 都从五个楼层中选一层居住，而且他们的选择必须各不相同。接下来可以看到，以传播子电路表示的、对他们选择的约束。某些单元，例如 b=5，被初始化为一个布尔值。因此，代码行 (p:= five baker b=5) 表示 Baker 不住五层这一约束。Cooper 和 Fletcher 不住相邻楼层这一约束，是通过将 fc 设为 #f 以及最后三个约束来实现的。This says that Baker, Cooper, Fletcher, Miller, and Smith all choose to live on one of the five floors, and their choices must be distinct. We then see the constraints on their choices represented as a propagator circuit. Some cells, such as b=5, are initialized to a boolean value. Thus, the line (p:= five baker b=5) represents the constraint that Baker does not live on the fifth floor. The constraint that Cooper and Fletcher do not live on adjacent floors is implemented by the assignment of fc to #f and the last three constraints.

要使用传播子系统，我们需要定义所有基本传播子，并对数据作适当的分层：To use the propagator system we need to define all the primitive propagators, with the appropriate layering of the data:

(define (setup-propagator-system arithmetic)

  (define layered-arith

    (extend-arithmetic layered-extender arithmetic))

  (install-arithmetic! layered-arith)

  (install-core-propagators! merge-value-sets

                             layered-arith

                             layered-propagator-projector))

这个相当复杂的设置过程提供了构建并安装传播子所需的信息：传播子使用一种算术，其上叠加了可跟踪的前提以及可供调试使用的理由。加载传播子系统时，默认设置针对的是数值数据：This rather complicated setup procedure gives the information required to build and install the propagators with an arithmetic, layered with premises that can be tracked and reasons that are available for debugging. The default setup, when the propagator system is loaded, is for numerical data:

(setup-propagator-system numeric-arithmetic)

现在可以运行我们的谜题示例了：We are now in a position to run our puzzle example:

(initialize-scheduler)



(define answers (multiple-dwelling))

(run)

(map (lambda (cell)

       (get-base-value (cell-strongest cell)))

     answers)

;Value: (3 2 4 5 1)



*number-of-calls-to-fail*

;Value: 106

我们看到了（正确的）结果：每位主人公所住的楼层。我们也看到，大约需要 100 次失败的赋值才能找到一个正确赋值。15 事实证明，该赋值是唯一的：不存在其他与给定约束一致的赋值。We see the (correct) result: the floor on which each protagonist lives. We also see that it takes roughly 100 failed assignments to find a correct assignment.15 It turns out that this assignment is unique: there are no other assignments consistent with the constraints given.

注意，不加约束时的赋值总数为 55 = 3125，但我们只尝试了大约 100 次就解决了问题。能够做到这一点，是因为系统会从错误中学习：每次失败时，它都会积累关于哪些前提集合不能同时被相信的信息。正确使用这些信息，就能避免探索那些根据先前试验结果已知毫无希望的路径。Notice that the total number of unconstrained assignments is 55 = 3125, but we are solving this with only about 100 trials. We are able to do this because the system learns from its mistakes: For each failure it accumulates information about which sets of premises cannot be simultaneously believed. Correctly using this information prevents the investigation of paths that are hopeless given the results of previous experiments.

练习 7.5：游艇名称谜题Exercise 7.5: Yacht name puzzle

使用传播子表述并求解下面的谜题。16Formulate and solve the following puzzle using propagators.16

Mary Ann Moore 的父亲有一艘游艇，他的四位朋友也各有一艘：Downing 上校、Hall 先生、Barnacle Hood 爵士和 Parker 博士。这五个人还各有一个女儿，并且每个人都用其他某人的女儿的名字来命名自己的游艇。Barnacle 爵士的游艇名叫 Gabrielle；Moore 先生拥有 Lorna 号，Hall 先生拥有 Rosalind 号。Downing 上校拥有的 Melissa 号以 Barnacle 爵士的女儿命名。Gabrielle 的父亲所拥有的游艇，以 Parker 博士的女儿命名。谁是 Lorna 的父亲？Mary Ann Moore's father has a yacht and so has each of his four friends: Colonel Downing, Mr. Hall, Sir Barnacle Hood, and Dr. Parker. Each of the five also has one daughter and each has named his yacht after a daughter of one of the others. Sir Barnacle's yacht is the Gabrielle, Mr. Moore owns the Lorna; Mr. Hall the Rosalind. The Melissa, owned by Colonel Downing, is named after Sir Barnacle's daughter. Gabrielle's father owns the yacht that is named after Dr. Parker's daughter. Who is Lorna's father?

练习 7.6：多户住宅谜题Exercise 7.6: Multiple-dwelling puzzle

很容易为 5.4 节的 amb 求值器表述多户住宅问题。事实上，这比为传播子系统表述还容易，因为我们可以用表达式来思考和编写。的确，像 Fletcher 和 Cooper 不住在相邻楼层这样的约束，可以写成类似下面的形式：It is easy to formulate the multiple-dwelling problem for the amb evaluator of chapter 5.4. In fact it is easier than for the propagator system, because we can think and write in terms of expressions. Indeed, you will be able to write constraints like the fact that Fletcher and Cooper do not live on adjacent floors as something like:

(require (not (= (abs (- fletcher cooper)) 1)))

而不必写成rather than

   (c:+ cooper f-c fletcher)

   (c:abs f-c af-c)

   (p:= one af-c fc)

后一种写法必须声明 f-c、af-c 和 fc 这样的单元，并初始化 one 和 fc。这是因为传播系统是一种通用的接线图系统，而不是表达式系统。where cells like f-c, af-c, and fc must be declared and one and fc are initialized. This is because the propagation system is a general wiring-diagram system rather than an expression system.

  1. a. 使用 5.4 节的 amb 求值器表述并求解多户住宅问题。为系统添加监测代码，确定失败次数。需要失败多少次？a. Formulate and solve the multiple-dwelling problem using the amb evaluator of section 5.4. Instrument the system to determine the number of failures. How many failures does it take?
  2. b. 编写一个小型编译器，把以表达式形式编写的约束转换为传播子图的片段。你会发现，这非常容易。在第 340 页的练习 7.1 中，我们已对此作过初步尝试。但这里真正想做的是一个翻译器，把 5.4 节的代码翻译为以传播子为目标的形式。证明你的编译能够得到正确答案。b. Write a small compiler that converts constraints written as expressions into propagator diagram fragments. You will find that this is very easy. We made a first stab at this in exercise 7.1 on page 340. But here we really want to make a translator for code from section 5.4 to a propagator target. Demonstrate that your compilation gets the correct answer.
  3. c. 使用你编译生成的传播子图来求解问题，需要失败多少次？如果失败次数超过约 200 次，你编译出来的代码就非常糟糕！c. How many failures are needed to solve the problem with the propagator diagram that you compiled into? If it takes more than about 200 failures you compiled into very bad code!

练习 7.7：重访纸牌游戏谜题Exercise 7.7: Card game puzzle revisited

使用传播子重做练习 5.17。Redo exercise 5.17 using propagators.

练习 7.8：类型推断Exercise 7.8: Type inference

在 4.4.2 节，我们构建了一个类型推断引擎，作为合一匹配应用的示例。在本练习中（其实这是一个相当大的项目），我们将利用传播来实现类型推断。In section 4.4.2 we built a type-inference engine as an example of the application of unification matching. In this exercise (which is really a substantial project) we implement type inference taking advantage of propagation.

  1. a. 给定一个 Scheme 程序，构建一个传播网络，为每个值得确定类型的位置设置一个单元。每个这样的单元将保存程序中相应位置逐步积累的类型信息。构造连接这些单元的传播子，施加程序结构所隐含的类型约束。使用合一匹配作为 cell-merge 操作。如果程序无法赋予类型，合一可能产生矛盾。a. Given a Scheme program, construct a propagation network with a cell for every locus that is useful to type. Each such cell will be the repository of the type information that will be accumulated about the type information at that locus in the program. Construct propagators that connect the cells and impose the type constraints implied by the program structure. Use unification match as the cell-merge operation. The unification may yield a contradiction if the program cannot be typed.
  2. b. 程序中某些单元的类型，可能无法由相邻单元的类型充分约束。不过，可以向这种单元中放入一个通用类型变量，让该变量通过传播积累约束，从而激发传播。这称为“投放”（plunking）。试试看。b. There may be some cells of a program where a type is not sufficiently constrained by the types of the neighboring cells. However, propagation can be stimulated by dropping a general type variable into such a cell and allowing that variable to accumulate constraints by propagation. This is called “plunking.” Try it.
  3. c. 在困难情形中，类型推断可能需要作出猜测（使用假设性前提），并在发现矛盾时回溯。给出必须这样做的例子。c. In hard cases a type inference may require making guesses (using hypotheticals) and backtracking on discovery of contradictions. Show cases where this is necessary.
  4. d. 跟踪前提和理由，可以构建信息丰富的错误说明；但为此，必须把程序中的每个位置与其单元关联起来，使通过传播获得的知识能对应到正在标注的程序。你可以使用任何喜欢的“便笺”方式，在位置与单元之间建立双向关联。无论如何，都请尝试给出良好的解释，说明为什么某个特定位置具有所确定的类型，或者为什么无法为程序赋予一致的类型。d. Tracking of premises and reasons enables the construction of informative error comments, but to do this you must associate each program locus with its cell so that things that are learned by propagation can be related to the program being annotated. You may use any kind of “sticky note” you like to associate the locus bidirectionally with the cell. In any case, try to make good explanations about why a particular locus has the type that was determined, or why a program could not be consistently typed.
  5. e. 这种类型推断实现实用吗？为什么？如果不实用，该如何改进？e. Is this implementation of type inference practical? Why or why not? If not, how can it be improved?

这段故事的一个启示A moral of this story

解组合谜题很有趣，但这并不是我们所做工作的真正价值所在。确实，“SAT 求解器”对于解决这类现实问题十分重要。但对于计算系统的设计，这里还有更深层的启示。把编程从表达式结构推广到接线图（这可能不太方便——但可以通过编译来缓解），就能够以一种自然而高效的方式，将非确定性选择平滑地融入程序。我们可以引入假设性前提，它们提供由命题支持的备选值，而这些命题可以轻松舍弃。这让我们能够正确处理诸如二次方程之类的问题。它们确实有两个解，而任何基于其中一个解的选择所进行的计算，都可能决定拒绝这个解；另一个解则可能经过长时间计算后，导向可接受的结果。例如，已知 p:sqrt 计算传统的实数正平方根，我们就能构建一个以单元 x∧2 为输入、单元 x 为输出的有向传播子构造器 p:honest-sqrt，为其使用者提供一个（隐藏的）平方根选择：Solving combinatorial puzzles is fun, but it is not the real value of what we have done. Indeed, “SAT solvers” are important for solving real-world problems of this kind. But there is a deeper message here for the design of computational systems. By generalizing our programming from expression structures to wiring diagrams (which can be inconvenient—but that can be mitigated with compiling) we have made it possible to smoothly integrate nondeterministic choice into programs in a natural and efficient way. We can introduce hypotheticals, which provide alternative values supported by propositions that may be discarded without pain. This gives us the freedom to treat things like quadratic equations correctly. They really have two solutions, and any computation based on a choice of one solution may decide to reject it, while the other solution may lead, after a long computation, to an acceptable outcome. For example, given that p:sqrt computes the traditional positive square root of a real number, we can build a directional propagator constructor p:honest-sqrt, with input cell x∧2 and output cell x, that gives its users a (hidden) choice of square roots:

(define-p:prop (p:honest-sqrt (x∧2) (x))

  (let-cells (mul +x)

    (p:amb mul ’(-1 +1))

    (p:sqrt x∧2 +x)

    (p:* mul +x x)))

这里重要的是，可以引入这样的选择，而不必安排外围机制去理解如何处理这种歧义。例如，将数与其平方联系起来的约束传播子，直接使用 p:honest-sqrt 就可以了：What is important here is that such choices may be introduced without arranging that the enclosing machinery knows how to handle the ambiguity. For example, the constraint propagator that relates numbers to their squares can just use p:honest-sqrt:

(define-c:prop (c:square x x∧2)

  (p:square x x∧2)

  (p:honest-sqrt x∧2 x)))

7.6 传播使简并成为可能7.6 Propagation enables degeneracy

设计任何规模可观的系统时，在每一层细节上，都会为每个组件提出许多实现方案。然而，在最终交付的系统中，这种方案多样性却消失了，通常只采纳并实现一种统一方案。就像生态系统一样，传统工程过程中多样性的丧失会带来严重后果。In the design of any significant system there are many implementation plans proposed for every component at every level of detail. However, in the system that is finally delivered this diversity of plans is lost, and usually only one unified plan is adopted and implemented. As in an ecological system, the loss of diversity in the traditional engineering process has serious consequences.

我们很少在程序中构建简并，一方面因为代价高昂，另一方面因为传统上我们没有提供协调其使用的形式化机制。但传播这一思想提供了一种自然机制来纳入简并。单元中使用部分信息结构（由 Radul 和 Sussman [99] 引入），使来自多个、也许相互重叠的信息源的信息能够合并。我们在恒星距离的例子中用区间展示了这一点，见We rarely build degeneracy into programs, partly because it is expensive and partly because we traditionally have supplied no formal mechanisms for mediating its use. But the propagation idea provides a natural mechanism to incorporate degeneracy. The use of partial information structures in cells (introduced by Radul and Sussman [99]) allows multiple, perhaps overlapping, sources of information to be merged. We illustrated this with intervals in the stellar distance example in 7.1 节section 7.1。但合并部分信息有许多方式：部分指定的符号表达式可以通过合一进行合并，如 4.4.2 节所示。因此，部分指定信息这一思想并不局限于用传播子构建的系统；但如果按照第 368 页练习 7.8 的建议，在传播子系统中这样做，我们就有了一种范式，可以组合多个独立机制所作的贡献。同样，我们还考虑了来自 AI 问题求解领域的另一个适用于简并设计的思想：目标导向调用。其想法是，我们不再通过指定完成目标的过程名称，来说明希望“如何”完成目标，而是说明希望完成“什么”，并把能够完成该目标的过程与目标联系起来。这种联系常常通过模式匹配建立，但那只是偶然的实现方式，而非本质要求。17 如果完成目标有不止一种方式，那么选择适当过程就是一个可以登记以供回溯的选择点。然而，受面向表达式语言的控制流约束的时间顺序回溯极其低效。要让依赖导向回溯良好运作，就必须跳出表达式求值结构，而传播正是一条可行之路。搜索仍有可能呈指数级，但利用从经验中学到的禁配集排除大量不良选择，可以显著减少组合数量。. But there are many ways to merge partial information: partially specified symbolic expressions can be merged with unification, as shown in section 4.4.2. So the idea of partially specified information is not restricted to systems built with propagators, but if this is done in a propagator system, as proposed in exercise 7.8 on page 368, we have a paradigm for combining the contributions of multiple independent mechanisms. Similarly, we considered another idea from the AI problem-solving world for degenerate designs: goal-directed invocation. The idea is that instead of specifying “how” we want a goal accomplished, by naming a procedure to accomplish it, we specify “what” we want to accomplish, and we link procedures that can accomplish that goal with the goal. This linkage is often done with pattern matching, but that is accidental rather than essential.17 If there is more than one way to accomplish the goal, then the choice of an appropriate procedure is a choice point that can be registered for backtracking. But chronological backtracking, constrained by the control flow of an expression-oriented language, is extremely inefficient. We must break out of the expression-evaluation structure to make dependency-directed backtracking work well, and propagation is one way to go. We still have a potentially exponential search, but the combinatorics are significantly reduced by eliminating many bad choices using nogood sets learned from experience.

当然，除了使用回溯搜索来选择完成目标的某个特定方式之外，目标还可以通过其他方式调用简并方法。例如，我们可能希望并行运行几种可能解决问题的方法，选择最先终止的一种。Of course, besides using a backtracking search for choosing a particular way to accomplish a goal, there are other ways that the goal can invoke degenerate methods. For example, we may want to run several possible ways to solve a problem in parallel, choosing the one that terminates first.

假设我们有几个独立实现的过程，它们都旨在解决同一类（规定得不精确的）一般问题。暂且假定每种设计都相当称职，对于实际运行中可能遇到的大多数问题，确实能够正确工作。我们知道，可以把这些给定过程组合成一个更大的系统，独立调用每个过程并比较其结果，为每个问题选择最好的答案，从而构建一个更加健壮的系统。如果这个组合系统有独立的方式判断哪些答案可以接受，情况就非常理想。但即使只能依靠投票，我们得到的系统也能可靠地覆盖一个更大的解空间。此外，如果这样的系统能自动记录某个设计失败的所有情形，就可以利用运行反馈改进失败过程的性能。Suppose we have several independently implemented procedures all designed to solve the same (imprecisely specified) general class of problems. Assume for the moment that each design is reasonably competent and actually works correctly for most of the problems that might be encountered in actual operation. We know that we can make a more robust system by combining the given procedures into a larger system that independently invokes each of the given procedures and compares their results, choosing the best answer on every problem. If the combination has independent ways of determining which answers are acceptable we are in very good shape. But even if we are reduced to voting, we get a system that can reliably cover a larger space of solutions. Furthermore, if such a system can automatically log all cases where one of the designs fails, the operational feedback can be used to improve the performance of the procedure that failed.

这种简并设计策略可以用于每一层细节。每个子系统的每个组件，本身也可以采用简并设计。如果组件在子系统之间共享，就得到一种相当强大的受控冗余。然而，我们还可以做得更好。即使一个子系统中的某个值并不与另一个子系统中的某个值精确对应，我们仍然可以提供一种机制，对独立设计的子系统的中间结果进行一致性检查。This degenerate design strategy can be used at every level of detail. Every component of each subsystem can itself be degenerately designed. If the components are shared among the subsystems, we get a controlled redundancy that is quite powerful. However, we can do even better. We can provide a mechanism for consistency checking of the intermediate results of the independently designed subsystems, even when no particular value in one subsystem exactly corresponds to a particular value in another subsystem.

举个简单例子，假设有两个子系统，它们旨在给出同样的结果，但计算方式完全不同。假定设计者们达成一致：在其中一种设计的某个阶段，该设计中两个变量的乘积必须等于另一种设计中两个变量的和。18 没有理由不在这个谓词所依赖的四个值全部可用时立即计算它，从而在运行时提供一致性检查，并向设计者提供强有力的调试信息。这可以通过一个局部嵌入的约束网络来安排。For a simple example, suppose we have two subsystems that are intended to deliver the same result, but computed in completely different ways. Assume that the designers agree that at some stage in one of the designs, the product of two of the variables in that design must be the same as the sum of two of the variables in the other design.18 There is no reason why this predicate should not be computed as soon as all of the four values it depends upon become available, thus providing consistency checking at run time and powerful debugging information to the designers. This can be arranged using a locally embedded constraint network.

No global notion of equivalence can represent the criteria for equivalence without additional local information. To address this problem we could provide a local equivalence predicate for each cell, with a default value for exact quantities.
11 我们的实现中有一个非常糟糕的主意。前提相信状态的变化被实现为全局操作——在并行过程的模拟中，这绝不是个好主意！更好的实现应通过局部过程传播相信状态的变化，类似于传播它们所支持的值的方式。但我们没有这么做——抱歉！11 There is a very bad idea in our implementaton. A change of the belief status of a premise is implemented as a global operation—this is never a good idea in a simulation of a parallel process! A better implementation would propagate the change of belief by local processes, similar to the way the values that they support are propagated. But we didn't do this—sorry!
12 什么是最佳选择，实际上是一个相当复杂的判断。如果一个带支持的值比另一个更具体，例如区间更窄，它就是更好的选择。此外，如果一个值的支持集中的前提比某个“等价”值的少，它也更好，因为需要被相信的前提更少。这通过值集合并机制实现，我们将在下节介绍：12 What is the best choice is actually a rather complex judgment. If one supported value is more specific than another, for example a narrower interval, this is a better choice. Also, if a value has fewer premises in its support set than an “equivalent” value, it is better because it requires fewer premises to be believed. This is implemented by the mechanism of merging value sets, which we will describe in 7.4.3 节section 7.4.3.

A very similar technique, “clausal learning,” was developed in the context of logic by Karl Lieberherr [84]. Clausal learning is now used in the best SAT solvers. Ramin Zabih, David McAllester, and David Chapman showed one way to build this technique into Lisp code [132]. Guy Steele showed an elegant way to incorporate dependency-directed backtracking into a constraint language [116]. Building on the work of Jon Doyle [30] and David McAllester [88], Ken Forbus and Johan deKleer elaborated the theory and practice of dependencies and “truth-maintenance systems” [36], a general way to think about dependencies and backtracking. The way we implement dependency-directed backtracking in this book was developed by Alexey Radul and Gerald Jay Sussman [99, 100].

In propositional logic the cut rule is written (A ∨ B) ∧ (¬B ∨ C) ⊦ (A ∨ C). This rule, combined with unification (section 4.4), is the basis of the famous resolution theorem proving algorithm invented by Robinson [104].

8 尾声8 

Epilogue

真正意义上的工程学只有几千年的历史。我们有意识地构造非常复杂而健壮的系统的尝试，充其量还很不成熟。我们还没有领会生物演化在过去几十亿年里学到的经验。Serious engineering is only a few thousand years old. Our attempts at deliberately producing very complex robust systems are immature at best. We have yet to glean the lessons that biological evolution has learned over the last few billion years.

我们更关心效率和正确性，而不是生物系统通过优化可演化性、灵活性和抗攻击能力所获得的那种健壮性。对于资源仅仅足够履行其功能的关键任务系统，这样做很合理。然而，微电子技术的飞速发展，已经缓解了大多数应用的资源问题。我们对计算和通信基础设施的依赖日益加深，针对这些基础设施的攻击也日趋复杂，因此我们必须把注意力转向健壮性。We have been more concerned with efficiency and correctness than with the kind of robustness of biological systems that comes from optimizing evolvability, flexibility, and resistance to attack. This is sensible for developing mission-critical systems that have barely enough resources to perform their function. However, the rapid advance of microelectronics has alleviated the resource problem for most applications. Our increasing dependence on computational and communications infrastructure, and the development of ever more sophisticated attacks on that infrastructure, make it imperative that we turn our attention to robustness.

我们并不是在倡导仿生学；但观察生物系统，能为我们如何把强大的健壮性原则纳入工程实践提供线索。其中许多原则，与优化效率和优化正确性可证明能力的既有做法直接冲突。在本书中，我们有意违背这些既有做法，探索以灵活性为优化目标的可能性。促使我们采取这种方法的一个观察是：大多数经受住时间考验的系统，都是由一组领域专用语言构建而成的，每种语言都适合让系统的某些部分易于构造。We are not advocating biomimetics; but observations of biological systems give us hints about how to incorporate powerful principles of robustness into our engineering practice. Many of these principles are in direct conflict with the established practices of optimization of efficiency and of the ability to prove correctness. In this book we deliberately violate these established practices to explore the possibilities of optimizing for flexibility. A motivation of our approach is the observation that most systems that have survived the test of time are built as an assembly of domain-specific languages, each of which is appropriate to make some parts of the system easy to construct.

在构建具有人工智能的符号系统的过程中，AI 界顺带开发了一些技术工具，它们可以用来支持灵活而健壮的设计原则。例如，我们不必把回溯仅仅看作组织搜索的一种方法，还可以用它来提高复杂系统中组件的普适性，让系统自行组织，以满足外部施加的约束。我们相信，沿着这种新的综合思路探索下去，将会获得更好的硬件和软件系统。As part of the effort to build artificially intelligent symbolic systems, the AI community has incidentally developed technological tools that can be used to support principles of flexible and robust design. For example, rather than thinking of backtracking as a method of organizing search, we can employ it to increase the general applicability of components in a complex system that organizes itself to meet externally imposed constraints. We believe that by pursuing this new synthesis we will obtain better hardware and software systems.

在第 2 章开篇，我们介绍了一些普遍适用、几乎不会引起异议的技术。我们引入了构建组合子系统的策略——建立具有标准化接口的参数化部件库。这样的部件可以用多种方式组合起来，满足各种各样的需求。我们展示了如何用这一思想简化正则表达式匹配器语言的构造。我们引入了包装器系统，使部件能适应那些标准与部件原先构建标准不同的应用，并用它创建了一种单位换算包装器语言。接着，我们构建了一个规则解释器，用于一种表达西洋跳棋等棋盘游戏规则的语言。We started out in chapter 2 with some rather unobjectionable techniques that are universally applicable. We introduced the strategy of building systems of combinators—libraries of parametric parts that have standardized interfaces. Such parts can be combined in many ways to meet a great variety of needs. We demonstrated how this idea can be used to simplify the construction of a language of regular-expression matchers. We introduced systems of wrappers that allow us to adapt parts to applications with different standards than the parts were built to, and we used this to make a language of unit-conversion wrappers. We progressed to build a rule interpreter for a language to express the rules of board games like checkers.

在第 3 章，我们踏上了一场激动人心却又危险的冒险：研究如果允许调节一种语言中基本过程的含义，能够做些什么。我们扩展了算术，使其不仅能处理数，还能处理符号表达式和函数。我们创建了可扩展的泛型过程，并利用扩展机制，把前向模式自动微分融入算术。这类扩展是危险的，但只要小心，就能让旧程序拥有新能力，同时不失去原有能力。为了让这一策略更高效、更强大，我们继续探索了用户定义类型及其可声明的子类型关系，并据此制作了一个简单但易于扩展的冒险游戏。In chapter 3 we embarked on an exciting and dangerous adventure: we investigated what can be done if we are allowed to modulate the meanings of the primitive procedures of a language. We extended arithmetic to handle symbolic expressions and functions, as well as numbers. We created extensible generic procedures and used the extension mechanism to integrate forward-mode automatic differentiation into our arithmetic. This kind of extension is dangerous, but if we are careful, we can make old programs have new abilities without losing their old abilities. To make this strategy efficient and even more powerful, we proceeded to explore user-defined types, with declarable subtype relationships, and we used that to make a simple but easily extensible adventure game.

第 4 章引入的模式匹配和模式导向调用，是建立领域专用语言的关键技术。我们从用于代数化简的项重写规则开始。随后展示了一种优雅的策略，在模式匹配组合子系统中，把模式编译成基本模式匹配器的组合。接着，我们扩展了模式匹配工具，允许匹配双方都包含模式变量，从而实现了合一，并用它构建了一个基本的类型推断系统。最后，我们构建了能够匹配任意图、而不仅仅是表达式树的匹配器，并使用图和图匹配，以优雅的方式表达国际象棋的走子规则。Pattern matching and pattern-directed invocation, introduced in chapter 4, are crucial techniques for erecting domain-specific languages. We started with term-rewriting rules for algebraic simplification. We then showed an elegant strategy for compiling patterns into a composition of elementary pattern matchers in a system of pattern-matching combinators. We then expanded our pattern-matching tools to allow pattern variables on both sides of a match, implementing unification, which we then used to make an elementary type-inference system. Finally, we built matchers that match arbitrary graphs, not just expression trees, and used graphs and graph matching to express the rules for moves in chess in an elegant manner.

由于所有设计合理的计算机语言都具有通用性，程序员就不能以某种语言无法表达解决方案为借口。如果确实被逼到这一步，优秀的程序员可以在自己不得不用的任何语言中，为自己喜欢的任何语言制作解释器或编译器。这并不是很难，但可能是程序员所能采取的最强有力的举措。在第 5 章，我们展示了如何通过解释和编译，制作能力不断增强的语言。我们从一个类 Scheme 语言的简单应用序解释器开始。为了可扩展性，解释器建立在泛型过程之上。随后扩展它，允许在过程定义中声明惰性形式参数。接着，我们把该语言编译成执行过程的组合——一个组合子系统。然后添加了带有 amb 运算符的非确定性求值模型。最后，我们展示了如何通过暴露底层续延，获得底层 Scheme 系统中的 amb 能力。在第 6 章，我们开始探索多层计算，其基础是一种与泛型过程密切相关的新机制。例如，我们修改了算术，使一个原本从数值参数计算数值结果的程序，无须修改，就能扩展为计算相同的结果，并附带单位。结果的单位由输入的单位自动推导，且会检查组合时单位是否一致：把 5 千克加到 2 米上会发出错误信号。我们用同一分层机制增强程序，使其携带依赖关系，这样结果就会自动引用生成该结果所用各项材料的来源。Because all sane computer languages are universal, programmers do not have an excuse that a solution cannot be expressed in some language. If seriously pressed, good programmers can make an interpreter or compiler for any language they please in any language they are stuck with. This is not very hard, but it is probably the most powerful move a programmer can make. In chapter 5 we showed how to make increasingly powerful languages by interpretation and compilation. We started with a simple applicative-order interpreter for a Scheme-like language. For extensibility, the interpreter was built on generic procedures. We then extended it to allow procedure definitions to declare lazy formal parameters. Next we compiled the language to a combination of execution procedures—a system of combinators. We then added a model of nondeterministic evaluation, with the amb operator. Finally, we showed how by exposing the underlying continuations we could arrange to get the power of amb in the underlying Scheme system. In chapter 6 we began to explore multilayer computations, based on a novel mechanism closely related to generic procedures. For example, we modified our arithmetic so that a program that computes numerical results from numerical arguments could be extended, without modification, to compute the same results, augmented with units. The units of the result are automatically derived from the units of the inputs, and combinations are checked for consistent units: adding 5 kilograms to 2 meters will signal an error. We used the same layering mechanism to augment programs to carry dependencies, so that a result automatically has reference to the sources of the ingredients that went into making that result.

第 7 章的传播子模型，实际上是一种思考大型系统内部管线连接的方式。尽管本章展示的例子中，传播子都是简单的算术函数或关系，但这一思想要普遍得多。传播子可以是硬件，也可以是软件。它可以是一个简单函数，也可以是一台执行海量运算的大型计算机。如果是软件，可以用任何语言编写。事实上，传播子系统不必是同质的。不同传播子可以用不同方式构建。单元可以专门保存不同种类的信息，并按自己偏好的方式合并信息。传播子与单元之间的通信，可以是芯片上的信号，也可以是全球网络上的信号。唯一重要的是，传播子查询单元以及向单元添加信息的协议。The propagator model of chapter 7 is really a way of thinking about the plumbing of large systems. Although, in the examples we show in this chapter, the propagators are all simple arithmetic functions or relations, the idea is far more general. A propagator could be hardware or software. It could be a simple function or a huge computer doing an enormous crunch. If it is software, it could be written in any language. Indeed, a system of propagators does not have to be homogeneous. Different propagators may be constructed differently. Cells may be specialized to hold different kinds of information and they may merge information in their own favorite way. The communication between propagators and cells may be signals on a chip or on a global network. All that matters is the protocol for a propagator to query a cell and to add information to a cell.

本书介绍了许多编程思想。现在该由你来评估（evaluate）这些思想，或许还要应用（apply）它们。In this book we introduced many programming ideas. It is now up to you to evaluate them and perhaps apply them.

Appendix: Scheme

编程语言的设计，不应该靠把一个功能堆叠在另一个功能之上，而应该通过消除那些使额外功能显得必要的弱点和限制来完成。Scheme 证明，只需极少数构造表达式的规则，且不限制它们的组合方式，就足以形成一种实用而高效的编程语言，并具备足够的灵活性，支持当今使用的大多数主要编程范式。Programming languages should be designed not by piling feature on top of feature, but by removing the weaknesses and restrictions that make additional features appear necessary. Scheme demonstrates that a very small number of rules for forming expressions, with no restrictions on how they are composed, suffice to form a practical and efficient programming language that is flexible enough to support most of the major programming paradigms in use today.

《Scheme 编程语言 IEEE 标准》[61]，第 3 页IEEE Standard for the Scheme Programming Language [61], p. 3

这里对 Lisp 的 Scheme 方言作一个初步介绍。更详细的介绍请参阅教科书《计算机程序的构造和解释》（SICP）[1]。Here we give an elementary introduction to the Scheme dialect of Lisp. For a longer introduction see the textbook Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (SICP) [1].

关于该语言更精确的说明，请参阅 IEEE 标准 [61] 和《算法语言 Scheme 第七次修订报告》（R7RS）[109]。For a more precise explanation of the language see the IEEE standard [61] and the Seventh Revised Report on the Algorithmic Language Scheme (R7RS) [109]

本书中的一些程序依赖 MIT/GNU Scheme 的非标准功能；有关该系统的文档，请参阅《MIT/GNU Scheme 参考手册》[51]。此外，对于在其他地方记录的 Scheme 功能，《参考手册》的索引提供了指向相应文档的线索。Some of the programs in this book depend on nonstandard features in MIT/GNU Scheme; for documentation of this system see the MIT/GNU Scheme Reference Manual [51]. Also, for Scheme features that are documented elsewhere the index to the Reference Manual provides pointers to the appropriate documents.

B.1 Scheme 基础B.1 Essential Scheme

Scheme 是一种基于表达式的简单编程语言。一个表达式指称一个值。例如，数码 3.14 指称一个熟悉的数的近似值，而数码 22/7 则指称它的另一个近似值。既有我们能直接识别的基本表达式，例如数码，也有若干种复合表达式。Scheme is a simple programming language based on expressions. An expression names a value. For example, the numeral 3.14 names an approximation to a familiar number, and the numeral 22/7 names another approximation to it. There are primitive expressions, such as numerals, that we directly recognize, and there are compound expressions of several kinds.

复合表达式由圆括号界定。以 if 这样的特定关键字开头的，称为特殊形式。不是特殊形式的复合表达式称为组合式，表示将过程应用于参数。Compound expressions are delimited by parentheses. Those that start with distinguished keywords, such as if, are called special forms. Those that are not special forms, called combinations, denote applications of procedures to arguments.

组合式Combinations

组合式——也称过程应用——是由圆括号界定的一个表达式序列：A combination—also called a procedure application—is a sequence of expressions delimited by parentheses:

(operator operand-1 ... operand-n)

组合式中的第一个子表达式称为运算符，被视为指称一个过程；其余子表达式称为运算对象，被视为指称该过程的参数。将过程应用于给定参数时返回的值，就是该组合式所指称的值。例如，The first subexpression in a combination, called the operator, is taken to name a procedure, and the rest of the subexpressions, called the operands, are taken to name the arguments to that procedure. The value returned by the procedure when applied to the given arguments is the value named by the combination. For example,

(+ 1 2.14)

3.14



(+ 1 (* 2 1.07))

3.14

这两个组合式所指称的数，都与数码 3.14 相同。1 在这些例子中，符号 + 和 * 分别指称执行加法和乘法的过程。如果把任意表达式中的任意子表达式，替换为一个与原来的子表达式指称同一事物的表达式，那么整个表达式所指称的事物保持不变。are both combinations that name the same number as the numeral 3.14.1 In these cases the symbols + and * name procedures that add and multiply, respectively. If we replace any subexpression of any expression with an expression that names the same thing as the original subexpression, the thing named by the overall expression remains unchanged.

注意，在 Scheme 中，每一个圆括号都必不可少：既不能增加多余的圆括号，也不能去掉任何一个。Note that in Scheme every parenthesis is essential: you cannot add extra parentheses or remove any.

Lambda 表达式Lambda expressions

正如用数码指称数一样，我们用 lambda 表达式指称过程。2 例如，对输入求平方的过程可以写为：Just as we use numerals to name numbers, we use lambda expressions to name procedures.2 For example, the procedure that squares its input can be written:

(lambda (x) (* x x))

这个表达式可以读作：“一个接收一个参数 x、将 x 与 x 相乘的过程。”当然，可以在任何需要过程的上下文中使用这个表达式。例如，This expression can be read: “The procedure of one argument, x, that multiplies x by x.” Of course, we can use this expression in any context where a procedure is needed. For example,

((lambda (x) (* x x)) 4)

16

lambda 表达式的一般形式为The general form of a lambda expression is

(lambda formal-parameters body)

其中，formal-parameters（通常）是一个用圆括号括起的符号列表，这些符号将作为过程的形式参数名称。当过程应用于参数时，形式参数就以这些参数为值。body 是一个可以引用形式参数的表达式。过程应用的值，就是把过程体中的形式参数替换为相应参数之后，过程体的值。3 where formal-parameters is (usually) a parenthesized list of symbols that will be the names of the formal parameters of the procedure. When the procedure is applied to arguments, the formal parameters will have the arguments as their values. The body is an expression that may refer to the formal parameters. The value of a procedure application is the value of the body of the procedure with the arguments substituted for the formal parameters.3

在上面的例子中，符号 x 是 (lambda (x) (* x x)) 所指称过程的唯一形式参数。该过程应用于数码 4 的值，因此在过程体 (* x x) 中，符号 x 的值为 4，组合式 ((lambda (x) (* x x)) 4) 的值为 16。In the example shown above, the symbol x is the only formal parameter of the procedure named by (lambda (x) (* x x)). That procedure is applied to the value of the numeral 4, so in the body, (* x x), the symbol x has the value 4, and the value of the combination ((lambda (x) (* x x)) 4) is 16.

上面说“通常”，是因为存在例外。有些过程，例如符号 * 所指称的数值乘法过程，可以接收数量不定的参数。我们稍后会解释如何做到这一点（第 389 页）。We said “usually” above because there are exceptions. Some procedures, such as the procedure that multiplies numbers, named by the symbol *, can take an indefinite number of arguments. We will explain how to do that later (on page 389).

定义Definitions

可以用 define 特殊形式为任何对象赋予名称。我们说，该名称标识了一个以该对象为值的变量。例如，如果作出如下定义，We can use the define special form to give a name to any object. We say that the name identifies a variable whose value is the object. For example, if we make the definitions

(define pi 3.141592653589793)



(define square (lambda (x) (* x x)))

就可以在原先可出现该数码或该 lambda 表达式的任何地方，使用符号 pi 和 square。例如，半径为 5 的球的表面积为we can then use the symbols pi and square wherever the numeral or the lambda expression could appear. For example, the area of the surface of a sphere of radius 5 is

(* 4 pi (square 5))

314.1592653589793

使用“语法糖”可以更方便地表达过程定义。求平方过程可以定义为Procedure definitions may be expressed more conveniently using “syntactic sugar.” The squaring procedure may be defined

(define (square x) (* x x))

可以将它读作：“要对 x 求平方，就把 x 与 x 相乘。”which we may read: “To square x multiply x by x.”

在 Scheme 中，过程是一等对象：它们可以作为参数传递，作为值返回，也可以纳入数据结构。例如，可以制作一个过程，实现两个函数复合这一数学概念：4In Scheme, procedures are first-class objects: they may be passed as arguments, returned as values, and incorporated into data structures. For example, it is possible to make a procedure that implements the mathematical notion of the composition of two functions:4

(define compose

  (lambda (f g)

    (lambda (x)

      (f (g x)))))



((compose square sin) 2)

.826821810431806



(square (sin 2))

.826821810431806

值得注意的是，返回的过程 (lambda (x) (f (g x))) 中，f 和 g 的值，就是外层过程 (lambda (f g) ...) 的形式参数的值。这正是 Scheme 词法作用域规则的本质。任何变量的值，都是通过在词法上可见的上下文中查找其绑定来获得的。系统在全局定义的所有变量，都有一个隐含的上下文。（例如，系统在全局将 + 绑定到数值加法过程。）One thing to notice is that the values of f and g in the returned procedure, (lambda (x) (f (g x))), are the values of the formal parameters of the outer procedure, (lambda (f g) ...). This is the essence of the lexical scoping discipline of Scheme. The value of any variable is obtained by finding its binding in the lexically apparent context. There is an implicit context for all the variables defined globally by the system. (For example, + is globally bound by the system to the procedure that adds numbers.)

利用上面用于 square 的语法糖，可以更方便地写出 compose 的定义：Using the syntactic sugar shown above for square, we can write the definition of compose more conveniently:

(define (compose f g)

  (lambda (x)

    (f (g x))))

在 MIT/GNU Scheme 中，可以递归使用这种语法糖，写成：In MIT/GNU Scheme we can use the sugar recursively, to write:

(define ((compose f g) x)

  (f (g x)))

有时，把一个定义置于另一个定义的局部范围内会更有利。例如，可以如下定义 compose：Sometimes it is advantageous to make a definition local to another definition. For example, we may define compose as follows:

(define (compose f g)

  (define (fog x)

    (f (g x)))

  fog)

名称 fog 在 compose 定义之外并没有定义，所以在这个例子中并没有特别大的用处；但对于较大的代码块，为内部各部分命名，常常能使代码更易读。在过程体中，内部定义必须始终位于所有非定义表达式之前。The name fog is not defined outside the definition of compose, so it is not particularly useful in this case, but larger chunks of code are often easier to read if internal pieces are given names. Internal definitions must always precede any expressions that are not definitions in the body of the procedure.

条件式Conditionals

条件表达式可用于从几个表达式中选择一个，以产生一个值。例如，实现绝对值函数的过程可以写成：Conditional expressions may be used to choose among several expressions to produce a value. For example, a procedure that implements the absolute value function may be written:

(define (abs x)

  (cond ((< x 0) (- x))

        ((= x 0) x)

        ((> x 0) x)))

条件式 cond 接收若干子句。每个子句都有一个值可为真或假的谓词表达式，以及一个后件表达式。cond 表达式的值，是第一个谓词表达式为真的子句的后件表达式的值。条件表达式的一般形式为The conditional cond takes a number of clauses. Each clause has a predicate expression, which may be either true or false, and a consequent expression. The value of the cond expression is the value of the consequent expression of the first clause for which the corresponding predicate expression is true. The general form of a conditional expression is

(cond (predicate-1 consequent-1)

      ...

      (prredicate-n consequent-n))

为了方便，有一个特殊关键字 else，可以用作 cond 最后一个子句中的谓词。For convenience there is a special keyword else that can be used as the predicate in the last clause of a cond.

当只需作二选一的选择时，if 特殊形式提供了构造条件式的另一种方式。例如，由于只有在参数为负时才需要特殊处理，因此可以将 abs 定义为：The if special form provides another way to make a conditional when there is only a binary choice to be made. For example, because we have to do something special only when the argument is negative, we could have defined abs as:

(define (abs x)

  (if (< x 0)

      (- x)

      x))

if 表达式的一般形式为The general form of an if expression is

(if predicate consequent alternative)

如果谓词为真，if 表达式的值就是后件的值；否则就是替代项的值。If the predicate is true the value of the if expression is the value of the consequent, otherwise it is the value of the alternative.

递归过程Recursive procedures

有了条件式和定义，就能编写递归过程。例如，要计算 n 的阶乘，可以写成：Given conditionals and definitions, we can write recursive procedures. For example, to compute the nth factorial number we may write:

(define (factorial n)

  (if (= n 0)

      1

      (* n (factorial (- n 1)))))



(factorial 6)

720



(factorial 40)

815915283247897734345611269596115894272000000000

局部名称Local names

let 表达式用于在局部上下文中为对象命名。例如，A let expression is used to give names to objects in a local context. For example,

(define (f radius)

  (let ((area (* 4 pi (square radius)))

        (volume (* 4/3 pi (cube radius))))

    (/ volume area)))



(f 3)

1

let 表达式的一般形式为The general form of a let expression is

(let ((variable-1 expression-1)

      ...

      (variable-n expression-n))

  body)

let 表达式的值，就是在变量 variable-i 分别以表达式 expression-i 的值为值的上下文中，主体表达式的值。表达式 expression-i 不得引用在该 let 表达式中被赋值的任何变量 variable-j。The value of the let expression is the value of the body expression in the context where the variables variable-i have the values of the expressions expression-i. The expressions expression-i may not refer to any of the variables variable-j given values in the let expression.

let* 表达式与 let 表达式相同，区别在于：表达式 expression-i 可以引用在该 let* 表达式中更早被赋值的变量 variable-j。A let* expression is the same as a let expression except that an expression expression-i may refer to variables variable-j given values earlier in the let* expression.

let 表达式的一个小变体提供了编写循环的便捷方式。可以如下编写一个过程，实现计算阶乘的另一种算法：A slight variant of the let expression provides a convenient way to write a loop. We can write a procedure that implements an alternative algorithm for computing factorials as follows:

(define (factorial n)

  (let factlp ((count 1) (answer 1))

    (if (> count n)

        answer

        (factlp (+ count 1) (* count answer)))))



(factorial 6)

720

这里，紧跟在 let 之后的符号 factlp，在局部被定义为一个以变量 count 和 answer 为形式参数的过程。第一次调用时以 1 和 1 为参数，对循环进行初始化。之后每次调用名为 factlp 的过程时，这些变量都会获得新值，分别是运算对象表达式 (+ count 1) 和 (* count answer) 的值。Here, the symbol factlp following the let is locally defined to be a procedure that has the variables count and answer as its formal parameters. It is called the first time with 1 and 1 as arguments, initializing the loop. Whenever the procedure named factlp is called later, these variables get new values that are the values of the operand expressions (+ count 1) and (* count answer).

表达这个过程的另一种等价方式，是显式定义一个内部过程：An equivalent way to express this procedure has an explicitly defined internal procedure:

(define (factorial n)

  (define (factlp count answer)

    (if (> count n)

        answer

        (factlp (+ count 1) (* count answer))))

  (factlp 1 1))

过程 factlp 是局部定义的，只存在于 factorial 的过程体内。由于 factlp 在词法上被包含在 factorial 的定义内，因此其过程体中 n 的值，就是 factorial 形式参数的值。The procedure factlp is defined locally; it exists only in the body of factorial. Because factlp is lexically enclosed in the definition of factorial, the value of n in its body is the value of the formal parameter of factorial.

复合数据——列表、向量和记录Compound data—lists, vectors, and records

数据可以组合在一起，构成复合数据结构。列表是一种元素按顺序链接的数据结构。向量是一种元素紧密存放在线性数组中的数据结构。可以向列表添加新元素，但访问列表中的第 n 个元素需要与 n 成正比的计算时间。相比之下，向量长度固定，其元素可以在常数时间内访问。记录与向量相似，只是其字段通过名称而不是索引数来寻址。记录还提供新的数据类型，可以通过类型谓词加以区分，并且保证不同于其他类型。Data can be glued together to form compound data structures. A list is a data structure in which the elements are linked sequentially. A vector is a data structure in which the elements are packed in a linear array. New elements can be added to lists, but to access the nth element of a list takes computing time proportional to n. By contrast, a vector is of fixed length, and its elements can be accessed in constant time. A record is similar to a vector, except that its fields are addressed by names rather than index numbers. Records also provide new data types, which are distinguishable by type predicates and are guaranteed to be different from other types.

复合数据对象通过称为构造器的过程由各个组成部分构造而成，其组成部分则通过选择器访问。Compound data objects are constructed from components by procedures called constructors and the components are accessed by selectors.

过程 list 是列表的构造器。谓词 list? 对任何列表都为真，对所有其他类型的数据都为假。5The procedure list is the constructor for lists. The predicate list? is true of any list, and false of all other types of data.5

例如，For example,

(define a-list (list 6 946 8 356 12 620))



a-list

(6 946 8 356 12 620)



(list? a-list)

#t



(list? 3)

#f

这里，#t 和 #f 分别是布尔真值和假值的打印表示。6Here #t and #f are the printed representations of the boolean values true and false.6

列表由序对构成。序对用构造器 cons 创建。序对两个组成部分的选择器是 car 和 cdr（读作“could-er”）。7Lists are built from pairs. A pair is made using the constructor cons. The selectors for the two components of the pair are car and cdr (pronounced “could-er”).7

(define a-pair (cons 1 2))



a-pair

(1 . 2)



(car a-pair)

1



(cdr a-pair)

2

列表是一串序对构成的链，每个序对的 car 是列表元素，每个序对的 cdr 是下一个序对，唯独最后一个 cdr 除外，它是一个可区分的值，称为空列表，写作 ()。因此，A list is a chain of pairs, such that the car of each pair is the list element and the cdr of each pair is the next pair, except for the last cdr, which is a distinguishable value called the empty list and written (). Thus,

(car a-list)

6



(cdr a-list)

(946 8 356 12 620)



(car (cdr a-list))

946



(define another-list

  (cons 32 (cdr a-list)))



another-list

(32 946 8 356 12 620)



(car (cdr another-list))

946

列表 a-list 和 another-list 共享它们的尾部（即它们的 cdr）。The lists a-list and another-list share their tail (their cdr).

谓词 pair? 对序对为真，对所有其他类型的数据为假。谓词 null? 仅对空列表为真。The predicate pair? is true of pairs and false of all other types of data. The predicate null? is true only of the empty list.

向量比列表简单。有一个可用于创建向量的构造器 vector，以及一个用于访问向量元素的选择器 vector-ref。在 Scheme 中，所有使用数值索引的选择器都从零开始计数：Vectors are simpler than lists. There is a constructor vector that can be used to make vectors and a selector vector-ref for accessing the elements of a vector. In Scheme all selectors that use a numerical index are zero-based:

(define a-vector

  (vector 37 63 49 21 88 56))



a-vector

#(37 63 49 21 88 56)



(vector-ref a-vector 3)

21



(vector-ref a-vector 0)

37

向量的打印表示，在开头的圆括号之前有一个字符 #，以此区别于列表的打印表示。The printed representation of a vector is distinguished from the printed representation of a list by the character # before the initial parenthesis.

有一个谓词 vector?，它对向量为真，对所有其他类型的数据为假。There is a predicate vector? that is true of vectors and false for all other types of data.

Scheme 提供了一个通过数值索引选择列表元素的选择器 list-ref，与向量的选择器类似：Scheme provides a numerical selector for the elements of a list, list-ref, analogous to the selector for vectors:

(list-ref a-list 3)

356



(list-ref a-list 0)

6

记录更复杂一些，因为必须先声明，才能构造。一个简单的记录声明可以是Records are more involved, as they must be declared before they can be constructed. A simple record declaration might be

(define-record-type point

    (make-point x y)

    point?

  (x point-x)

  (y point-y))

作出这一声明后，就可以创建和使用点：After this declaration, we can make and use points:

(define p (make-point 1 2))



(point? p)

#t



(point-x p)

1

(point-y p)

2

列表、向量和记录的元素可以是任何种类的数据，包括数、过程、列表、向量和记录。在 Scheme 在线文档中，还能找到许多其他操纵列表、向量和记录的过程。The elements of lists, vectors, and records may be any kind of data, including numbers, procedures, lists, vectors, and records. Numerous other procedures for manipulating lists, vectors, and records can be found in the Scheme online documentation.

参数数量不定的过程Procedures with an indefinite number of arguments

我们已经看到的过程，都是用一个形式参数列表来规定的，这些形式参数绑定到调用过程时所传入的参数。然而，有许多过程接收数量不定的参数。例如，执行数值乘法的算术过程，可以接收任意数量的参数。要定义这样的过程，我们把形式参数指定为单个符号，而不是符号列表。这个单一符号随后会绑定到调用过程时所传入参数组成的列表。例如，给定一个二元乘法过程 *:binary，可以写成The procedures that we have seen are specified with a list of formal parameters that are bound to the arguments that the procedure is called with. However, there are many procedures that take an indefinite number of arguments. For example, the arithmetic procedure that multiplies numbers can take any number of arguments. To define such a procedure we specify the formal parameters as a single symbol rather than a list of symbols. The single symbol is then bound to a list of the arguments that the procedure is called with. For example, given a binary multiplier *:binary we can write

(define * (lambda args (accumulate *:binary 1 args)))

其中，accumulate 就是where accumulate is just

(define (accumulate proc initial lst)

  (if (null? lst)

      initial

      (proc (car lst)

            (accumulate proc initial (cdr lst)))))

有时，我们希望一个过程既接收一些具名参数，又接收数量不定的其他参数。在过程定义中，如果参数列表在最后一个参数名称前有一个点（称为点尾记法），就表示点之前的参数将绑定到最前面的实参，而最后一个参数则绑定到所有剩余实参组成的列表。在上面的 * 示例中，没有开头的实参，因此 args 的值是全部实参组成的列表。所以，也可以把 * 定义为：Sometimes we want a procedure that takes some named arguments and an indefinite number of others. In a procedure definition a parameter list that has a dot before the last parameter name (called dotted-tail notation) indicates that the parameters before the dot will be bound to the initial arguments, and the final parameter will be bound to a list of any remaining arguments. In the example of * above there are no initial arguments, so the value of args is a list of all the arguments. Thus, alternatively, we could define * as:

(define (* . args) (accumulate *:binary 1 args))

由 - 指称的过程更有趣，因为它要求至少有一个参数：当只有一个参数时，- 对其取负；当参数多于一个时，它从第一个参数中减去其余参数：The procedure named by - is more interesting, as it requires at least one argument: when given one argument - negates it; when given more than one argument it subtracts the rest from the first:

(define (- x . ys)

  (if (null? ys)       ; Only one argument?

      (-:unary x)

      (-:binary x (accumulate +:binary 0 ys))))

这也可以写成This can also be written

(define -

  (lambda (x . ys)

    (if (null? ys)

      (-:unary x)

      (-:binary x (accumulate +:binary 0 ys)))))

上面例子中的 args 和 ys 这样的参数称为剩余参数，因为它们绑定到剩余的实参。Parameters like args and ys in the examples above are called rest parameters because they are bound to the rest of the arguments.

符号Symbols

符号是一种非常重要的基本数据类型，我们用它来构造程序和代数表达式。你大概已经注意到，Scheme 程序看上去就像列表。事实上，它们就是列表。构成程序的列表中，有些元素是符号，例如 + 和 vector。8Symbols are a very important kind of primitive data type that we use to make programs and algebraic expressions. You probably have noticed that Scheme programs look just like lists. In fact, they are lists. Some of the elements of the lists that make up programs are symbols, such as + and vector.8

如果要编写能够操纵程序的程序，就需要能够写出一个指称这种符号的表达式。这通过引用机制实现。符号 + 的名称是表达式 ’+；一般而言，一个表达式的名称，就是在该表达式之前加上一个单引号字符。因此，表达式 (+ 3 a) 的名称是 ’(+ 3 a)。If we are to make programs that can manipulate programs, we need to be able to write an expression that names such a symbol. This is accomplished by the mechanism of quotation. The name of the symbol + is the expression ’+, and in general the name of an expression is the expression preceded by a single quote character. Thus the name of the expression (+ 3 a) is ’(+ 3 a).

可以使用谓词 eq? 检验两个符号是否同一。例如，可以编写一个程序，判断某个表达式是否是一个和式：We can test if two symbols are identical by using the predicate eq?. For example, we can write a program to determine if an expression is a sum:

(define (sum? expression)

  (and (pair? expression)

       (eq? (car expression) ’+)))



(sum? ’(+ 3 a))

#t



(sum? ’(* 3 a))

#f

考虑一下，如果省去表达式 (sum? ’(+ 3 a)) 中的引用符号，会发生什么。如果变量 a 的值为 4，我们问的就会是 7 是否是一个和式。但我们想知道的是，表达式 (+ 3 a) 是否是一个和式。这就是需要引用符号的原因。Consider what would happen if we left out the quote in the expression (sum? ’(+ 3 a)). If the variable a had the value 4, we would be asking if 7 is a sum. But what we wanted to know was whether the expression (+ 3 a) is a sum. That is why we need the quote.

反引号Backquote

要操纵模式以及其他形式的基于列表的语法，常常需要在同一个表达式中交错放置引用的部分和求值的部分。Lisp 系统提供了一种称为准引用的机制，可以轻松做到这一点。To manipulate patterns and other forms of list-based syntax, it is often useful to intersperse quoted and evaluated parts in the same expression. Lisp systems provide a mechanism called quasiquotation that makes this easy.

正如使用单引号字符表示普通引用一样，我们使用反引号字符表示准引用。9 这种部分引用的表达式写成一个列表，其中需要求值的部分以逗号字符为前缀。例如，Just as we use the apostrophe character to indicate regular quotation, we use the backquote character to indicate quasiquotation.9 We specify such a partially quoted expression as a list in which the parts to be evaluated are prefixed with the comma character. For example,

‘(a b ,(+ 20 3) d)

(a b 23 d)

反引号机制还支持向列表表达式中“拼接”：一个子表达式经过求值产生一个列表，随后把它拼接到外围列表中。例如，The backquote mechanism also provides for “splicing” into a list expression: an evaluated subexpression produces a list, which is then spliced into the enclosing list. For example,

‘(a b ,@(list (+ 20 3) (- 20 3)) d)

(a b 23 17 d)

关于准引用的更详细说明，请查阅《Scheme 报告》[109]。Consult the Scheme Report [109] for a more detailed explanation of quasiquotation.

效应Effects

有时，在计算过程中，我们需要执行某个动作，例如绘制一个点或打印一个值。这样的动作称为效应。10例如，为了更详细地观察阶乘程序如何算出答案，我们可以在内部过程 factlp 的过程体中插入一条 write-line 语句，在每次迭代时打印一个包含计数值和答案的列表：Sometimes we need to perform an action, such as plotting a point or printing a value, in the process of a computation. Such an action is called an effect.10 For example, to see in more detail how the factorial program computes its answer, we can interpolate a write-line statement in the body of the factlp internal procedure to print a list of the count and the answer for each iteration:

(define (factorial n)

  (let factlp ((count 1) (answer 1))

    (write-line (list count answer))

    (if (> count n)

        answer

        (factlp (+ count 1) (* count answer)))))

调用修改后的 factorial 过程时，我们可以看到计数器逐次递增、答案逐步形成的过程：When we call the modified factorial procedure we can watch the counter being incremented and the answer being built:

(factorial 6)

(1 1)

(2 1)

(3 2)

(4 6)

(5 24)

(6 120)

(7 720)

720

每个过程或 let 的体，以及每个 cond 子句的结果部分，都允许使用具有效应的语句。效应语句通常没有有用的值。体或子句中的最后一个表达式产生要返回的值。在这个例子中，if 表达式产生 factorial 的值。The body of every procedure or let, as well as the consequent of every cond clause, allows statements that have effects to be used. The effect statement generally has no useful value. The final expression in the body or clause produces the value that is returned. In this example the if expression produces the value of the factorial.

赋值Assignments

打印一个值或绘制一个点这样的效应相当温和，但还有更强大（因而也更危险）的效应，称为赋值。赋值会改变变量的值，或数据结构中某个条目的值。我们所计算的几乎都是数学函数：对于特定的输入，它总是产生相同的结果。然而，借助赋值，我们可以创建行为会随着使用而变化的对象。例如，可以用 set! 创建一个每调用一次就把计数值加一的装置：11Effects like printing a value or plotting a point are pretty benign, but there are more powerful (and thus dangerous) effects, called assignments. An assignment changes the value of a variable or an entry in a data structure. Almost everything we are computing is a mathematical function: for a particular input it always produces the same result. However, with assignment we can make objects that change their behavior as they are used. For example, we can use set! to make a device that increments a count every time we call it:11

(define (make-counter)

  (let ((count 0))

    (lambda ()

      (set! count (+ count 1))

      count)))

我们来创建两个计数器：Let's make two counters:

(define c1 (make-counter))

(define c2 (make-counter))

这两个计数器拥有各自独立的局部状态。调用一个计数器，会使其局部状态变量 count 递增，并返回它的值。These two counters have independent local state. Calling a counter causes it to increment its local state variable, count, and return its value.

(c1)

1



(c1)

2



(c2)

1



(c1)

3



(c2)

2

为了对序对、列表或向量等数据结构中的元素赋值，Scheme 提供了：For assigning to the elements of a data structure, such as a pair, a list, or a vector, Scheme provides:

(set-car! pair new-value)

(set-cdr! pair new-value)



(list-set! list index new-value)

(vector-set! vector index new-value)

定义记录时，可以允许对其字段赋值（对比第 388 页：A record may be defined to allow assignments to its fields (compare page 388:

(define-record-type point

    (make-point x y)

    point?

  (x point-x set-x!)

  (y point-y set-y!))



(define p (make-point 1 2))



(point-x p)

1

(point-y p)

2



(set-x! p 3)



(point-x p)

3

(point-y p)

2

一般来说，尽可能避免赋值是一种良好的实践；不过，需要时也可以使用赋值。12In general, it is good practice to avoid assignments when possible, but if you need them they are available.12

B.2 更高级的内容B.2 More advanced stuff

Scheme 提供了许多更强大的特性，但我们不打算在这里逐一介绍。例如，你很可能会想了解哈希表。一般来说，最好的资料是Scheme provides many more powerful features, but we won't try to describe them here. For example, you will probably want to know about hash tables. In general, the best sources are the

《算法语言 Scheme 修订报告》（R7RS）[109] 和《MIT/GNU Scheme 参考手册》[51]。不过，下面介绍两个相当复杂的特性，在阅读本书时，你可能需要查阅它们：Revised Report on the Algorithmic Language Scheme (R7RS) [109] and the MIT/GNU Scheme Reference Manual [51]. But here are two fairly complex features that you may need to reference while reading this book:

动态绑定Dynamic binding

有时，我们希望指定某项求值或某个动作的执行方式——例如，指定打印数字时使用的进制。为此，我们使用一种称为参数对象的对象。We sometimes want to specify the way in which some evaluation or action will be accomplished—for example, to specify the radix to use when printing a number. To do this we use an object called a parameter.

例如，Scheme 过程 number->string 会生成一个字符串，以给定进制表示一个数：For example, the Scheme procedure number->string produces a character string that represents a number in a given radix:

(number->string 100 2)

"1100100"

(number->string 100 16)

"64"

假设我们希望在一个复杂程序的许多地方使用 number->string，该程序通过调用 myprog 运行，但我们又希望能够控制程序运行时所使用的进制。我们可以创建一个默认值为 10 的参数对象 radix 来做到这一点：Suppose we want to use number->string in many places in a complex program that we run by calling myprog, but we want to be able to control the radix used when the program is run. We can accomplish this by making a parameter radix with the default value 10:

(define radix (make-parameter 10))

不带实参调用参数对象，即可取得它的值：The value of a parameter is obtained by calling the parameter with no arguments:

(radix)

10

我们定义一个专用版本的 number->string，用来代替 number->string：We define a specialized version of number->string to use instead of number->string:

(define (number->string-radix number)

  (number->string number (radix)))

执行 (myprog) 时，每次调用 number->string-radix 都会产生一个十进制字符串，因为 (radix) 的默认值为 10。不过，我们可以用 parameterize 包裹程序，使这次执行改用另一种进制：In an execution of (myprog), every call to number->string-radix will produce a decimal string, because the default value of (radix) is 10. However, we can wrap our program with parameterize to change the execution to use another radix:

(parameterize ((radix 2))

  (myprog))

parameterize 的语法与 let 的语法相同，但它只能用于由 make-parameter 创建的参数对象。The syntax of parameterize is the same as the syntax of let, but it can be used only for parameters created by make-parameter.

过程束Bundles

MIT/GNU Scheme 提供了一种简单的机制，用于构建一组共享状态的相关过程：过程束。过程束是一个将工作委派给一组具名过程的过程：传给过程束的第一个实参是要使用的被委派过程的名称，其余实参则传给所指定的被委派过程。这类似于某些面向对象语言的工作方式，但要简单得多，而且没有类或继承。MIT/GNU Scheme provides a simple mechanism for building a collection of related procedures with shared state: a bundle. A bundle is a procedure that delegates to a collection of named procedures: the first argument to the bundle is the name of the delegate to use, and the rest of the arguments are passed to the specified delegate. This is similar to the way that some object-oriented languages work, but much simpler, and without classes or inheritance.

过程束有时也称为接收消息的过程，其中消息类型是被委派过程的名称，消息体则是实参。13这种说法强调，过程束支持一种消息传递协议，可以把它看作通信网络中的一个节点。A bundle is sometimes called a message-accepting procedure, where the message type is the delegate name and the message body is the arguments.13 This emphasizes that the bundle supports a message-passing protocol and can be thought of as a node in a communications network.

下面是一个简单的例子：Here is a simple example:

(define (make-point x y)

  (define (get-x) x)

  (define (get-y) y)

  (define (set-x! new-x) (set! x new-x))

  (define (set-y! new-y) (set! y new-y))

  (bundle point? get-x get-y set-x! set-y!))

过程 make-point 定义了四个内部过程，它们共享状态变量 x 和 y。bundle 宏创建一个过程束过程，以这四个过程作为被委派过程。The procedure make-point defines four internal procedures, which share the state variables x and y. The bundle macro creates a bundle procedure, for which those procedures are the delegates.

bundle 宏的第一个实参是一个用 make-bundle-predicate 创建的谓词。所创建的过程束将满足这个谓词：The first argument to the bundle macro is a predicate, which is created with make-bundle-predicate. The bundle that is created will satisfy this predicate:

(define point? (make-bundle-predicate ’point))



(define p1 (make-point 3 4))

(define p2 (make-point -1 1))



(point? p1)

#t

(point? p2)

#t

(point? (lambda (x) x))

#f

make-bundle-predicate 的实参是一个符号，用于在调试时标识该谓词。The argument to make-bundle-predicate is a symbol that is used to identify the predicate when debugging.

如果不需要谓词，bundle 也接受 #f 作为第一个实参。在这种情况下，将无法把所创建的过程束过程与其他过程区分开来。If a predicate is not needed, bundle alternatively accepts #f as a first argument. In that case there will be no way to distinguish the created bundle procedure from other procedures.

bundle 宏的其余实参是被委派过程的名称：get-x、get-y、set-x! 和 set-y!。宏在其词法环境中查找这些名称，取得相应的被委派过程。然后创建一个过程束过程，其中包含从各个名称到相应被委派过程的关联。The remaining arguments to the bundle macro are the names of the delegate procedures: get-x, get-y, set-x!, and set-y!. These names are looked up in the lexical environment of the macro to get the corresponding delegate procedures. A bundle procedure is then created, containing an association from each name to its delegate procedure.

调用所生成的过程束过程时，它的第一个实参是一个符号，而且必须是某个被委派过程的名称。利用这一关联，便能选出所指定的被委派过程，然后以过程束过程的其余实参作为实参调用它。When the resulting bundle procedure is called, its first argument is a symbol that must be the name of one of the delegate procedures. The association is used to select the named delegate procedure, which is then called with the bundle procedure's remaining arguments as its arguments.

使用过程束比描述它容易得多：It is easier to use a bundle than to describe it:

(p1 ’get-x)

3

(p1 ’get-y)

4

(p2 ’get-x)

-1

(p2 ’get-y)

1



(p1 'set-x! 5)



(p1 ’get-x)

5

(p2 ’get-x)

-1

 

1 在示例中，我们在输入表达式之后，用 slanted 字符显示 Scheme 系统将打印的值。1 In examples we show the value that would be printed by the Scheme system using slanted characters following the input expression.
2 逻辑学家 Alonzo Church [16] 发明了 λ 记法，用来指定一个具有具名形参的匿名函数：λx[关于 x 的表达式]。它读作：“这样一个单实参函数：在所示表达式中用实参替换 x，便得到其值。”2 The logician Alonzo Church [16] invented λ notation to allow the specification of an anonymous function of a named parameter: λx[expression in x]. This is read, “That function of one argument whose value is obtained by substituting the argument for x in the indicated expression.”
3 我们说，形参被绑定到实参，而绑定的作用域就是过程体。3 We say that the formal parameters are bound to the arguments, and the scope of the binding is the body of the procedure.
4 示例采用缩进来改善可读性。Scheme 不在意多余的空白，因此我们可以按需要添加空白，使代码更容易阅读。4 The examples are indented to help with readability. Scheme does not care about extra white space, so we may add as much as we please to make things easier to read.
5 谓词是返回真或假的过程。按照 Scheme 的惯例，我们通常给谓词起一个以问号（?）结尾的名称，基本算术比较谓词除外：=、<、>、<= 和 >=。这只是一种风格约定。对 Scheme 而言，问号只是一个普通字符。5 A predicate is a procedure that returns true or false. By Scheme cultural convention, we usually give a predicate a name ending with a question mark (?), except for the elementary arithmetic comparison predicates: =, <, >, <=, and >=. This is just a stylistic convention. To Scheme the question mark is just an ordinary character.
6 条件表达式（if 和 cond）将任何不是显式的 #f 的谓词值都视为真。这很方便，但也令一些人感到不快。6 It is convenient, but irritating to some, that the conditional expressions (if and cond) treat any predicate value that is not explicitly #f as true.
7 这些名称是历史偶然的产物。它们分别代表 IBM 704 计算机的“寄存器地址部分的内容”和“寄存器减量部分的内容”；20 世纪 50 年代末，第一个 Lisp 实现就是在这台计算机上完成的。Scheme 是 Lisp 的一种方言。7 These names are accidents of history. They stand for “Contents of the Address part of Register” and “Contents of the Decrement part of Register” of the IBM 704 computer, which was used for the first implementation of Lisp in the late 1950s. Scheme is a dialect of Lisp.
8 符号可以包含任意多个字符。通常，符号不能包含空白或分隔字符，例如圆括号、方括号、引号、逗号或 #；不过，有一些特殊记法，可以让符号名称包含任意字符。8 A symbol may have any number of characters. A symbol may not normally contain whitespace or delimiter characters, such as parentheses, brackets, quotation marks, comma, or #; but there are special notations that allow any characters to be included in a symbol's name.
9 在美式键盘上，反引号字符“‘”位于以波浪号“∼”作为上档字符的那个键的下档位置。9 On an American keyboard the backquote character “‘” is the lowercase character on the key that has the tilde character “∼” as the uppercase character.
10 这是计算机科学术语。效应就是对某种事物的改变。例如，write-line 通过在显示屏上打印某些内容来改变显示。10 This is computer-science jargon. An effect is a change to something. For example, write-line changes the display by printing something to the display.
11 另一个惯例是，把具有“副作用”的过程的名称以叹号（!）结尾。这是在提醒读者：改变效应发生的顺序，可能会改变程序运行的结果。11 It is another cultural convention that we terminate the name of a procedure that has “side effects” with an exclamation point (!). This warns the reader that changing the order of effects may change the results of running the program.
12 不使用赋值的编程方式称为函数式编程。函数式程序通常比命令式程序更容易理解，错误也更少。12 The discipline of programming without assignments is called functional programming. Functional programs are generally easier to understand and have fewer bugs than imperative programs.
13 这一术语可以追溯到 ACTOR 框架 [58] 和 Smalltalk 编程语言 [46]。13 This terminology dates back to the ACTOR framework [58] and the Smalltalk programming language [46].
